author: shykes
body:
## Problem

To test the Go client library, we built a custom test harness. That harness only runs in GitHub Actions; it relies heavily on single-use glue code; and it jams together testing dimensions that should be decoupled.

Concretely: the `TestProvision` test is wired into `publish.yml` and only runs on pushes to main and tags, never on a PR. The rest of the suite runs through `go-sdk-dev`, a Dagger module built only to call `go test`. And one suite does three jobs at once — bootstrap the CLI, start an engine, test the client — so a developer with plain `go test` can't run any of it.

## Solution

Turn them into ordinary Go tests. The engine-dependent tests move to `sdk/go/e2e`, a normal Go module which can be tested by `go test`, either called directly by the user, or orchestrated by a generic Dagger module such as `github.com/dagger/go`.

| Dependency | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Github Actions | required 🔴  | not required 🟢  |
| Single-use Dagger module | required 🔴 | not required 🟢  |
| Run with native `go test` | not supported 🔴  | supported 🟢  |


- `sdk/go` holds unit tests with no engine dependency, and pre-existing documentation examples.
- `sdk/go/e2e` holds two e2e test suites: `TestBootstrap` (the library downloads and runs a CLI), and `TestAgainstEngines` (call the library against a matrix of engines)

## Task list

> **TL;DR:** `sdk/go/e2e`'s `TestBootstrap` and `TestAgainstEngines` both fail during their shared harness setup. The nested Dagger client detects the container's projected filesystem as its workspace instead of inheriting the caller's workspace.

- [ ] Fix both tests by implementing [#13054](https://github.com/dagger/dagger/issues/13054).

author: jeswr
body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** (site lane). Self-identifying: this PR was prepared by an automated agent.

Fixes the firefox-specific red in the **nightly cross-browser** lane (`e2e/download-app.spec.ts`), bead **sq-bx1zv** (a `sq-0rbfn` follow-up).

## Root cause (a real Firefox robustness gap, not a test artifact)

The download-app specs run with Playwright's `serviceWorkers: "block"`. In **Firefox**, `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` *fulfils* its promise with `registration === undefined` when SW registration is disallowed for the context, rather than rejecting. The vendored `coi-serviceworker.js` fulfilment handler then read `registration.scope`, throwing:

```
TypeError: can't access property "scope", registration is undefined
```

**Chromium** rejects that same case and takes the existing `(err)` branch, so the error only surfaced in the nightly firefox lane (first seen run 28853194264). The same `undefined`-registration fulfilment can be hit by a real firefox user in private-browsing / policy configs — so this is a genuine (if minor) UX/robustness defect, not something to paper over in the spec allowlist.

## Fix

In `site/public/coi-serviceworker.js`, guard the fulfilment handler: if `registration` is falsy, log once and return — the isolation headers simply are not applied and the page keeps working single-threaded. This is the **same graceful-degradation posture as the existing reject branch**, so no real behaviour is hidden. An explicit `!registration` guard (not `?.`) is used so this vendored file still parses in the oldest SW-capable engines.

I did **not** touch the spec's console-error allowlist: hardening the source removes the throw in *both* browsers, so the error is no longer produced at all (the correct fix per the bead — "do NOT blanket-ignore all console errors").

## Gates (all green)

- `cd js && build:wasm` prereq satisfied (bundle present); `cd site && npm run build` static export ✅ (`out/coi-serviceworker.js` emitted with the guard)
- `npm run lint` — 0 warnings/errors ✅
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅
- basePath `/sparq` unchanged; no route touched; no axe rule / visual threshold weakened.

**Not armed** — leaving for review.

author: acuhlmann
body:
Adds Matter.js (2D rigid-body physics) as the second allowlisted library for Anything-mode documents, alongside the existing d3 support. This enables pages to use physics simulations and constraints via the `<!-- @lib:matter -->` marker.

## Key changes

- **Registry & vendoring**: Added Matter.js 0.20.0 to `ANYTHING_LIBS` in `packages/shared/src/anythingLibs.ts` with metadata (name, version, global, prompt summary). Pinned the devDep in `packages/shared/package.json` and regenerated vendored bytes via `vendorAnythingLibs.mjs`.

- **Runtime sandbox robustness**: Enhanced `anythingRuntimeSandbox.js` with three new Proxy traps (`has`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `defineProperty`) to support libraries that monkey-patch host objects by walking the prototype chain with `hasOwnProperty` and destructuring property descriptors (the Tone.js pattern). This prevents "descriptor is undefined" errors when libraries introspect inert stubs.

- **Test coverage**: 
  - Added `host-object monkey-patching` test in `anythingRuntimeCheck.test.js` to verify the new descriptor trap works.
  - Added `vendored libraries execute cleanly` test that runs real d3 + matter bytes through the sandbox, catching future version bumps that break under jsdom.
  - Extended bench corpus with `valid-lib-matter` case (physics simulation on canvas).
  - Added drift guard in `anythingPrompts.test.js` to ensure design-guide prose only references allowlisted lib ids.

- **UI & documentation**:
  - Added lib badge component in `AnythingRenderer.jsx` that displays injected library names and versions in the corner of rendered pages (via `getAnythingLibInfo` lookup from registry metadata).
  - Styled the badge in `App.css` with tooltip showing provenance ("nothing loads from the network").
  - Hidden badge in thumbnail contexts (too small to read).
  - Updated ADR-0008 addendum with accurate chunk size (~355KB raw / ~117KB gzipped for d3 + matter combined).
  - Added `docs/recipes/add-anything-lib.md` playbook for future library additions (gate questions, step-by-step process).

- **Shared exports**: Added `findAnythingLibMarkers` and `getAnythingLibInfo` to the public API for marker detection and registry lookups; updated `ANYTHING_LIB_IDS` export for prompt drift guards.

## Implementation notes

- The lib badge is observable but non-intrusive: injection is deliberately invisible in the document (no visible script tags), so the badge makes the otherwise-hidden vendoring observable to users.
- Matter.js was chosen as the second lib because it's compact (81KB), executes cleanly under jsdom (unlike Tone.js, which validates Web Audio semantics at load), and solves a real class of asks (physics/constraints/collisions).
- The descriptor trap returns a configurable accessor for non-existent properties, allowing libraries to safely redefine them without triggering proxy invariant violations.
- Bench results included: 23 test cases, 34.78% accept rate (8 valid + 15 policy/quality/runtime rejections), 100% expectation match, all runtime checks passed.

body:
Migrates the alignment conversions to taffy's new safe-alignment style types: `AlignItems`/`AlignContent` and friends are now structs pairing a keyword with a safety modifier, constructed via associated constants (e.g. `AlignItems::START`) instead of enum variants.

The motivating change in this release is [taffy #911](https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/commit/df2663aad35801f7522f6878a0300646dfe624f7) ("More correct caching logic"), which keys taffy's per-node measure cache on axis, parent size, and available space. Today GPUI is largely immune to the old cache-key conflation because text answers every sizing probe with the same width; the follow-up PR in this stack (honest min-content text measurement) returns different sizes for different constraints, which makes cache-key correctness a prerequisite. 0.12.1 additionally hotfixes two block layout/caching regressions in 0.12.0, and 0.11.0's grid fix (resolving item percentages against the grid area rather than the container) comes along as well.

Stack:
1. **This PR** — taffy 0.12.1
2. #60722 — honest min-content text measurement
3. #60723 — CSS `auto` grid tracks for table-like column sizing

author: mikeldking
body:
# Support `trace_annotations` in the span filter DSL

Closes #14055.

## What changed

The span filter DSL (`src/phoenix/trace/dsl/filter.py`) now understands
**trace-level** annotations via a new `trace_annotations` accessor, mirroring
the existing span-level `annotations` / `evals` vocabulary:

```python
trace_annotations['quality'].score >= 0.5
trace_annotations['quality'].label == 'good'
trace_annotations['quality']              # existence check
```

These expressions are usable anywhere the span/trace filter DSL is accepted —
the Phoenix UI filter bar, the `validateSpanFilterCondition` GraphQL resolver,
and `SpanQuery().where(...)` in the Python client.

### Backend (`filter.py`)

- Added `trace_annotations` to the DSL vocabulary. The annotation accessors are
  now defined once in `_ANNOTATION_ACCESSORS` and reused to build both regex
  patterns and the `_is_annotation` guard (previously the list was duplicated in
  three places).
- `AliasedAnnotationRelation` gained a `kind` field (`"span"` | `"trace"`). A
  `"trace"` relation aliases `models.TraceAnnotation` and is joined on
  `TraceAnnotation.trace_rowid == Span.trace_rowid`, so a span matches when the
  **trace it belongs to** carries the annotation. Span relations are unchanged
  (`SpanAnnotation.span_rowid == Span.id`).
- `_apply_eval_aliasing` now keys aliases by `(kind, name)` so a span- and a
  trace-level annotation that share a name resolve to two distinct joins.
  Because `annotations['q'].score` is a substring of
  `trace_annotations['q'].score`, replacements are applied **longest-match
  first** to keep the global `str.replace` from corrupting the longer
  expression.
- New helper `_annotation_relation_kind()` maps an accessor to its relation.

### Frontend (`SpanFilterConditionField.tsx`)

- Added a `trace_annotations` keyword to the typeahead field completions and two
  suggestion snippets (`filter by trace annotation score` / `... label`), so the
  accessor is discoverable in the filter bar.

> Note: surfacing real trace-annotation **names** in the typeahead (the way
> `spanAnnotationNames` powers `annotations[...]` completions) would wire the
> already-existing `Project.traceAnnotationsNames` GraphQL field into the
> field's completions query. That requires regenerating Relay artifacts
> (`relay-compiler`), which isn't available in this change's environment, so it
> is intentionally left as a follow-up. The static keyword + snippets already
> make `trace_annotations` discoverable and usable.

### Docs

- `extract-data-from-spans.mdx` and `exporting-annotated-spans.mdx` now document
  `trace_annotations` filtering alongside the existing `annotations` / `evals`
  examples.

## How to verify

Unit tests in `tests/unit/trace/dsl/test_filter.py`:

- `test_apply_eval_aliasing` — new cases for `trace_annotations` score/label/
  existence aliasing and mixed span+trace conditions (asserting distinct,
  correctly-indexed aliases and no substring corruption).
- `test_trace_annotation_filter_joins_trace_annotation_relation` — a
  `trace_annotations[...]` filter joins the `trace_annotations` table (not
  `span_annotations`) and the statement compiles and executes.
- `test_span_and_trace_annotations_join_distinct_relations` — a span- and a
  trace-level annotation of the same name produce two distinct joins.

Run: `make test-python` (or `pytest tests/unit/trace/dsl/test_filter.py`).

Manual check in the UI: open a project's span/trace filter bar and type
`trace_annotations` — the keyword completion and snippets appear; a condition
such as `trace_annotations['quality'].score >= 0.5` validates and filters.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #35988

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On a new session's first prompt, the TUI navigates to the session view and runs `session.sync()` before the server has persisted the user message. Hydration can complete with only the assistant reply, so the user bubble never appears.

This adds an optimistic user message in the sync store at submit time, keeps it through hydration merge, and removes it when the real `message.updated` arrives (or on prompt failure).

### How did you verify your code works?

- `cd packages/tui && bun test test/cli/cmd/tui/sync-live-hydration.test.tsx`
- `cd packages/tui && bun test`
- `cd packages/tui && bun run typecheck`

Added regression test: `optimistic user message survives new session hydration race`.

author: agenciaseniors
body:
## Problema

Un usuario con el **mismo teléfono** en las dos apps (`apps/client` pasajero y `apps/driver` conductor): al iniciar sesión en una, se le **cierra la sesión en la otra**.

## Causa raíz (confirmada con datos de prod)

Ambas apps resuelven el mismo teléfono al **mismo `auth.users`** (email sintético `phone_<n>@tricigo.app` — correcto y por diseño: una persona = un `users`, el tier cuenta viajes como rider + driver).

El problema: `verify-otp` **rotaba el password del usuario en cada login** (`admin.updateUserById(userId, { password })`, Strategy A). En GoTrue, **cambiar el password revoca las demás sesiones del usuario**. Como ambas apps son el mismo `userId`, loguear en la app B revocaba la sesión de la app A → su próximo auto-refresh fallaba → `SIGNED_OUT` → `reset()` de los stores → aparecía deslogueada.

**Evidencia (`auth.sessions` / `auth.refresh_tokens` en prod):**

| Tipo de usuario | Cómo mina sesión | Sesiones concurrentes |
|---|---|---|
| Email / OAuth (`admin@`, Google) | `signInWithPassword` / OAuth — **no rota password** | hasta **5** ✅ |
| Teléfono (`phone_<n>@tricigo.app`) | `verify-otp` → **rota password cada login** | **siempre 1** ❌ |

Conductores con teléfono tienen `sessions=1`, `rt_active=1` y 3–6 refresh tokens revocados; ninguno llega a 2 sesiones jamás. `signInWithPassword` por sí solo **no** revoca. No hay "single session per user" activado.

## Fix

Dejar de rotar el password en cada login. Se deriva un **password determinístico y estable** por usuario (HMAC-SHA256 sobre `userId`, hex) y se reusa, de modo que el happy path es **solo `signInWithPassword`** (que no revoca) → ambas apps coexisten (igual que hoy los usuarios de email).

Cambios (todos en `supabase/functions/verify-otp/index.ts`):

1. **Helper `deriveStablePassword(userId)`** — `Otp1_` + HMAC-SHA256(secret, `otp-pw:<userId>`) en hex. `secret = OTP_PASSWORD_SECRET ?? SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
2. **Strategy A** ahora hace `signInWithPassword(stable)`; solo si falla escribe el password una vez (heal para usuarios existentes / primer login post-deploy) y reintenta. En steady-state: **cero escrituras de password → cero revocación**.
3. **Seed** del password estable al crear usuario nuevo (no hay sesión previa → no revoca; primer login toma el happy path).
4. **Update de `phone` condicional** — solo cuando el phone falta, no en cada login (elimina una segunda posible fuente de revocación).
5. **Magic-link** queda como fallback (tampoco rota password → también preserva sesiones).
6. Comentario del **conflicto latente** con `set-password-after-otp` (inactivo hoy).

## Comportamiento residual (aceptado)

- **Heal de una sola vez:** el primer login post-deploy de cada usuario existente escribe el password una vez (revoca su única sesión previa; invisible porque se está logueando de nuevo). A partir de ahí, write-free.

## Secret

Recomendado setear `OTP_PASSWORD_SECRET` (dedicado) en los EF secrets. Cae a `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` si no existe, así que **funciona out-of-the-box**.

## Verificación

- **Funcional:** loguear en driver (capturar `refresh_token_A`), luego en client con el mismo teléfono (`refresh_token_B`), y confirmar que **ambos** siguen válidos (`POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=refresh_token` → 200 para los dos). En los celulares: driver → client → volver a driver, la sesión sigue viva.
- **SQL read-only:** tras loguear en ambas apps, `auth.sessions` del usuario debe mostrar **2 filas** y ambos refresh tokens `revoked=false`; en un login steady-state `auth.users.last_sign_in_at` se mueve pero `updated_at` **no** (el password dejó de rotar).
- **Regresión:** registrar un teléfono nuevo desde cero → loguea sin 500.

## Notas

- **Server-side puro: no requiere rebuild de las apps.** Los usuarios lo obtienen en su próximo login.
- Deploy de la EF: `npx supabase functions deploy verify-otp` (o MCP con `index.ts` + `_shared/rate-limiter.ts`).

author: vivekschaudhary
body:
**First slice of the re-foundation: templates in Compass, instances in Jira.** ⚠️ Stacked on #124 (base = `feat/mvp1-jira-status-transitions`) — merge #124 first, then this re-targets `main`.

## The wedge

A bug filed in Jira → **`/fix KAN-99`** → Compass reads it, fixes it, opens the PR, and drives it **To Do → In Progress → Done** — with **no `docs/fixes/*.md`.** That single demo *is* the enterprise pitch: "Compass executes your Jira."

## What's in it
- **`stores.jira_get_issue(auth, key)` + `_adf_to_text`** — READ a ticket (summary, description, status, category, issuetype, parent, labels); ADF description flattened to text. Best-effort, transport-injectable.
- **`_resolve_jira_work_item(raw)`** — if `/fix`'s input is a Jira key and Jira is wired, the ticket's summary+description become the engineer's context. **Refuses loud** (exit 3) on missing / already-Done / no-creds — no dead-ends. Plain-text `/fix` is unchanged.
- **Wiring** — `main()` resolves `/fix <KEY>` → passes context + `work_item_key` into `_run_workflow`; #124 transitions drive that key; the repo fix-record projection is **skipped** when Jira-sourced (the ticket already IS the record).

## Test
`jira_get_issue` (read/normalize/404/ADF) · key detection · plain-text passthrough · reads-ticket-as-context · refuses done/missing/no-creds. Full suite green (**502**); consistency clean.

## Next (same program)
1b `/fix <text>` creates the Bug in Jira · 1c create-story→Jira + build←Jira · 1d ops→Jira · Phase 2 links · Phase 3 Confluence.

author: huangruiteng
body:
## Summary
- require Agent Todo terminal transitions to use `todo complete`, preventing `todo update --status done` from bypassing completion policy
- allow evidence-backed side-agent `continuous_monitor` todos with no required write scope to close with explicit `--no-follow-up`
- migrate lifecycle smokes and document the terminal-transition contract

## Product / architecture judgment
This fixes a state-machine inconsistency observed while closing a no-change watch lane. The change keeps one terminal policy entry point instead of adding a new state: delivery-capable work remains review/self-merge gated, while observation-only monitors can terminate without manufacturing another handoff.

## Validation
- `python3 examples/control_plane/todo-cli-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/control_plane/todo-lifecycle-cli-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/control_plane/side-agent-self-iteration-state-machine-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/control_plane/todo-succession-contract-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/control_plane/todo-user-gate-scope-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/control_plane/control-plane-integrated-canary-smoke.py`
- `loopx canary premerge --from-git-diff` (17/17, no warnings or manual holds)
- public/private boundary scan clean

## Risk
The deliberate compatibility change is that Agent Todo callers using `todo update --status done` now receive an actionable error and must use `todo complete`. User Todo lower-level closure remains supported.

author: lilseancoc-png
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #562's discovery: the 2026-07-08 Gemini model shutdown ran **~2 days with zero operator signal**. That silence wasn't a bug — it's the repo's graceful-degradation design working as intended: narratives fell back to last-good, briefs carried forward, judgments served from cache, theses shipped deterministic cards, the workflows stayed green, and the site kept rendering. The only tells were buried log lines and `ai-usage.json`'s calls/day quietly halving — and nothing watches either. The build must never *fail* on AI trouble, so the alarm has to be out-of-band.

## What changed

### `scripts/build.mjs` — per-run AI health verdict
- A lightweight `AI_HEALTH` tally counts every fresh AI outcome: successes in `recordAiUsage` (the one place every successful `generateContent` lands), failed attempts by class (dead-model / quota / server / network / other) in `classifyAiError` (the one funnel every bake call site's catch runs through).
- `computeAiHealthReport()` distills a verdict at end of run:
  - **`ok`** — fresh calls succeeded (or none were needed: full cache reuse)
  - **`degraded`** — a dead model id was probed (the ladder recovered, but a pinned env var needs repointing — the report names the exact fix) or >30% of attempts failed
  - **`down`** — a key is present and *every* fresh call failed
  - **`keyless`** — no `GEMINI_API_KEY`; skipped by design, not an incident
- `writeAiHealthReport()` logs the verdict, emits a `::warning`/`::error` Actions annotation on degraded/down, appends a markdown block to the job summary, and writes `./ai-health.json` (repo root, gitignored) for the workflow step below.

### `.github/workflows/daily.yml` — the "AI health alert" step
- On **degraded/down**: opens **one** `ai-health`-labeled GitHub issue — issue creation is what emails the owner. While the incident stays open, later runs only refresh the issue body (title/status/table/run link), so 8 bakes/day can't generate notification spam.
- On the next clean **ok** run: closes the issue with a recovery comment.
- **Optional Discord ping**: set the `DISCORD_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` Actions secret and the step also posts to Discord on incident open + recovery (one ping each; completely dormant unless the secret is set — no code change needed later).
- Workflow gains `issues: write` permission; the step runs `if: always()` and no-ops gracefully when the build died before writing the report (the run is red in that case — already visible).

Had this existed last week, the July 8 open bake would have filed: *"🚨 AI layer DOWN — every fresh AI call failed (115 failed attempts, 0 successes)"* with a class breakdown pointing at dead-model 404s. With #562's ladder fix in place, the same event today reads *degraded* ("dead model id probed: gemini-2.5-flash-lite — calls recovered via the fallback ladder; repoint the AI_MODEL/NARRATIVES_MODEL Actions Variables") — an actionable heads-up instead of an outage.

## Verification

- `node --check scripts/build.mjs` clean; `daily.yml` YAML-validated.
- `computeAiHealthReport()` exercised keyless → `{"status":"keyless"}` as designed.
- `node scripts/picks-smoke.mjs` — 190/190 checks pass (no engine behavior touched).
- The scanners (`scan-unusual`/`refresh-heatmap`) retry unconditionally and already self-heal; the bake (8×/trading day, same models) is the canary, so the alert step rides only `daily.yml`.

## Follow-up (optional, no deploy)

- Create a Discord webhook in your server (Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks) and add it as the `DISCORD_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` Actions secret to get pinged where you actually live. The GitHub-issue email path works with zero setup.

author: youshinh
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a durable vendor-neutral evidence schema and session metadata and persist per-event evidence for Phase 1 Evidence Recorder MVP.
- Eliminate deadlock/racy shutdown paths in the recorder where blocking channel sends under a shared mutex could hang worker callbacks.
- Ensure captures cannot leak goroutines indefinitely and make Stop/cleanup idempotent and robust on hook startup failure.

### Description

- Add `capture/evidence.go` with `EvidenceEvent`, `EvidenceSession`, `ImageEvidence`, `UIAElementInfo`, `WindowInfo`, `Rect`, and `CaptureStatus` to represent persisted evidence and session metadata.
- Rework `capture/recorder.go` to split recorder state and data locks, add `stopMu`, `stateMu`, `dataMu`, `senderWG`, `workerWG`, `hookWG`, and `channelClosed` state, and reinitialize transient channels/state on `Start` to avoid sends to closed channels.
- Replace the quit-channel flow with a bounded `captureChan` drained via `for ev := range r.captureChan` and add `finishRecording()` used both by normal `Stop()` and hook-startup-failure cleanup to perform ordered shutdown (stop accepting events → stop hooks → wait senders → close channel once → drain worker → close files).
- Implement one-at-a-time capture semaphore (`captureSem`) and a `callCapture` wrapper that recovers panics and enforces timeouts to avoid unbounded leaked capture goroutines; record capture failures/timeouts in `CaptureStatus` and write per-event JSONL to `events.jsonl` while maintaining legacy `log.json` compatibility.
- Misc: switch to `runtime.LockOSThread`/`UnlockOSThread`, alias Wails runtime import for event emit, add `writeSessionJSON()` to produce `session.json`, and include `phase1-evidence-recorder.patch` in the repo.

### Testing

- Ran formatting: `gofmt -w capture/recorder.go capture/evidence.go` — succeeded.
- Platform Windows package smoke test: `env GOOS=windows go test -run '^$' ./capture` — succeeded (build/test run for Windows-specific package verified in cross-build mode).
- Full test run: `timeout 60s go test ./...` — failed in this Linux workspace due to existing Windows-only APIs (`syscall.NewLazyDLL`, `syscall.NewCallback`, `syscall.UTF16ToString`) and missing project artifacts (`act_gram/manual`, `frontend/dist`), therefore not applicable here.

author: juliansommer
body:
## Summary

Follow-on to #495, Both levers cut fixed wall-clock waits from slow test packages behind injectable seams. **No production defaults change** — every seam keeps its original value outside tests, and no assertions were removed.

## Lever 2 — RSA key-size seam in `admin`

A single `certKeyBits` package seam (default 4096) replaces the hardcoded key sizes in CA / server / IPSec keygen. Cert tests override it to 2048 (still valid, ~8-10x faster keygen).

## Lever 3 — remaining non-injectable fixed waits

- **vm `WaitForUnixSocket` 3s.** New `qmpSocketWaitTimeout` seam (default 3s, mirrors the adjacent `qmpDialTimeout`) makes the socket-appear wait in `newQMPClientWithHandshake` injectable. `TestAttachQMP_DialFailure_NoHeartbeatLeak` overrode nothing and paid the full 3s against a never-appearing socket; it now uses 50ms. `TestStartupTimeouts` locks the 3s production default.
- **utils `TestExecProcessAndKill` gratuitous 500ms sleep -> 20ms.** The backgrounded `sleep 30` child is already running; nothing depended on the wait.

## Speed impact

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| admin | ~17s | 0.82s |
| vm | ~7.0s | 4.1s |

author: stefan-cruceru
body:
## What this is

Dashboard-side fixes from a **verified adversarial multi-lens review** of the open Eaglesoft PRs. **#900 (WARP-1101) merged before these could fold in**, so they land as a **follow-up off `main`**. They pair with the backend-side fixes on **#916 (WARP-1137)** — together the two make the frontend↔backend API contract consistent (they were authored separately and had diverged).

## Fixes (each maps to a confirmed review finding)

| Fix | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Contract adapters** (`api.erp.ts`) match the backend routes #916 now serves — unwrap the read envelopes (patients / patient / schedule `{ connected, reason, items \| patient }`), adapt connection-test `{ ok, reason, message }` → `{ reachable, message }`. Without this, patient search + the connect test read as broken end-to-end. | #5, #10 |
| **RBAC** — drop the household-default `family` role from `canViewPhi` (matches the backend `PHI_READ_ROLES` = owner/admin). `roleFromGroups` assigns `family` to any un-grouped account, so it was fail-open patient-PHI exposure. | #2 |
| **Write-confirm** only reports success on `APPLIED` — a `FAILED`/`DISCREPANCY` (or a missing request id) surfaces honestly instead of reading as written. | #6 / #22 |
| **`formatDate`** parses date-only ISO as **local** time, so a DOB / visit date no longer renders one day early in US timezones. | #12 |
| **Write affordances** gated on the access flags — the Schedule button and the ManageSheet write toggle are hidden from non-privileged roles. | #21 |

> **#11** (the schedule date stepper) was already fixed in merged #900 via `useEaglesoftSchedule` — not re-touched. **#16** (a TOCTOU on the confirm transition) is a low-severity concurrency item left for a follow-up (it needs the atomic `updateMany` + a mock update); noted here so it isn't lost.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean · 13 unit/component tests · `next build` compiles `/integrations` + `/integrations/eaglesoft`.

## Note on the process

The review ran across #900 (dashboard) + #916 (orchestrator). The backend half of every cross-PR finding is on **#916**; this PR is the dashboard half. Merge both to get the consistent contract.

Refs: WARP-1164 (this) · epic WARP-1093 · merged dashboard #900 (WARP-1101) · backend #916 (WARP-1137).

author: zeehio
body:
## Summary
- `utils-integration.R` (RIP detection and peak-integration helpers) had 0% test coverage.
- While building test fixtures for `find_regions_rip_saturated()`, found that it computed:
  ```r
  rip_chrom <- rowSums(rip_region) / nrow(rip_region)
  ```
  `rowSums()` collapses across retention-time columns, producing one value per drift-time row — but the function then treats the resulting indices as retention-time positions (`retention_time[rt_saturated_regions[, 1L]]`), and its only caller, `integratePeaks(GCIMSSample)`, documents and uses the result as a retention-time-indexed saturation window (compared against each peak's `rt_cm_s`). That only works with one value per retention-time column, i.e. `colSums()`, not `rowSums()`. Fixed by swapping `rowSums()` for `colSums()`.
  - **Impact / severity**: this is a bugfix to the `Saturation` column computed by `integratePeaks()`, which flags peaks whose retention-time window overlaps a RIP-depleted region as a QC signal ("more likely that the ROI suffers from non-linearities"). It does **not** affect `Area`, `Volume`, `Asymmetry`, peak clustering, or any other quantification result. I also checked and `Saturation` is currently **not consumed anywhere downstream** in the package — `peakTable()` doesn't read, filter, or aggregate it, and no plotting/reporting code touches it either — so today this column is a QC diagnostic that isn't surfaced past the per-sample peak list unless a user manually inspects `peaks(dataset)`. The fix is still correct and worth having, but the practical blast radius before this PR was a broken-but-unused diagnostic column, not a wrong quantification result.
- Adds `tests/testthat/test-utils-integration.R`, covering:
  - `find_half_max_boundaries()`: exact half-max crossings on a known peak, and the NaN-`fwhm_sym` case for a flat vector
  - `find_rip()`: the FWHM-clip path for an isolated RIP peak, the valley-preferred path when real TIS valleys sit inside the clip radius, the verbose message, and the "could not locate the RIP width" abort on a degenerate/flat matrix
  - `find_regions_rip_saturated()`: a saturated retention-time window correctly reported in retention-time units (regression test for the bug above), and the empty-matrix case when nothing is saturated
- `utils-integration.R` coverage: 0% → 93%. Package-wide coverage: 45.0% → 47.8%.

## Test plan
- [x] `testthat::test_local(".")` — full existing suite passes, including the new file (21 assertions)
- [x] `covr::package_coverage()` confirms `utils-integration.R` at 93% and no regressions elsewhere

body:
Completes the tracking half of the adaptive-loop milestone (gap-analysis Sharp Next Step 1) and stops there per direction: live token budgets are explicitly deferred until after the planned control-plane refactoring, and all docs reflect that boundary.

## What changed

- **`internal/app/adaptive/ledger`**: durable findings ledger at `~/.config/ai-agent/adaptive-findings.json`, written atomically via the owner-only temp-fsync-rename path. Entries are keyed by a stable fingerprint (kind + repository), carry first/last-seen, `open`/`accepted`/`dismissed` status, and an evidence snapshot at acceptance. Explicit 500-entry budget with deterministic pruning that never drops accepted findings and records what it removed; corrupt or newer-schema ledgers fail the command instead of being clobbered.
- **`runs analyze`** syncs the ledger on every invocation, annotates each recommendation with fingerprint + status, and renders an "Accepted findings, outcome since acceptance" section: per-metric deltas against the acceptance baseline, or "no longer flagged in this window". Report JSON schema unchanged (annotations are text-mode; machine access via `runs findings --json`).
- **`ai-agent runs findings`** + `accept`/`dismiss`/`reopen` verbs with unique-prefix fingerprint matching. Accepting requires the finding to be present in the current window so every delta has a real baseline.
- The analyzer remains a pure function of history; the CLI composes it with the ledger. ADR 0016 records the decision; gap analysis, capability map, manual, and architecture doc updated to the delivered/deferred split.

## Verification

`make test` / `make verify` / `make lint` all green. Tests: fingerprint stability and scope-sensitivity, sync/new/seen semantics, status transitions with snapshot handling, ambiguous-prefix rejection, atomic roundtrip with schema and corruption fail-closed, budget pruning that preserves accepted entries, and a CLI-level lifecycle test driving seeded history through analyze → accept → analyze (outcome section asserted) → list → dismiss.

author: kev1n
body:
## What

Agents were piping `.anyapi/*.json` files into python heredocs to extract fields and slice long strings. This release makes jq the steering language and the saved file a paid-once cache.

- **`anyapi run`** now ALWAYS fetches and saves the FULL envelope; `--jq` (new) / `--fields` / `--max-items` / `--summary` shape only the stdout view, locally - no shape query params are sent upstream anymore. Shape flags + no `--json` prints the 3 summary lines plus the shaped JSON: one command = slim transcript view + complete disk copy.
- **New `anyapi view [path] [--last [sku]] [--jq ...] [--fields ...] [--max-items N] [--summary] [--json]`** - re-shapes any saved run file at zero network/cost. `--last` resolves newest by mtime. The direct python-heredoc replacement.
- **jq engine**: bundled WebAssembly jq 1.8.2 (`jq-wasm`, no system install needed), system `jq` as fallback. Expressions target the `output` value (`{found, data}`), matching the gateway's server-side jq semantics - `.data.markdown[3500:7000]` reads the next chunk.
- `summary` now includes `fieldBytes` so an agent sees WHAT is huge before slicing.
- Server `hint` (which recommends server-side reshaping - wrong advice for CLI users) is stripped; large unshaped results get a local hint pointing at `anyapi view`.
- Bundled `anyapi-run` skill rewritten jq-first ("run once, then view --last at $0 - never re-run just to reshape").

## Behavior change

With shape flags, the saved file is now FULL rather than server-trimmed (that is the point). Hence 0.1.1 -> **0.2.0**.

## Verification

- `npm run build` clean; `npm test` green (27 tests incl. new shape/jq/view suites).
- Dogfooded against prod: `run web.scrape --jq '.data | {title, description, md: .markdown[:3500]}'` -> slim stdout + full 9.7KB file; `view --last web.scrape --jq '.data.markdown[3500:7000]'` -> next chunk, zero network; jq error -> stderr + exit 1, data safe on disk.

Companion gateway PR: getanyapi-com/anyapi#250 (server-side jq + free result re-reads for MCP/REST agents).

## Release

Merging then tagging `v0.2.0` publishes to npm via Actions (`NPM_TOKEN`).

No server change needed; only the client `canManage` gate around `FutureCandidatesWall` was removed (`kind-tab.tsx`). The dense 7-col editor kept desktop proportions below ~899px. author: dustinkeeton
body:
Closes #157.

## Summary

Gives each spawned agent a **distinct avatar on GitHub commit views**, building on the per-agent commit emails shipped by #156.

**The mechanism, stated honestly.** GitHub picks a commit's avatar from the **author email**: an account's avatar when that email is registered there → otherwise that email's **Gravatar** → otherwise the gray Octocat. The `bot+<agent>@domain` aliases #156 derives belong to no GitHub account, so they land on the Gravatar path. **Registering one Gravatar per agent email is a manual, one-time step this toolkit does not and cannot perform.** So the deliverable is *artifacts + a reproducible documented procedure*, never a claim that avatars "just appear" — and the generated manifest says so in those words.

### What ships

- **`.waffle/avatars/<agent>.svg`** — one **static** (`animated: false` — SMIL doesn't rasterize predictably), deterministic waffle SVG per installed agent, sized 512px for upload. Same name-seeded character `team.html` already draws; `agentAvatarSvg` itself is untouched.
- **`.waffle/AVATARS.md`** — the reproducibility artifact. Per agent: display name, syrup flavor, avatar file, and **the exact commit email to register**. Plus the GitHub-avatar mechanics, the Gravatar procedure, one-line SVG→PNG conversion commands, a smoke test, GitHub's email→avatar **caching caveat**, and the anti-recommendation (*never* add these aliases as secondary emails on the bot's GitHub account — that relinks every agent to one profile and one avatar, defeating the whole point).
- Both flow through render's `emit()` choke point → lock-tracked, `doctor`-drift-checked, pruned when a selection drops every agent, refreshed on every render. Same lifecycle as `TEAM.md`.
- **`extractBaseEmail` / `deriveAgentEmail`** — new pure helpers in `waffledocs.mjs`, kept **in lockstep** with the delegate skill's prose derivation rules (lockstep comments on both sides; tests pin the three documented examples). Bare `git.cmd`, an unresolved `{{git.botEmail}}`, a `*.noreply.github.com` base, or a local part that already carries a `+` each report honestly rather than inventing an address to register.
- **`identity.avatar`** — the `identity:` allowlist widens from `{displayName}` to `{displayName, avatar}`. An optional *reference* (repo-relative path or `https://` URL), pattern-guarded in the same trust-boundary style as its sibling (no whitespace, quotes, backtick, `\`, `$`, `${{`, `..`). It renders through to `.claude/agents/*.md` and `.agents/agents/*.md` with **zero render-code change** (`renderAgent` already passes the validated block verbatim); codex TOML drops it, as before. Absent ⇒ the generated default path. Shipped agents author none, so there's no churn in the committed render.
- **No raster dependency.** Gravatar takes PNG/JPG/GIF only; `sharp`/`resvg` ship native binaries and are far too heavy for an `npx`-run installer whose entire dependency footprint is `yaml`. Conversion is a documented one-liner the human runs once, during the same manual registration session.
- Docs: delegate `SKILL.md` avatar caveat, github-workflow `setup:` note (5), `schema/FORMAT.md`, `AGENTS.md` registry, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`, `.gitignore`.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
| --- | --- |
| A documented, reproducible way to get a DISTINCT avatar per agent on GitHub commit views | generated `.waffle/AVATARS.md` (mechanics → conversion → Gravatar registration → smoke test), delegate `SKILL.md`, github-workflow setup note (5) |
| The agent identity metadata carries the avatar reference | `identity.avatar` — validated, rendered through, deterministically defaulted to `.waffle/avatars/<agent>.svg` |
| No regression to TEAM.md/team.html avatar rendering | `agentAvatarSvg` unmodified; existing determinism tests pass byte-for-byte |

## Verification

- `npm run validate` → **toolkit is valid**
- `npm test` → **500 pass, 0 fail** (474 before; +26)
- `npm pack --dry-run` → clean, 110 files
- `node installer/cli.mjs render` → 54 files; **re-render byte-identical** (determinism held: no `Date`, no `Math.random`)
- `node installer/cli.mjs doctor --allow-missing` → **all managed files match the lock manifest**

New test coverage: avatar emission (static, 512px, lock-tracked, pruned, byte-identical across renders); manifest variants (derived plus-address / verbatim noreply base with the shared-email warning / `git.agentIdentities.botEmail` override applied verbatim / no-bot-identity / unresolvable placeholder); `extractBaseEmail`+`deriveAgentEmail` unit tests pinning the documented examples; `identity.avatar` accept + reject cases (whitespace, quotes, backtick, `$`, `${{ }}`, `..` traversal, backslash, non-string) and render passthrough across all three targets.

## Divergences from the plan

Only one, found while testing: the manifest's footnote markers were originally positional (`¹`/`²`), which made `¹` mean "email override" in the configured branch and "authored avatar" in the unconfigured one. Switched to fixed-per-meaning markers (`†` authored avatar, `‡` email override) so a marker reads the same in both branches. Otherwise the plan was followed as written.

Two known, expected consequences worth flagging for review:

- **Lock churn on consumer upgrade.** New `AVATARS.md` + `avatars/*.svg` entries appear on every consuming repo's next render. The manifest's content depends on `git.cmd` / `git.agentIdentities`, so editing those will (correctly) drift the lock — a repo that commits its render must commit `botEmail` and any `agentIdentities` entries, which the github-workflow setup note already required.
- **Emit clobber refusal.** If a consumer already has an unmanaged `.waffle/avatars/<name>.svg`, render refuses to overwrite it — existing, correct `emit()` behavior.

body:
## Summary
- A cargo debug-profile `_turbovec` extension (`maturin develop` without `--release`) runs vector search roughly 100x slower than release with no runtime signal: 126 ms vs 0.95 ms single-query p50 at 20k x 1536 on an M-series CPU (the release scan beats the numpy fp32 full-scan baseline of 3.9 ms). The editable install imports `src/lodedb/_turbovec.abi3.so` from the source tree, so a stale debug artifact silently shadows every later run. Published wheels and `uv sync` / `pip install -e .` builds are release-profile and unaffected.
- Expose `native_build_profile()` from the bundled extension and re-export it at `lodedb._native_core`, tolerant of extensions that predate the API (reports `unknown`).
- Emit a one-time `RuntimeWarning` at native-core import when the loaded extension is a debug build.
- Report the profile in `lodedb doctor` (text and JSON), with a warning line when it is `debug`.
- Document the release-profile requirement in `docs/deployment-and-performance.md`; record the binding in `LOCAL_PATCHES.md`.

## Testing
- `cargo check` on the binding crate; extension rebuilt with `maturin develop --release`.
- `ruff check src tests`.
- `pytest tests -q`: 600 passed; the 11 failures in this venv are pre-existing on a clean tree (missing optional `[embeddings]`/`[image]`/torch extras) and unrelated.
- Verified both paths live: the release extension reports `release` with no warning; swapping in a debug build fires the RuntimeWarning and doctor prints the warning line.

author: maxthomas95
body:
## Release blocker RB-2 — Windows local launch arguments can cross the cmd.exe boundary

From the 2026-07-09 review. Local and Coder sessions launched the CLI as `cmd.exe /d /c <binary> <args>` on Windows, escaping arguments with `escapeCmdExeArgForNodePty`, which never handled an embedded double quote.

**Reproduced with node-pty on Windows:** an initial prompt of `foo"&echo x>SENTINEL` created the sentinel file — the argument escaped its boundary and cmd.exe ran a second command. (The hole: the escaper skipped metacharacter escaping entirely whenever the value contained whitespace, and never escaped `"`.)

### Fix — resolve the binary, then branch
`resolveWindowsLaunch(binary)` (new `win-binary-resolver.ts`) searches PATH × PATHEXT and classifies the target:

- **Native executable** (`.exe`/`.com`, or an absolute path to one) → **spawned directly through node-pty with raw argv, no cmd.exe.** With no second parser, node-pty's MSVCRT quoting is safe. Verified via node-pty that quotes, `&&`, `%VAR%`, `^`, spaces, unicode, and `--flag value` all arrive as exact single argv entries with **no injection**.
- **Batch shim** (`.cmd`/`.bat`) or a name PATH/PATHEXT can't resolve → cmd.exe is still required. On that path every metacharacter is caret-escaped and **embedded double quotes are rejected (fail closed)**, because batch argument passing can't be made injection-safe (confirmed: a `.cmd` can't even be spawned directly, and the wrapper is injectable by design).

`escapeCmdExeArgForNodePty` now always caret-escapes metacharacters and throws on `"`.

### Tests
- `win-binary-resolver.test.ts` — direct vs shell classification, explicit paths, extensionless binaries, PATHEXT, quoted PATH entries, case-insensitivity, unresolved fallback.
- `launch-safety.win.test.ts` — **Windows-only node-pty integration test** replaying the injection payloads; asserts each hostile value returns as one faithful argv entry and no sentinel is created. **Passed on a real Windows machine.**
- `shell-quote.test.ts` updated for the new always-escape + reject-quotes behavior.
- Full suite: **745 passing**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Notes / follow-ups
- On the batch-shim path, a prompt containing `"` now fails closed with `cmd.exe arguments with double quotes are not supported here`. This only affects CLIs installed as `.cmd` shims; native `.exe` installs are unaffected. A friendlier, CLI-named error message would be a nice follow-up.
- Touches `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` in a different section than #204/#205; should auto-merge but may want a trivial rebase depending on land order.

author: spencerbeggs
body:
Migration #6. The upward walk `@effected/config-file` carried in an internal module becomes a package, and config-file consumes it. There is now exactly one absorbing loop in the repository, and the walking resolvers inherit their best-effort guarantee from its type rather than from a comment.

## `@effected/walker`

Boundary tier: `effect` is its only peer, it takes no runtime dependencies, and it needs no platform package **even in its tests** — `Path.layer` and `FileSystem.layerNoop` come from `effect` core. `Path` and `FileSystem` arrive through the requirements channel, so the consumer's platform layer is the one place POSIX-vs-win32 semantics are chosen. Every public error channel is `never`; there is no error module.

One primitive does the work:

- `Walker.firstMatch(candidates, predicate)` — the first candidate the predicate accepts. Absorbs **each probe individually**, so a permission error on one ancestor cannot hide a valid root above it, and short-circuits once a candidate matches.
- `Walker.findUpward(dirs, candidatesFor)` and `Walker.findRoot(dirs, isRoot)` — specializations over different candidate generators.
- `Walker.ascend(start, options?)` — a bounded loop, lexical rather than physical (`Path.dirname` does not resolve symlinks). Rejects a `maxDepth` that is not a positive integer rather than returning a silently empty chain.

25 tests. `dist/prod/issues.json` is `{errors: 0, warnings: 0, suppressed: 0}` — the first package in the repo with a genuinely empty suppression list, because it declares no classes.

## `@effected/config-file`

Internal refactor; **the public `ConfigResolver` surface is unchanged.** `src/internal/walkUp.ts` and `probeSubpaths` are deleted. The three walking resolvers no longer wrap themselves in an absorbing `catch` — walker's channel is already `never` — while `absorb` survives on the three that call `fs.exists` directly. The marker predicates carry a typed `PlatformError.PlatformError` where they previously carried `unknown`.

A reviewer proved the refactor behavior-preserving rather than merely green: the candidate sequences are identical, the removed `absorb` wrappers caught nothing the inner per-probe catch didn't already handle, and `Walker.ascend`'s `maxDepth` defect is unreachable from any public config-file API. `isWorkspaceRoot`'s `try`/`catch` around `JSON.parse` turns out to be load-bearing — a parse throw is a **defect**, and `Effect.catch` does not absorb defects.

## Eight coverage holes, found by mutation

The shipped code was correct every time. What was broken was the ability to detect if it had not been. Each hole is now pinned by a test verified to fail against the implementation it forbids.

| Mutant that passed a fully green suite | Why nothing caught it |
| --- | --- |
| `firstMatch` probes every candidate, then picks the first hit | the only order-observing test matched on the **last** candidate |
| a match at index 0 is dropped | no test's winning match was the **first** candidate |
| `findRoot` returns the **last** accepting directory | no fixture had more than one accepting directory |
| `findUpward` interleaves candidate-major | no test had **both** several directories and several candidates per directory |
| `findUpward` drops per-candidate absorption | every filesystem fixture succeeded |
| `findRoot` scans linearly, no short-circuit | tests asserted only the returned `Option` |
| `upwardWalk` drops `stopAt` entirely | six tests pass `stopAt`; every one finds its match **before** the ascent reaches it |
| `rootAnchored` probes the whole ascent chain | every fixture put the config **at or above** the anchor |

Two would have been real bugs: the candidate-major interleave lets a distant ancestor's `.apprc` beat a nearer `config/.apprc`; the anchor mutant collapses `gitRoot` into a plain `upwardWalk`, returning a config located *below* the repository root. The last two predate this migration — `walkUp.ts` carried the same `stopAt` and the same blind tests.

Every hole has the same shape: **tests that exercised the middle of a range and never its edges.**

## Also on this branch

- **Three-tier library taxonomy.** The old scheme conflated dependency surface with whether a package does IO, and walker is where they come apart — `effect`-only, yet it traverses the filesystem. `pure` / `boundary` / `integrated`, with R1 ("tiers 1 and 2 take no external runtime dependencies") restated as **direct policy** rather than derived from *no IO ⟹ pure*. That derivation is what forces `@effected/toml` to vendor `smol-toml`, so it had to survive the rewrite. `package-json` reclassified to `integrated` for `spdx-expression-parse`. `effect-standards.md`'s worked example — "walker is pure tier because its probe is a parameter" — is deleted.
- **pnpm 11.11.0**, which lands the upstream peer-resolution fix, so `@savvy-web/bundler` moves from the root into each package that builds. It had landed in `@effected/package-json`'s `dependencies` rather than `devDependencies`, which would have shipped a build tool as a runtime dependency of a published package; fixed and verified against the generated manifest.
- **`pnpm lint:md` is now read-only.** The config set `fix: true`, so a verification command rewrote all 88 markdown files. Removing the key — rather than setting it `false`, which would have silently disabled the pre-commit hook — makes the flag decide.
- **`@effected/glob`** added to the roadmap, next after walker.

## Gates

`pnpm test` 1869/1869 · `pnpm typecheck` 17/17 · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm lint:md` clean · 13 changesets validate · both packages build with zero warnings.

Signed-off-by: C. Spencer Beggs <spencer@beggs.codes>

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Resolves the stated open direction of **shannon-channel-coding-awgn-oq-02-oq-02**: the **correlated-noise** MRC output-SNR optimum, where the noise covariance is a full matrix Σ (not diagonal). The existing gallery entry handled only the uncorrelated/diagonal case (`mrc_signal_sq_le`, `mrc_signal_sq_eq_iff`, `mrc_snr_matched`) plus the output-power identity `awgn_weighted_power_eq_covariance_quadratic_form` (output power = aᵀΣa). This PR supplies the missing optimization.

## Key idea (inverse/square-root free)

The classical route uses matrix whitening (Σ^{-1/2}), which is heavy in Lean. The observation that makes it session-sized: the two combiners `∑ᵢ aᵢWᵢ` and `∑ⱼ bⱼWⱼ` are *themselves scalar random variables*, so the entire matrix Cauchy–Schwarz reduces to the **scalar** covariance Cauchy–Schwarz (`covariance_sq_le_variance_mul_variance`, already in the file) after bilinearly expanding the forms via Mathlib's `covariance_sum_sum'` and the file's `variance_smul_sum'`. No matrix inverse or square root appears.

## New theorems (all VERIFIED, 0 sorry, 0 new axioms)

- `covariance_smul_sum'` — bilinear expansion `cov[∑aᵢWᵢ, ∑bⱼWⱼ] = ∑∑ aᵢbⱼ cov[Wᵢ,Wⱼ]` (= aᵀΣb); the two-vector companion of `variance_smul_sum'`.
- `covariance_quadratic_form_cauchy_schwarz` — **correlated generalized Cauchy–Schwarz**: `(aᵀΣb)² ≤ (aᵀΣa)(bᵀΣb)`.
- `mrc_correlated_snr_le` — output-SNR bound `(aᵀΣb)² / (aᵀΣa) ≤ bᵀΣb` (matched power = optimum sᵀΣ⁻¹s at s = Σb).
- `mrc_correlated_snr_matched` — the matched combiner `a = b` attains `bᵀΣb` exactly, so the bound is **sharp**.

## Verification

`./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.ShannonChannelCodingAWGNOQ02OQ02` → **Build succeeded** (elaboration clean; required a couple of retries past a transient dependency-olean-corruption / SIGSEGV-at-write under fleet memory pressure — not a code issue).

author: bdubdesigns
body:
## Summary

Issue #29 implements the Alpha 1 read-only execution bodies for the fixed `read`, `list`, and `grep` tools. They are in-process, Node-built-in-only, workspace-bounded file tools that let a future OAF loop inspect an `oaf init` app without granting raw shell access. The metadata registry remains contract-only.

## Files changed

- `lib/agent/tool-execution.mjs` — dependency-free `executeRead`, `executeList`, and `executeGrep` bodies. No process spawning, network access, or file mutation.
- `tests/agent-read-tools.test.mjs` — temporary workspace fixture coverage for normal behavior, ranges, recursive list, grep/glob/binary skipping, boundary rejection, symlink escapes, and immutability.
- `docs/agent-tools.md` — documents the explicit `workspaceRoot` execution context, boundary behavior, line ranges, recursive listing, and grep semantics.

## Checks run

- `node tests/agent-read-tools.test.mjs` — PASS
- `node tests/agent-tools.test.mjs` — PASS
- `node tests/agent-events.test.mjs` — PASS
- `node tests/oaf-init.test.mjs` — PASS
- `node tests/sandbox.test.mjs` — PASS

## Boundary / security decisions

- Each execution function requires an explicit `workspaceRoot`; the future loop supplies it outside the agent-visible tool arguments.
- User paths reject absolute paths (including Windows-style absolute paths) and `..` segments before resolution.
- The workspace root and requested target are resolved with `realpath`; the resolved target must remain within the real workspace root. Direct symlinks escaping the root fail closed.
- Recursive `list` and `grep` never follow nested symlinks. `list` reports them as `other`; `grep` skips them.
- Read/list/grep use Node filesystem APIs only. They never invoke a shell, reach the network, or mutate fixture files.

## Grep behavior choice

`grep` uses **plain substring matching**, not regular expressions, avoiding regex parsing/ReDoS complexity in this first slice. It walks regular files recursively from `path` (default project root), skips files containing a NUL byte as binary, and supports a small workspace-relative glob matcher: `*`, `?`, and `**`.

## Intentional limits

- `read` supports 1-based, inclusive line ranges. A ranged read sets `truncated` only if it omitted lines; full reads preserve source content.
- No output-size or match-count cap is imposed in this focused execution slice. The future agent loop is responsible for model-context limits; adding caps here would require a contract/schema update and focused tests.
- Recursive listing is supported, but only inside the real workspace root and without following symlinks.

## What is intentionally not implemented yet

- Agent loop orchestration, provider seam, or `AgentEvent` emission.
- `write` tool implementation.
- Sandbox-routed `command` tool implementation; sandbox behavior is unchanged.
- Receipt emission or persistence.
- Dynamic tool discovery / registration.

Closes #29

body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** (site lane). Self-identifying: this PR was prepared by an automated agent.

Bead **sq-2av3s**: stop the `surface-inference` visual baseline from baking the lean-wasm reasoner load-error toast.

## Problem

The `/surface/inference` live-reasoner status badge (`EngineIndicator`) reflects the **W-reason wasm bundle load outcome** (`cold → warming → ready | error`). In the lean-wasm **visual** lane the reason bundle genuinely cannot load, so that region renders the *"Reasoner failed — retries on reason"* state (plus a load-error toast), and those runtime-dependent pixels were baked into `e2e/visual/baselines/visual-{desktop,mobile}/surface-inference.png` — a recurring source of screenshot drift.

## Fix

Wrap the `EngineIndicator` status region in a `data-vr-mask` span — the same **"mask, don't chase"** convention the benchmarks provenance strip adopted in #1801. The `vrMasks()` helper in `e2e/visual/*.spec.ts` (`page.locator("[data-vr-mask]")`) already masks every such node, in **both** the live capture and the stored baseline at comparison time, so the region is no longer compared. The baseline now guards the **static playground layout**, not the runtime bundle-load outcome.

**No baseline re-mint required**: adding a mask only *removes* a region from comparison (Playwright overlays the mask colour on the masked bounding box in both images), and the wrapping span keeps the badge in the same flex position — so the existing baseline stays valid. No axe rule or visual threshold weakened.

## Gates (all green)

- `build:wasm` prereq satisfied; `cd site && npm run build` static export ✅ — `data-vr-mask` verified present in exported `out/surface/inference/index.html`
- `npm run lint` — 0 warnings/errors ✅
- `tsc --noEmit` ✅
- basePath `/sparq` unchanged; no other route touched.

**Not armed** — leaving for review.

author: mikayla-maki
body:
Previously, text elements answered every unconstrained sizing probe with their full unwrapped width, so a text node's min-content size equaled its max-content size. Flexbox's automatic minimum size (`min-width: auto`) therefore pinned flex items at full unwrapped text width — the reason text never shrinks or wraps in flex rows without an explicit `min_w_0()` (66 files carry that workaround today) — and content-sized grid tracks (`minmax(min-content, 1fr)`) could never shrink text below one unwrapped line.

Text now answers `AvailableSpace::MinContent` with the width of its widest unbreakable segment, computed by `LineLayout::min_content_width`. The segment walk mirrors `compute_wrap_boundaries`' break-candidate rules over the same shaped glyph positions, so wrapping at any width ≥ the min-content width provably never breaks mid-word; a property test pins the theorem with the bundled IBM Plex face, including tightness (one pixel narrower forces a mid-word break).

`TextLayout`'s cache is now keyed by the full constraint pair it was computed under: min-content and max-content probes are answered from dedicated slots that never overwrite the wrapped lines used for painting (those belong to the final measure call, which taffy delivers with the resolved width), a definite-width layout only answers calls with the identical wrap width, and — completing the constraint key that #61107 added for truncation — truncated layouts never answer anything else. The measure closure body is extracted into `TextLayout::measure` so tests can drive arbitrary constraint sequences directly; a new history-independence test asserts that the answer to any measurement depends only on that measurement's constraints, with named regression tests for the truncation-poisoning collapse and the exact-fit truncation loss fixed in #61107 (the poisoning tests fail if #61107's cache guard is removed).

**Behavior change**: text in flex rows and content-sized grid tracks now shrinks to its container and wraps, instead of overflowing at full unwrapped width. Existing `min_w_0()` calls remain harmless (0 ≤ min-content). Nowrap and truncated text are unaffected. Characterization tests cover all three; the flex and grid tests fail against the old behavior.

Stacked under #60723. (Originally stacked on #60721, since merged; rebased over #61107.)

Release Notes:

- Fixed text in flexbox and grid layouts overflowing its container instead of wrapping when no explicit minimum width was set

## What this adds
A repeatable, scientific **benchmark suite** for the accelerator plus the resulting
**guidance paper**, and a **how-it-works doc** — all integrated into the doc site.

- `benchmarks/` — harness (corpus generators with exact ground truth, config/doc matrices,
  run orchestrator, resolver-free scorer, variance-aware aggregator), the results paper, and
  committed per-release scored summaries.
- `docs/benchmarking.md` (how the suite works), `docs/benchmark-results.md` (the paper),
  `docs/extraction-scaling-guide.md` — added to the doc-site nav under **Benchmarks & Performance**.
- `.claude/skills/run-benchmarks.md` — repeatable per-release/PR workflow.

## Results (v0.6.0.dev14 — systematic run on a clean stack; CORE 80/80, SCALING 14/14, REFERENCE 30/30, all completed)
- **Mode is a cost/robustness decision, not accuracy, up to ~800 rows** — simple is complete
  (recall 1.0) and ~2.3–2.9× cheaper *and* far more predictable (cost CV 0.4% vs 29–41% for agentic).
- **Simple completeness cliff ~800→1,200 rows** (silent truncation); **advanced holds recall 1.0
  to 3,200 rows** at up to ~$25/doc.
- **Real-world accuracy:** RealKIE-FCC 0.80, OCR-Benchmark 0.87 (0 parse failures).
- **Two genuine defects surfaced & reproduced** (backlog §7): integrated-confidence+simple drops
  rows (recall 0.21); agentic mode occasionally nulls a whole list on OCR-corrupted tables.
- The v0.6 efficiency fixes (#456 summarization, #457 agentic writeback + lazy-images) show
  **no accuracy/completeness regression**; #457's ~57% agentic cost cut is from a controlled 4-arm A/B.

## Cost-variance detection (built in per review feedback)
`cost` suite (repeats=5) + `run_matrix --repeats`; `aggregate.py` cell_stats (mean/stdev/CV),
`--cost-var` view, CV>0.25 warning, and `compare_cells` that only flags a cost shift beyond the
combined sampling spread — so agentic run-to-run noise can't masquerade as a regression.

- **`globals.css`** — activate it via the Tailwind v4 `@plugin` directive, plus a design-system adaptation: the plugin **inlines literal colors at build time**, which would bypass the runtime-re-pointed neutral ramp that powers dark mode (prose text would stay dark-on-dark). A `.prose` override routes every `--tw-prose-*` color through the `--color-*` custom properties, so rich text adapts to dark mode automatically. `prose-invert` is deliberately **not** used — it would double-invert against the re-pointed ramp. Links pick up the semantic `primary-600` token.
- **`article-detail-client.tsx`** — the knowledge-base body used `prose-sm` without `prose` (sizing only, no colors); now `prose prose-sm max-w-none`.

- Inspected the compiled CSS: the plugin's `.prose` rule sits in `@layer utilities` with inlined hex values; the override is **unlayered and later in the cascade**, so the variable routing wins on both counts.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `node scripts/check-design-system.mjs` all pass.

Backlog status: items #1 (view-as), #2 (shared-Modal sweep), and #3 (server-side pagination) are done; this is #4. Remaining: #5 (dark-mode chip variants + human dark-mode click-through) and #6 (ui-primitives gray-400 pass).

## TL;DR

Move WidgetDataStore read-only presentation accessors into a focused extension, keeping behavior byte-for-byte while making the store responsibilities easier to navigate. In the intended stack with #913, the main store falls to 478 lines.

## What was happening

- Refresh orchestration, persistence state, metric resolution, and read-only UI accessors all lived in one large store file.
- The refresh coalescing work in #928 brought the standalone file to 683 lines, well beyond the repository guideline.

## What this changes

- Moves error/warning/header access, widget-data projection, plan access, and staleness presentation into `WidgetDataStore+Presentation.swift`.
- Leaves the private snapshot error classifier with refresh ingestion in the main store.
- Preserves the moved declarations, comments, and bodies exactly; only cross-file visibility for the injected clock and legacy resolver changes temporarily.

## Heads-up

- This is stacked on `codex/coalesce-forced-refresh` (#928).
- #913 should land before this stack is finalized. A synthetic merge reproduced one expected conflict in `WidgetDataStore.swift`; the mechanical resolution is to keep #913’s private `reportMalformedTextMetrics` validator, remove the obsolete legacy resolver/parser chain, and call `WidgetDataResolver.resolve` from the presentation extension.
- That resolved stack has a 478-line main store, 90-line presentation extension, and 139-line resolver. Only the injected clock remains widened; the temporary legacy `resolve` widening disappears.
- Before #913 is applied, this isolated PR reduces the main file from 683 to 597 lines but cannot reach the 500-line guideline because the legacy resolver remains.

- Standalone: 50/50 focused WidgetDataStore tests passed; full suite passed with 977 XCTest tests, 3 skipped, plus 3 Swift Testing tests; release build staged, signed, restarted, and confirmed from this worktree.

author: itschriswang
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #261 (merged), which added an ink-spread reveal after the preloader. On review the first pass was reading **backwards** and off-brand, so this reworks how the sprite is used.

### The problem with the first pass
I inspected the actual sprite (`ink-spread.png`, 25 frames): it's a **dark-plum blot** (`rgb(63,47,68)`) that grows from 0% → **100% coverage**. Painting it directly meant the intro *filled the screen with dark ink and then faded it out* — a **cover** transition, not a reveal (it reads reversed), and it dropped a dark full-screen wash onto a light, luminous site, against the design system in `CLAUDE.md` ("everything stays light and luminous"). It also layered at `z-40` *beneath* the `z-50` preloader, so the ink formed hidden behind the intro.

### The fix
- Use the sprite **only as an alpha mask** over a **paper-coloured fill** (`#F7F4EF`, the `paper` token) — its dark colour is never painted, so nothing dark ever flashes.
- Play the sprite **in reverse (frame 24 → 0)**: a paper sheet starts fully covering the page and **retracts along the spreading-ink edge** to unveil it. That reads as a reveal.
- Trigger the peel off the preloader's fade; both share the paper ground, so the hand-off is seamless and the two read as one continuous unveiling.
- Swapped the preloader's clip-path circle exit for a plain fade (the circle collapse fought the ink retraction).
- **Reduced motion:** the ink cover is omitted entirely (and CSS-guarded) so the page is never trapped under a non-animating sheet — the preloader fade is the reveal there.

## Changes
- `src/components/InkSpreadReveal.jsx` — rewritten: paper sheet + CSS `mask-image`/`mask-position` sprite animation, reversed, alpha-only.
- `src/components/Preloader.jsx` — peel triggered on `gone`, fade exit, motion-flow-only mount, retimed (900ms peel start, 1400ms done).

The `ink-spread.png` asset already landed with #261, so it isn't re-added here.

## Verification
Ran the dev app and captured the intro frame-by-frame with Playwright. Confirmed: the paper sheet retracts along a feathered ink edge, the hero's own apricot / yellow-green washes bleed through, **no dark flash**, and it lands cleanly on the full hero. `npm run build` passes.

author: madfam-io
body:
## Problem

`POST /v1/admin/status/regenerate` is permanently refused for the madfam site:

```
409 {"error":"status regenerate refused for madfam: generated 16 services below safety floor 60",
     "existing_service_count":68,"generated_service_count":16}
```

Two causes:

1. **Stale snapshots**: `buildServiceListForSite` reads status entries only from onboarding `ConfigSnapshot`s, which are written at onboard/ensure time and go stale the moment a project merges new status entries. Concretely: blueprint-harvester merged its API `/ready` probe (RFC 0015) on 2026-07-09 and regenerate could not see it.
2. **Replace semantics**: the generator replaces the whole `services-config`, so the ~50 hand-maintained legacy entries no project declares yet would be mass-deleted. The safety floor correctly refuses that — which made regenerate permanently unusable, blocking every new enclii.yaml status declaration.

## Fix

- **Live-fetch first**: for each onboarded repo, fetch `enclii.yaml` live (`fetchStatusEntriesForProject`, previously dead code) and fall back to the snapshot when the fetch yields nothing (no token, GitHub outage).
- **Reconcile, don't replace**: `mergePreserveExistingStatusEntries()` appends existing entries whose Name+Group identity the generator did not produce. Generated (project-declared) entries win identity collisions, so ownership transfers cleanly as projects adopt `status.entries[]`. The floor + shrink guard remain as backstops, validating the merged count.
- Response now reports `preserved_legacy` per site so operators can watch the legacy set shrink toward zero as projects take ownership.

Also: `test(secretsintake)` — 8a929ee1 added an 11th registry entry without updating count assertions, leaving main's suite red; assertions now track it.

## Tests

- `TestStatusHandler_MergePreservesUnownedLegacyEntries` — unowned survive, generated wins collisions
- `TestStatusHandler_MergeUnblocksFloorScenario` — reproduces the exact prod refusal (16 vs 68 vs 60) and shows the merged count passes
- `TestStatusHandler_MergeEmptyExisting` — first-ever regenerate passes through
- Full `internal/api` + `internal/secretsintake` suites green

## Follow-up after deploy

Re-run `enclii admin status regenerate --force` — expected: madfam count ≥ 68, `preserved_legacy` reported, and the blueprint-harvester API probe (`api.blueprint.tube/ready`) projected to status.madfam.io.

author: singlepixel12
body:
Addresses the concrete defects from the June risk audit, then the findings of a high-effort code review over that work.

API resilience (lib/api/supabase.ts):
- All four fetchers now go through one supabaseFetch(queryUrl, context) helper owning auth headers, a 10s AbortController timeout (cleared in finally so the timer can never leak), and error mapping. This also fixes the two gaps the review caught: getWubbySummaryByHash previously had no timeout at all, and getWubbySummary cleared its timer outside a finally.
- describeHttpError prefixes every message with the call site, so a list failure no longer reads like a single-video lookup failure.
- Timeout detection checks error.name without an instanceof Error gate, so DOMException is caught even on engines where it doesn't subclass Error.
- New PlatformFilter type ('twitch'|'kick'|'both') makes an invalid platform filter unrepresentable at compile time; the runtime whitelist remains as a backstop and throws rather than silently returning unfiltered data.

Accessibility (VideoCard):
- The play affordance was a <div onClick> with an aria-label but no role, tabIndex, or key handler, so keyboard and screen-reader users could not open /watch (WCAG 2.1.1 Level A). It is now a real <Link>, keeping the new-tab behavior via target=_blank + rel=noopener noreferrer.
- A video without a hash renders an inert thumbnail that keeps the img's accessible description and drops the play button entirely - a control that cannot be activated is not shown.
- Focus ring uses the shared ring token instead of an ad-hoc accent ring.
- Drop the hand-rolled basePath prefix and window.open; next/link applies the configured basePath itself (verified against the production build).
- Route raw console.* through the logger util.

Tests:
- createMockVideo now includes a videoHash by default; the hashless case asserts no link, no play affordance, and a labelled img.
- Rewrite the vacuous new-tab navigation E2E (its a[href="/player"] locator could never match) to target a[href*="/watch?id="] and assert.
- Delete two E2E tests whose only subject was the removed PlatformSlider.

Docs: gitignore the standalone extension and mark it out of scope; fold the WEAKSPOTS.md audit into CLAUDE.md (open items + settled non-issues) and delete the file; update tests/README.md.

Verified: 126/126 unit tests pass, production build succeeds, no new lint or type errors. The E2E suite has not been run end-to-end.

In scope of https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/17063, the `HttpContentEncoder` got a new property `maxPipelineDepth` and the respective constructor variant. However, the subclasses, notably `HttpContentCompressor` have not been updated to allow changing `maxPipelineDepth` and always use the default `128`.

Modification:

Add `HttpContentCompressor` constructor variant with ability to specify desired `maxPipelineDepth`. It would help us to absorb the change through configuration setting.

@chrisvest would appreciate your feedback, thank you.

author: peilin-wang-git
body:
### Motivation

- The Sanatorium 3D pipeline raised `ValueError: expected 3D data, got shape (88,320,320,1)` because the 3D loader sometimes produced pseudo-3D arrays with a trailing singleton axis or stacked already-3D per-file pixel arrays incorrectly. 
- The loader must guarantee a strict `ndim == 3` volume contract so the orientation helper receives real 3D data and does not become a brittle fallback.

### Description

- Added `_normalize_sanatorium_3d_slice(pixel_array, path)` which explicitly accepts only true 2D slices or 2D-with-a-singleton-axis (`(H,W)`, `(H,W,1)`, `(1,H,W)`) and rejects true multi-frame/multi-channel inputs instead of calling `np.squeeze()` indiscriminately. 
- Changed `_load_sanatorium_3d_dicom_volume(source)` to log raw `pixel_array.shape` for each file, normalize each per-file slice via `_normalize_sanatorium_3d_slice` before stacking, verify consistent 2D slice shapes, and raise a clear error if normalized shapes are inconsistent. 
- Added special handling for single-file 3D DICOM payloads by checking DICOM `Rows`/`Columns` and converting frame-first arrays (e.g. `(Z,H,W)`) into the Sanatorium convention `(H,W,Z)` instead of producing an extra singleton axis. 
- Added explicit pre-orientation checks and clearer error messages in `export_sanatorium_3d()` so pseudo-3D/4D-with-singleton volumes fail in the loader layer, and added debug metadata/logging keys including `slice_pixel_array_debug`, `final_volume_shape`, and `orientation_input_shape` to help verification.

### Testing

- Ran `python -m py_compile SanatoriumHospital/loader.py` which succeeded. 
- Executed synthetic tests that patch `pydicom.dcmread` to simulate a single-file 3D DICOM (`pixel_array` shape `(88,320,320)`) and confirmed the loader returns a strict 3D volume with shape `(320,320,88)` and `debug['final_volume_shape']` matches. 
- Ran normalization checks for singleton slice cases by calling `_normalize_sanatorium_3d_slice` with shapes `(320,320,1)` and `(1,320,320)` and confirmed they normalize to `(320,320)` successfully.

author: zakinadhif
body:
Follow-up to #51, which merged before these two commits were pushed — hence GitHub's "recent pushes" banner on the branch. The design in `main` is already correct (per-PR buckets); this fixes the *rationale*, which is the part an implementer reads before starting #44.

Net effect is two hunks:

**1. Why the shared bucket was rejected.** `main` currently says a shared bucket "would leak objects between PRs on key collision" — true but unevidenced, and it reads like an aesthetic preference. The concrete reason is in the code: `coverKeyFor` returns `karya/${karyaId}/cover.${ext}` and the seeders plant fixed ids (`seed_k1`…`seed_k3`) into *every* preview database, so two reviewers uploading a cover for the same seeded karya write byte-identical keys — and `karya.ts` deletes the previous object when the extension differs. Avoiding it requires a prefix wrapper plus a var threaded into `worker.ts`: application code whose only purpose is serving previews.

**2. The credential exposure, stated honestly.** `main` currently implies the R2 admin token introduces a new class of risk. It doesn't. Per-PR *databases* are the whole design, Cloudflare's `D1:Edit` permission cannot be scoped to a set of databases, and D1 Time Travel restores a point in time *within* a database rather than resurrecting a deleted one — so `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` can already run `wrangler d1 delete buildersnetwork`. Same teardown path, same name-computed-from-a-PR-number accident shape.

R2's account-wide token is therefore a **second instance of an exposure CI already carries and cannot shed**, not a new one. Recorded as deliberately accepted, with the guard stated uniformly for both resources: anchored `^buildersnetwork-pr-[0-9]+$` and `^buildersnetwork-pr-[0-9]+-uploads$`, names built from `github.event.pull_request.number`, and explicit tests that the production database *and* bucket names are refused.

The branch history contains a shared-bucket commit and its revert; the net diff against `main` is the two hunks above. #44 and #45 already carry this reasoning — only the doc was out of sync.

Docs only.
