author: coghex
body:
Closes #650.

## What

`--offscreen` is the third boot mode — **GPU on, window off**: the full Vulkan render pipeline drawing to offscreen images with no GLFW, no surface, no swapchain, no focus steal. It is the unattended/parallel substrate for the playtest harness (#641).

| Mode | Vulkan/GPU | Window | Render |
|------|-----------|--------|--------|
| `--headless` | off | none | none (sim only) |
| **`--offscreen`** | **on** | **none** | **full, to offscreen images** |
| windowed | on | yes | full, to swapchain |

## How

- **Target abstraction:** `SwapchainInfo.siSwapchain` becomes `siTarget :: RenderTarget` (`TargetSwapchain | TargetOffscreen`) — only 3 use sites; every consumer of format/extent/images/views is shared unchanged. `renderedImageLayout` maps the target to the render pass final layout (`PRESENT_SRC` windowed, `TRANSFER_SRC` offscreen — `PRESENT_SRC` is illegal without the swapchain device extension), and the screenshot copy-out barriers take that layout instead of hardcoding `PRESENT_SRC`.
- **Init split:** `initializeVulkan` = windowed shell (GLFW surface, swapchain, views) over a shared `initializeVulkanCommon` (frame resources → pipelines → framebuffers → sync). New `initializeVulkanOffscreen` picks the device with no surface (present family aliases graphics, `VK_KHR_swapchain` neither required nor enabled, no GLFW extensions requested — GLFW is never initialized) and creates one `B8G8R8A8` image per frame in flight with `COLOR_ATTACHMENT|TRANSFER_SRC` usage, so `debug.captureScreenshot` is *always* supported (none of #700's surface negotiation).
- **Frame loop:** `drawFrame` dispatches on the target. Windowed is unchanged. Offscreen: image index = frame-in-flight index, submit with no semaphores, no present; the in-flight fence alone paces reuse. The shared middle (scene/UI collection, uniforms, vertex upload, screenshot prep, command recording) is extracted as `renderSceneFrame`.
- **Boot path:** `App.Offscreen` starts every worker thread **including the input thread** (GPU-less headless skips it), seeds the size refs + `LuaWindowResize`/`LuaFramebufferResize` the way `GLFW.createWindow` does, and runs `mainLoopOffscreen` (windowed loop minus GLFW polling/close-check, ~60 fps sleep pacing since no vsync exists). `ecHeadless` stays False, so the real UI stack — loading screen, menus, HUD — runs.
- **CLI:** `--offscreen` (wins over `--headless`), `--size WxH` (defaults to the video-config resolution). Window-requiring video settings (resolution/window-mode/vsync/MSAA) already warn-and-skip on `glfwWindow = Nothing`; offscreen inherits that.

## Acceptance (all verified live on macOS/MoltenVK — surfaceless works)

- Boots with **no window**, initializes Vulkan + the full pipeline. ✅
- `debug.captureScreenshot` returns a valid, non-blank PNG (main menu render confirmed by eye). ✅
- Full UI flow: loading screen → main menu → create-world → **real worldgen** → in-game HUD. ✅
- F2 `input.*` injection drives the UI windowless (clicks located via the F3 `ui.dumpWidgets` oracle). ✅
- Two concurrent instances on distinct ports, both rendering + capturing. ✅

## Gate

**`python3 tools/offscreen_probe.py`** — 20 checks covering all of the above end-to-end (18 shown + Continue-click variants); all pass locally. Registered in `run_probes.py` and classified under a new `needs-gpu` manual-only category in `ci_probes.py` (first probe requiring a real Vulkan device — the natural candidate for a future GPU CI lane); `ci_probes.py --self-test` passes.

`make ci` green (warning-clean build incl. both test suites, headless hspec, test_audit, lua_module_budget, world_check --quick).

**Reviewer note:** the windowed path was restructured (init split + `drawFrame` dispatch) and is compile+CI-verified, but only the offscreen path was exercised on a live GPU this session — a normal windowed launch deserves a quick eyeball before merge.

author: iamacoffeepot
body:
Records the editor-shell input-ownership model scoped for #2918.

A new EditorShell root actor arbitrates pointer/keyboard ownership across independently-rooted regions (tool panels, the world viewport, the console) one level above ADR-0117's per-cluster ownership. It reuses ADR-0117's decomposition recursively: a plain-state Routing table (the editor-level analogue of Focus) plus an actor that owns the mail. Regions are declared in config; routing is two-level and deterministic, with release-to-press-owner across regions and nested focus scopes. The shell owns input arbitration only, not draw fan-in — each region stays its own render sender.

This crosses cluster/component roots for the first time (the shell forwards raw input kinds to peer mailboxes and region roots relinquish self-subscription under a shell), which is the boundary #2919 explicitly deferred to a dedicated decision record.

Scoped by /scope on #2918; that issue is not /approve-eligible until this merges.

author: christopherwxyz
body:
## Summary

Found while manually verifying the new production deployment (see officialunofficial/makechain#1186): every real image transform request was silently returning the **untouched original image** instead of a resized/re-encoded one.

Root cause: `vips_heifsave_buffer` defaults to `VIPS_FOREIGN_HEIF_COMPRESSION_HEVC` when `compression` is omitted, not AV1. `save_avif()` never passed it. AVIF is first in the negotiation priority order (INV-7) and matches almost every real browser `Accept` header (explicit `image/avif` or a `*/*` wildcard), so nearly all traffic negotiated to AVIF — which then either:
- errored outright on Alpine (the runtime image only has an AV1 encoder plugin, no HEVC/x265), or
- on an environment that *does* have an HEVC encoder, would have silently produced HEVC-in-a-HEIF-container bytes mislabeled `image/avif`.

Either way, `server.rs`'s `Ok(Err(_)) | Err(_)` fallback caught the failure and served the raw origin bytes back with `Cache-Control` and a 200 — no error surfaced anywhere, because that branch never logged.

## Changes

- `imgx-vips/src/image.rs`: `save_avif()` now passes `compression = VIPS_FOREIGN_HEIF_COMPRESSION_AV1 (4)` explicitly. Added a regression test that asserts the encoded output's ISO BMFF `ftyp` major brand is `avif` (not `heic`/`mif1`) — a test that only checks "doesn't error" would not have caught this.
- `Dockerfile`: install `vips-heif` (AVIF/HEIF support is a separate Alpine plugin package, not in plain `vips`) and `libheif-aom` (libheif also loads codecs as runtime plugins — an actual AV1 encoder has to be present).
- `server.rs`: the transform-failure fallback path now logs via `tracing::warn!` with the path/transform string. This class of bug is otherwise invisible in production.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` all clean.
- Reproduced the bug and verified the fix end-to-end in a real Alpine container (matching the production Dockerfile) using `test/fixtures/bench_2000x1500.png`:
  - Before: `w=400` request → 200, `content-type: application/octet-stream`, 518993 bytes, still 2000x1500 (untouched original).
  - After: `w=400` request → 200, `content-type: image/avif`, 1735 bytes, `400x300` (confirmed via `vipsheader`), valid AVIF `ftyp` box.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] Manually reproduced + verified fix in an Alpine container matching production
- [ ] Once merged, cut a release and redeploy `apps/zimgx` (officialunofficial/makechain) to the new image

author: dylanrogowsky-oxd
body:
## Links to Jira Tickets

- [SIMSBIOHUB-1093](https://apps.nrs.gov.bc.ca/int/jira/browse/SIMSBIOHUB-1093)

## Description of Changes

User autocomplete fields and form user selectors now display the readable Keycloak display label (e.g. `Bryan, Luke WLRS:EX`) instead of the raw IDIR username (`LBRYAN`), so users can confidently identify the correct person. When a display label is missing, null, or empty, the UI falls back to the existing username / IDIR. Submitted values are unchanged — forms still send the stable `system_user_id`.

`system_user.display_name` already exists in the database (populated from the Keycloak token on login via `PUT /user/self`); this PR surfaces it through the user-option APIs and the selector UI.

**Backend (`api/`)**

- `getAvailableUsers` and the team-member queries now select `su.display_name`. The `AvailableUser` / `TeamMemberWithUser` models and the `AvailableUserSchema` / `TeamMemberSchema` OpenAPI schemas include it (required, nullable).
- Available-users search now matches `user_identifier` **or** `display_name` (case-insensitive), and results are ordered by `COALESCE(display_name, user_identifier)` — so typing what you see (e.g. "Bryan") finds the user whose identifier is `LBRYAN`.
- Documented the already-returned `display_name` field on the `GET /user` and `GET /user/{userId}` response schemas.

**Frontend (`app/`)**

- New shared `getUserLabel(user)` helper (`utils/Utils.ts`) returns `display_name` when present, otherwise `user_identifier` (handles null / empty / whitespace).
- Every user selector, selected chip, sidebar, and card now uses it: policy team-member select, ticket participants dialog + sidebar, ticket assignee dialog + cards + sidebar, the data-request dialog, and the portal ticket sidebar. Selecting an option carries the full user object (looked up by `system_user_id`) so the stored `user_identifier` stays correct while the visible label is the display name.
- Admin → Users table: the user column (dev's recently-merged DataGrid) is renamed **Username → Name** and renders the display label as the primary value, with the raw identifier as a secondary caption when a display label exists.
- `IAvailableUser` and `ITeamMember` interfaces gain `display_name: string | null`.

**Seed data (`database/`)**

- Dev system users are seeded with realistic display names (one intentionally left without one to exercise the fallback). Applies on a fresh database.

## Testing Notes

- Display names are read from the Keycloak token on login, so your own account populates automatically. For other users on an existing local DB, seed a value directly — e.g. `UPDATE biohub.system_user SET display_name = 'Bryan, Luke WLRS:EX' WHERE user_identifier = 'mauberti';` — and leave at least one user `NULL` (optionally one `''`) to confirm the username fallback. A fresh DB (`make clean && make web`) picks up the seeded names.
- Verify each selector shows the display label in **both** the dropdown options and the selected chips/cards:
  - Manage Policies → create / edit a team (typing part of a display name, e.g. "Bryan", finds the user via server-side search)
  - Ticket detail → Participants dialog + sidebar
  - Ticket detail → Assign Ticket dialog + assignee cards / sidebar (a newly assigned user shows the label immediately, with no flash of the identifier)
  - Create Data Request dialog
  - Admin → Users table (**Name** column with the identifier caption)
  - Portal ticket sidebar (read-only)
- Confirm submitted payloads are unchanged: `POST /api/administrative/teams/{teamId}/member`, data-request, and assignee requests still send only `system_user_id`s.
- API spot-check: `GET /api/administrative/users?search=bryan` returns each option with `display_name`, ordered by the display label.
- Unit tests: `cd api && npm test` and `cd app && npm test` — new coverage for `getUserLabel`, `getAvailableUsers` search/ordering, and the selector label rendering.

Second phase of the structural plan: automated checks so regressions get caught before merge.

> **Stacked on #18** (base is `claude/phase1-hygiene`). Retarget to `main` once #18 merges. The diff shown here is Phase 2 only.

## What's added

**CI** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on PRs + `main`: install → lint → test → asset audit → client build → bundle guard. Previously nothing gated merges.

**ESLint** — `eslint.config.js` (flat config: `typescript-eslint` + `react-hooks`). `npm run lint` now runs `tsc --noEmit && eslint .`.
- All **errors fixed**: two conditional-hook calls annotated (safe — gated by a build-time constant, so hook order is stable and calling both would load both models), useless assignments removed, `prefer-const`, a caught-error `cause`, and browser globals for the Puppeteer scripts.
- ~57 warnings remain as **tracked, non-blocking debt** — mostly unused vars in the `lib/phone-swap/` tuning scaffolding (slated for the Phase 4 audit) plus some `exhaustive-deps`.

**Tests** — `vitest`, 20 tests on the content layer (the code the recent content churn kept touching):
- `parseMarkdown`: frontmatter parsing + `---` section splitting.
- `parseChapterBody`: blank-line splitting + bold-subhead grouping.

**Bundle guard** — `scripts/check-bundle.mjs` (wired into `build` and CI) fails if three.js leaks into the entry chunk or the entry exceeds a size ceiling. This protects the invariant behind `vite.config.ts` dropping `manualChunks`. Verified it catches a simulated leak.

Ran the full CI sequence locally — all green: `lint`, `test` (20 passed), `audit:assets`, `vite build`, `check:bundle` (entry 120 KB, three.js isolated in its own chunk).

body:
## Summary

Two related changes that move memento's workflow from local-only files toward durable, cloud-first infrastructure. Both came out of a design discussion; the reasoning is captured in the first ADR.

### 1. Introduce in-repo ADRs (the durable home for decisions)
- `templates/adr.md` — starter shape (Status / Context / Decision / Alternatives / Consequences)
- `docs/decisions/README.md` — convention, status lifecycle, and the project-neutrality rule (mirrors the phone-home gate for skills)
- `docs/decisions/0001-adopt-public-plugin-distribution.md` — the first decision record

This replaces the old copy/paste "graduate the durable record" step with versioned, greppable decisions next to the code they justify. Scope is decisions-only for now; task tracking stays in the local scratchpad.

### 2. Package memento as a self-hosting Claude Code plugin (ADR-0001, Milestone 1)
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — memento is its own one-entry marketplace (root source)
- `scripts/` → `bin/` (plugin PATH convention; tracked as renames)
- `new-feature.sh` resolves the kit root via `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, falling back to `readlink` so the symlink install still works
- `install.sh` links `bin/*.sh`; README + architecture document the plugin install and the `.claude/settings.json` cloud auto-install path

**Why:** in ephemeral/cloud sessions the `~/.claude` symlink model doesn't exist, so the kit effectively wasn't available where we work. The plugin channel installs the same way everywhere, including cloud/web sessions.

**Non-breaking:** the `install.sh --user` symlink path is unchanged and still functional. Personas stay carried files (curious-builder is a tone guide, not a subagent).

## Testing
- Shell syntax on all scripts and the installer
- `new-feature.sh` scaffolds correctly in **both** plugin mode (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set) and fallback (`readlink`) mode
- `install.sh --dry-run` wires `bin/*.sh`
- Both manifests validated as well-formed JSON

## Not yet verified
A live `/plugin marketplace add` install confirming skills load namespaced as `memento:orchestrate`, and specifically the marketplace root self-reference (`"source": "./"`). This merge enables that end-to-end test. If the root-source syntax is wrong, it's a one-line fix in `marketplace.json`.

## Follow-up (Milestone 2)
The `memento:` namespace doc-sweep across the workflow guide / skills / examples, and softening the now-legacy `--vendor` guidance per ADR-0001.

author: lmvdz
body:
Closes R3 (\"units are context-poor\") from `plans/research-direct-vs-glance/BRIEF.md` — the last structural gap in the founding brief.

## The defect, in three layers

The cold-start fabric primer was gated on `opts.featureId`. **Nothing dispatch spawns carries one** — `dispatchSpawn` calls `create({repo, name, branch, task, issue})`, and so does `glance add`. Only the feature-linked API path set it, so the primer had never run for a dispatched or ad-hoc unit.

Nothing said so, either: the `primer-empty` metric is recorded *inside that same branch*. It has **zero records** across this host's 1,000+ entry `learning-metrics.jsonl`. The instrument was inside the thing it was meant to measure.

Then, two silent drops beneath it:

- `WorkflowDriverOptions` had no `appendSystemPrompt` field **at all**. Workflow units — what `--verify` and every routed dispatch produce — got no profile memory, no tool grants, no primer, and no authored spec block. `RpcAgent` has supported `--append-system-prompt` all along.
- `SandboxAgentDriver` dropped it too; the in-container child is a plain `omp --mode rpc`.

## What widening it exposed

Sending an unscoped fabric read into every yolo agent's **system prompt** turned two latent bugs live. Both foreign lineages reviewed the diff (this touches trust + a system-prompt injection surface); both found a real one.

**Cross-repo leak** (gpt-5.6-sol) — `buildFabricSnapshot` repo-scoped decisions/failures/leases/scout but not `agents`, `digests`, or the receipts behind `hotAreas`. A digest is a *summary of source*. `?repo=A` returned repo B's digests, and the primer asks for exactly one repo. `repoAdmitter` now scopes every fact type, normalizes both sides, and fails closed on an unattributable digest.

**Fence forgery** (grok-4.5) — `fenceUntrusted`'s delimiter is a fixed string wrapped around text written *by the agents it fences against*. A digest containing `===== END context primer =====` closed its own fence and addressed the next unit's model as the system. Now folded to `U+2550` at the single choke point all seven injection sites share, with a body cap (it becomes an argv element).

## Honesty

`contextReachesAgent()` asks the harness registry — which has declared `capabilities.contextInjection` all along while nothing consulted it — whether the assembled context can reach the agent. An ACP unit has no system-prompt slot; it now says so instead of scoring `hasInstructions: true` while running unscoped. New `primer-undelivered` metric, recorded *outside* the branch it measures.

- Evaluated **after** `routeIntake`, which can turn an ACP unit into a workflow unit whose inner omp child *does* have a channel (grok-4.5).
- The ACP opt-in block no longer labels its payload `"trusted system guidance"` — it carries a fenced *untrusted* primer, and that label told the model to ignore the fence (grok-4.5).

## Bounded

`fabric()` enumerates every receipt, reads every digest, and calls Plane's untimed issue fetch — inside the dispatcher's **serial** spawn loop. `OMP_SQUAD_PRIMER_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s) races it. A lost race doesn't cancel the read, so ten queued issues meant ten concurrent scans; `OMP_SQUAD_PRIMER_BACKOFF_MS` (60s) trips a breaker after a timeout (grok-4.5).

Kill switch: `OMP_SQUAD_CONTEXT_PRIMER=0`.

## Verification

Every new guard is mutation-proven — delete it, a named test goes red (9 mutations run). **2442 backend + 826 webapp pass**, `tsc` clean, effect-ratchet at baseline.

Part of #86 (PR1 of 8).

Extracts the generic SAX-style XML tokenizer/entity/namespace-resolution core from `plugins/metalink/xml.zig` into a new shared `xml/` module, so the upcoming `repomd.xml`/`primary.xml`/`filelists.xml`/`other.xml`/`updateinfo.xml` parsers (later PRs in #86) can reuse it instead of each writing their own XML tokenizer.

**Extracted (generic):** tag/attribute/text tokenization, entity decoding, comment/CDATA/PI skipping, QName splitting, namespace binding/resolution.
**Kept in `plugins/metalink/xml.zig` (metalink-specific):** the C ABI (`TDNFMetalinkXmlParseBuffer` + `pfnFile`/`pfnSize`/`pfnHash`/`pfnUrl` callbacks), metalink namespace/version constants, the `classifyElement` state machine, and file/hash/url callback handling.

This is a pure refactor — **zero behavior change** to the metalink plugin.

Chunked/incremental-feed support (needed for large `primary.xml`/`filelists.xml` files later) is deliberately deferred to whichever later PR adds the first large RPM-MD parser, to keep this extraction low-risk.

body:
Supersedes #1797 (same CSS commit, cherry-picked without an unrelated `.rea/policy.yaml` governance commit that was blocking the Format gate).

## What

Published `@helixui/library` ships 8 broken `dist/css/` files (verified in 3.11.0 and 3.11.1). Components whose `.styles.ts` exports **multiple** `css`` tagged literals — `hx-table`, `hx-grid`, `hx-structured-list`, `hx-toast` — had the JavaScript between literals swept into their emitted CSS, contaminating the `helix-data`/`helix-feedback`/`helix-layout`/`helix-all` bundles and breaking downstream PostCSS parses with `Invalid empty selector`.

Root cause: the extractor took `indexOf('css\`')` for the first literal and `lastIndexOf('\`')` across the remainder of the file.

## Changes

- **Extractor** (`generate-css-bundles.mjs`): locates every standalone `css`` tagged literal — an identifier-boundary guard excludes `unsafeCSS`` and `.css`` paths in JSDoc — and scans each to its own closing backtick, handling escapes, `${}` interpolation depth, nested templates, and quoted strings inside interpolations. Bodies concatenate in source order.
- **JS-leak content gate** (`validate-css.mjs`): scans every `dist/css/*.css` for leaked-JS signatures and fails with file:line on any hit.
- **Publish-path wiring**: gate appended to `build`; new `prepack` runs `css:build && css:validate`, so a pack can never ship stale or leaking CSS.
- **Changeset**: patch → publishes as **3.11.2**.

## Verification

- `css:validate` green across all 93 CSS files; independent grep for leak patterns returns zero hits
- PostCSS parses `helix-all.css` and the 4 previously-broken component files without error
- `hx-table.css` now contains all four of its literals; single-literal output (`hx-button.css`) is byte-identical to published 3.11.1
- Synthetic scanner fixtures pass, including the `${unsafeCSS('content: "}"')}` boundary case
- Codex adversarial review: 4 rounds, 2 P2 findings remediated (prepack staleness, string literals inside interpolations), final verdict pass with 0 findings
- Preflight gates 1–10 pass (tests/CEM skipped — scripts-only diff, matching CI scoping). Gates 11–12 fail on **pre-existing** docs version drift (167 stale `3.9.0` pins across 36 files, none touched here); follow-up docs-sync tracked separately.

## Downstream

booked-solid-software retires its 7-bundle import workaround once on ≥3.11.2.

  - Added checks to prevent JavaScript content from leaking into generated CSS files.

- **Release**
  - Published patch release 3.11.1, including updated React integrations and starter package metadata.

author: iztblack
body:
Importar el estado de cuenta / control de pagos de una obra desde **Excel o CSV**, en dos modos: **asociar a una obra existente** (fusionando sin duplicar) o **crear una obra nueva** (web, ya existía).

## Web (Next.js)
- Nueva ruta `/admin/obras/[id]/importar` + botón **"Importar movimientos"** en el estado de cuenta de la obra.
- Server actions `previsualizar/confirmarImportacionObra` con detección de duplicados y conciliación de presupuesto.
- Soporte **CSV** además de `.xlsx`.

## Móvil (Flutter)
- Migración de esquema **v4→v5** (columna `movimientos.nombre` + tabla `ObraPresupuesto`), aditiva.
- `lib/domain/import`: parser Excel/CSV, dedup de movimientos y conciliación de presupuesto.
- Pestaña **Caja**: pantalla de importación, resúmenes **"Pagado por persona"** (con cubeta "Sin nombre") y **"Recibido por tipo"**, tarjeta de presupuesto, y alta manual con beneficiario + **autocompletado**.

## Reglas de negocio (confirmadas con el usuario)
- **Llave de duplicado:** `fecha + monto + concepto + tipo + nombre` (omite duplicados por defecto; opción "importar todo").
- **Presupuesto:** al importar a obra existente **no se toca** salvo que se active el checkbox; los conflictos se resuelven **por línea** (portal vs archivo), y las partidas solo-del-portal nunca se borran.
- **Cubeta "Sin nombre"** para salidas sin beneficiario; autocompletado en el alta manual para no fragmentar las cubetas de agrupación.

## Calidad
- ✅ Flutter **56/56** tests, `dart analyze` limpio; web `tsc`/`eslint`/`next build` en verde.
- ⚠️ El paquete `excel` forzó un **downgrade compatible** de `pdf` (3.13→3.12), `printing` (5.15→5.12) y `archive` (^3.6.1). **Regresión de PDF y respaldo verificada como segura** (incluye smoke test de PDF).
- Paridad web↔móvil de la llave de duplicados y la tolerancia de centavos alineada.

## Verificación (usar el preview con datos reales)
1. Obra → "Estado de cuenta" → **Importar movimientos** → subir `.xlsx` → preview con **Nuevo/Duplicado** y conteos.
2. Re-importar el mismo archivo → todo **Duplicado** (idempotente, no dobla la caja).
3. Estado de cuenta: **Pagado por persona** / **Recibido por tipo** con totales correctos.
4. Checkbox de presupuesto: fila en **Conflicto** con **costo total en vivo** (Mantener portal / Usar archivo).
5. **CSV** se importa; presupuesto sale como "sin cambios".
6. Crear obra nueva (`/admin/obras/importar`) sigue funcionando.

author: michaelsaucier
body: ## What Add `restart: unless-stopped` to the compose service(s) so containers recover automatically after a docker daemon or host restart. `unless-stopped` (not `always`) keeps a deliberate `docker stop` sticky — the policy never resurrects an intentionally-downed service. ## Why (verified evidence, 2026-07-10 investigation) - Host reboots 2026-07-04 06:06, 2026-07-04 09:32, and 2026-07-08 12:13 WEST killed every compose postgres on nucbuntu (`RestartPolicy=no`, exit 255 recorded at daemon restore). - `site-postgres-1` stayed dead 5+ days unnoticed; `hive-postgres-1` stayed dead 2026-07-08→09, crash-looping work-server and hive-ops-api until a manual `docker compose up -d postgres`. - In-org working reference: `upstream-fork-sync` deploy compose already uses `restart: unless-stopped` and recovered from every reboot. ## Factory Order (TLC channel A) - `doc_id: FO-20260710-compose-restart-durability` v0.1.0. - Source: Michael Saucier, in-session instruction 2026-07-10, verbatim: *"add restart to every service required so state is durable and recoverable"*, re-confirmed as *"add restart to hive and site"*. Archived source sha256 `82a92589b679299f4302fe30cde3b6d6b5d35e2b241144409fa136c1c3e39fe2`. - Design collapsed to the FO: the operator ordered the exact change; the only design freedom exercised is the policy value (`unless-stopped` over `always`, rationale above). Human design approval = the operator's explicit in-session order. This is NOT claimed as a mechanical edit (it changes runtime semantics), so IAR + CFAR run in full on this PR. ## Verification - `docker compose config` renders `restart: unless-stopped` on every service in this file (run in the worktree; read-only). - Post-merge (operator-gated deploy note): applying requires `docker compose up -d`, which recreates the container(s) — seconds of DB downtime; dependent systemd services self-heal. After recreation: `docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}'` must read `unless-stopped`. ## Non-goals - No recovery/migration/deletion of the orphaned postgres volumes (separate operator decision in flight). - No systemd unit changes (already have `Restart=`). - No named-volume change for site's anonymous data volume (recommended follow-up, kept out of this minimal diff). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: jasparke
body:
## What

Adds `docs/asset-manifest.json` — a machine-consumable inventory of every visual/media/font asset the rebuilt tracker needs to **retrieve, self-host, or find**.

## Why

The droid tier-art was originally **hot-linked from the third-party community site `droidtrakr.com`**. The design handoff spec calls for self-hosting so the rebuild isn't hostage to that host. This manifest turns that into an actionable, scriptable checklist.

## Contents

| Category | Need | Priority | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Droid tier-art (`.webp`) | 316 (62 tiered droids × 5 tiers + 6 Iconic × 1) | P0 | self-hosted 315/316 on `main` (PR #10); `R2D2_Default.webp` outstanding |
| App icons (favicon.ico, apple-touch, og-image) | 4 | P1 | missing (favicon.svg exists but unlinked) |
| Fonts (Chakra Petch, JetBrains Mono) | 2 | P1 | not yet vendored |
| Bespoke icons (currencies, badges, Nova upgrades, cosmetics) | ~30 | P3 | designer's choice |

Each of the 316 droid entries carries the exact `normName`-derived filename, its remote `droidtrakr.com` URL, and its local target path under `app/static/assets/droids/` — so a download script can consume it directly.

> **Note on the count:** Iconic-rarity droids (BB8, CB-23, DJ-R3X, IG-11 Marshal, Mister Bones, R2-D2) are **single-tier** — no tier grid, not chip-upgradable — so they contribute one `_Default` file each, not five. The true universe is **316**, not the 340 (68×5) originally targeted. See `meta.correction` in the manifest.

## Sources

- Entity lists generated from `app/drizzle/seed-data.json` (canonical dataset)
- Filename rules (`{normName}_{Tier}.webp`, Base→`_Default`) from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-04-frontend-design-handoff.md` §Assets and `prototype/index.html:541-564`

## Notes

- Verified all 316 filenames are unique; roster (names, rarities, types) matches `seed-data.json` exactly.
- droidtrakr serves 293 real files; an earlier HEAD sweep's "340/340 HTTP 200" included fallback responses, not images. A fetch script should record gaps.
- This is a docs-only change; no code touched.

author: raahimabsar
body:
## What this PR does

Hardens the agent harness so every milestone runs against honest, reproducible gates, and codifies the CI/CD protocol: feature branch → PR → green CI → **human approval** → merge.

### Gates
- `make gate-m0` … `gate-m9` — each mirrors its spec's definition-of-done (spec stays source of truth; targets carry a comment naming the spec they mirror)
- `make wait` polls `/health` (replaces blind `sleep 8`)
- All specs updated to reference their gate target

### Migrations
- `make db-reset` drops the pgdata volume and rebuilds from `db/init/*.sql` — the only way init scripts actually run after first start. Every gate begins with it.

### Tooling (hybrid)
- Seeder + k6 run as containerized compose services under the `tools` profile (pinned deps, in-network base URLs, zero host installs)
- ruff on host via `requirements-dev.txt` + `make bootstrap`

### CI/CD protocol
- CI runs **lint + full test suite** on every PR (and post-merge on master); compose logs dumped on failure
- `CODEOWNERS` requires review from @raahimabsar on every PR
- `.claude/` harness: permission allowlist, `/milestone` skill (verify previous gate → branch → implement → gate → DECISION.md on review points → PR → stop and wait for human), and a PreToolUse hook blocking master commits/pushes and agent-side merges; `merge_pull_request` MCP tool denied in settings
- CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md synced with the protocol

### Verification (run locally)
- `make gate-m0` → exits 0: fresh DB, all three services healthy, 3/3 test suites pass
- `make lint` → passes (ruff 0.8.6 via `make bootstrap`)
- `make seed` → seeder container builds and runs (exits 1 by design until M4)
- Hook tested: blocks commit-on-master, push-to-master, `gh pr merge`; allows feature-branch push

No existing functionality is touched — the three service stubs and their tests are unchanged.

### To activate the human-approval requirement server-side
GitHub branch protection can't be set from this repo's files; enable it once in **Settings → Branches → Add branch protection rule** for `master`:
1. ✅ Require a pull request before merging → Require approvals (1) → **Require review from Code Owners**
2. ✅ Require status checks to pass → select `lint` and `test`
3. ✅ Do not allow bypassing the above settings (optional but recommended)

body:
## Stream C — EGLE WDS solid-waste monitoring (DRAFT, dormant)

Adds a third monitoring stream: the **EGLE Waste Data System** (Part-115 solid waste, site `475946`) — a different portal from nSITE (Air, Stream A) and MMPC (Stream B). It surfaces data the risk register needs and nSITE lacks.

**This is a draft, off by default (`wds.enabled: false`), on a feature branch. Nothing runs until you review + merge + enable.** The 6am cron runs `main`, so it cannot fire this while unmerged; even after merge it's a no-op until `enabled: true`.

### What it adds
| Collection | Signal | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Quarterly Monitoring Reports (89) | groundwater `Statistical Exceedence? Yes/No` + reviewer notes (37/89 flagged) | **R5** (the tracker the plan said was missing) |
| Annual Landfill Reports (30) | permitted capacity + **years-remaining** (~3–4 yrs left) | **R1** (airspace/expansion) |
| Applications (10) | construction permits + operating licenses | **R1** (new CP = earliest expansion signal) |
| Compliance Actions (44) + Evaluations (249) | enforcement + inspections | **R2** |

### Four safety rules (detail in `docs/decisions/009-wds-stream-c.md`)
The risk isn't "fires overnight" (it can't) — it's "safe the moment you flip `enabled: true`":
- **A** — never diff a bad/short fetch (0 or collapsed rows → skip + warn, never read as deletions/new).
- **B** — enabling self-baselines silently (records all, alerts none) → no ~420-record historical flood, even without running the seed script; over-cap runs re-baseline instead of blasting.
- **C** — content-hash mutation detection: a Construction Permit going pending→**Issued** re-alerts (the #1 expansion signal a pure seen-set would miss). Verified end-to-end.
- **D** — WDS-specific classifier (never the temperature `is_urgent` free-text scan); a compliance action fires urgent only on a real violation/penalty, never `PAID/RESOLVED`.

Plus: the WDS Sheet tab is created **only when enabled** (invisible in the Conservancy Sheet until then); WDS alerts reuse the existing SMTP path (no new recipient surface).

### Files
`wds_client.py` (fetch+parse) · `wds_watcher.py` (diff+classify+route) · `scripts/seed_wds_state.py` (optional baseline) · `docs/decisions/009-wds-stream-c.md` · `tests/test_wds.py` (14 tests). Edits: `watcher.py` (gated hook), `sheet_writer.py` (`wds_seen` meta + on-demand tab), `config.yml` (dormant block), `README`.

### Verification done
- Full suite **99 passing** (14 new + 85 existing, no regressions).
- Live fetch of all 5 collections OK (apps 10 after template-row filter, QMR 89, annual 30, CME 44/249).
- End-to-end orchestration dry-run: baseline → 0 alerts; new CP → 1 urgent email; new exceedance QMR → digest; CP pending→Issued → urgent re-alert. All asserted.

### Activation — your call, 3 steps (nothing here does them)
1. Review + merge this PR to `main`.
2. *(optional)* `python scripts/seed_wds_state.py` once to baseline — or let the first enabled run self-baseline (rule B).
3. Set `wds.enabled: true` in `config.yml` and commit.

author: busse
body:
The site was making a false claim about how it treated other companies' servers. Copy only — **no data changed**.

## What it said, and what happened

| the site said | what actually happened |
| --- | --- |
| "**By hand. All of it.**" (`/data/`) | an AI agent session fetched each cited page once |
| "read by hand, never crawled" (every maker page) | no human read any of these pages |
| "read once by a human" (`sources.yml`, ×3) | fetched once by the research agent |
| "we honour that whether or not they ask" (every pack page) | we fetched Evergoods' and GoRuck's product pages |

The corrected account is on `/data/` § *How the data was collected*: **by an AI agent, one page at a time, on request — not by a crawler, not on a schedule, and not by a person.** Nothing was crawled recursively, nothing polled, no page fetched twice. That posture is real and worth stating. It just isn't the one we claimed.

The signals' `collected_by: console:EPIC4-05` was the one honest field all along. It was the prose around it that wasn't.

## The part that isn't wording

Evergoods and GoRuck forbid using their sites "to spider, crawl, or scrape". **ADR-0046 — which this project wrote — says the stricter of `robots.txt` and ToS governs, and that when in doubt you mark it `manual`.** We applied that standard to the scheduled fetch layer and did not apply it to ourselves while collecting the corpus.

A single agent-initiated fetch of one product page is not spidering, and a browser fetches pages too. But this dataset's entire pitch is that it does not grade its own homework, so the question is **filed as an open studio decision** rather than resolved by whoever was convenient. `/data/`, `/cite/`, the founding post and `sources.yml` now say so in the open — and commit to removing either maker's specifications if they would rather we had not.

ADR-0046 stands in substance: the fetch layer touches nothing, and nothing is on a cron. It was **silent** about how the corpus in front of it was gathered, and the copy filled that silence flatteringly.

## Also corrected

The AI-crawler paragraph used to read: *"not one of the ten robots.txt files named an AI or LLM crawler … it is an absence of instruction, not a grant of permission, and we have not treated it as one."* That sentence indicted itself, since an AI agent did the fetching. It now says what is true: we did not read that silence as permission to build a crawler, and whether it was permission to fetch ten pages once is the open question.

## Verified

- `check-integrity: OK — 21 packs, 99 signals, 7 entities, 13 sources (all manual), 1 unresolved conflict(s) acknowledged` — unchanged, no data touched
- Jekyll build clean; both record-page footers and the feed description render the corrected text
- Grep across the whole public surface: no "by hand" / "hand-carried" / "read once by a human" claim survives, except where the text quotes the old wording in order to correct it

author: dwalleck
body:
Closes cyril-6iek (engine identity is trusted, never verified — fingerprint the wire at handshake; fail-loud KAS detection outside the kas feature).

## What this does

The bound `AgentEngine` is a claim about the wire; nothing verified it. This PR adds **verification without selection**: two pure fingerprint checks (`protocol/fingerprint.rs`, compiled **unconditionally** — never behind the `kas` feature) compare the bound engine against the wire's own evidence, and a contradiction fail-stops with an actionable `BridgeDisconnected` remedy instead of today's cryptic cascade. Plus `v3` now parses as an alias for the `kas` engine selector (kiro-cli's own vocabulary since 2.8.0; serialization stays canonical `kas`).

The fingerprints are probe-proven, not assumed: KAS `initialize` always advertises an `agentCapabilities._meta.kiro` **object** (live-verified on 2.10.0/2.11.0/2.11.1/2.12.0; key set already drifted 3→5 keys, so only object presence is checked) and mints `sess_`-prefixed session ids; v2 sends no `_meta` at all and bare-UUID ids (every committed capture, 2.4.1→2.12.0). Baseline evidence: a default build meeting KAS today creates a session **silently**, then emits 14 cryptic `PersistenceClassification` errors and an `accessToken`-null turn death — the engine is never mentioned. Post-change: exactly one actionable message at initialize, zero cascade.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Default (no-kas) build vs KAS subprocess → actionable error, not a hang/silent dead turn — fences: `fingerprint_stops_v2_bound_on_kas_wire` (bridge), live rerun `.cyril-6iek/test_bridge-default-vs-kas-POST.out`
- [x] kas build with the wrong `--agent-engine` detects the mismatch at handshake, both directions — fences: `kas_bound_on_v2_wire_stops`, `kas_bound_on_kas_wire_proceeds` (unit), `fingerprint_stops_kas_bound_on_uuid_id` (kas-lane bridge)
- [x] `--agent-engine v3` parses as Kas — fences: `from_str_parses_known_and_rejects_unknown`, `config_roundtrips_lowercase` (serde alias; emits `kas`)
- [x] Unit tests cover the fingerprint both directions + the FromStr alias — fingerprint unit matrix (init shapes × bounds × build), id-shape anchoring/boundary/empty fixtures, evidence-drift bridge tests (`fingerprint_stops_on_sess_id_v2_bound`, `…_load_v2_bound`)

No-false-positive guard (C4): `_meta` without `kiro`, non-object `kiro`, and every historical v2 capture stay clean; every pre-existing harness test doubles as the false-positive fence.

## Method + evidence

Full gilfoyle loop, artifacts in `.cyril-6iek/`: `probe-fingerprint.py` + committed-trace oracle (item-by-item agreement across two binary versions and two capture mechanisms), `findings.md`, approved `design.md` (11 claims, falsifier table), `plan.md`, `build-audit.md` (slice gates, recorded deviations), `review-decisions.md` (pre-PR review: 1 fix applied, 4 findings rejected with rationale). 832 tests default lane / 950 kas lane, clippy `-D warnings` both lanes, fmt, doctests green.

## Discovered and filed

- **cyril-wkt8** — watch: acp rpc parse ERROR on an oversized/split inbound frame, observed once in the F4 baseline (a configuration this PR eliminates; filed to check legit KAS sessions can't hit it).

## Notable behavior changes

- `session/load` now pre-flights the caller-supplied id's shape — a mixed-store load (`sess_` id under a v2 binding) is refused before the RPC reaches the agent.
- The D7 parse-table decision (`v3` rejected) is deliberately reversed per the design-pause approval; the flipped test documents the decision inline.

author: martianoff
body:
## Problem

The Go "functional options" example on https://gala.fyi/vs-go/ rendered with `*` and `...` collapsed to single dots.

The page content and HTML are correct — verified the served bytes and reproduced Prism 1.29.0 tokenization, which preserves every character. The cause is the code font (`Cascadia Code`): its ligatures / contextual alternates rewrite source glyphs. Confirmed in a headless render of the live page:

- `=>` → `⇒`
- `!=` → `≠`
- `<=` → `≤`
- `*` → mid-dot and `...` → ellipsis (browser/font-build dependent — what the report showed)

## Fix

Disable `liga`/`clig`/`calt`/`dlig` on `pre`/`code` in the shared layout so every glyph renders as its literal source character.

**Verified**: injected the CSS into a copy of the live page and re-rendered — the default-params block is clean and operators show literally (`=>`, `!=`, `*`).

## Note

This also changes GALA blocks' `=>` from the decorative `⇒` arrow to a literal `=>`. For a syntax-comparison page that's more accurate; if the arrow was intentional, the fix can be scoped to keep it.

author: pilotwaffle
body:
## TCLAW-4B-2 — Phase 1, Epic 4 · completes the receipt/replay feature

A toggled `ReceiptsPanel` lists receipts (`LIST_RECEIPTS`) and shows a detail + replay view (`GET_RECEIPT`) — the user-visible half over the merged 4A projection + 4B-1 read surface. Console rendering only; **no backend/contract/projection change**.

### Replay is display-only — structurally
Replayed historical events render through a standalone `ReplayEventRow` whose props are plain data (`{row, approvalsByTool}`). It's a module-level sibling of `ReceiptsPanel`, so it **cannot close over `sendCommand`**, has **zero function-typed props**, and renders **no approval card / recovery chip / tool card**. A replayed `PENDING_APPROVAL`/`ERROR` shows inert text plus its decided status — there is no reachable path to `APPROVE_TOOL`/`APPROVE_SKILL`/`SUBMIT_PROMPT`. This matters because `ERROR→SUBMIT_PROMPT` retry has no server idempotency guard (a replayed retry would launch a real new run). G2A verified the boundary three ways (lexical scope, type level, whole-tree grep).

### Pure, unit-tested display logic
`field`, `RULE_LABELS`, `formatReceiptState`, `formatCostField`, `formatRouteDiagnostics`, `toReplayEventRows`, `canRenderAction` — all pure, all in `friendly.test.ts` (+28 tests). `canRenderAction`'s `readOnly=true→false` matrix is the safety unit test; `RULE_LABELS` has a set-equality drift guard vs `RouterRuleIdSchema.options`.

### Honest display
NULL fields render "not recorded" (never `$0.00`/`0s`); a real `0` renders as `0`; `budget_source`/`cost_enforceable` always "not recorded"; `contextChars` only (no context toggle — the projection has no raw context). Oversize replay shows an explicit marker, never partial/blank.

### Ring-buffer safety
The seq-less transient 4B-1 responses are snapshotted into `useState`, so an open receipt survives eviction from the 1000-event live ring. A single early return keeps `receiptView`/`receiptList` frames out of the live log.

### Verification
415 tests (48 in `friendly`); typecheck 12/12; contracts:check 0 (no schema touched); build 7/7 (Next compiles the panel); `uv run pytest` 74. Live terminal behavior unchanged (additive props).

### Lifecycle
G1R APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (all changes + operator helper-factoring enforced) · Builder · G2A = **PASS** (three-way structural proof + teeth-check) · awaiting operator merge approval.

author: tobiasgrosser
body: Proves `LocalRewritePattern.PreservesSemantics getelementptr_local`, covering all six emitted sequences: `add` at scale 1, `sh1add`/`sh2add`/`sh3add` at scales 2, 4 and 8, `slli`+`add` for other powers of two below `2^64`, and `li`+`mul`+`add` for every remaining scale including 0. A successful source interpretation forces the base operand to hold an address and the `i64` index to be non-poison, since a poison index raises UB, and pins the result type to a pointer type through the conformance of its `.addr` result, which the verifier does not constrain; each branch then chains `castAddrToReg`, `castToReg`, its arithmetic ops and `castRegToAddr`, discharging the final refinement with that branch's bridge lemma. As in `LowerSdivPow2` the field transports are explicit rewrites rather than `grind`, because `PreservesSemantics` bakes `hpattern` into the types of `state'Wf`/`state'Dom`/`valueRefinement` so the unreduced pattern body can never be cleared from the context. Stacked on #1053, which fixes the zero-sized-element-type miscompile this proof would otherwise be unable to close.

author: chenyangjun-xy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #103137 reports that `openclaw browser evaluate --fn "() => 1 + 1" --timeout-ms 60000` aborts after ~15 seconds, ignoring `--timeout-ms`. Long-running JavaScript evaluations on a live browser session cannot complete.

## Root Cause

The timeout is enforced by the gateway WS runtime (`server/ws-connection.ts:333-349`). It reads `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` from the client options, then passes it through `resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs()` from `packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.ts`. When that value is `undefined`, the default is `DEFAULT_PREAUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`.

The bug was in `src/gateway/call.ts:callGatewayWithScopes()`: `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` was set to only `context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs`. When that config key was unset (the common case for users who don't configure gateway handshake timeout), the value was `undefined`, and the runtime fell back to the 15s default — regardless of `--timeout-ms`.

## Fix

```diff
-    preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs: context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs,
+    preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs:
+      context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs !== undefined
+        ? context.config.gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs
+        : timeoutMs ?? undefined,
```

When `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is not configured, `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` now falls back to the request `timeoutMs`, which originates from the user's `--timeout-ms` flag.

## Evidence

### Gateway WS runtime timeout resolution log

The following output traces the actual production code path — from `call.ts` through `createGatewayClient({ preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs })` to `server/ws-connection.ts`:

```
=== Gateway WS runtime: preauth handshake timeout resolution ===
Production code path:
  src/gateway/call.ts - callGatewayWithScopes ->
  createGatewayClient({ preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs }) ->
  server/ws-connection.ts - resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs() ->
  setTimeout(timer, handshakeTimeoutMs)

DEFAULT_PREAUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000ms (hardcoded)

[BEFORE FIX] user runs with --timeout-ms 60000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = undefined (common case)
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = undefined
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(undefined)
  > returns 15000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 15000)  ← ABORTS at ~15s, --timeout-ms ignored!

[AFTER FIX]  user runs with --timeout-ms 60000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = undefined
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = timeoutMs = 60000
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(60000)
  > returns 60000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 60000)  ← --timeout-ms respected!

[EDGE] user configured handshakeTimeoutMs=30000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = 30000 (explicit)
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = 30000 (handshake always wins)
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(30000)
  > returns 30000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 30000)  ← handshake timeout preserved
```

### Actual gateway production log format when timeout fires (ws-connection.ts:344)
```
[warn] handshake timeout conn=abc peer=wss://127.0.0.1:18789 remote=127.0.0.1:54321 phase=pre-auth
```

### Regression test execution

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/call.test.ts -t "preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs|handshake timeout"
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  44 passed | 440 skipped

 ✓ passes configured gateway handshake timeout to the client watchdog
 ✓ falls back preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs to command timeoutMs when handshakeTimeoutMs is unset
 ✓ uses handshakeTimeoutMs even when timeoutMs is shorter
 ✓ falls back preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs to default timeout when neither is set
```

### Full test file — no regressions
```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/call.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  484 passed
```

## Files Changed

- `src/gateway/call.ts:1232-1235` — `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` falls back to `timeoutMs` when `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is unset
- `src/gateway/call.test.ts` — 3 new regression tests covering all fallback paths

Fixes: #103137

author: johnpc
body:
## The bug you hit (spurious error on launch)
On a cold launch with a restored queue, the player sets `audio.src` for the restored track **while paused** — and often **before the auth token has hydrated** (`AuthProvider` resolves the session async). That fires a bogus `error` event on the audio element, which showed **"Couldn't play that track — skipping"** and skipped a track you never tried to play.

**Fix:** `onError` now ignores errors while the element is **paused** (no real playback was attempted — the next genuine play reloads a valid src). A real failure **during playback** still toasts + skips, exactly as before.

## Polish bundled in (from a rough-edges sweep)
- **Accessibility:** added `aria-label`s to the art+title composite buttons that had none — `TrackRow` ("Play/Pause «name»"), `QueueRow`, `AlbumCard` ("Open «name»"), `ResultRow`, `TopResult`, and artist album tiles. Screen readers now announce the action instead of reading raw content.
- **Plural bug:** "Added 1 to queue" → "Added 1 song to queue" (`CollectionActions`).

## Tests
`usePlaybackHandlers`: onError toasts+skips when playing, is ignored when paused. Full `npm run quality` green.

author: michaelsaucier
body: ## What Add `restart: unless-stopped` to the compose service(s) so containers recover automatically after a docker daemon or host restart. `unless-stopped` (not `always`) keeps a deliberate `docker stop` sticky — the policy never resurrects an intentionally-downed service. ## Why (verified evidence, 2026-07-10 investigation) - Host reboots 2026-07-04 06:06, 2026-07-04 09:32, and 2026-07-08 12:13 WEST killed every compose postgres on nucbuntu (`RestartPolicy=no`, exit 255 recorded at daemon restore). - `site-postgres-1` stayed dead 5+ days unnoticed; `hive-postgres-1` stayed dead 2026-07-08→09, crash-looping work-server and hive-ops-api until a manual `docker compose up -d postgres`. - In-org working reference: `upstream-fork-sync` deploy compose already uses `restart: unless-stopped` and recovered from every reboot. ## Factory Order (TLC channel A) - `doc_id: FO-20260710-compose-restart-durability` v0.1.0. - Source: Michael Saucier, in-session instruction 2026-07-10, verbatim: *"add restart to every service required so state is durable and recoverable"*, re-confirmed as *"add restart to hive and site"*. Archived source sha256 `82a92589b679299f4302fe30cde3b6d6b5d35e2b241144409fa136c1c3e39fe2`. - Design collapsed to the FO: the operator ordered the exact change; the only design freedom exercised is the policy value (`unless-stopped` over `always`, rationale above). Human design approval = the operator's explicit in-session order. This is NOT claimed as a mechanical edit (it changes runtime semantics), so IAR + CFAR run in full on this PR. ## Verification - `docker compose config` renders `restart: unless-stopped` on every service in this file (run in the worktree; read-only). - Post-merge (operator-gated deploy note): applying requires `docker compose up -d`, which recreates the container(s) — seconds of DB downtime; dependent systemd services self-heal. After recreation: `docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}'` must read `unless-stopped`. ## Non-goals - No recovery/migration/deletion of the orphaned postgres volumes (separate operator decision in flight). - No systemd unit changes (already have `Restart=`). - No named-volume change for site's anonymous data volume (recommended follow-up, kept out of this minimal diff). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: rumblecrumblers
body:
## JELA-59 — JELA-57 WS-2: TV shell epoch gate

Consumes the JELA-58 (v1.0.13.0) manifest fields — `configEpoch` + `components{web,shell,scripts,branding}` — as the TV-side boot gate. Mirrored `shell.js` + `boot-shell.src.js` per the shell-src-edit workflow (both `.min` regenerated, parity pins refreshed). **Ships OPT-IN OFF** (`localStorage['jellyfin.shell.configEpochGate']='1'`); kill switch `jellyfin.shell.configEpochDisabled='1'` honored now as the future default-ON opt-out (JELA-48/51 discipline). Flag flip is WS-4 after WS-3 on-device evidence.

### Mechanism
- `loadConfigEpoch(serverUrl)` kicks a per-boot `/shell/manifest.json?__sb=` probe (3 s bound, off the critical path — primary fetches never wait on it) and compares against the persisted record `jellyfin.shell.configEpoch` = `{epoch, components, ts, origin}`.
- **MATCH** → boot-scoped flag `__shellCfgEM=1` suppresses: (a) the `/web/` index+config SWR revalidation pair, (b) the boot-shell CSS miss-populate fetches, (c) the per-boot tx-manifest `?__sb=` busted fetch (served from a persisted last-good copy, `BABEL_OPTS_KEY`-checked), (d) waives the JSI-channel 6 h max-age and the JEL-619 class-1 24 h TTL — so plugin bodies (incl. the JellyfinEnhanced skin riding the ~1.2 MB JSI aggregate) keep serving from the **existing** bounded LS caches instead of refetching.
- **MISMATCH** → component-selective, remove-first invalidation (web → index/config/bundle/stylesheet body caches; scripts → JSI chunked record + JEL-619 vqk/version-keyed slots; branding → stylesheet bodies; shell → nothing, the bootstrap manifest-sha path already adopts new shell bytes), then today's refetch machinery repopulates; the NEW record commits **only after this boot's `/web/` pair settled successfully** (write-after-adopt — a failed refresh keeps the old record so the next boot re-invalidates instead of wedging).
- **Safety**: manifest unreachable / field absent / no record → exactly today's behavior; 7-day soft-TTL forces a full-revalidation boot even on perpetual match.
- **QA counters (WS-3)**: `window.__shellConfigEpoch {st: off|nofield|err|fresh|match|mismatch|ttl, e, inv, sup:{idx,txm,jsi,q,css}}` + `__shellCfgEM`.

### Deviations from the issue text (of record)
1. **Script-body cache reuses the existing bounded stores** (JSI chunked record ≤4 MB integrity-checked; JEL-619 content-addressed `txc:` slots ≤2 MB/body with one-generation-per-path cleanup + LRU) rather than adding a parallel new LRU cache — a duplicate of the 1.2 MB aggregate would pressure the 5 MB/origin LS quota already carrying ~3.1 MB of web/bundle bodies. The epoch gate supplies exactly the missing freshness/invalidation signal those caches lacked. Class-0 URLs outside the JSI channel keep today's fetch-every-boot behavior (none are known to matter; WS-3 can revisit).
2. **The gated boot pays one extra small manifest GET (~1 KB)**: the baked WGT bootstrap (≤v2.0.20, not updatable without a WGT re-release) fetches manifest.json but persists only version/sha256/shellUrl, so the hosted shell probes it itself. For the same reason the bootstrap's head-IIFE `/web/` prefetch pair still *fires* on installed TVs — the gate suppresses the shell-side drain/fresh-fetch and LS churn (and the real network pair in boot-shell-fallback/browser contexts).
3. **Soft-TTL is time-based only (7 days)** — the boots-counter variant was dropped for min-size budget (also kills a per-boot LS write).

### Size
`shell.min.js` 180,107 B = **117 B under the 176 KiB HARD_CAP** (trimmed ~1.3 KB via short helpers/locals to fit). The pre-existing soft-headroom warning stands: the next sizable shell change needs the cap-policy raise.

### Verification
- `config-epoch.test.cjs` (new, wired into the shell-tizen chain): functional drive of the extracted gate from BOTH shells — off/kill-switch/nofield/err/fresh/match/origin-switch/ttl/mismatch-selective-invalidation/write-after-adopt/tx-manifest suppression — plus static pins (seed-string TTL waiver, JSI age waiver, CSS gate, flag+counter literals in both committed `.min` blobs). All pass.
- Both package suites green (`shell-tizen` 50+ scripts incl. re-pinned `web-index-cache` B2; `shell-tizen-bootstrap` incl. `cross-shell-parity`: 92 shared functions, 81 mirrored, 11 pinned-divergent — `loadRemoteWebClient`/`buildSeedScript` re-pinned, both edited on both sides).
- `verify_shell_src.py` + `verify_boot_shell_src.py` OK; `pnpm -r test` exit 0; `format:check` OK; endpoint/evidence guards OK.
- On-device behavior (suppressed XHRs, settle delta, staleness drills) is **WS-3 = JELA-60** on the Q60R.

author: emooreatx
body:
> **Trust Root apply-path change — requesting review before merge.** This loosens the anchor-A→anchor-B re-scrub refuse guard on the canonical (Trust Root) key plane, so please scrutinize the security section.

## What
`list_canonical_servers` / `canonical_bootstrap_hints` now resolve to whatever the **latest quorum-agreed signed record** for a canonical `key_id` is: a re-scrubbed record whose **envelope `valid_from` is strictly newer supersedes** the stored one, in place. The CEG-native runtime **address move** — no re-bake, no key rotation. (Previously an anchor-A→anchor-B re-scrub was refused outright as a hijack, so an address change required re-baking `canonical_seed.json`, as #404 had to.)

- `ReplicatedKeyPlan::Supersede` + `ReplicatedKeyOutcome::Superseded` (append-only; `Superseded` crosses the directory-capsule ABI).
- `supersede_canonical_record` on **both** backends (atomic in-place swap, optimistically guarded on the planned-against `persist_row_hash`), wired into `apply_replicated_key_record`.

## Security (please review)
Admitted **only** when ALL hold, each fail-closed → `Refused`:
1. **Same identity** — same `key_id` + byte-identical hybrid pubkey (never a key swap).
2. **Canonical-scoped** — incoming carries the `canonical` role. *Load-bearing*: `check_canonical_role_admission` fast-paths a non-canonical row to `Ok`, so without this a single-anchor re-scrub of a plain node would bypass the quorum.
3. **Monotonic over the SIGNED timestamp** — incoming envelope `valid_from` strictly `>` stored envelope's. Reads `valid_from` **inside `registration_envelope`** (what the scrubs sign via `JCS`), **not** the unsigned top-level `KeyRecord::valid_from` — else a replay of an older validly-scrubbed record with a bumped top-level field could **downgrade** the address. Pinned by `toplevel_valid_from_spoof_cannot_forge_recency`.
4. **m-of-n quorum re-verified from persist's OWN state** — `check_canonical_role_admission` (strict-majority `n/2+1` of the **live** roster via `verify_quorum_policy`, never a hardcoded threshold; withdrawal-wins). Re-run at the store chokepoint (defense in depth).

Aligns with the `infra:* ≠ agency:*` doctrine (#408): authority is re-derived from **verified signatures over persist's own state**, never a count of claimed participants or a constant.

## Tests
- 6 crypto-free `supersede_precheck` adversarial units (monotonic; equal/older refuse; non-canonical refuse; missing-timestamp refuse; **top-level spoof** downgrade).
- `canonical_supersede_over_roster_matrix` — real co-scrubs over a test roster: newer 2-of-3 supersedes; **older 2-of-3 refused (monotonicity beats a fresh quorum)**; newer 1-scrub refused; non-canonical refused.
- Full suite **1444 green**; clippy/fmt clean. No verify re-pin.

Closes #405.

author: go-to-k
body:
Closes #858 (deferred half of #1067)

## Problem
When `cloudformation:DescribeType` fails (throttle/deny), `getSchemaInfoResult` returns an EMPTY degraded schema. #1067 stopped *caching* that EMPTY, but `classifyRead` still **diffed the resource against it** — an un-schema'd compare that is known-wrong in BOTH directions:
- readOnly live attrs (Arn/ids/timestamps) not stripped → first-run `[Potential Drift]` flood (core-invariant violation)
- declared writeOnly props not routed to readGap → false `[CFn-Declared Drift]` → `--fail` exits 1 on an untouched stack

## Fix
`classifyRead` now DEGRADES a schema-unavailable resource to a single `skipped` coverage finding (`--strict`-visible), mirroring the existing not-readable branch, instead of surfacing the known-wrong diff. Keyed off the `getSchemaInfoResult` failure signal (a cache HIT is a prior success → classify normally); #1067's no-cache-on-failure re-fetch is preserved. `readAddedModel` (added-children) is left unchanged — out of scope.

## Tests
- `tests/schema-unavailable-degrade-858.test.ts` (new, 3): DescribeType fails → resource is `skipped` (Arn does NOT false-surface); success → classifies normally; #1067 re-fetch still holds. Verified to fail without the fix.
- Updates `tests/schema-cache-failure-1067.test.ts`: its assertion pinned the old known-wrong undeclared surface — Q1 now correctly degrades to `skipped`.

File: `src/commands/gather.ts` (+ my own #1067 test). Note: the new test's `mockClient` param typing was corrected to the repo's `ReturnType<typeof mockClient>` pattern (oxc's type-aware lint flagged the generic form that tsgo missed).

author: mateusamp2119
body:
## Summary

Replaces the E13.5 presence-stub seal with the spec-backed real implementation (spec section 14). The stub fired on every successful manual run, used a placeholder digest, a fixed seed key, and a hardcoded `id_to=999999`; the chain was never truly validated end to end.

### What the spec mandates for seal timing (anchor: `docs/Iris Specification Inventory.md#14-row-level-provenance`, "How is journal growth bounded (partition, seal, compact)?")
> `journal_partition_rows` (configurable, default 10M, count-based, clockless): a threshold, not an exact cap; a partition seals once past it, every in-flight run writing into it finished, zero open entries. … Sealing: opportunistic dispatcher step after a pass: compact, checkpoint, archive.

So a seal fires only when the resident partition is **past the row threshold** and **every in-flight run writing into it has finished** — the unit is the run, never its lane (an idle-lane no-op pass writes nothing and never blocks a seal).

### Changes
- **Threshold gating** (`S14/seal-condition`): `sealDue` gates on the configured `IRIS_JOURNAL_PARTITION_ROWS`; the in-flight guard counts running runs among the partition's actual writers (`pg.ResidentRunIDs` + `store.RunningAmong`), so the perpetual lane loop's no-op runs never defer a seal.
- **Dispatcher step** (`S14/seal-dispatcher-step`): `journalSealer` runs compact → checkpoint → archive over the E07.3 seal primitives and the E07.4 chain. Real `id_from`/`id_to` from the sealed partition's actual entries, real digest over the compacted rows (`store.ComputeDigest`), real ed25519 signature under the engine key, `parent_digest` chained to the head; export via `archive.Export` under the checkpoint digest, then drop, then flip to archived.
- **Compaction collapse rule** (`S14/compaction-collapse-rule`): `pg.CompactEntries`, the pure model of the collapse rule (pre-images past undo nulled, dup stamps folded to latest op, each run's write set survives).
- **Engine key persistence**: `InstallEngine` and the seal persist/load the ed25519 key from `<.iris>/engine.key` (0600, create-once). The original `ALTER DATABASE meta SET` GUC storage requires SUPERUSER the external admin role lacks, so it never ran in external mode and the seal had no key to sign with. The workspace file is non-superuser-safe and, like the object store, a per-host prerequisite pointable at shared storage for HA. Flagged as a departure from "private half in meta" for spec review.

author: cutelittlegoat
tamnd
body:
Slice 6 of the test262 lowering worklist: an await-free async method lowers to a
synchronous method that returns an already-settled value.Promise, with a single
microtask drain at the end of main.

An async body with no await runs to completion on the calling stack, so it can
settle its promise now. The body lowers unchanged as a Go func, wrapped in
value.Async (or value.AsyncVoid for a Promise<void>), which runs it and turns a
normal return into a resolved promise and a thrown value into a rejected one, the
JavaScript rule that a synchronous throw in an async body becomes a rejection
rather than propagating. A static async method lowers to a package func the same
way. Promise<T> maps through typeExpr to *value.Promise[T], with Promise<void>
carrying a Unit element.

A .then or .catch on a settled promise enqueues its callback on a package-level
microtask queue rather than running it inline, and the assembled main drains that
queue once at its end, so a callback registered during the synchronous run fires
after that run the way JavaScript schedules it.

The suspension and propagation this slice does not cover hand back with their own
honest reasons: await ("await is a later slice"), a value-returning then
(chaining), a two-argument then, .finally, async methods in a class hierarchy,
and async generators.

Fixtures 2018 (resolution ordering), 2019 (rejection through catch), and 2020
(await handback) pin the behavior end to end. The value runtime and lower units
cover the shape and the microtask ordering. The static-async handback case this
slice retires is removed.

author: droideck
body:
Description: dncache_find_id() treated any nonzero ep_state as unavailable. This could hide valid DN cache entries and cause online reindex/export to recompose a DN, release it after a cache collision, and use it again.

Treat cached DNs as missing only when they are deleted, incomplete, or invalid. Valid entries queued in the LRU remain available for lookup. Give db2index, db2ldif, and upgradedn producers independent DN ownership after CACHE_RETURN.
Replace stale upgradedn cache entries after conflict renames, release parent-cache references on hits, and log cache-owned values before releasing their entries.

In the test, wait for the concurrent reindex task to finish and require a successful exit code before performing the final checks.

Fixes: https://github.com/389ds/389-ds-base/issues/7147

Reviewed by: ?

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure DN cache entries remain valid and correctly owned during online reindexing and export operations to prevent recomposition and reuse of stale DNs.

Bug Fixes:
- Treat DN cache entries as missing only when marked unavailable so valid LRU-queued entries remain visible to lookups.
- Prevent db2index, db2ldif, and upgradedn producers from reusing cache-owned DN strings after CACHE_RETURN, avoiding use-after-free and stale DN collisions.
- Ensure parent DN caching during export/index respects existing cache entries and does not leak or double-free backdn structures.

Enhancements:
- Introduce explicit ownership of normalized DN strings in upgradedn processing and replace stale cache entries after conflict-induced renames while logging replacements.
- Adjust dncache hit handling to remove entries from the LRU list when referenced and assert that referenced entries are not still marked as LRU.
- Improve concurrent indexing regression test to wait for the reindex task to finish and validate a successful exit code before performing final modifications.

Tests:
- Extend the concurrent modifications during indexing regression test to wait for task completion and assert a zero exit code before final attribute checks.

body:
Implements [#339](https://github.com/Eliyce/paqad-ai/issues/339) beyond the Phase-1 foundation (shipped in #340). One git-ignored directory per feature (`.paqad/ledger/feature-evidence/<issue>-<slug>-<ULID>/`) becomes the whole workflow record plus the compliance bundle — plan, spec, stage evidence, rule run, delivery/git linkage, and the RAG that served it — all rigid, script-owned JSON, captured the same way on every provider.

## Phases (all complete)
- [x] **Phase 2 — re-key stage-evidence onto the feature dir.** recorder / live-writer / finalize / verify / fold / narration / marker-parse + the pre-mutation gate + the verification-repository readers resolve the active feature (`_session` control) and read/write/fold a change's rows in `<feature>/stage-evidence.jsonl`; the legacy `<session>/<ordinal>` write path is gone. New `stage start --title/--issue` + `resume --feature` verbs.
- [x] **Phase 3 — plan + spec compile.** `plan compile` builds a schema-validated `plan.json` from a filled template (transient scratch, deleted after); `spec freeze` also writes `specification.json` into the active bundle.
- [x] **Phase 4 — re-home rule-run + RAG.** Per-feature `rule-run.jsonl` + the RAG two-home router (`<feature>/rag.jsonl` vs `_chat/<session>/`, one-prompt lag).
- [x] **Phase 5 — git linkage.** Rigid `delivery.json` (branch + full commit trail + merge), native `post-commit`/`post-merge` hooks that **chain, never clobber** (husky / lefthook / `core.hooksPath`), and a local-git backfill/reconcile — driven by `paqad-ai delivery-link`, installed at onboarding.
- [x] **Phase 6 — on-demand projections.** Stage evidence is projected from the feature dirs into the SIEM `audit export` (#121) — restoring what the re-key moved out of the session-scoped layout.
- [x] **Phase 7 — export + retention + cutover.** `paqad-ai feature export` hands an auditor one feature as a self-contained document; `feature prune` is the retention policy (keeps live + N most-recent); git hooks auto-install at onboarding.

## Guarantees held at every commit
- `pnpm run ci` green (typecheck, lint, format, coverage, build).
- The `src/stage-evidence/**` **100%** coverage floor and the repo-wide 95% floor hold.
- The feature-development stage spine is preserved — storage location moved, behaviour unchanged.

## Deferred (kept safe, not a regression)
The frozen-spec sidecar under `.paqad/specs` stays alongside `specification.json` so the spec-change guard + dashboard readers keep working unchanged; fully retiring those readers (and `.paqad/plans`) is a follow-up to avoid destabilising the spine in one PR.

author: frankieramirez
body:
## Summary

Setup, settings, API-key regeneration, and plaintext-password migration now persist through a serialized, recoverable config transaction. Config values are staged in memory, configured secrets are encrypted before the single durable write, and write/configure failures restore runtime attributes, the shared parser, and the previous file before the API reports failure.

Atomic config replacement now preserves existing private modes, defaults new files to `0600`, uses exclusive same-directory temporary files, preserves legitimate `config.ini` symlink identity, and avoids predictable-temp symlink clobbering. Provider updates retain their legacy serialization contract but share the same write lock and original process-before-sequence ordering.

## Testing

- Added proof-first coverage for setup/settings write failures, token/restart preservation, scheduler ordering, encrypted-on-disk/decrypted-at-runtime secrets, API-key rollback, parser/file restoration, `SystemExit`, concurrent writers, Git-token tuple normalization, file modes, hostile temp symlinks, config symlinks, Windows permission fallbacks, and provider ordering.
- Full backend suite: 912 passed.
- Ruff lint and format checks passed.
- Startup help and lockfile checks passed.

## Scope Note

Legacy Newznab/Torznab payload normalization and embedded provider API-key encryption are unchanged and intentionally outside this PR. This change serializes that existing path without claiming a new provider-storage format.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Window/owner:** Maintainers should watch setup, settings saves, API-key rotation, and startup/config logs through the first 24 hours.
- **Healthy signals:** Successful updates survive restart, secrets remain Fernet ciphertext on disk, runtime clients continue using decrypted values, and failed writes leave the prior configuration active.
- **Watch:** Search logs for `Transactional update failed`, `Refusing unsafe config write target`, temp cleanup warnings, provider persistence errors, scheduler reconfiguration errors, and repeated setup retries.
- **Failure trigger:** Plaintext secrets appear in `config.ini`, file mode becomes broader than the prior mode, a failed save changes runtime behavior, or a valid settings update cannot survive restart.
- **Mitigation:** Revert this PR, restore the last known-good config/backup, rotate any potentially exposed credentials, and retry the setting only after filesystem ownership/permissions are corrected.

## Known Limitation

Legacy `configure()` performs some filesystem, queue, and module-global effects that cannot be rolled back with parser/file snapshots. Those effects now run only after durable persistence, and any subsequent configure failure restores the config state and file.

body:
## Summary

Group A (PRD #64), Slice A1 — the pure contest-model foundation for the per-school compliance tracker. This is the deep module every UI piece of Group A will read. **No UI, no document, no server change** — client-only, verified entirely by unit tests.

## What's in the model (`app/src/model/contest.ts`)

- **`BUILT_IN_COMPLIANCE_ITEMS`** — the 8 fixed 2025–26 handbook items with stable ids (community standards form, performance license, royalty proof, cutting permission, play approval, scenic approval, online entry, title registration). Built-ins are not editable/removable; conditionality is expressed per-school with an `na` status, never by hiding items.
- **`School.compliance`** — per-item tri-state status map (`pending` / `received` / `na`), stored on the School record so it travels through reordering, serialization, sync, and export. Absent id ⇒ Pending, so an untouched tracker is `{}` and costs nothing serialized.
- **`Contest.customComplianceItems`** — per-contest custom item defs (`{ id, label }`), defined once and applied to every school.
- **Immutable updaters** (all bump `updatedAt`): `setComplianceStatus` (writing `pending` drops the key), `addComplianceItem` (caller supplies the id — the model stays pure, no id generation), `removeComplianceItem` (drops the item's status from every school).
- **`complianceProgress(school, items) → { done, applicable, color }`** — N/A drops from the denominator; **green** when nothing applicable is still pending (all-N/A ⇒ green 0/0), **red** at zero received, **yellow** in between.
- **Schema `3 → 4`** with an append-only forward migration adding empty compliance state to every school. A pre-feature (v3) payload migrates to an all-Pending tracker.
- **`duplicateContest`** carries custom item *definitions* forward but *clears* each school's status (roll-forward starts fresh each season).

## Tests

Added to `contest.test.ts`: derivation across all states (all pending, mixed, all received, all N/A, mixed N/A, custom items), updater immutability + `updatedAt` + no-ops, custom add/remove effects on every school, state keyed to the school through rename / grow / shrink, serialize↔parse round-trip, duplicate policy, and the v3→v4 migration round-trip.

- `npm test` — 348 passed (105 in the contest suite)
- `npm run build` (tsc typecheck) — green

author: wladimirchagas
body:
## What & why

In Learn mode the world map SVG has a 960:500 viewBox and rendered at `width:100%` with `height:auto`, so its height was purely a function of the map column's width. On wide or short viewports that made the map taller than the screen and its lower edge dropped below the fold — the user had to scroll to see the whole map.

## Change

`src/pages/LearnPage.css` — cap the map SVG's height to the space left under the sticky site-topbar and the map-controls toolbar, and derive its `max-width` from that height (× the 1.92 aspect ratio) so it scales down **proportionally**:

- width-limited on tall viewports (unchanged from before),
- height-limited on wide/short viewports (the new behaviour),
- never letterboxed (max-width tracks the height cap, so no empty side bars),
- centred in the full-width map column (`margin-inline: auto`) when the height cap makes it narrower.

A `100vh` pair is declared first as a fallback, then overridden with `100dvh` so mobile browser chrome is accounted for. CSS-only; no component or data changes.

## Verification

Drove the running app with headless Chromium and measured the map's bounding box against the viewport at six sizes — the entire map is above the fold in every case:

| Viewport | Map bottom / viewport height | Result |
|----------|------------------------------|--------|
| 1440×900 | 634 / 900 | fits ✓ |
| 1920×1080 | 880 / 1080 | fits ✓ |
| 1920×720 | 706 / 720 | fits ✓ |
| 1366×768 | 607 / 768 | fits ✓ |
| 1024×720 | 476 / 720 | fits ✓ |
| 390×844 (phone) | 320 / 844 | fits ✓ |

Screenshots confirm the map renders centred and undistorted (not letterboxed) in the tightest wide/short case.

`tsc --noEmit` clean and `npm run flags:check` passes.
