🐛 Bug → 🎯 Root Cause → 🔧 Fix → ✅ Test → 🚀 Release Impact

🐛 Bug: `ghc_compiler_python/wrapper.py` was susceptible to crashes due to unhandled `OSError`s when accessing directories without permissions and silently swallowing exceptions, masking underlying issues. Also, a temporary directory leak occurred due to unbounded `tempfile.mkdtemp` calls without cleanup.
🎯 Root Cause: Naked `except ...: pass` blocks hid errors, `iterdir()` lacked `try...except OSError` handling, and `safe_home` fallback used `tempfile.mkdtemp` directly instead of a deterministic, reusable path.
🔧 Fix:
- Replaced naked `pass` blocks with `sys.stderr.write` logging for better traceability.
- Added `try...except OSError` around `iterdir()` calls.
- Replaced `tempfile.mkdtemp(...)` with `Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "ghc-compiler-python-home"` to fix the temporary directory leak.
- Updated `.jules/forge.md` to document findings and fixes.
✅ Test: Ran `PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/` which all pass. 
🚀 Release Impact: Improves stability, prevents unbounded disk usage, and enhances debugging by properly logging exceptions.

author: abanoubemhanna
body:
## Summary

`staged`/`branch`/`file` currently ship the *entire* diff to the AI provider, including lockfiles (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`), `dist/**`/`build/**` output, and minified/sourcemap files. That's pure noise for a code-review tool: it burns tokens on generated content the AI can't meaningfully review, and it dilutes the actual feedback with junk observations about lockfile diffs.

This adds ignore-pattern filtering, applied before the diff is sent to the AI provider (and before secrets would be redacted, if that lands separately — filtering happens first in the pipeline either way since this doesn't touch `packages/ai`).

- **`apps/cli/src/diff-filter.ts`** (new) — splits a unified diff into per-file blocks and drops any whose path matches an ignore pattern, using simplified `.gitignore`-style semantics: patterns without a `/` match the basename at any depth, patterns with a `/` match the full path, and `**` spans directories. Handles new files (`--- /dev/null`) and deleted files (`+++ /dev/null`) by keying off the correct side of the diff header.
- Built-in defaults apply automatically: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `*.min.js`, `*.min.css`, `*.map`, `dist/**`, `build/**`.
- **`--ignore <pattern>`** (repeatable) adds more patterns; **`--no-default-ignore`** turns off the built-ins for anyone who wants everything reviewed.
- **`.ai-reviewrc.json`** now accepts a persistent `"ignore": string[]` array, merged with the CLI flags.
- Prints which files were skipped to stderr (`⚠ Ignored N file(s) matching ignore patterns: ...`), suppressed in `--json` mode. If every file in the diff ends up excluded, fails with a friendly "No changes to review after applying ignore patterns." instead of silently calling the AI with an empty diff.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — compiles cleanly across all packages
- [x] `pnpm test` — **124/124 tests pass** (16 new in `diff-filter.test.ts`)
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean
- [x] `pnpm format:check` — clean
- [x] Manual: created a real git repo, staged changes to a normal file + `pnpm-lock.yaml` + `dist/bundle.js`; confirmed the default ignore list drops the lockfile and dist file, the stderr warning lists both, `--no-default-ignore` sends everything, and `--ignore "src.ts"` on top of the defaults filters every file down to the friendly "no changes to review" error

## Notes for reviewer

This repo currently has a large backlog of open PRs from prior sessions. I surveyed them before starting: none touch `diff-filter.ts` (new), and my only shared-file edits are additive (`config.ts` gains an optional `ignore` field, `index.ts` gains new flags/a helper function without changing existing option behavior), so this should merge without conflict against anything else outstanding. A separate note follows summarizing the state of the existing open PRs.

author: wmostert76
body:
## Summary

- start local runtime setup automatically after selecting a different model
- poll the authoritative backend status until setup reaches ready, error, or setup-required instead of leaving the frontend's optimistic `Bootstrapping` state in place
- disable setup and model-selection controls while a setup is genuinely active
- persist bootstrap errors in runtime state so a missed Tauri event still resolves to an actionable error
- clear stale setup errors on retry, model changes, and environment reset
- add a regression test proving completed setup cannot report stale `Bootstrapping`

## Problem

After switching models, the selected model was saved and the frontend could display `Bootstrapping` indefinitely even though the backend setup task had already stopped. Live reproduction showed Nemotron selected with no setup, pip, warmup, or sidecar process running. The backend correctly knew setup was required, but the frontend retained its locally assigned loading state.

Model selection also only saved the setting; users still had to press **Set up selected model** separately.

## Fix

Selecting **Use this model** now saves the choice and immediately starts setup. While setup runs, the frontend polls `get_runtime_status` every 500 ms in addition to receiving events. The polling loop exits as soon as the backend reports any non-bootstrap state.

The backend now stores the most recent setup failure. `get_runtime_status` returns:

- `Bootstrapping` only while `setup_in_progress` is actually true
- `Error` with the captured failure after an unsuccessful setup
- `Idle / Ready` after success
- `Idle / ASR environment setup required` when no setup is running and dependencies are missing

This ensures every setup path reaches a terminal UI state.

## Test plan

- `bun run build`
- `cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check`

author: rajat315315
body:
Close: #66268

**Description:**

### Description
This PR implements a homogeneous single-block fast-path in `DataFrame.dropna()`.

When the input DataFrame has exactly one block of a homogeneous NumPy dtype and no subset/threshold is specified:
1. We bypass general BlockManager validation and indexing.
2. We run direct vectorized checks on the underlying 2D NumPy array.
3. We slice the array and index/columns directly.
4. We assemble the resulting DataFrame by creating a single block and wrapping it in a BlockManager, bypassing `.loc` and `reindex_indexer` overheads.

If the DataFrame is multi-block or has custom extension arrays, it falls back to the baseline multi-block dropna implementation.

### Performance Benchmarks
Tested on float64 DataFrames (Python 3.14 / NumPy 2.5.1):

| Dimension (Rows x Columns) | Baseline (Slow Path) | Optimized (Fast Path) | Speedup |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Medium** (100 x 100) | 0.000551s | 0.000085s | **6.47x** |
| **Extremely Wide** (10 x 1000) | 0.000713s | 0.000153s | **4.65x** |
| **Wide & Short** (1000 x 500) | 0.001074s | 0.000477s | **2.25x** |
| **Tall & Narrow** (10000 x 5) | 0.000720s | 0.000376s | **1.91x** |

author: crambelsoupy
body:
Four east-ui fixes for large surfaces in a fixed-height app shell, bundled together.

## 1. Planner — bounded vertical scroll with sticky-top header (Closes #302)

Opt-in `maxHeight` (CSS): the plan body scrolls vertically within the cap with the header pinned (sticky-top), mirroring the Table's `stickyHeader`. Absent ⇒ content-sized (unchanged). Static scroll styling lives in a recipe `scroll` variant; only the dynamic cap is inline. `maxHeight` added to both Planner structs (`PlannerRootType` + the inline `UIComponentType` variant in `component.ts`). Example `plannerScroll` + `maxHeight` round-trip tests.

## 2. Schematic — memoise Slice chrome so it doesn't re-render every pan frame (Closes #305)

On a large Schematic with the Slice chrome, pan was ~600–800ms/render (measured; paint was ~0.1ms) because `setCameraSnapshot` re-renders the whole component each frame, dragging the Slice rail's live affordance components (which recompute over the whole dataset). `useSliceReactivity` now returns the slice **version**; the `<SliceRailCluster>` element is memoised on `[hasSliceChrome, sliceHandle, affordanceKinds, sliceVersion]`, so camera-only re-renders reuse the same element and React skips the O(rows) subtree. Pan render → single-digit ms. Adds a 3k slice-enabled `schematicStress` probe.

## 3. Chart — hover tooltip z-index on positioned content (Closes #307)

A Chart tooltip was painted under a sibling Table's sticky column header. visx `useTooltipInPortal` sets the z-index on the portal's `position:static` wrapper (ignored); the tooltip content was z-auto (0), so a `position:sticky` header (z 2) won. Put `zIndex` on the tooltip's own positioned content (z 1800). DOM regression guard + `tooltipOverStickyTable` example.

## 4. Chart — negative stacked columns render (Closes #308)

Stacked `Chart.Column` with negative values drew no bars: the vertical bar used `height={Math.max(0, bot - top)}`, which collapses to zero when `hi < lo`. Use `Math.min(top, bot)` + `Math.abs(bot - top)` (mirrors the horizontal bar path). `columnStackedDiverging` example (snapshot confirms both directions).

---

## Test

- `make build` / `make lint` (0 errors) / `make test` green across Planner, Schematic, and Chart suites.

## Summary

- Add a search box to the Implementation Guide that matches across pillar, objective, strategy, policy action, description, and state/local actor names in one field, and jumps straight to the matching policy solution.
- Add a "Note" callout on policy solution cards for Description text that carries real caveats (e.g. "no example yet", "private sector only", "(proposed)"), while suppressing the ~400 rows where Description just restates the state/local links already shown.
- Fix two related parsing bugs that were breaking card display: "City, State" local examples were being split into unrelated bullet fragments and mispaired with URLs, and URLs containing literal commas (Ballotpedia slugs, query strings) were being shredded into dead links.
- Fix several data quality issues found while testing the above: a typo, missing state suffixes, links filed under the wrong state, and links that were missing entirely.
- Add 5 new signatory organizations and fix the signatories list overflowing horizontally on mobile.

## Details

### Signatories
- Add 5 new organizations (BLKHLTH, Public Citizen, Urban Ocean Lab, Whole Health Consortium at Virginia Tech, Clarion Call Capital), alphabetized into the existing list.
- Fix the signatories grid overflowing horizontally on mobile by adding responsive column counts at the existing breakpoints (6 → 3 → 2 → 1 columns).

### Implementation Guide search
- Search box on the focus-area picker screen, matching across pillar, objective, strategy, policy action, description, and state/local actor names.
- Word-boundary matching so short queries (e.g. "CA") don't match substrings inside unrelated words (e.g. "vacant", "healthcare").
- Replaced a silent 20-result cap with a "Show all N results" expansion, so a legitimately broad query (e.g. a state name) isn't truncated without indication.

### Policy solution cards
- "Note" callout surfaces Description text only when it carries information beyond the state/local links already shown on the card.
- "Not applicable" text shown when a policy action has neither a state nor a local example, instead of an empty "Policy in action" block.
- Fixed Local Link Title parsing: "City, State" pairs (e.g. "Multnomah County, Oregon, New York City, New York") were being split on every comma into unrelated fragments and mispaired with URLs. Local names are now grouped by recognizing state names/abbreviations.
- Fixed Link URL parsing: URLs containing literal commas (Ballotpedia slugs, query strings) were being shredded into dead fragments. URL parts that don't start with "http" are now rejoined to the prior URL.
- When exactly one URL is given for multiple state/local names sharing a single source, that URL is now applied to every name instead of only the first.

### Policy database data fixes
- Fixed 4 rows where "State Link Title" held non-state text (a stray Description fragment, a private-sector org, a federal regulation reference) instead of an actual state name.
- Fixed "Los Angeles County, Los Angeles" typo → "Los Angeles County, California".
- Added missing "Texas" suffix to Austin/Houston/Fort Bend/Hidalgo in the school bond funding row.
- Completed/corrected the Ballotpedia bond measure URL and its city links.
- Added missing Austin Energy and LADWP rebate links (previously missing, or misfiled under the wrong state's link list).
- Moved the Louisiana emergency-declaration link, the Hennepin County link, and the Arizona resilience-office link to the correct state/local entries they were misaligned with.

author: firmantr3
body:
## Problem
When a primary Antigravity account hits quota exhaustion (429 QUOTA_EXHAUSTED,
"Individual quota reached. Resets in 160h..."), the router retried indefinitely
against the same account instead of falling back to the secondary account.

Root causes:
1. `AntigravityExecutor` had no `parseError()` method, so the precise
   `quotaResetTimeStamp` / `quotaResetDelay` from AG's error JSON was ignored.
   The account was locked for only 30 min (MAX_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS cap)
   instead of the real ~160h, causing repeated hammering after cooldown.
2. The text "Individual quota reached" didn't match any ERROR_RULES entry
   ("quota exceeded" exists, but not "quota reached" / "individual quota").
3. MAX_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS was capped at 30 min, too short for AG's weekly
   quota windows.

## Fix
- Add `parseError()` to `AntigravityExecutor` — reads `quotaResetTimeStamp`
  (ISO string) and `quotaResetDelay` (e.g. "160h19m55s") from `error.details[].metadata`,
  returns precise `resetsAtMs` (same pattern as Codex executor)
- Add `"quota reached"` and `"individual quota"` to `ERROR_RULES` text matchers
- Raise `MAX_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS` from 30 min to 7 days

Fixes #1308

author: alessiorendina
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-93742

## What Is Being Fixed

The platform ships the lazy-reference mechanism (EmptyModelManager.getOrAddEmptyModel in the export/import kernel), but no Commerce service participated, so a Commerce entity referenced by external reference code during an import could not be resolved or stub-created. Four Commerce entities already met the schema prerequisites (ERC + status columns) but were not wired: CommerceOrderType, CPInstance, CPAttachmentFileEntry, and CPConfigurationList.

## How It Is Being Fixed

getOrAddEmptyModel is wired on each of the four local services, following the AccountEntry reference implementation. Each add path branches on isEmptyModel() to persist a STATUS_EMPTY stub and skip workflow, while mandatory fields are satisfied with mutable placeholders (the external reference code as name/sku/title, the current date for display dates) rather than gating validation. The one exception is CPAttachmentFileEntry's file/CDN URL, which has no valid placeholder and is therefore gated. Each update path clears STATUS_EMPTY through solveEmptyModel when a stub is later completed, resolving its export/import report entries. EmptyModelManager is injected via @Reference. Integration tests cover the get-or-add flow (including idempotency and the normal not-found throw outside an import) and the complete-later flow for all four entities.

body:
# E2E-7 — hard-DOM fixture page + characterization suite

Follow-up to PR #31 (plan_E2E), user-directed: the fixture app covered every tool but only mainstream elements. This adds the odd DOM corners — shadow roots, iframes with weird properties, contenteditable, `<select multiple>`, inline SVG, `<canvas>`, `<details>` — and pins exactly how the tool surface behaves against each. Tests + fixtures ONLY: zero `src/` changes, zero new dependencies, zero CI changes; coverage manifest untouched (no new tools). Governed by `audit/stage2/plan_E2E.md` rules (§2.1 fixture contract, §2.6 determinism, characterize-don't-fix).

## What this adds

- **`tests/fixture_app/hard_dom.html`** — open shadow root (pinned `rgb(9, 99, 199)` internal style, logging button, named `<slot>` + slotted light-DOM span), closed shadow root (reference kept private in the app.js closure), three iframe flavors (`src=iframe_child.html`, inline `srcdoc`, and `sandbox="allow-scripts"` **without** `allow-same-origin` → opaque origin), contenteditable with pinned initial text, `<select multiple>`, inline SVG circle, deterministically-painted `<canvas>`, `<details>/<summary>` — every interactive element logs to `window.__actions` per the fixture contract.
- **`tests/fixture_app/iframe_child.html`** — self-contained child document owning its OWN `window.__actions`, so a cross-frame oracle can prove a child-side click.
- **`tests/test_e2e_hard_dom.py`** — 4 real-Chrome characterization tests (one spawn per test, `navigate_and_settle` on every navigation, bounded polls only, all `@pytest.mark.characterization`).
- Smoke-test coverage for both new pages (`test_fixture_app_server.py`); the no-external-URL + ASCII guards pick the new files up automatically via rglob.

## Findings (characterized/pinned, NOT fixed here)

| # | Finding | Kind | Where pinned | Route |
|---|---------|------|--------------|-------|
| E7-1 | **`type_text` `clear_first` cannot clear a contenteditable** — the clear path runs `elem.value = ''` (`dom_handler.py:347`), a no-op on an editable div (no meaningful `.value`); the Ctrl+A fallback (`:350-351`) only fires if that `apply()` throws, which it doesn't. author: darkviruzz
body:
Two bugs found live-testing the PR #12 rollout on the real GPU instance (server logs + bot logs cross-checked side by side).

## 1. Live transcript push was silently a no-op

`control.js`'s `serverCommand` allowlist (the switch that decides which incoming message types get forwarded via `this.emit('serverCommand', msg)`) never included `'transcript_event'`. `transport/index.js` already has a correct `case 'transcript_event': writeTranscriptEvent(...)` — but it was never reached, because `control.js` dropped the message into its `default` branch first, only logging `control: unknown msg type transcript_event`. Confirmed live: this line appeared on essentially every STT/LLM/TTS event during a real session, and no session JSONL was ever written on the bot host. Likely lost during the `transport/index.js` merge-conflict resolution mentioned in the plan doc. Fix: add `case 'transcript_event':` to the same allowlist as `chat_message` etc.

## 2. `/join`'s status message went stale after a delayed autostart

If `ensureServerReachable()` times out during `/join`, the ephemeral reply says `⚠️ Server-Start fehlgeschlagen (Timeout)` and is never touched again — but the watchdog in `transport/index.js` keeps retrying independently, and in live testing the instance came up successfully about 5 minutes later with no visible change in Discord (the stale warning just sits there). `handleServerLink` already has a correct, tested recovery-notification path (`_outage.active` tracking → a fresh ephemeral "🟢 Server wieder verbunden"), it just never triggers for "never connected in the first place" — only for "was connected, then dropped". Fix: set `_outage.active = true` at the moment we report the `/join` timeout, so the existing recovery path fires once the delayed connection succeeds, instead of adding a parallel notification mechanism.

## Separately confirmed, NOT fixed here (Phase B, needs its own PR)

Server logs also show `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/data/transcripts'` on nearly every event — this is the already-planned Phase B / C1 volume-ownership fix (`docker-entrypoint.sh` + `Dockerfile` `USER app` removal), now live-confirmed rather than just predicted. Left for its own branch per `docs/plans/fix-gpu-deployment-and-webui-merge.md`.

Verified: `node --check` on both files, full suite 117/117 green.

author: chairulakmal
body:
## Why

`conserve-main` requires the `Lint, security & test` and `Lint, typecheck & build` checks. A docs-only change had to run a full Rails suite (Brakeman, bundler-audit, RuboCop, RSpec against Postgres) and a full Next build just to report green.

## Why not `paths-ignore`

A required status check that is **skipped** stays `expected` rather than passing, and blocks the merge forever. Path-filtering the workflow trigger would have deadlocked `main` on every docs commit.

## How

Each workflow now splits into three jobs:

- **`changes`** — always runs, classifies the diff, outputs `code=true|false`
- **`verify`** — the real work; `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`
- **`gate`** — always runs (`if: always()`), owns the required context name, and reports green when `verify` succeeded **or** was skipped

`gate`'s `name:` must stay byte-identical to the ruleset's context string. Renaming it silently breaks the merge gate, so that constraint is documented in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Safety

- Unrecognised paths are treated as **code**, so the filter errs toward running CI rather than skipping it.
- A force-push or first push has no reliable base commit, so it runs everything.
- `web-ci`'s `e2e` job used `needs: check` and was updated for the `check` → `verify` rename.

Docs are `*.md`, `LICENSE`, `notes/`, and `web/public/llms.txt`. Everything else is code.

## Verification

This PR is self-testing. If `gate` is misconfigured it will not report, and the PR will be unmergeable — the failure surfaces here rather than on `main`.

Note the required checks on **this** PR run in full, because it changes `.github/workflows/`, which is code. The docs-only path is exercised by the next docs commit.

## Summary

A edição mensal 2606-07 enviada saiu com um parágrafo de apoio via Apoia.se ao lado do convite social (LinkedIn/Facebook) no bloco de encerramento — um ajuste feito manualmente direto na campanha (não no template/repo). Mesmo padrão do #2866: um ajuste de redação aprovado numa edição específica vira fonte canônica permanente.

- Extrai o texto exato aprovado pelo editor (260710, extraído do HTML enviado) para um snippet canônico `context/snippets/encerramento-social-apoio.md`, seguindo a convenção já usada por `clarice-divulgacao.md`/`livros-divulgacao.md`. Parametrizado via marcador `{{OPENING}}` — a frase de apoio ("Quem quiser apoiar a curadoria...") e o convite social (LinkedIn/Facebook) são **idênticos** nos dois formatos; só a abertura muda ("Essa edição mensal nasce da diar.ia.br..." no mensal, vazio no diário, já que a frase não faz sentido dentro do próprio diário).
- Novo loader compartilhado `scripts/lib/shared/encerramento-snippet.ts` (em `lib/shared/` por ser consumido por diário e mensal — `test/lib-boundary.test.ts`).
- **Diário**: `scripts/stitch-newsletter.ts` (determinístico, sem LLM) — `buildParaEncerrar()` agora injeta o parágrafo de apoio + convite social a partir do snippet, mantendo o cabeçalho/parágrafo de ferramentas/pills "Acesse:" existentes intocados.
- **Mensal**: `.claude/agents/writer-monthly.md` (passo 8) — instruído a ler o snippet e substituir `{{OPENING}}` pela variante mensal, **preservando** o parágrafo de encerramento padrão pré-existente ("Quer sugerir um tema...", protegido por `test/writer-monthly-prompt.test.ts` #2866) e adicionando os 2 parágrafos novos na sequência.
- Corrige o drift de nome `ENCERRAMENTO` → `PARA ENCERRAR` em `context/templates/newsletter-monthly.md` — o `writer-monthly` sempre gerou `PARA ENCERRAR` na prática (`data/monthly/2606-07/draft.md:183`); `scripts/lib/mensal/monthly-render.ts` já aceitava os dois labels (back-compat), então o rename é só documentação alcançando a realidade, sem mudança de comportamento de render.
- `scripts/lib/canonical-urls.ts`: novo `DIARIA_APOIASE_URL` + `"apoia.se"` adicionado a `FOOTER_DOMAINS` (senão o invariant `urls_accessible` do Stage 2 flagaria o link fixo como `not_in_cache`, mesmo bug do #2498 pro cursos/livros.diaria.workers.dev).

## Test plan

Regressão determinística (#633) — o bloco PARA ENCERRAR do diário é gerado por script TS (`stitch-newsletter.ts`), então é testável de ponta a ponta; o do mensal é gerado por um prompt de LLM (`writer-monthly`), coberto no padrão já estabelecido pelo #2866 (grep tests travando texto/label no arquivo-fonte) mais testes de integração passando o texto real pelos renders determinísticos (`renderEncerrar` diário, `renderEncermento` — leia-se `renderEncerramento` — mensal).

author: workofneo
body:
Two cohesive refinements to the per-style run list from #208 (stacked in one branch).

## 1. Queued vs Generating + live refresh
- Splits the in-flight state into **Queued** (accepted, waiting for the runner) vs **Generating** (rendering now) — the "system picked it up" confirmation.
- **Live auto-refresh** while any row is in flight (green **live** pill), so a row moves Queued → Generating → done with no reload. Polling stops when nothing's in flight. Plus a manual **Refresh** button.

## 2. Flag outputs whose layout changed since last render
Surface when an Output Builder layout was edited after a style's current asset was generated (`layout.updatedAt` > `asset.createdAt`) — "there's been a change and it hasn't been rerun." **Manual only, no auto/cron behavior.**
- **Non-approved** changed outputs → folded into the run set, shown as a violet **N changed** badge (Run / Run all regenerate them).
- **Approved** changed outputs → **not** auto-added; shown as a flag-only orange **N outdated** chip + a spec-level **N with outdated approved** notice, so approved work isn't blasted back into review without a deliberate rerun.

- **conftest.py** — fixtures wired to the real packs (`dummy_pack_complete/missing`, `dummy_plan`, `design_package`, real `mcp_executor`); a replay gateway keyed by work-item id with a `RECORD=1` switch (record once, replay forever); `use()`/`use_sequence()` for variant payloads. Committed hand-authored `.broken1`/`.fixed`/`.badjson` recordings drive the failure paths against the REAL compiler.
- **test_imp001.py** — real-compile suite: backend + frontend happy paths, repair loop (real fail → real pass), cap → needs_human_review, bad-JSON failure, and the pure manifest-gate check. Tests that need the sandbox are `@integration` and skip cleanly when `SANDBOX_MCP_URL` is unset.

## Résumé

Campagne **G2.3** complète : un moteur à précision pilotable par famille d'ops au runtime, un protocole pré-enregistré, et le verdict — **les 12 familles d'ops de Gemma 4 tolèrent l'arrondi bf16, individuellement ET ensemble**.

### Les 3 gates (toutes PASS, 10 juil 2026)

- **G2.3.0 — Neutralité** : refactor `PrecCfg` comptime → `PrecRt` runtime (12 familles, 1 binaire pour toutes les configs). Preuve gold : HLO `before_optimizations` **byte-identique** à la baseline pré-refactor ; D0 **1020/1020 == HF** ; non-régression G2.2 reproduite (KL 0.271×, bifurcation 96 exacte).
- **G2.3.1 — Sweep one-hot** : **12/12 familles SAFE** (toutes ≤ 0.14× l'enveloppe HF-bf16). Classement : softcap (la plus sensible — dernière op avant les logits) > norms > mlp > … > softmax (la moins sensible). L'oracle anti-câblage-croisé (comptage de converts HLO) finit **12/12 exact**.
- **G2.3.2 — Config combinée** : **les 12 familles ensemble = SAFE à 0.486× l'enveloppe** (critère ≤ 2×, passé au 1er essai). Interaction quasi-additive (D\*/somme = 1.06×). Stabilité S49 : ordre des rangs conservé. VRAM kv_store : −17 MiB = exactement ½ cache (protocole G2.1).

### Découvertes

1. **Déduplication de nœuds au traçage ZML** : deux `convert` du même tenseur émettent UN nœud (établie empiriquement 4 points de données, réconciliation du recensement D0 à l'unité) — règle d'émission non documentée jusqu'ici.
2. **Dédup inter-familles norms×ple** : un nœud partagé unique, localisé par bisection exhaustive + diff de signatures, consigné dans `_interfamily_dedups` (appliqué indépendamment par les scripts 52 et 53).
3. **Le bit-à-bit n'existe pas entre deux compiles XLA-GPU** (autotuning) — critère de déterminisme pré-enregistré réfuté et publié tel quel ; bruit compile-à-compile ~2 % (grands effets) à ~16 % (petits effets).
4. **kv_store bf16 quasi-gratuit** (0.0079× l'enveloppe) — la donnée clé pour TurboQuant.

### Discipline

Protocole **pré-enregistré avant tout run** (`docs/G2_3_OP_SENSITIVITY.md`) : métriques, seuils (source normative = manifest non-arrondi), directions KL, gates par run (sanité/non-vacuité/anti-câblage), procédure d'échec du combiné. Les runs INVALID d'investigation restent au manifest (trace auditable). Constats d'honnêteté consignés : seuils de sanité non-mordants sur S46, valeurs de première compile vs re-runs upsertés.

### Contenu

- `engine.zig` : `PrecRt` runtime + wrappers d'arrondi aux bornes (GEMM/norms/softmax/rope/softcap/kv_store) + `Cache.checkDtype`
- `gemma4_g23_sweep.zig` : runner unique (familles par argv) ; l'ex-runner G2.2 supprimé après le PASS de non-régression
- `scripts/52_g2_3_analyze.py` (métriques/verdicts/custody/manifest, selfcheck M1), `53_g2_3_hlo_check.py` (delta converts pré-opt), `g2_3_sweep.sh` (orchestrateur durci)

body:
## What changed

The three bottom-right HUD action buttons (Gear/Satchel/Trades) were floating as individual chips with no visual grouping. Each button already uses `WyrdUi.style_kit_button()` and trade-tinted fonts, but there was nothing tying them together as a single crafted piece — unlike the hotbar, which sits on `HotbarTray`.

This PR adds **`ActionTrayArt`**, a new inner `Control` class in `player_hud.gd` that draws a carved wooden plank behind the action button row.

## Why it reads as more artistic

The improvement brings the action bar into the same visual family as the hotbar tray:

| Element | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Background | None — buttons float against the world | Carved parchment-wood plank |
| Depth | Flat | Soft drop shadow + honey-lit top bevel |
| Texture | None | Sparse parchment grain (seed 37) |
| Border | None | Ink border + burnished-gold inner inset |
| Ornament | None | `── ◆ ──` flourish at each end |

## Reference

Moves toward the **`hud2_cradle_3`** reference: grouped, framed, crafted-looking HUD elements that sit *on* the world rather than floating flat in it. The hotbar tray already uses this language; the action bar now speaks the same dialect.

## Implementation

- **`player_hud.gd`, `_build_action_bar()`**: instantiates `ActionTrayArt`, anchors it to the bottom-right corner (8 px wider/taller than the button `HBoxContainer` on each side), adds it to the CanvasLayer *before* the bar so it renders behind the buttons.
- **`ActionTrayArt extends Control`**: pure `_draw()` — shadow, plank face, top/bottom bevel, `WyrdUi.draw_parchment_grain`, ink border, gold inset, end flourishes. No textures in `_draw` (avoids the white-rect gotcha).

39 lines added, 0 deleted. No logic, interaction, or data changes.

## Tests

Godot is not installed in this cloud environment. The change is purely additive (one new inner class, one `add_child` before the existing bar). All four test suites (`test_wyrd_loop`, `test_wyrd_dungeon_scene`, `test_wyrd_transitions`, `test_skills`) are unaffected — they exercise game logic and the hotbar dispatch path, not the HUD action bar layout.

## What changed

- adds `skills/LOOP-21-merge-protocol.md`, a complete 14-node Merge Protocol specification
- composes the five meta-loops (LOOP-16 through LOOP-20) with LOOP-08, LOOP-11, and LOOP-15 hard gates
- defines immutable remote/PR capture, a junior-readable simplicity goal, adversarial review, one-change ratcheting, real CI-liveness proof, SHA-locked operator-approved merge, whole-trunk post-merge replay, and a scoped follow-up PR decision
- updates the README catalog from 20 to 21 loops and adds the Merge Protocol usage chain

## Why

A PR should not be considered complete merely because its isolated diff is green. This protocol preserves the original PR state and goals as an immutable oracle, prevents stale-base/head merges, and replays that contract against the entire integrated default branch so cross-file regressions and missing seams become explicit follow-up work.

The spec preserves each source loop's authority boundary. In particular, LOOP-15 can improve procedural memory only; application changes serialize through LOOP-18 and require evidence before they are welded.

## Impact

This is documentation/specification only. It adds no runtime dependency and changes no existing loop contract. Operators gain a runnable merge lifecycle that defaults to minimal, organized, working code understandable by a junior developer while retaining explicit merge and follow-up approval gates.

author: stubbi
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Mitos boots Firecracker microVMs from a pool template snapshot. When a pool's template CONTENT changes, `poolBuildIdentity` changes and the controller rebuilds the snapshot; while it is rebuilding, the pool does not serve its warm husk pods.
> - Bumping the hosted `python` pool's base image (to ship the run_code kernel PRNG reseed, #882) took production down for about twenty minutes. Every rebuild attempt failed with `create tap sbtap-template: ip: exit status 1: ioctl(TUNSETIFF): Device or resource busy`, the pool reported `TemplateBuilt=False/BuildFailed`, and every create went Pending and timed out.
> - Root cause 1: EVERY template build binds its placeholder NIC to the SAME tap, the constant `sbtap-template`. A build that pulls and unpacks an image takes minutes, while the controller re-reconciles the pool every ~20 seconds and calls `CreateTemplate` again. The second call raced the first over that one tap.
> - Root cause 2: forkd's `network.setup` creates the tap without removing a leftover one first, so a build or fork that died before its deferred teardown ran poisons the node permanently. The husk egress path has done delete-before-create since #428; forkd's had not.
> - This pull request derives the placeholder tap per template id, adds an in-flight guard so a template cannot race itself, and makes forkd's tap creation idempotent.
> - The benefit is that a template rebuild, which is the normal response to any pool content edit, stops being able to wedge a pool permanently.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

No issue existed. Production incident, 2026-07-10.

**Observed** (controller, once per reconcile, indefinitely):

```
failed to build template snapshot for husk pool (warm pool still maintained)
error: build template snapshot python: node mitos-kvm-1: rpc error: code = Internal
desc = create placeholder tap for template python: create tap sbtap-template:
ip: exit status 1: ioctl(TUNSETIFF): Device or resource busy
```

On the node, `sbtap-template` was present and held by a stranded template-build firecracker (`--id python`).

**Expected:** a template rebuild converges.
**Actual:** it never converged, and because a rebuilding pool serves no warm husk pods, `POST /v1/fork` returned `the sandbox did not become ready within 2m0s; it is still Pending` for every caller.

Recovery was: roll the pool image back, `ip link del sbtap-template` inside the forkd pod, wait for the build to converge.

Related: #428 (the same `EBUSY` poisoning, fixed on the husk egress path).

## What Changed

- `firecracker.PlaceholderTapNameFor(id)` replaces the `PlaceholderTapName` constant. `sbtap-t` plus 8 hex characters of `sha256(id)` is exactly 15 characters, the kernel's interface-name cap.
- `fork.Engine.CreateTemplate` holds an in-flight guard keyed by template id (`sync.Map`), and returns the typed `ErrTemplateBuildInProgress` to a second concurrent caller. A DIFFERENT template is never blocked.
- The daemon maps that error to gRPC `Unavailable`, a retry-later signal, instead of flattening it to `Internal`. Reporting `BuildFailed` on every re-reconcile while a slow build was still working is what made the pool flap.
- `network.setup` removes a leftover tap of the same name before creating it, best effort. This is safe precisely because of the two changes above: a tap of that name is now a leak, never a live peer (template builds cannot race themselves, sandbox taps are per sandbox).
- `placeholderNetIdentity(templateID)` and the orphan-build reaper follow.

## Verification

- [x] `go test -race ./internal/fork/ -count=1`
- [x] `go test ./internal/network/ ./internal/firecracker/ ./internal/daemon/ -count=1`
- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `golangci-lint run --timeout=8m` on those four trees, and again with `GOOS=linux`. The two `gofmt` reports (`internal/fork/childmemfd.go`, `internal/daemon/expose_conn_test.go`) and the darwin-only `testBit is unused` are pre-existing on main and untouched here.

New tests, each of which fails on the unfixed code:

- `TestCreateTemplateRefusesAConcurrentBuildOfTheSameTemplate`: the second concurrent build of one template gets `ErrTemplateBuildInProgress`; a different template is not blocked; the guard is released when the build returns.
- `TestSetupRemovesALeftoverTapBeforeCreatingIt`: the first command is the link delete.
- `TestSetupSurvivesADeleteOfAnAbsentTap`: on a clean node the delete finds nothing, which is the normal case and must never fail the setup.
- `TestPlaceholderTapNameForIsPerTemplateAndFitsIFNAMSIZ`: per template, deterministic, and within the 15-character cap.

The existing `network_apply_test.go` sequence assertions are updated to include the delete, so the exact command order stays pinned rather than loosened.

## Risks

`internal/fork`, `internal/firecracker`, and `internal/daemon` are security-sensitive paths per CLAUDE.md and **need a named human reviewer before merge**.

The delete-before-create is the change to scrutinise: it removes a host interface by name before creating it. It is safe only because the tap name uniquely identifies its owner. Template builds now take a per-template name AND cannot race themselves; sandbox taps are already per sandbox. So a tap of that name at setup time is a leak from a dead owner. This is the same reasoning, and the same fix, as the husk egress path in #428.

A second concurrent build now returns an error where it previously proceeded and corrupted the first build's tap. Callers that relied on that (there are none; the controller retries) would see `Unavailable`.

Not covered here: a build that dies mid-flight still leaks its firecracker process until the build journal reaps it (#469). That leak no longer wedges the pool, because the next build removes the tap and takes a name of its own, but it is worth a follow-up.

## Model Used

- Claude Opus 4.8 (`claude-opus-4-8`), 1M context, extended thinking.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title is a conventional commit (feat, fix, docs, ci, chore, refactor, test)
- [x] Thinking Path traces from project context to this change
- [x] Model Used is filled in (with version and capability details)
- [x] Tests added for behavior changes, in the same commit (TDD)
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR
- [x] Threat-model delta (docs/threat-model.md) included if the security surface moved
- [x] Benchmark run (bench/) included if the hot path was touched
- [x] No em or en dashes introduced anywhere
- [x] Secret values never logged, in errors, in condition messages, or on host paths
- [x] No internal/instance-local references (only public `#NNN` / mitos-run/mitos URLs)
- [x] Every commit carries a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`git commit -s`)

author: jorgensandhaug
body:
# Fate-isolate the Connected Machine supervisor from host-work OOM (per-op cgroups)

Closes part of #345.

## Problem

The control supervisor (heartbeat + `ping`) and every native `exec` descendant
share ONE systemd service cgroup. On a swapless host under memory pressure,
`systemd-oomd` — or the kernel OOM killer — selects that cgroup and SIGKILLs the
whole unit, taking the supervisor down with a runaway command. Bounded concurrency
is not resource-aware and gives no process/cgroup **fate** isolation.

## What this PR does (Linux cgroup v2 only)

The least-privileged mechanism the issue asks us to choose: **per-op memory
sub-cgroups under a user-or-system-delegated service cgroup**, plus an
unprivileged `oom_score_adj` bias. No root, no `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE`, no new
privileged helper.

1. **Unit template hardening** (`service.rs`). Both the user and system systemd
   units now render `Delegate=yes`, `ManagedOOMPreference=avoid`, and
   `MemoryHigh=75%`. Delegation gives us a writable subtree; `ManagedOOMPreference`
   biases `systemd-oomd` away from a whole-unit kill; `MemoryHigh` throttles under
   sustained pressure and turns on the memory accounting the sub-cgroups need.
2. **Per-op sub-cgroup module** (`cgroup.rs`). At startup the agent runs the
   cgroup v2 no-internal-processes dance — move itself into a `<service>/supervisor`
   leaf, then enable the memory controller in `<service>/cgroup.subtree_control`.
   Each `exec` then places its child **and** the #344 process-group anchor into a
   fresh `<service>/op-<n>` memory leaf (optional `memory.max`/`memory.high` from
   `OPENGENI_AGENT_OP_MEMORY_MAX`/`_HIGH`, default unset). The leaf is `rmdir`'d
   once the process tree is reaped, tolerating a transient `EBUSY` with a bounded
   retry; a leaked empty leaf is cosmetic and reclaimed on the next unit stop.
3. **`oom_score_adj`** (`cgroup.rs` + `native.rs`). Every exec child is stamped
   `oom_score_adj=500` post-spawn (inherited by descendants on fork), so even the
   kernel's GLOBAL OOM killer sacrifices a runaway child before the supervisor,
   which stays at its default. This composes with (2) and works even when cgroup
   delegation is unavailable.

**Fallback ladder — never fail to serve.** Not Linux, no cgroup v2, the memory
controller not delegated, or any `EPERM`/IO error: the reason is logged **once**
and the agent keeps serving exactly as before (all work in the service cgroup, no
per-op isolation). Isolation being unavailable must never stop the agent answering
control RPCs.

## Which #345 invariants this PR satisfies

- **"Accepted native work cannot make the supervisor an OOM victim merely because
  it shares the service cgroup."** — Satisfied: per-op memory leaves + a dedicated
  supervisor leaf + the `oom_score_adj` bias.
- **"Each request has enforceable memory limits or an equivalently isolated work
  scope; one request cannot consume the supervisor budget."** — Satisfied: each
  exec runs in its own memory leaf (optional hard cap), and the supervisor's own
  leaf is never in that scope.
- **"Deadline/cancellation cleanup (#343) remains complete across the new scope
  boundary."** — Satisfied: the op leaf holds the child + the #344 anchor (one PGID
  tree, one memory fate); teardown runs on normal completion, timeout, and cancel,
  and the #344 group-kill is unchanged.
- **"Restart/reconnect semantics and enrollment identity remain unchanged."** —
  Satisfied: establish is a startup-only, pre-serve step; connect/hello/epoch and
  enrollment are untouched; the fallback keeps the agent serving.
- **"Cross-platform behavior is explicit."** — Satisfied: **Linux-only** guarantee.
  macOS/Windows are a documented no-op (`establish_oom_isolation` returns `None`,
  no cgroup is touched, `oom_score_adj` is skipped).
- **"Structured diagnostics without logging command contents."** — The isolation
  lifecycle (establish result, once-logged fallback reasons, teardown) is
  structured `tracing`; no command contents are ever logged.

## Explicitly complementary (NOT in this PR)

`#345` also asks for resource-aware **admission** (typed retryable backpressure
before starting work when a supervisor reserve / machine budget would be violated)
and heartbeat **metric fields** (admission rejections, cgroup peaks). Those are a
separate lever: admission is enforced in the supervisor's work pool, and new metric
fields would touch the shared wire proto. This PR builds the isolation substrate
they sit on; it does not add or change admission or the metrics proto.

## Rollout note (from the unit change)

Existing installs keep their **old** unit file until it is re-rendered — the new
`Delegate=yes` / `MemoryHigh=` directives only take effect after
`opengeni-agent service install` re-renders the unit (and `systemctl daemon-reload`
+ restart). The rollout runbook must refresh the unit on already-enrolled service
installs. Follow-up: teach `self-update` to refresh the unit automatically.

Until the unit is re-rendered, the agent still runs safely: on a unit without
`Delegate=yes` the memory controller is not delegated, `establish_oom_isolation`
logs the reason once and returns `None`, and the agent serves with today's behavior
plus the always-on `oom_score_adj` bias (which needs no delegation).

## Linux-only guarantee

Per the issue's cross-platform requirement: the cgroup dance and `oom_score_adj`
are Linux cgroup v2 features. On macOS/Windows this PR is a compile-time no-op and
promises nothing; the systemd directives are inert on the launchd/SCM backends.

## Tests + verification

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt
  --check`: clean. Full workspace `cargo test`: green.
- Unit tests: renderer snapshots assert the OOM directives are in `[Service]` for
  both scopes; cgroup path-derivation / `/proc/self/cgroup` parsing / controller
  parsing / config-from-env / fallback helpers.
- `oom_score_adj`: a Linux test runs a real exec and reads the child's live
  `/proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj == 500` (no cgroup delegation required).
- Env-gated integration test (`tests/cgroup_placement.rs`): runs the real startup
  dance + a real exec and asserts the child lands in an `op-<n>` leaf with
  `oom_score_adj=500` while the supervisor stays in `supervisor/`. It self-skips
  loudly unless the process is the sole member of a delegated cgroup v2 service
  cgroup (normal `cargo test` / CI skip without mutating anything).

### Live evidence (delegated `systemd-run --user --scope`)

Integration test, run alone in a delegated scope:

```
supervisor (this process) cgroup: .../run-<scope>.scope/supervisor
exec child <pid> cgroup:          .../run-<scope>.scope/op-0
exec child <pid> oom_score_adj:   500
```

Real `opengeni-agent run` binary, run in a delegated scope, at startup:

```
INFO established per-op OOM cgroup isolation: host execs run in memory sub-cgroups;
     the control supervisor is fate-isolated in its own leaf
     service_cgroup=.../oom-verify-agent-<pid>.scope memory_max=None memory_high=None
# and the agent process's own cgroup:
0::/.../oom-verify-agent-<pid>.scope/supervisor
```

author: rasros
body:
## What

Previously `run_vector_search` called `storage.initialize()` (which creates the `<name>/runs/<timestamp>/nodes/` output tree) *before* loading the reference image. A missing or corrupt input therefore left an empty project directory behind on every failed invocation.

Now the image is loaded and validated first; `storage.initialize()` only runs once the input is known-good. On failure, nothing is written to disk.

`_load_image` is also hardened to distinguish the two failure modes:
- missing path → `FileNotFoundError` (rendered by `main.py` as `Error: input image not found: <path>`)
- exists but not decodable → `ValueError: input image could not be read as an image: <path> (...)` (rendered as a clean `Error:` line)

Together with PR #5 this closes the missing-image handling: clean message *and* no stray directories.

## Tests

Added two fast tests (no LLM/workers reached, so unmarked) asserting a missing path raises `FileNotFoundError` and a corrupt file raises `ValueError`, and that in both cases `storage.project_dir` is never created. Full suite: 363 passed.

body:
## What does this PR do?

The persistent Telegram polling heartbeat (`_polling_heartbeat_loop`) did not recognize python-telegram-bot (PTB) `NetworkError` or `TimedOut` exceptions as connectivity failures. These PTB exceptions inherit from `TelegramError`, not `OSError`, so the existing handler `(asyncio.TimeoutError, OSError)` missed them. A broad `except Exception` block subsequently swallowed these errors silently, preventing the gateway from detecting and recovering dead TCP connections.

This fix extracts the reconnect trigger logic into a helper and explicitly checks for PTB `NetworkError` / `TimedOut` in the exception handler, routing them to the existing reconnect ladder. Non-connectivity PTB errors (e.g., `BadRequest`, `InvalidToken`) remain swallowed as before.


## Related Issue

Fixes #62047


## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)


## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: Modified `_polling_heartbeat_loop` to catch and handle `telegram.error.NetworkError` and `telegram.error.TimedOut` as connectivity failures. Added a local helper `_trigger_reconnect` to deduplicate the reconnect scheduling logic.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_network_reconnect.py`: Added regression tests for PTB `NetworkError`, `TimedOut` (trigger reconnect) and `BadRequest` (ignore).


## How to Test

1. Run the new regression tests: `pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_network_reconnect.py::test_heartbeat_loop_triggers_reconnect_on_ptb_network_error tests/gateway/test_telegram_network_reconnect.py::test_heartbeat_loop_triggers_reconnect_on_ptb_timed_out tests/gateway/test_telegram_network_reconnect.py::test_heartbeat_loop_ignores_ptb_bad_request`
2. Run the full Telegram network reconnect test suite to ensure existing behavior is preserved: `pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_network_reconnect.py`
3. Observed result: All 3 new tests pass, confirming that PTB `NetworkError` and `TimedOut` now trigger `_handle_polling_network_error` (task created), while `BadRequest` does not. Existing tests for `OSError` and `asyncio.TimeoutError` continue to pass.

## Regression

v0.13.0 (#38) switched `FitnessRule.enumerate_files` to git-tracked enumeration filtered by `is_in_scope`. But `is_in_scope` with EMPTY `roots` matches on extension alone (scans everything), whereas the pre-v0.13.0 loop over `self._roots` enumerated **nothing** for empty roots. So a check run with no config (`run_core_check` → `config=None` → empty class-default roots) went from scanning nothing to scanning the whole repo.

This broke taz's `tests/fitness/test_run_checks.py::test_gate_runs_a_passing_check_and_returns_clean`, which dispatches `no_duplicate_string` as a subprocess **without** its config — clean under v0.12.0, failing under v0.13.0. The real gate (which passes `roots=["scripts","tools"]`) was never affected.

## Fix

`enumerate_files` guards at the top: `if not self._roots: return []` — restoring the contract that the default enumeration over empty roots yields nothing (scan-by-extension-alone requires a configured root or an `enumerate_files` override). The #25 tracked-only behavior is preserved for configured-roots checks.

## Tests

- New `test_empty_roots_enumerate_nothing` guards the regression.
- The two #25 tests that used empty-roots `NoLlmAttribution` now use the explicit `roots=("",)` scan-all idiom (same as `readme_resolver_coverage`), exercising the identical git-tracked path with 100% of their detection intent intact.

author: eichhorl
body:
https://github.com/dfinity/ic/pull/10897 added the infrastructure for delivering initial and asynchronous HTTP outcalls refunds to the DSM. For now, only initial refunds are delivered.

This PR implements the DSM side, which is responsible for:
1. Updating the context's `RefundStatus` based on the delivered refunds
2. Crediting the refunded cycles to the calling canister of the HTTP outcall
3. Reporting the amount of cycles spent (both normal and free subnets) as a metric.

The refund lifecycle of an HTTP context happens after a response to the canister was delivered: When a response is delivered, the context is removed from `canister_http_request_contexts`. If the context uses pay-as-you-go pricing, then the context is instead re-inserted into the `delivered_canister_http_request_contexts` collection.

Refunds may only be applied for contexts residing in the latter collection, which is why it happens at the end of the execution round.

While the context is in `delivered_canister_http_request_contexts`, delivered refunds may be applied, respecting the following invariants:
1. Initial refunds must be applied first, while `refunding_nodes` is still empty. 
2. A node may not issue refunds multiple times.
3. Collectively, not more than `refundable_cycles = committee_size * per_replica_allowance` may be refunded.

After a timeout of 2 minutes (after the original context was created), contexts in `delivered_canister_http_request_contexts` time out, and refund the full allowance for all replicas that haven't responded so far.

author: mangelajo
body:
## Summary

Remove the `off()` calls from `reset()` and `close()` in `DutlinkPower` and `DutlinkStorageMux`.

## Problem

Depending on the hardware configuration, DUTLink power control USB transfers can block for **15-20+ seconds**. Since `reset()` is called at lease start and `close()` at lease end, this means up to ~40 seconds of exporter blocking per lease cycle just for implicit power-off operations — even when the device is already off or the user is about to power it on.

## Solution

Remove the implicit `off()` from both lifecycle methods. Power and storage mux state management becomes the responsibility of:

- **The user** — via explicit `power.off()` / `storage.off()` calls during their session
- **The admin** — via pre/post lease hooks (e.g. `j power off` in an `afterLease` hook)

This is consistent with how other hardware drivers already behave — they don't implicitly power off on lease boundaries.

## Changes

- `DutlinkPower`: removed `reset()` and `close()` overrides (both just called `self.off()`)
- `DutlinkStorageMux`: removed `reset()` and `close()` overrides (both just called `self.off()`)

The base `Driver.reset()` / `Driver.close()` methods still run (recursing into children), but since these sub-drivers have no children of their own, it's effectively a no-op.

body:
Mechanical bump to [midi-access-kit v0.3.0](https://github.com/ragb/midi-access-kit/releases/tag/v0.3.0), which widens the `Device::store` hook:

```diff
-fn store(dest: &str, ch: u8) -> Option<Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceError>>
+fn store(area: &str, doc: &Value, dest: &str, ch: u8) -> Option<Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceError>>
```

The extra params exist for **copy-to-slot** devices (Roland RE-202: no save command, volatile edit buffer, so committing means re-writing the document's bytes to the slot address). The CK is a **command-store** device — `Store-To-Flash` commits its own edit buffer — so it ignores `area`/`doc`.

No behaviour change. `store_to_flash_frames_match_capture` (byte-exact vs the Melas editor capture) still passes; schema regeneration shows no drift.

author: zeta-develop
body:
## Resumen Ejecutivo
Se realizó una auditoría del proyecto detectando un problema de escalabilidad en los módulos de clientes, préstamos y pagos, donde se utilizaba `.select()` sin paginación en tablas transaccionales, trayendo todos los registros a memoria para filtrarlos en el cliente. Se ha implementado la paginación del lado del servidor para el módulo de Clientes como primer paso seguro para establecer la arquitectura estándar.

## Hallazgos
- `src/app/clientes/page.tsx` obtenía todos los clientes sin límite y los filtraba en memoria.
- `src/services/databaseService.ts` carecía de un método de paginación para clientes.

## Riesgos
- Potencial impacto en rendimiento y costos de Supabase si el volumen de clientes aumenta significativamente.
- Retrasos en la UI durante la carga inicial.

## Arquitectura Objetivo
- Toda consulta a tablas transaccionales debe utilizar paginación y búsqueda del lado del servidor (`.range()` y `.ilike()`).
- Implementar debounce para minimizar las llamadas a la API durante las búsquedas.

## Solución implementada
1. Se creó el hook `useDebounce` en `src/hooks/useDebounce.ts`.
2. Se agregó el método `getPaginated` en `clienteService` (`src/services/databaseService.ts`) que delega el conteo, búsqueda y paginación a Supabase.
3. Se refactorizó `src/app/clientes/page.tsx` para utilizar `useDebounce`, controles de paginación y el nuevo método del servicio.

## Validación
- Se ejecutó `pnpm run build` y `pnpm run lint` validando que la aplicación compile correctamente sin errores de React hooks.
- Asegurados los filtros por `user_id` para cumplir con las reglas de Multi-Tenant.

## Recomendaciones y Próximos Pasos
- Aplicar el mismo patrón a `src/app/prestamos/page.tsx` y `src/app/pagos/page.tsx`.

author: jholt1988
body:
## Summary
Now that #90 registers `OrgContextGuard` as a global `APP_GUARD`, listing it in each controller's `@UseGuards()` is redundant — it would run twice per request. This PR removes the per-controller `OrgContextGuard` and its now-unused imports.

## 🔗 Stacked on #90 — merge after it
This PR is **based on the `fix/global-org-context-guard` branch (#90)**, not `main`, because the removal is only safe once the global guard exists. GitHub will auto-retarget the base to `main` when #90 merges. **Do not merge before #90** — otherwise these controllers would lose org-context resolution entirely.

## Scope (heads-up: 62 controllers, not ~20)
The redundant guard was on **62 controllers** (124 `@UseGuards` occurrences) — more than the rough “~20” estimate. All usages were uniform, which made this a safe mechanical change:
- Two shapes only, both with `OrgContextGuard` **last**: `@UseGuards(AuthGuard('jwt'), RolesGuard, OrgContextGuard)` and `@UseGuards(AuthGuard('jwt'), OrgContextGuard)`.
- Every occurrence also had `AuthGuard`; imports were all standalone.

## What changed
- Strip `, OrgContextGuard)` → `)` in every `@UseGuards()` (so `AuthGuard`/`RolesGuard` are always preserved).
- Delete the now-unused `import { OrgContextGuard } ...` line in each file.
- **`@OrgId()` usages are untouched** — they read `req.org`, which the global guard still populates.

author: paulareixach
body:
## Objetivo

Rediseñar el flujo de añadir restaurante para dejarlo listo para una experiencia de producto final, conseguir que los restaurantes creados manualmente aparezcan correctamente en Mapa y permitir una foto de portada opcional por restaurante.

## Diseño final

- Nueva implementación de pantalla desacoplada de la ruta de Expo para facilitar mantenimiento y revisión.
- Interfaz compactada para pantallas Android reales: menos altura en cabecera, grupo, titular, pestañas, tarjetas, campos y botones.
- Tarjeta contextual con el grupo de destino, imagen real y fallback seguro.
- Selector `Buscar | Manual` compacto y con estado activo claro.
- Placeholders breves que no se cortan (`Ej. Kaizen Sushi`, `Ej. Palma`).
- Iconos Material Icons para evitar glifos rotos o inconsistentes en Android.
- Variantes compactas reutilizables para `FormField` y `PrimaryButton`.
- Acción final fija sobre la navegación inferior cuando existe algo guardable.

## Buscar

- Formulario reducido a una sola tarjeta compacta.
- Nombre, ciudad opcional y acción principal visibles antes del primer scroll.
- Resultados con miniaturas, dirección, categoría y selección visible.
- Atajo responsive `¿No aparece? · Añadir manual`.
- Notas, foto opcional y guardado aparecen únicamente después de seleccionar un restaurante.

## Manual

- Flujo organizado en tres pasos claros:
  1. `Datos básicos`: foto de portada opcional, nombre y categoría.
  2. `Ubicación`: dirección, ciudad, país, geocodificación y mapa.
  3. `Notas del grupo`.
- Dirección, ciudad y país quedan dentro de Ubicación.
- Botones compactos para buscar dirección, usar la posición actual o elegir el punto en el mapa.
- Previsualización del mapa y estado de ubicación confirmada.
- Guardado desactivado hasta disponer de nombre y coordenadas válidas.

## Foto de portada

- Una única portada opcional y global para el restaurante, no específica de cada grupo.
- Se puede elegir desde la galería, hacer una foto, cambiarla o retirarla antes de guardar.
- Recorte `4:3`, compresión desde el cliente y límite de 5 MB.
- Si la subida de la foto falla, el restaurante permanece creado y se informa del error para evitar duplicados al reintentar.
- La portada se expone en las respuestas de restaurante y de mapa.
- Las tarjetas de grupo y las tarjetas del mapa prefieren la imagen real; si no existe, mantienen el fallback actual.
- Endpoints:
  - `PUT /groups/{groupId}/restaurants/{groupRestaurantId}/image`
  - `DELETE /groups/{groupId}/restaurants/{groupRestaurantId}/image`
  - `GET /restaurants/{restaurantId}/image`
- La lectura de imágenes es pública y cacheable; las modificaciones requieren permisos de gestión del restaurante dentro del grupo.
- Migración `V102__add_restaurant_cover_images.sql` para `restaurants.image_url` y `restaurant_images`.

## Ubicación de restaurantes manuales

- Endpoint `GET /restaurants/geocode` para localizar direcciones mediante Nominatim/OpenStreetMap.
- El cliente de Nominatim reutiliza la caché y el límite global de una petición por segundo ya existentes.
- Si se modifica dirección, ciudad o país después de confirmar, la ubicación se invalida para evitar guardar coordenadas antiguas.
- El payload manual envía `latitude` y `longitude`, por lo que el restaurante entra automáticamente en `/restaurants/map` y aparece en Mapa.

## Validación pendiente

- [ ] `cd backend && mvn clean test`
- [ ] `cd mobile && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] Abrir desde `Buscar restaurante` y confirmar que inicia en Buscar.
- [ ] Abrir desde `Añadir manualmente` y confirmar que inicia en Manual.
- [ ] Buscar un restaurante, seleccionarlo, añadir portada y guardarlo.
- [ ] Crear un restaurante manual con foto de galería.
- [ ] Crear un restaurante manual haciendo una foto con la cámara.
- [ ] Cambiar y retirar la foto antes de guardar.
- [ ] Probar JPG, PNG, WEBP y una imagen superior a 5 MB.
- [ ] Confirmar que el restaurante sigue creado si falla únicamente la subida de portada.
- [ ] Confirmar que la portada aparece en la tarjeta del grupo y en la ficha seleccionada del mapa.
- [ ] Confirmar que sin foto se mantienen los fallbacks actuales.
- [ ] Buscar una dirección manual y elegir uno de los resultados.
- [ ] Usar la ubicación actual con permiso concedido y denegado.
- [ ] Elegir un punto manualmente, mover el marcador y confirmarlo.
- [ ] Modificar dirección o ciudad tras confirmar y comprobar que obliga a reconfirmar.
- [ ] Crear un restaurante manual y confirmar que aparece en Mapa.
- [ ] Revisar el footer fijo con teclado abierto y cerrado.
- [ ] Probar errores de búsqueda, geocodificación, duplicado y subida de imagen.
- [ ] Aprobación visual final de Paula.

La PR permanece en draft y no debe fusionarse sin aprobación expresa.

body:
Fixes #136, fixes #137. Both bugs surfaced while shooting README screenshots on production.

## Demo seed amounts (#136)

`DemoDataSeeder` multiplied totals by 100, but JPY has no minor unit — `amount_cents` stores whole yen (see `frontend/src/shared/lib/format.ts`, `docs/development/naming-conventions.md`). The demo document list showed ¥149,300,000 where the generated PDF said ¥1,493,000.

- Store `$total` as-is with a comment pinning the convention.
- The line generator already yields a realistic received-invoice band (¥33,000–¥3,300,000, 1–2 lines of ¥33k–¥1,650k), consistent with the invoice/deal demo world — no value redesign needed.
- `DemoSeedLifecycleTest` now asserts MIN/MAX `amount_cents` stay inside that band; a reintroduced ×100 blows the upper bound on every row.

## Upload dialog hint (#137)

`document.upload.file_hint` rendered its `{{max_size_mb}}` placeholder literally because `DocumentUploadModal` passed no interpolation params.

- Authoritative limit: backend `NENE_VAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB` (default 20, `DocumentServiceProvider`). Mirrored into frontend config as `env.uploadMaxFileSizeMb` (`VITE_NENE_VAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB`, default 20, zod-validated) and passed to `t()`.
- New `DocumentUploadModal.test.tsx` pins the rendered hint (contains "20 MB", never "{{").
- Documented the new env var in `docs/terms.md` §20.

## Cross-check for the same bug class

Audited every `{{…}}` key in `locales/ja.json` / `locales/en.json` (the only two locales) against all `t()` call sites, static and template-literal: `file_hint` was the only key rendered without its params. Three parameterized keys (`document.detail.version_number`, `document.search.results_count`, `organization.messages.delete_confirm`) are currently unreferenced by the frontend — dormant, not user-visible; left as-is.

## Verification

- `composer check` green (308 tests, PHPStan, CS, locales, OpenAPI, MCP, conformance)
- `npm run check --prefix frontend` green (type-check, lint, tests incl. new regression tests, build)

body: ## Summary Adds a self-contained **Oracle Forms → Spring Boot** modernization demo under `oracle-forms/`, plus the two decoupled authoring artifacts (portable Playbook + repo Skill). The demo's point is the **programmatic verification loop**: a Python contract-parity harness encodes every Forms trigger as an HTTP assertion and gates the conversion, catching a real cross-field business rule a naive rewrite drops. The durable **before-state on `main`** is an unimplemented scaffold — every `BillingService` method throws `NotImplementedException` (HTTP 501), so the harness is red except `/health`. Devin's live work is implementing the service from the Forms triggers until green. The reference implementation lives on the **unmerged `oracle-forms/answer-key` branch**, never on `main`, so the exercise repeats. ``` oracle-forms/ legacy/BILLING.fmb.xml + triggers/*.plsql + schema/ # source of truth (Forms export) contracts/openapi.yaml # REST contract distilled from Forms spring-boot-app/ # target (Java 21, Spring Boot 3.2.4, H2/PG, :8092) verify/test_contract.py + run_contract.sh # pytest harness, black-box over HTTP .workshop/playbooks/modernize-oracle-forms.devin.md # portable Playbook (→ !modernize-oracle-forms) .agents/skills/oracle-forms-modernization/SKILL.md # repo mechanics (auto-loaded) Makefile: forms-build / forms-run / forms-verify / forms-clean ``` **The caught bug (centerpiece).** `SUBSCRIPTIONS.DISCOUNT_PCT` has a `WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM` trigger capping the discount at the plan's `MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT` (0 for every plan except `ENTERPRISE`). A field-only conversion maps the `0..100` range and stops, so a 15% discount on `PRO` returns `201`: ``` test_subscription_discount_over_plan_max_400 FAILED ...a field-only 0..100 range check would return 201. Got 201: {"planCode":"PRO","discountPct":15,...} ``` Fix looks up the plan and enforces the plan-dependent cap → `400`, harness green (15/15): ```java if (discount.compareTo(plan.getMaxDiscountPct()) > 0) throw new ValidationException("discountPct", "Discount exceeds plan maximum"); ``` ## Verification - `make forms-verify` on `main` → red (only `/health` passes; data endpoints 501). - `make forms-verify` on `oracle-forms/answer-key` → **15 passed**. - Scaffold builds clean with `./gradlew spotlessCheck build` (Java 21). ## Notes - The answer key is intentionally **not** merged to `main`. - Uses Gradle to match the existing `services/` Java convention in this repo. - The presenter thread ships separately in `workshop-metadata`. Link to Devin session: https://partner-workshops.devinenterprise.com/sessions/10f6e8245b2f4246823c07a2d8a6c78a Requested by: @bsmitches ---

author: prashantm912
body:
# fix(strategy-signal): completed-bucket read contract for live coarse series (B1 / FID P0-1)

**Merge tier: HOLD — left open for the owner.** This changes what every armed live scalper sees at evaluation time. Read "Expected live behavior shift" before merging/deploying.

## What

Audit item B1 (`docs/audits/2026-07-10-research-fidelity-audit.md` §3.1, P0-1): live coarse-primary series (3m/5m/15m/1h) accrued FROZEN first-minute partial buckets — `refreshFromRest`'s fetch window ends ~60s into the new bucket, the read returns that bucket as a 1-minute partial, and `EngineSeries`' strictly-increasing append silently drops the completed correction at the next boundary. Every live 3m scalper evaluation and every 5m/15m/1h gate series judged first-minute slices (~1/3 volume, truncated H/L) while the backtest rolls full buckets.

Fix — strategy-signal-service only, `EngineSeries`/libs/goldens untouched:

1. **Completeness filter** in `LiveSeriesStore.ensureWarm`/`refreshFromRest`: skip any fetched candle whose bucket end (`bucketStart + interval`) is still in the future per the injected Clock. Applied to 1m/3m/5m/15m/1h; **1d/1w and unknown intervals fail OPEN** (unchanged — the btst pre-close 1d append + daily-context semantics are FID P1-9, out of scope).
2. **Exit-anchor reconstruction fix** (found by adversarial review, HIGH): `generatedAt` is stamped from the 1m trigger bar (= the boundary that opens bucket k+1) while the entry evaluates the just-completed bucket k; `indexAtOrBefore(generatedAt)` therefore anchored exits one bucket late once the completed k+1 landed (and flip-flopped on the intrabar path). Coarse primaries now reconstruct the anchor at `generatedAt − primaryDuration`; 1m primaries unchanged. Aligns ATR-at-entry, trailing window start, and time-stop counts with the bar the entry actually evaluated (= backtest anchoring).
3. **PartialBucketCanary** (the audit's done-check): 60s scheduled sweep comparing each warmed 3m series' last completed bar volume to the in-memory 1m sum of the same bucket. Mismatch → `ay_signal_partial_bucket_mismatch_total` + one warn per (series, bucket). No REST/DB/endpoint; gated on `artha.signals.engine-enabled` like SignalEngine; tolerance knob `artha.signals.partial-bucket-canary.volume-tolerance` (default 0).

## Adversarial review (4 Opus lenses: parity/golden, IST-time, concurrency, blast-radius)

Found N / fixed M / accepted-documented K (final tally in comments):
- **FIXED (HIGH):** exit-anchor off-by-one (above) — two lenses found it independently, confirmed in code.
- **FIXED (MED):** canary torn-read containment — per-key try/catch (canary is the first cross-thread reader of the unsynchronized series; observational only, cannot corrupt eval state).
- **ACCEPTED (documented + test-pinned):** 1h session-truncated final bucket (15:00–15:30 IST, IST-:00-anchored cagg) reads as in-progress until 16:00 → a post-close warm/restart omits it. Verified benign: next session's first boundary refresh re-fetches from `lastBarTime` and restores it BEFORE the first evaluation. No session-calendar logic added to the filter (simplicity).
- **PRE-EXISTING, not this PR:** (a) live entry price/stops derive from the 1m trigger bar close vs backtest's coarse-bucket close — alignment claim covers gate/indicator evaluation, not emitted price; (b) backtest 1h rollup is UTC-hour-anchored (= IST :30) vs live cagg IST :00 — 30-min phase gap for 1h gates, chip task_1b85c64f filed; (c) backtest context advancement look-ahead = FID P1-9/B11.
- **Residual accepted:** wall-clock completeness ≠ data completeness (a lagging cagg could still serve a data-partial "completed" bucket) — the canary is the standing detector for exactly that.

## Expected live behavior shift — owner MUST read before arming

This is a regime change, not a transparent bugfix. The 3m tail flips from first-minute partials (~5k volume operands, truncated ranges, dead volume dot, composite capped ~0.816) to full buckets (~3× volume, true ranges):
- **Entries UP, step-change:** the volume rail — the binding veto in every session forensics to date — passes the volume-expansion bars it was structurally truncating; the volume dot comes alive and lifts the composite cap. Both binding constraints relax together.
- **Stops WIDEN:** structural/first-candle/VWAP stops capture the full 3-minute range → larger per-trade risk, different risk-based sizing (`suggestedQty` shrinks where risk-sized).
- **Calibrations now stale:** #605 (relative vol floor k=1.5), #675/#676 (dot recalibrations) were all tuned on the partial regime. **E8 re-tune is a prerequisite to trusting the first sessions, not a follow-up.** Treat the first armed session as fresh calibration; watch `/signal-rejections`, the shadow book, and `ay_signal_partial_bucket_mismatch_total` (tol-0 may be noisy — knob exists).
- Rollback: plain revert + rebuild strategy-signal-service; series rebuild from warm-up on restart. Only tail: a position opened under the fix carries its (wider) persisted stop through a rollback.
- **Deploy OUTSIDE market hours** (post-close): scalper positions are intraday, so a post-close deploy guarantees zero positions spanning the anchor-semantics change (a pre-deploy entry evaluated on the old frozen-partial regime would reconstruct one bucket earlier under the new math).

## Verification

- Full reactor `-pl services/strategy-signal-service -am verify` green (both commits) — includes ModularityTest + engine-disabled paper ITs (canary excluded there, verified).
- Regression tests: two-boundary freeze scenario (frozen-100 vs full-300 volume), partial-drop, 1d passthrough, fail-open, 1h post-close acceptance, anchor stability (coarse k stays k; 1m unchanged).
- Scope: all changes under `services/strategy-signal-service/` — goldens byte-identical by construction (backtest never touches `LiveSeriesStore`; grep-verified).
- Live done-check after deploy (audit §10 P0-1): canary green across a full session; live 3m volumes ≈ 3×1m; re-run the 125k-floor forensics.

author: v22kumar
body:
Executes **P0** from the [interface diagnostic](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5ae183ff-97e4-4d80-88d4-00533418b3d0) — the highest-impact, lowest-risk fixes, both contained to two files.

### 1. One palette, app-wide
The app was running **two design systems at once**: the live forest-green `AppColors` and the unused Navy·Mint·Amber `DSColors`. That seam is the "here and there" the user reported.

`AppColors` now aliases the DSColors scale:
- `primary` `#0F5132` → **`#16255A`** (Deep Navy)
- `primaryLight` `#16A34A` → **`#14B891`** (Live Mint) — so `gradientPrimary` becomes navy→mint
- dark surfaces → navy-black (`#080B14` / `#141A2B`)
- Gold + Rose kept (they anchor the logos / blood + danger semantics)

Because every shipping screen reads `AppColors.*` / `context.c*`, this **re-skins the whole app** — buttons, headers, nav, gradients — in one reversible change.

### 2. Icons with a spine (Services grid)
`_BentoTile` used OS **emoji** as iconography (render differently on every Samsung/Xiaomi/Pixel, no shared weight, reads as template). Replaced with a single **Material rounded-icon family** at one stroke width, shown in a **color-coded gradient chip** with a soft directional shadow — color becomes wayfinding and the tiles gain depth. Labels bumped 11px → 12px.

### 3. Press-state
`Pressable` (scale-to-0.96, 110ms) already exists and wraps the tiles — the motion primitive is in place.

## Scope / risk
- Two files: `core/theme/app_theme.dart`, `features/home/presentation/screens/home_screen.dart`.
