author: wombat164
body:
feat(#84): fresh-reader comprehension gate for text documents

## Summary

Diagrams have a vision-review gate (D8/D16, `lint/vision_review_contract.py`): a fresh, author-independent model looks at a rendered diagram cold and reports what's confusing. No equivalent existed for rendered TEXT documents. Vale and the plain-language work catch deterministic phrasing patterns, but neither can answer "does a reader who has never seen this understand what each section is for, and where does the flow break down" -- a comprehension question, not a style one.

Adds `lint/comprehension_review_contract.py` (`render comprehension-review`), the text peer of the diagram gate, reusing the SAME D8 contract machinery (`contracts/schema_utils.py`, `contracts/copy_paste.py`, `contracts/init_ai.py`) rather than inventing parallel plumbing:

- Chunks a rendered `.md` or `.docx` into reader-sized snippets, first at fence-aware ATX heading (leaf-section) boundaries, then at paragraph boundaries only when a section runs long. A `.docx` is extracted via python-docx into the same markdown-ish shape so one chunker serves both formats.
- One INPUT_SCHEMA (task intent, doc title, the ordered chunk list) and one OUTPUT_SCHEMA (per-snippet purpose/confusing/fluff/cuttable findings plus a whole-document synthesis: doc purpose, worst-flow snippet, what a length-budget cut removes first), identical across harness, copy-paste, and the D17 direct-API channel.
- Report-only: findings are printed or emitted as JSON, nothing is rewritten.

**The D16 gate decision (`docs/DECISIONS.md` D19).** Every other gated step has a real deterministic proxy for "the model's judgment probably isn't needed here" (vision-review's geometry/contrast numbers; decision-capture and contextualize's descriptive-vs-intent change-kind split). Comprehension has none: document length, section count, and similar structural signals predict review cost, not comprehension risk, in either direction. Inventing a formula from them would dress up a guess as a measurement, so `confidence()` is pinned at a constant 0.0: this step always escalates. That is a legitimate D16 outcome (vision-review's own `confidence()` already returns 0.0 when its metrics give no signal), not a departure from it -- this is simply the first step where that is the permanent case rather than one branch of a heuristic. An operator who explicitly sets `--threshold <= 0` still gets the accept path: an honest "not reviewed" stub (`status: WARN`, empty findings, `reviewer_mode: deterministic`), never a fabricated verdict. The decision entry also checks this reasoning against the plain-language work that landed alongside this PR (issue #76: `SentenceLength` / `NominalisationDensity` / repeated-phrase detection) and explains concretely why none of those signals substitute for a confidence proxy either.

Wired as its own top-level `render comprehension-review` command (like `decision-capture` / `contextualize`) rather than folded into `render qa`, since `lint/render_qa.py`'s own docstring states it is "a deterministic, zero-LLM gate" -- adding an LLM-escalating step there would contradict that contract, and the generic `render copy-paste <step>` `HAS_OWN_GATE` redirect message assumes the step name matches its own top-level command.

## Test plan

- [x] 26 new tests in `tests/test_comprehension_review.py`: chunking (heading/paragraph boundaries, code-fence and div-fence awareness, frontmatter stripping, oversized-paragraph handling), `.docx` extraction, the D8 contract (copy-paste driver forces `reviewer_mode`), the always-escalate confidence/gate behaviour and its `threshold<=0` escape hatch, the deterministic stub, the CLI end to end (needs-review / threshold-0-accept / copy-paste-escalate paths), the `copy-paste` `HAS_OWN_GATE` redirect, and `init-ai` harness exposure.
- [x] Full suite: 635 passed, 2 skipped (was 609 passed before this change). One pre-existing failure, `tests/test_gates.py::test_demo_source_passes_its_own_skin_rules` (a Vale spelling/style finding on demo content), reproduces identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout with none of this PR's changes present -- confirmed via a throwaway worktree before relying on it -- and is unrelated to this change.
- [x] `python scripts/generic_gate.py` -- clean.
- [x] `python scripts/check_wiki_sync.py` -- clean (`wiki/content/reference/index.md` updated with the new command, env var, and D16-gate-contract note; `wiki/content/explanation/index.md` gets a third D16 worked example).
- [x] Docs updated in this PR: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (new section + render-modes table row), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (D19), `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased).

Fixes #84

author: osolmaz
body:
## Summary

Privileged execution brokers need approved target-user processes to keep their normal Unix filesystem permissions.
This change adds an explicit Brokerkit systemd capability for that case while preserving `ProtectSystem=strict` for every broker by default.
`sudo-broker` will opt into the capability during its shared installer cutover.

## What Changed

The systemd model now distinguishes credential brokers from deliberate host privilege brokers.
The less restrictive behavior cannot be selected accidentally through an untyped directive.

- Added typed `HostFilesystemAccessDeny` and `HostFilesystemAccessAllow` policies.
- Rendered `ProtectSystem=false` only for the explicit allow policy.
- Kept the zero value fail-closed as `ProtectSystem=strict`.
- Documented the intended privileged-broker use case.
- Added policy rendering and invalid-value tests.

## Testing

The full local Brokerkit quality gate passed without running mutation locally.
Mutation remains configured in CI.

- `GOWORK=off go mod verify`
- `GOWORK=off go vet ./...`
- `GOWORK=off go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...`
- `./scripts/check-go-coverage.sh` (87.3%)
- `GOWORK=off golangci-lint run ./...`
- `GOWORK=off govulncheck ./...`
- `GOWORK=off slophammer-go dry .`
- `GOWORK=off slophammer-go crap .`
- `GOWORK=off slophammer-go check .`

## Risks

Selecting the allow policy deliberately removes systemd write isolation for the service and its children.
The API is explicit, typed, and defaults to denial so ordinary brokers retain the existing hardened behavior.

author: apagplayz
body:
Builds on PR #1 — approve that one first; this stacks on top.

## What this changes

**1. Fallback footage now matches what the beat is actually about.**
Videos have a "footage ladder" — if there's no AI image, no stock clip, and no archive photo for a moment (say, a courtroom scene), it was supposed to fall back to a generic atmosphere clip from our local mood bank. But the mood bank only had 5 moods (rain, foggy house, police lights, newspaper close-ups, night street) — so a courtroom, prison, forest, highway, water, or interrogation moment had nothing to match and just grabbed a random unrelated clip instead.

Now those 6 themes are recognized too, so those beats reach for something on-theme. A few of the new categories don't have a downloaded clip yet (that needs a one-time `npm run moodbank:populate` run, which searches archive.org for a free, real clip) — until then they gracefully fall back to whatever atmosphere IS available, exactly like before. Nothing is broken by this, it only adds more good matches over time.

**2. Small, blown-up archive clips look intentionally filmic instead of blocky.**
Some of our free archive.org source clips are old and small (think 320×240), and stretching them up to fill a phone screen (1080×1920) made them look pixelated/blocky. Added a light "smooth the grain, then scale up cleanly" step so the same small clip now reads as an intentional vintage/film look instead of a compression mess. Also made the clip-downloader prefer the highest-resolution version when an archive.org item offers more than one file size.

Nothing about how footage is labeled or licensed changed — real-person tagging, AI-generated tagging, and license fields are untouched.

- [x] Type check passes clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] Manually ran the new ffmpeg filter strings against test video clips to confirm they parse and produce the right output size
- [x] Confirmed the manifest JSON is still valid and every new entry is honestly marked as unresolved until a real clip is downloaded

body:
Makes Band surface/resume a Claude session started **outside** Band (agent-dashboard orchestrator, CLI, or Remote Control) when you open a worktree — no manual picker step. Both sides already write the same `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>` transcript store keyed by cwd; this closes the two gaps that stopped it working.

## Step 2 — adopt an existing on-disk worktree instead of twinning
`workspaces.create` checks `listWorktrees(project.path)` and, if a worktree for the branch exists, adopts it instead of `git worktree add`. One worktree per branch; avoids `git worktree add -b` failing when the branch is checked out elsewhere.

## Step 3 — auto-attach the latest on-disk session on open (tombstone-gated)
When a chat has no active session, `ensureActiveSessionSummary` resolves `agent.getLatestSession(worktree)` and adopts it. Gated on a new `sessionCleared` tombstone so it does NOT reintroduce #478 (the old fallback re-promoted a session the user had just left via "New session"). Tombstone set on clear, reset on set. author: phsb5321
body:
## Symptom (10/07/2026, live)

`/__throttle/health` reported `distinct:2, duplicates:{pedrobalbino@pm.me:[A,B]}` for ~2.6 h while live `/api/oauth/profile` probes showed **three distinct accounts** (A=pm.me, B=proton.me, C=gmail). False alarm.

## Root cause

`claude-account-promote` swapped `.credentials.json` between `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-b` at 10:22:07 (`PROMOTED [pressure]`, 7 s before the first guard warning) but left both `.claude.json` files behind. The guard compared A's **fresh network email** (profile probe) against B's **stale local label** — mixed provenance → false duplicate. It self-cleared only when B's throttled profile probe finally succeeded.

Impact during the window: `promote` sees IDOK=-1 and refuses swaps → the auto-switch rail stalls exactly when a real pressure event would need it.

## Fix — verify-before-warn

- `accounts.guard_email(path) -> (email, verified)` — verified only from a mtime-fresh profile probe; the `.claude.json` fallback is unverified (it lies after a promote swap).
- `accounts.identity_state` — shared-email group with ANY unverified member → `suspected`, not `duplicates`; `collapsed` requires no pending suspicion. Back-compat: rows without `verified` = verified.
- `accounts.force_verify_email(path)` — cache-bypassing live profile probe.
- `proxy._note_identity_collision` — warns immediately only on VERIFIED duplicates. Suspected groups spawn a **background** verification task (2 attempts, never inline — health invariant #4 <50 ms) which then:
  - warns verified (exact original message) when the probe confirms one account,
  - warns `(unverified)` when the probe fails — the 09/07 dead-token collision class stays detectable,
  - logs a clear when the label was stale (this incident).
- `anthropic_accounts_distinct` gauge reads **-1 (unknown)** while a suspicion is pending, not 1 (distinct).

## Tests (346 pass)

- `guard_email` provenance: local→unverified, probed→verified, cred-rewrite→drops to unverified.
- `identity_state` suspected split + collapsed-requires-verified + back-compat.
- End-to-end promote-swap scene ×3: probe clears stale label (no warning), probe confirms real duplicate (verified warning, gauge 2), probe dead (`(unverified)` warning, suspected persists).
- Gauge: suspected → -1.

## Falsifiability

If a promote swap still produces an immediate `ACCOUNT COLLISION:` warning without a probe, or a dead-token real collision goes silent, the fix is wrong.

## Deploy plan

Merges to main → next NixOS pin bump (Nix pane 19 currently landing 8d57df6→03ba9e5 as NixOS PR #1187; this rides the following bump). Client-side hardening (promote swaps `.claude.json` synchronously) lands separately as NixOS PR #1188 — this PR is the proxy-side belt-and-suspenders.

author: deforexopleiding-bit
body:
## Doel
Sluit de loop tussen bulk-aanmaan-cron en de dunning-engine: **elke succesvolle bulk-send wordt gelogd in `dunning_log`**, en **de engine gebruikt die log-entries voor een instelbare cooldown** zodat klanten niet dubbel worden aangemaand.

## Recon-bevindingen (cruciaal voor gate)

**1. `dunning_log.run_id` is NULLABLE** ✅ (bron: `2026-06-07-dunning-foundation.sql` r75-83). Alleen `id`, `event_type`, `created_at` zijn NOT NULL. Bulk-entries kunnen direct met `run_id=null`.

**2. Engine event_types voor 'sent'** — bekende issue:
- `executeEmailStep` schrijft `'email_sent'` (r125).
- `executeWhatsappStep` schrijft **géén** `whatsapp_sent`-event — alleen skipped/failed varianten (`whatsapp_skipped_template_error`, `whatsapp_skipped_no_meta`). Er is geen enkelvoudig success-event voor WA-sent.
- Engine schrijft ook `'started'` bij run-start (r311).

**3. Bewuste scope-keuze voor cooldown**: **alleen `bulk_reminder_sent`-entries** worden gebruikt, geen engine-events. Redenen:
- Engine-dubbeling wordt al gedekt door de bestaande "actieve run bestaat"-check op `dunning_workflow_runs` (r281-289). Een klant met actieve run wordt sowieso niet opnieuw gestart.
- Combined lookup over engine-events zou fragiel worden omdat WA geen success-event schrijft.
- Cooldown maakt de engine **CONSERVATIEVER** (slaat vaker over), nooit agressiever.

**4. Waar per-klant cooldown-check invoegen**: net **ná** de actieve-run-check (r289), vóór de run-insert. Cooldown vult de skip-lijst aan, vervangt 'm niet.

**5. `app_settings` — RBAC**: bestaand endpoint `api/app-settings.js` PUT vereist `super_admin`. **Te strikt voor de finance-user**. Ik bouw een dunne wrapper met `finance.dunning.execute` die alleen `dunning_cooldown_days` mag zetten (1..90). Waarde-shape `{days: <int>}` — spiegel van `cron-events-signups-auto-close.js` r91.

**6. `finance-dunning-history`**: gebruikt geen switch/map — `event_type` wordt letterlijk als string gerenderd. `'bulk_reminder_sent'` verschijnt automatisch (geen label-map-uitbreiding nodig; kan als follow-up nice-to-have).

## Deel A — bulk logt naar `dunning_log`

`api/cron-dunning-bulk-send.js`:
```js
if (successAny && rec.customer_id) {
  try {
    await supabaseAdmin.from('dunning_log').insert({
      run_id: null, step_id: null,
      event_type: 'bulk_reminder_sent',
      payload: {
        customer_id: rec.customer_id,
        channels: { whatsapp: waOk, email: emOk },
        total_open_cents, invoice_ids, job_id,
        bulk_recipient_id: rec.id,
        wamid, email_message_id,
      },
    });
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('[cron-dunning-bulk-send] dunning_log insert soft-fail', e?.message);
  }
}
```
- Alleen bij `successAny` (min. één kanaal geslaagd).
- **Fail-soft**: log-fail → verzending is al gebeurd en gaat door. Alleen console-warning.
- File-header comment bijgewerkt van "NIET geschreven" naar de nieuwe koppeling.

## Deel B — instelbare cooldown in engine

`api/_lib/dunning-engine.js`:

**Bovenaan outer-loop** (één keer per engine-run):
```js
let cooldownDays = 7;
try {
  const { data } = await supabaseAdmin
    .from('app_settings').select('value').eq('key', 'dunning_cooldown_days').maybeSingle();
  const n = Number(data?.value?.days);
  if (Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 1 && n <= 90) cooldownDays = Math.trunc(n);
} catch (e) { /* fail-soft, default 7 */ }
const cooldownCutoffIso = new Date(Date.now() - cooldownDays * 86400000).toISOString();
```

**Per klant, ná actieve-run-check**:
```js
const { data: recentBulk } = await supabaseAdmin
  .from('dunning_log')
  .select('id, created_at')
  .eq('event_type', 'bulk_reminder_sent')
  .eq('payload->>customer_id', customerId)
  .gte('created_at', cooldownCutoffIso)
  .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
  .limit(1)
  .maybeSingle();
if (recentBulk) continue;
```
- **Fail-open** bij DB-fout: tijdelijke glitch mag aanmaan-flow niet blokkeren.

## Deel C — settings-endpoints + UI

### `api/dunning-settings-get.js` (nieuw)
- GET → `{ dunning_cooldown_days, is_default, updated_at }`.
- RBAC `finance.dunning.view` (lezen mag ruimer).

### `api/dunning-settings-update.js` (nieuw)
- POST `{ dunning_cooldown_days: 1..90 }` → upsert.
- RBAC `finance.dunning.execute`.
- 2-staps upsert (spiegel van `app-settings.js`). Audit-log `dunning_settings.update` (fail-soft).

### `modules/finance.html`
Nieuwe instellingen-strip **bovenaan de Workflows-tab** (`#dunningSubWorkflows` r1703):
- Titel + hulptekst ("Klanten die binnen deze periode al zijn aangemaand …").
- `<input type="number" min="1" max="90">` + Opslaan-knop + inline feedback.
- Wire idempotent `_wireDunCooldownOnce`. Load bij openen Workflows-sub-tab; opslaan enabled alleen bij wijziging.

## Diff-overzicht (5 files, +260/-5)
| File | Verandering |
|---|---|
| `api/cron-dunning-bulk-send.js` | Fail-soft `dunning_log`-insert bij success + header comment |
| `api/_lib/dunning-engine.js` | app_settings-load boven outer-loop + per-klant cooldown-check |
| `api/dunning-settings-get.js` | Nieuw GET endpoint |
| `api/dunning-settings-update.js` | Nieuw POST endpoint (wrapper) |
| `modules/finance.html` | Instellingen-strip in Workflows-tab + wire |

## Geen SQL-migratie
`dunning_log.run_id` is al nullable. `app_settings` bestaat. Geen kolomtoevoegingen nodig.

## Verificatie
- `node --check` op alle 4 gewijzigde/nieuwe JS-endpoints → OK.
- Script-blocks van `modules/finance.html` via `node --check` → OK.

## Test-scenario's
1. **Bulk-log**: bulk-cron stuurt naar klant X → `dunning_log` heeft nieuwe rij met `event_type='bulk_reminder_sent'` en `payload.customer_id=X`. Zichtbaar in Geschiedenis-tab als letterlijke string.
2. **Cooldown werkt**: engine draait daarna (binnen 7 dagen) → X wordt overgeslagen (geen dubbele engine-aanmaning).
3. **Instelbaar**: Wanbetalers → Workflows-tab → cooldown-veld → zet op 3 → Opslaan → engine gebruikt 3 dagen.
4. **Fail-soft default**: ontbrekende/ongeldige setting → engine valt terug op 7 (log-warning, geen crash).
5. **Log-fail**: kunstmatige DB-glitch op log-insert → verzending slaagt alsnog, warning-log in Vercel.

**Niet zelf mergen — wachten op "go, merge PR #NNN".**

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [957728ab-7026-4518-bb36-d8b427a90664](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/957728ab-7026-4518-bb36-d8b427a90664?fix-finding-id=AZ9M3_GVTGeptNLGRfYD)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/957728ab-7026-4518-bb36-d8b427a90664?fix-finding-id=AZ9M3_GVTGeptNLGRfYD)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZ9M3_GVTGeptNLGRfYD. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in introduction/other_views.py ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in `introduction/other_views.py` ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application builds a system command from untrusted input and passes that command to a shell or command interpreter. An attacker can abuse that pattern to append extra arguments or shell metacharacters, causing the application to execute unintended commands. This can lead to arbitrary code execution, data exposure, or full compromise of the affected host. ## Changes Made The vulnerable code in `introduction/other_views.py` previously interpolated the POSTed `domain` value directly into a command string and executed it with `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)`. That pattern allowed user-controlled input to influence the operating system command line. The fix added a strict allowlist check with `re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9.-]+", domain)` and returned an error response when the value is missing or invalid. It also changed the subprocess invocation to pass the utility and hostname as a list, using `shell=False` so the input is treated as data rather than shell syntax. The existing behavior of choosing `nslookup` on Windows and `dig` on other platforms was preserved. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation instructions: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input to ensure that it does not contain any malicious commands**: The patch adds a whitelist validation with `re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9.-]+", domain)` and rejects empty/invalid domains before any command execution, which directly addresses the guidance by filtering malicious input. - **Avoid constructing OS commands from user-controlled data**: The patch stops building a single string with `.format(domain)` and instead passes `['nslookup', domain]` or `['dig', domain]` to `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False`, which removes shell interpretation and aligns with the guidance’s command-injection mitigation goal. Criteria assessment: - **Library Usage Compliance**: Compliant. The guidance did not require a new library; the fix uses Python's existing `re` module for validation. - **Code Pattern Matching**: Compliant. The fix follows the recommended pattern of sanitizing/validating input and avoiding shell command strings by using argument lists with `shell=False`. - **Security Approach Alignment**: Compliant. The remediation directly mitigates command injection by validating the domain and eliminating shell-based execution. - **Style Consistency**: Compliant. The change matches the file’s existing Django view style and preserves the existing render/error handling pattern. - **Dependency Manifest Updated**: Compliant by default. No new dependency was introduced, so no manifest update was needed.

body:
## Redeemable Rounds

Lets a venue owner/manager pick a **preset reward** and advertise it, flowing that choice to the public directory, the venue page, and the guest check-in/redemption flow — with the **weekly redemption limit enforced in data**.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-redeemable-rounds-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-09-redeemable-rounds.md`

### What's here
- **Registry** — one preset→label source of truth (`@happitime/shared-types`), mirrored in mobile (`rewards.mjs`) with a parity test.
- **DB** — two nullable columns on `venues` (`reward_preset` CHECK'd to the 4 keys, `reward_active` default false). Migration `20260709163733_venue_reward_config.sql`.
- **verify-checkin** — data-enforced **weekly cap** (`canRedeemWeekly`, one redeem / user / venue / 7 days) on the `redeem` path; returns `reward_preset` on both check-in and redeem responses.
- **Owner console** — a **Rewards** tab (pick preset + advertise toggle + guest preview). The Server Action `saveVenueReward` reuses the proven `requireVenueManagementAccess` role gate and zero-rows RLS check.
- **Directory** — offer badge on venue cards, a **Rewards** filter chip, and a venue-page banner (gated on offer-live).
- **Mobile** — the configured reward name flows through the stamp card and redemption screen; the `weekly_limit_reached` cap shows a friendly next-eligible message.

Offer is "live" iff `reward_preset IS NOT NULL AND reward_active = true`. Earn-it count stays **5** platform-wide (unchanged).

### Verification (done locally)
- `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ (0 errors) · `npm test` ✅ (273 pass / 0 fail)
- `deno test verify-checkin` ✅ (43 pass) · registry parity ✅
- `npm run typecheck --workspace directory` ✅ · `npm run build:directory` ✅ (directory is **not** in CI)

### Grant/RLS check (verified against prod)
`venues` uses **table-wide** grants (`role_table_grants` shows anon SELECT + authenticated UPDATE) — unlike the `user_profiles` column-lockdown trap, so the new columns are auto-readable by the directory's anon client and writable by owners. No extra grant needed.

### ⚠️ Deploy notes (post-merge, in order)
1. **Migration** deploys via `Supabase DB Deploy` on merge. It is **not yet applied to prod** (verified: columns absent remotely). db-deploy currently depends on the pending migration-history reconciliation — that must clear first, or the deploy still fails. Do **not** apply via the Supabase MCP `apply_migration` tool (stamps its own version → history drift).
2. **Redeploy** the edge function: `supabase functions deploy verify-checkin`.
3. Run `get_advisors` (type `security`) after the migration lands.
4. **Manual happy-path E2E** (Rewards tab → directory badge/filter/banner → mobile copy → redeem → second-redeem blocked) is **pending the migration deploy** — cannot run until the columns exist remotely.
5. Mobile changes are **OTA-able**.

### Known limitation (by design, in scope)
The weekly cap is enforced in the edge handler, not a DB constraint, so two truly-concurrent redeem requests could both pass the check. The 3/day network cap + 5-stamp floor make this a narrow race. A unique partial index on `round_redemptions` would make it airtight — deferred as out-of-plan-scope for a reviewer to decide.

body:
## Summary
Follow-up to v0.25.1. That fix (mobile Enter-key handling) was real and correct, but didn't resolve the user's actual report — the bug wasn't mobile-specific at all.

**Root cause**: unlocking Master requires scoring ≥5000 on Expert (`MASTER_UNLOCK_TIER`/`MASTER_UNLOCK_SCORE`). The leaderboard only offered to submit on a **personal-best run**, gated against the **all-time local best** (`bestScoreByTier`). So the moment a player unlocks Master, their Expert local best is already ≥5000 — every normal Expert run afterward fails to beat it, the name-entry UI never appears, and nothing ever reaches the Expert board. Beginner/Intermediate happened to work because those local bests stayed low for most players.

**Fix**: a new `bestSubmittedByTier` ledger, separate from the local high-score system, starting at **0 for every tier** (deliberately not seeded from local bests). The board-submission gate now checks "did this beat what I've already put **on the board**" instead of "did this beat my all-time local best" — so a high pre-existing local best no longer blocks a tier from ever reaching the leaderboard, while re-submission is still gated on improvement (board stays sparse).

## Test plan
- [x] `node --check` on the extracted script — OK
- [x] Constructed the exact bug scenario via a temporary debug hook (removed before commit): Expert local best 6200, submitted ledger 0
  - Old gate (`score > localBest`): blocked a 500-point run ✓ (reproduces the bug)
  - New gate (`score > submittedBest`): allows the same 500-point run ✓
  - Re-submitting the same 500 again: correctly blocked (no spam) ✓
  - Improving to 700: correctly re-fires ✓
- [x] No console errors, loads clean at v0.25.2
- [x] Version bumped in all spots (HTML badge, GAME_VERSION, sw.js CACHE_NAME, package.json)

## Note for existing players
Everyone gets a one-time "catch-up" submission per tier on their next qualifying run, since the new ledger initializes from 0 — that's intended, it's how current skill finally lands on each tier's board for the first time.

author: ivankuznetsov
body:
## Summary

Daemon-dispatched Hive children no longer depend on the machine-wide temporary directory for their combined stdout/stderr capture. The dispatcher now supplies Hive's durable XDG state home, and `ChildSupervisor` stores each capture under:

`~/.local/state/hive/logs/daemon-children/<project>/<slug>/`

This prevents a full or separately-quota-limited `/tmp` from terminating the daemon before `Process.spawn`. The capture also stays outside the project's tracked `.hive-state` worktree, so a child's final JSON envelope cannot dirty workflow Git state after the stage commit.

Standalone `ChildSupervisor` callers that do not supply a state home keep the existing tmpdir fallback.

## Why

The benchmark daemon repeatedly exited with `Errno::EDQUOT` while opening `/tmp/hive-daemon-logs/...`. That exception occurred before child spawn and brought down the dispatcher, leaving otherwise runnable Hive tasks stalled.

## Validation

- All daemon unit tests: 706 runs, 2,268 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- Real child-spawn regression verifies the capture lands in XDG state and leaves a separate project Git worktree clean
- Dispatcher regressions cover ordinary status-row dispatch and queued dispatch requests
- Ruby syntax checks pass for every changed Ruby file
- `git diff --check` passes

Rubocop/Bundler executables are not installed in the host environment.

## Operations

No migration is required. New daemon child captures use the new directory after the updated daemon starts; existing `/tmp/hive-daemon-logs` files can age out independently.

author: zenetusken
body:
## What

Fixes the 2026-07-10 audit's one **verified silent-data-corruption** bug (finding #1, adversarially confirmed + reproduced): `_frontmatter`/`_is_mirror` close a frontmatter block on ANY line starting `---` (`^---\n(.*?)\n---`), but `_as_mirror` counted only bare stripped `---` lines. Two divergences, both measured:

- **Non-bare close (`----`, `--- notes`)**: the fact parses as relevant/replicable, but `_as_mirror` stays "inside frontmatter" to EOF — its v0.1.70 frontmatter-scoped strips **eat every body line starting `projects:`/`global_ref:`**. Reachable via `--pull` (corrupts the mirror in every puller) and `--promote` (the origin's OWN copy rewritten corrupted); the damaged mirror reads in-sync forever.
- **Indented `  ---`** (e.g. a block-scalar continuation): not a fence to the parser, but counted by `_as_mirror` → early close → canonical-only `projects:` provenance **leaks into every mirror** — the exact churn class the v0.1.26 root-fix closed, reopened.

Also fixes the sibling `_body` boundary: the close line is now consumed whole and may sit at EOF with no trailing newline — pre-fix, two body-less facts with differing frontmatter compared UNEQUAL and promote's Guard-5 spuriously refused a clean reconcile.

## How

One boundary rule everywhere: OPEN = the exact first line `---`; CLOSE = any later line whose RAW start is `---`. The `_is_mirror(_as_mirror(...))` round-trip and idempotence are pinned on the malformed shapes. Pre-existing corrupted mirrors in the wild **self-heal**: the corrected `want` differs → STALE → refreshed on the next pull.

## Empirical gate (measure-first)

- **RED**: 5/5 defects reproduced pre-fix with pure-function fixtures (including the parser-validity check proving the corruption was reachable, not contrived).
- **GREEN**: 0/5 post-fix; ported as the smoke `v0.1.74` block (6 checks).
- Gates: smoke **818 passed / 0 failed** · sim all lifecycle properties hold · mypy clean · manifests valid.

## Compatibility

No CLI/schema change; both deltas are correctness on malformed-but-parser-valid input ⇒ **patch** (CHANGELOG `## [0.1.74]`).

Stacked on #86 (both touch `sync_global.py`); retarget to `main` lands automatically when #86 merges.

author: mdorman
body:
Closes #359.

## What

Introduces `web::reactive::Invalidator` — a reusable revalidation primitive that
replaces the hand-rolled "bump a counter, refetch on change" boilerplate that had
accreted across the audiences vertical, and converts audiences to use it.

An `Invalidator` wraps a revision counter. A committed mutation `notify()`s it; every
`Resource` that `track()`s it refetches. Two ergonomic entry points keep the counter
fully encapsulated:

- `invalidator.resource(fetch)` — a `Resource` that refetches whenever the invalidator
  fires (nullary fetcher; the counter is an internal detail).
- `invalidator.action::<A>()` — a `ServerAction` that fires the invalidator **on
  success only** (`Some(Ok(_))`), never on dispatch or failure. The gating `Effect` is
  wired internally, so no call site writes it.

The `invalidator_scope! { struct Foo }` macro declares a distinct context-scope newtype
(with `Deref` to the full `Invalidator` API) for **cross-component** refetch scopes, so
scopes never collide by type in context. A *local* scope just uses a bare `Invalidator`.

## Why single-idiom + success-gating

Every audiences mutation now revalidates the same way, so the behaviour is consistent by
construction rather than by each call site remembering to re-implement it. Success-gating
means a failed mutation (e.g. a duplicate-name create) no longer triggers a spurious
refetch. The blast radius is deliberately audiences-only.

## Coverage

`notify`/`track`/`new`/`Default` and the macro-generated newtype are host-tested. The
`resource` fetcher and the `action` success-gating `Effect` are client-only reactive
plumbing (an `Effect` doesn't run host-side or in SSR), so they're `cov:ignore`'d and
exercised by the audiences e2e — which now asserts scoped invalidation (a membership
toggle does **not** refetch the list) and success-gating (a failed create does not
refetch).

## Decision record

ADR-0060 — web Invalidator revalidation idiom.

## Follow-ups (filed, not in scope here)

- #348 — non-keyed list rebuild remounts every row on create/rename/delete (pre-existing;
  this PR does not regress it).
- #372 — a sticky-resource retention helper joining the `web::reactive` family; this PR
  preserves the existing open-coded sticky signals as-is.

author: abrichr
body:
## Why

External criticism of this repo's benchmarks, which we accept: the real incumbent for "run the same GUI workflow 500 times" is not a computer-use agent — it is a DOM-selector script (Playwright/Selenium). Also $0, also fast, no OCR anywhere. Instead of arguing, this PR runs that experiment head-to-head against the compiled vision replay — same task, same frozen drift schedule, same arm-independent OCR + identity success check (`verify_hybrid_final`, reused from the hybrid benchmark), wrong-action events measured for every arm.

The task spec ("open the FIRST referral task") underdetermines exactly one selector, so **both readings run as steelman arms**: **DOM (positional)** = first row's Open button (literal reading); **DOM (name-filtered)** = the Open button in the row named `Jane Sample` (identity reading, hardcoding the demonstrated patient exactly as the compiled arm's recorded identity band does). Full generated report: `benchmark/dom/BENCHMARK.md`.

## Three-arm perturbation matrix (n=2 each, deterministic, $0)

| drift mode | compiled replay | DOM (positional) | DOM (name-filtered) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lookalike` | halt (fail-closed) | **WRONG ACTION** (`#patient/p0`) | success |
| `missing` | halt (fail-closed) | **WRONG ACTION** (`#patient/p2`) | halt (fail-closed) |
| `grow` | halt (fail-closed) | **WRONG ACTION** (`#patient/g1`) | success |
| `sort` | halt (fail-closed) | **WRONG ACTION** (`#patient/p2`) | success |
| `theme` | mixed* | success | mixed* |
| `rename` | success (2 heals) | halt — needs human edit | halt — needs human edit |
| `move` | success (2 heals) | success | success |
| `typelabel` | success (1 heal) | success | success |

\* one `theme` run per affected arm completed correctly (`#patient/p1`, right patient) but failed the dark-palette OCR judge — a judge false negative, disclosed, counted as a failure, and the two disputed final screenshots are committed alongside the report.

**Frozen 20-slot schedule: all three arms tie 14/20** (14 clean, 0/6 drifted — notice/reqfield/modal-once stop every arm). **Wrong-action totals: compiled 0, DOM-positional 8, DOM-name-filtered 0. Maintenance totals: compiled 0, DOM-positional 8, DOM-name-filtered 10.** Both DOM arms are ~36x faster per clean run (p50 0.2s vs 7.2s).

## Verdict (verbatim from the generated report)

**The wrong-action vector is spec underspecification, not "Playwright".** On the frozen schedule all arms tie (compiled 14/20; dom 14/20; dom_named 14/20): the drift that halts the compiled replay (notice/reqfield/modal-once) stops both DOM scripts too. Both DOM scripts are ~36x faster per clean run (p50 0.2s vs 7.2s). The perturbation matrix is where the arms separate, and they separate by HOW EACH ARM NAMES ITS TARGET, not by DOM vs vision. (a) **Positional selectors silently retarget under data drift.** The positional script ("first row" — the literal reading of the task spec) wrote to the WRONG PATIENT on 4 of 8 modes (grow, lookalike, missing, sort; 8 runs, every one with a healthy-looking final screen). A position-phrased spec cannot notice that the row's identity changed. (b) **The identity reading fixes it — and where a stable DOM exists, it also out-completes the compiled arm.** The name-filtered script (same code, one selector keyed to the demonstrated patient) completed CORRECTLY on grow, lookalike, move, sort, typelabel and failed closed on missing, rename, with zero wrong actions. The compiled arm was equally safe (wrong actions: 0) but never healed to the true row on these modes — every data-drift outcome was a halt: on data drift the name-filtered DOM arm finished the work the compiled arm safely declined. (c) **What demonstration buys: the identity came for free.** Nobody had to DECIDE that "first referral" really means Jane Sample — the demonstration captured the target's identity as a matter of course, while the DOM arms needed that judgment hand-written into a selector (and the positional variant shows what happens when it is not). The compiled arm's remaining browser-side edges on this data: demo-derived identity with no spec authoring, heal-through of label drift (`rename` broke both DOM scripts' Open selector — a human edit each — while the ladder healed through it), and fail-closed halts with an accurate report. Its costs are equally plain: ~36x slower per run, and an OCR judge with failure modes of its own. (One condition — `theme` — produced judge-disputed verdicts: an OCR-judge artifact affecting both arms equally, not an automation difference; see the measurement-validity section.) Boundary, stated plainly: this comparison exists ONLY on browser backends. On desktop, VDI/Citrix, or any pixels-without-DOM substrate there is no selector script to write — the criticism's own point — and wherever a stable, accessible DOM exists, an identity-keyed selector script is the honest incumbent to beat: as fast as the positional one and, on this matrix, as safe as the compiled arm.

## What's in the PR

- `openadapt_flow/benchmark/dom_arm.py` — both steelman scripts (positional + name-filtered, differing in exactly one documented selector), harness, outcome classification (success / halt-or-error / WRONG-ACTION / maintenance / verification-dispute), aggregation, three-column markdown renderer, three-arm chart with dispute footnote, orchestrator, CLI. Reuses the hybrid benchmark's frozen `SCHEDULE` and `verify_hybrid_final`.
- `openadapt_flow/mockmed/static/app.js` — flag-gated `sort` drift mode.
- `benchmark/dom/{BENCHMARK.md, results.json, outcome_matrix.png}` + the two disputed `theme` finals.
- `.gitignore` — ignores `benchmark/dom/{finals/,rows.jsonl}` (disputed finals force-added).
- Tests: `tests/test_dom_arm.py` (24) incl. the one-selector-difference and identity-scoping cases + `tests/test_mockmed.py` sort-mode tests. Full suite green.

Prior draft's asymmetric variant dismissal is **retracted in the report**: the compiled arm hardcodes the same patient constant in its recorded identity band; the arms differ in how identity is captured (demonstration vs hand-authored selector) and in fail-closed semantics, not in whether identity is encoded. The "writes to the wrong patient" framing is now scoped to positional selectors specifically. $0 spent: zero model calls anywhere.

## What

Adds an opt-in, separately-gated **adopt** stage to `/ggx-investigate`. After the engineer note is posted, a second HITL can hand an **actionable** ticket to `/ggx-dispatcher` — automating the manual "assign me + current cycle + To Do + `ready-to-dev`" quad the operator flips by hand every time. Every non-adopt run stays note-only (just Skip).

## Changes

- **`commands/dev/ggx-investigate.md`** — Step 0 parses `--adopt`/`--no-adopt`; Step 5 relabeled **HITL #1**; new **Step 7** = binary readiness read + `Adopt`/`Skip` gate + four writes (assign→me, cycle→current, status→To Do, single `ready-to-dev` label). The label leg re-fetches before write, sets `ready-to-dev` and drops the other three mutually-exclusive analyzer labels (conflict cleanup), preserves all non-analyzer labels (incl. `dispatcher-*-in-flight`), never blind-unions. Suppressed for `--verify-fixed`, comment-fallback posts, and out-of-scope lanes. Frontmatter / intro / D5 / Guardrails amended to drop the stale "the ONLY mutation is the note / never changes status-assignee" claims.
- **`commands/dev/_ticket-lib.md`** — new `set_cycle` row (Linear `save_issue --cycle` via `list_cycles type:current`; Jira no-op) + registered `/ggx-investigate` as a caller.

## Design boundaries (per pre-implementation consensus)

- **NEVER** writes `need-revision` / `need-dependency` — negative-readiness labeling stays owned by `/ticket-analyze`. Adopt only ever sets `ready-to-dev`.
- **No pipeline invocation** — adopt only *labels* the ticket so the dispatcher can pick it up; it never calls `/dev:ff`.
- Composes `_ticket-lib` primitives inline; no `_ticket-init` reuse; no `resolve_cycle.py`.
- Every adopt leg is idempotent + soft-fail (the note already landed).

## Verification (decorrelated auditor/implementer split)

- **verify-agent** (contract surface): **CLEAR** — primitives exist, no stale claims survive, label logic consistent.

author: baileyrd
body:
Twenty-seventh item from the C41–C73 pass — **closes out Tier IV completely (23 of 23)**. See `docs/CAPABILITY_GAPS.md`.

## What

- **Dynamic variables** computed at read time in `vars::get`: `$RANDOM` (seedable LCG in bash's 0..=32767 range — `RANDOM=42` makes the stream reproducible; assignment re-seeds rather than stores), `$SECONDS` (counts from shell start; `SECONDS=100` re-bases), `$EPOCHSECONDS`/`$EPOCHREALTIME` (system clock; the microsecond form agrees with the second form).
- **`${FUNCNAME[@]}`**: a real array mirrored from a call stack pushed/popped by `call_function` — innermost first, unset outside any function, like bash.
- **`${BASH_SOURCE[@]}`**: likewise from a source-file stack — the script at the bottom, `source`d files pushed on top; empty under `-c`, same as bash.
- **`$LINENO`** came cheaper than the M–L estimate: rather than threading line numbers through the whole AST, `RawPipeline` carries one `line` computed from newline-token counts at parse time, published by `run_andor` before each pipeline — values **byte-identical to bash** for the same script file.
- Documented approximations: a here-doc body's own newlines don't advance `$LINENO` (the lexer swallows them); `BASH_SOURCE` inside a function reflects the current source stack rather than the function's definition site.

## Verification

- Verified against real bash across the probe matrix; adds 1 integration test.
- Full suite passes (142 unit + 140 integration), clippy stays at the 11-warning baseline.

## What this adds

A new **Match center** (`src/matchcenter.py`, `src/football_data.py`) for player-level detail on real matches, pulled live from the [football-data.org](https://www.football-data.org/) API:

- **First XI** — starting lineup (shirt number, name, position) and formation for each side.
- **Goalscorers** — a minute-by-minute list of goals with scorer, assist, and type.
- **Man of the match** — a *heuristic* pick, since football-data.org doesn't publish an official award: scores goals (+4, own goals −2), assists (+2), and cards (yellow −1, red −3), with a small bonus for the winning side.

Available both as a CLI (`python -m src.matchcenter WC --matchday 1`) and a new "Match center" tab in the Streamlit app, where you can pick a competition (World Cup, Euros, Champions League, Premier League) and any finished match.

### Design notes

- This is the one place the project talks to an external API/key. It's fully optional — the rest of the app is unaffected, and the tab shows a plain "enter an API key" prompt until one is supplied (env var `FOOTBALL_DATA_API_KEY` or pasted into the sidebar, kept in-session only).
- **Free-tier caveat, documented in the README:** football-data.org's free plan covers World Cup/Euro/league fixtures and scores, but lineups, goal detail, and cards are a paid "player data" add-on. I verified this live against a real free-tier key — matches load correctly but return no lineup/goal arrays. Everything degrades gracefully: "no lineup data available" / "not enough match event data" instead of erroring, so the feature is ready to light up for anyone with a plan that includes player data.
- `src/football_data.py` translates the API's actual error responses (400 for a bad token, 403 for tier/competition restrictions, 429 for rate limits, 404) into clear messages instead of leaking raw HTTP errors.

## Verified

- Unit-style checks of `first_xi` / `goalscorers` / `man_of_the_match` against synthetic responses matching the real API schema (multi-goal games, own goals, cards, empty/no-event matches).
- Live end-to-end against the real football-data.org API (free-tier key) for both World Cup and Champions League competitions — confirmed graceful fallback text renders correctly.
- Screenshot-tested the app's error paths: no key (info prompt), invalid key (clean "Your API token is invalid." message, not a raw traceback), and valid key with competition/match switching.

author: kdonovan
body:
## Problem

When an action declares subfields on a parent (`expects :x, on: :parent`) and the `parent` is omitted or explicitly `nil` at call time, inbound validation blew up with a bare `RuntimeError` ("Unclear how to extract … from nil") → `result.error == "Something went wrong"` (an *exception* outcome), instead of treating the subfields as absent. **This happened even when every subfield was optional** — so an all-optional nested structure couldn't simply be omitted.

```ruby
klass = Class.new do
  include Axn
  expects :payload, optional: true
  expects :name, on: :payload, optional: true, type: String
  def call = nil
end
klass.call   # was: exception outcome (bare RuntimeError). now: ok
```

## Fix

A single guard in `FieldResolvers.resolve`: resolving any field from a `nil` source yields `nil` (a nil source means "absent"). This closes the whole class of the bug in one place:

- subfield **validation** (the reported path),
- subfield **preprocessing**,
- the generated **subfield readers**, and
- **`model:` subfields** — the Model resolver previously did `nil[field]` → `NoMethodError`.

Each subfield's own optional/required rules then apply against `nil`: an optional subfield passes; a required one fails with a clean `InboundValidationError` ("… can't be blank"), never a bare `RuntimeError`. A parent with a usable `default:` is unchanged (the default materializes before validation).

> Note: a dev-facing `InboundValidationError` still surfaces `result.error == "Something went wrong"` by design — the meaningful change is that `result.exception` is now a clean validation error rather than a bare `RuntimeError`.

## Schema-reflection follow-through (interaction with PRO-2842)

The reflection in PRO-2842 was built to *match current runtime* (a subfield parent was `required` unless defaulted, and **never nullable**). With the runtime fixed, requiredness was **already** correct (`field_optional?` handles it); only nullability needed revisiting. `apply_nested_subfields!` now advertises a nested-object parent as nullable (`type: ["object", "null"]`) exactly when it tolerates nil **and** strands no required child — mirroring the requiredness predicate `nil_allowed?(config) && !has_required_child`. A parent with a required child (which a nil parent can't yield) stays object-only.

## Tests

- `on_subfields_spec.rb` — nil/absent parent: optional children pass; required → clean `InboundValidationError`; preprocessed subfield doesn't raise.
- `extract_spec.rb` — nil source → nil.
- `model_id_reader_spec.rb` (PORO) + `spec_rails` `model_validator_spec.rb` (real AR model) — `model:` subfield on a nil parent resolves to nil / fails cleanly.
- `schema_spec.rb` — nullability now `["object", "null"]` for a nil-tolerant parent with all-optional children; object-only when a required child or a non-nil-tolerant parent.

Full core + Rails dummy-app suites green; rubocop clean.

Closes #1276

Implements the full simulation path (the issue's primary approach), per the Fable 5 plan posted at https://github.com/richkuo/go-trader/issues/1276#issuecomment-4937256559.

## What changed

- **Pure gate** — `_scale_in_decision` in `backtest/backtester.py` is a line-for-line port of `perpsScaleInDecision` (scheduler/scale_in.go): opt-in, direction match, `max_adds`, `max_added_notional_usd` (incl. the 1e-9 tolerance), signed ATR spacing from `last_add_price` with the `avg_cost` fallback and the positive-EntryATR requirement. The decision reads bar N's close; the add fills at bar N+1's open — the same look-ahead contract as entries.
- **Blend + frozen anchor** — mirrors `applyScaleIn`: `avg_cost` blends (drives PnL), `initial_quantity` grows, and the first add freezes `risk_anchor_price` to the pre-blend `avg_cost`. Every SL/TP geometry site (sl_after bumps, close-evaluator thresholds, ratchet watermarks, the fixed/trailing trigger seeded at open) derives from the frozen anchor, mirroring `Position.riskAnchorPrice()` on the live **on-chain** protection path. `EntryATR`, the stamped regime, and cleared-tier watermarks stay frozen at first entry.
- **Accounting** — each add pays a taker commission that joins the #1241 entry-fee pro-rating pool; a long add's notional leaves cash (may go negative — the spot-model image of live's margin-based virtual notional; equity stays exact, documented in the module docstring). Adds create no `Trade` rows (live `#T` parity); `results["scale_in_adds"]` / `scale_in_added_notional_usd` and a per-trade `scale_in_adds` field surface them.
- **Plumbing** — `load_strategy_config` threads `allow_scale_in`/`scale_in` and mirrors the live validateConfig rejects (perps/manual + hyperliquid only, block-without-flag, live-args static-scalar-SL resize guard). The #1268 `risk_per_trade_pct` × `allow_scale_in` reject is preserved verbatim and backstopped in `Backtester.__init__`; an `entry_fraction` column combined with `allow_scale_in` is rejected. Both engine signal paths (open/close and plain) take adds; adds bypass the regime entry gate (live `regimeBlocksOpen` passes posQty>0) and honor the #1025 position-frozen directional resolution.
- **Docs** — `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CLAUDE.md` `scale_in.go` rows, the backtester parity-limitations docstring, and the `backtest/AUDIT.md` matrix row no longer say "NOT backtested".

## Deviations from the plan (code contradicted it)

- The plan suggested deriving the engine-path add intent from the **bar-top** `_effective_directional_entry` resolution; the existing #1025 post-close re-resolution (which passes the live position qty and frozen regime) already produces the position-aware `open_action`, so the add branch consumes that instead — same semantics, no duplicate resolution.
- The plan's `df["_prev_close"]` column became a positional `shift(1)` array read (no DataFrame column pollution).

## Verification

- New `backtest/tests/test_backtester_scale_in.py` (37 tests): gate parity vectors (caps, spacing signs, boundary tolerances, fallbacks), `applyScaleIn` blend math over two adds, anchor-not-blend for the fixed SL and tiered-TP thresholds (both directions of the distinction: survives where a blend trigger would fire, and the frozen trigger exits the full grown quantity), per-add fees, partial-close pro-rating against the grown baseline, #T-parity counting, per-position state reset, short-side mirror, and the loader rejects.
- `test_backtester_lookahead.py` extended: add fills at N+1's open, fill-bar range perturbation changes neither decision nor size, spacing gate reads the signal bar's close.
- Full Python suite: `pytest shared_strategies/ shared_tools/ platforms/ backtest/ -n auto` — **2692 passed**. Default-off runs byte-identical (pinned by a golden-equality test).

`pagy_countless` raises `Pagy::OverflowError` when `page > 1` and the filtered scope has zero rows. Minimal repro: `/advisories?ecosystem=k8s&page=3` — `k8s` matches no advisories, page 3 asks for offset 100, gets nothing, Pagy raises, Rails returns 500.

author: pdfinn
body:
## Summary

Closes the enforcement gaps between the audit-log design (docs/compliance/audit-log-design.md) and the code. The design was sound; the parts that make a hash chain tamper-evident against a privileged adversary were designed but not enforced. No new daemons, formats, or crypto — policy moves into the two existing commands and anchoring stays namespace policy (`cp` + a verifier flag).

- **fix(factotum sign proto):** `op=pubkey` could never match a key (`op=` was treated as a key selector), so `/mnt/audit/pubkey` always served empty and offline verification had no key. Signing worked; the verify half was dead. Strip the verb attr before lookup.
- **auditverify:** with `-k`, signatures are mandatory — every checkpoint must verify and at least one must be present (a whole-file rewrite can recompute every chain hash but cannot mint a signature; tolerating unsigned/missing checkpoints was a clean bypass). New `-a anchorfile` verifies the chain against an off-host copy of `/mnt/audit/head` — the truncation defence.
- **auditfs:** checkpoints drive themselves (signed root at least every 64 records and within 10 min of any new record — CT signed-tree-head pattern) and are signed-only; the `checkpoint` event is reserved on `log`; a boot `auditfs start host=... replay=...` record makes restarts visible; `verify` detects live divergence of the backing file from the in-memory chain; `chain` reads stream by offset (the old path copied the whole log per 9P read, quadratically).
- **fail-closed emitters:** `module/audit.m` exports `ONFILE` (the opt-in marker). secstored refuses an authenticated session whose `authok` cannot be sealed; 2fa gates enroll/addkey/disable up front. Installs that never opted in keep the loose-coupling contract.
- **tests:** new `tests/auditverify_test.b` — 11 deterministic adversarial cases (rewrite, stripped sigs/checkpoints, truncation vs anchor, forged head, wrong key). Host integration test now gates PASS on the strict anchored verify; its old `sig=*` presence check tripped an Inferno sh parse quirk and never ran.
- **docs:** design doc updated to match (epoch timestamps, signed-only cadence, durability residual replacing the unimplemented fsync claim, threat-model rows for truncation and the claimed-source attribution residual).

## Testing
- `tests/auditverify_test.dis` 11 passed; `auditchain` 6 passed; `auditsign` 3 passed (post-merge with origin/master lockout work).
- `tests/host/audit_signing_test.sh`: reserved event rejected; `ok: 3 records, 1 checkpoints, 1 signatures verified, anchored at seq 3` → PASS.
- Live smoke: boot record, forced signed checkpoint, restart chaining, strict anchored offline verify.

author: lbliii
body:
## Summary

- add a private Postgres-first durable `PostgresJobStore` under `chirp.data._jobs`
- ship a deterministic, reviewable schema migration with queue-scoped idempotency, locked queue capacity, lease-token fencing, retry/exhaustion, and revisioned advisory progress
- keep the slice internal: no top-level or `chirp.data` export, `AppConfig` field, handler registry, poller, automatic DDL, or SQLite parity
- add live Postgres and Python 3.14t CI proof plus RFC, public-status, packaging, and changelog collateral

## Why

RFC 022 Phase 1 needs a directly exercisable durable store before Chirp approves public job definitions or an executor. PostgreSQL database time, row locks, queue capacity rows, and opaque per-claim tokens own cross-instance correctness. Persisted values are bounded and parameterized, and the store bypasses generic query echo so payloads, idempotency keys, progress, and failure details do not enter framework logs or errors.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/ruff check .`
- `.venv/bin/ruff format . --check`
- `.venv/bin/ty check src/chirp/`
- full non-slow suite: pass in 576.4 seconds
- 473 focused data, schema, Pelt, migration, and job tests: pass
- live Python 3.14t/Postgres job suite: pass, including concurrent idempotency, capacity-limited claims, expiry/reclaim, stale-owner rejection, renewal, nonzero database-clock backoff, terminal exhaustion, and progress fencing
- `uv build --out-dir /tmp/chirp-issue-677-dist`: pass; wheel contains `_jobs.py` and `001_durable_jobs.sql`
- towncrier 0.10.1 draft: pass

## Steward Notes

- Consulted: root `AGENTS.md`, `src/chirp/data/AGENTS.md`, and `tests/AGENTS.md`.
- Accepted data finding: keep dependencies optional, use the existing pool/transaction boundary, bind every durable value, ship deterministic SQL, and fail loud when the migration is absent. Required proof is the live Postgres matrix, missing-schema test, package build, and no-runtime-DDL source check. Collateral: RFC, public API status, package data, CI, and changelog.
- Accepted test finding: use frozen/slotted read models and issue-traceable tests that exercise actual Postgres races and visible failure behavior. Required proof is `@pytest.mark.issue(677)` coverage for concurrency, lease fencing, retry, capacity, redaction, and HTML-only isolation.
- Deferred to RFC 022 Phases 2 and 3: public definitions, setup/freeze contracts, `app.check()` categories, handler execution, lifecycle ownership, polling, and shutdown. No collateral: those behaviors are intentionally not implemented by this private store slice.
- Deferred example, site, scaffold, benchmark, and deployment guidance. No collateral: Phase 1 has no public application API or executor and makes no throughput claim.
- Dissent: none. Human review routing remains manual-confirmation-needed because the repository has no CODEOWNERS file.

Closes #677

author: warp-agent-staging[bot]
body:
## Description

Reduces peak memory during AI codebase indexing by processing files in batches of 100 rather than all at once.

This supersedes PR #13399 and PR #11982 (both in draft mode and significantly behind HEAD). This PR is based on current `master`.

**Sentry issue:** https://sentry.io/organizations/warpdotdev/issues/7259255054/

### Root Cause

`ai::index::file_outline::native::parse_symbols_for_files` consumed **5.5 GB (92%)** of the 5.96 GB heap snapshot captured when the process exceeded the 10 GB `phys_footprint` alert threshold.

Tree-sitter allocates significant temporary memory for each file's AST (up to the 3 MB `MAX_FILE_SIZE` limit per file). Processing all files in a single `rayon par_iter().collect()` keeps all those allocations live simultaneously and prevents jemalloc's background decay thread from reclaiming freed pages between files. With up to `MAX_REPO_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT = 5000` files indexed, this can result in gigabytes of simultaneous tree-sitter allocations.

### Fix

Added `PARSE_BATCH_SIZE = 100` and changed both parallel parse call-sites to iterate over chunks:

- **`build_outline`**: processes `files.chunks(100)` synchronously inside the `pool.spawn` thread, allowing jemalloc to decay dirty pages between batches.
- **`parse_symbols_for_files`**: processes chunks with an `async await` between each batch, giving jemalloc's decay thread a scheduling opportunity every 100 files.

This caps peak concurrent tree-sitter allocations to ~100 files at a time, rather than scaling to the full file count.

### Relationship to Earlier PRs

- PR #11982 (batch file-outline parsing): addressed the same root cause but is now significantly outdated against HEAD
- PR #13399 (batch file-outline parsing to bound peak memory): also addressed the same root cause but was left in draft mode and is 72 commits behind HEAD

## Testing

- [x] `cargo clippy -p ai --features local_fs -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test -p ai --features local_fs -- index::file_outline` passes (2/2 tests)
- [ ] Manual testing with large repo

author: miladaslaner
body:
## What & why

Fixes **IB-88**: the TLS branch of `SyslogSender.ensureConn` used `tls.DialWithDialer(dialer, ...)`, which does **not** accept a `context`. A canceled `ctx` could not interrupt a pending TCP connect or TLS handshake — only `dialer.Timeout` bounded it. Since every syslog send serializes behind `s.mu`, one hung TLS dial blocked all workers for the full dial timeout. The plain-TCP branch already honored `ctx` via `dialer.DialContext`.

## Change

`internal/transport/syslog.go` (~line 173): replace `tls.DialWithDialer` with a `tls.Dialer{NetDialer: dialer, Config: s.tlsConf}` and call `DialContext(ctx, network, address)`, so both branches honor cancellation. Stdlib-only — no new dependency.

**Non-scope (untouched):** the plain-TCP branch, framing, and send logic.

## Regression test

`TestSyslogSender_TLSDialHonorsContext` — a stub server accepts the TCP connection but never speaks TLS, so the ClientHello gets no ServerHello. Dial timeout is set long (10s); the assertion window is 2s.
- **Fails-before:** the ctx-ignoring dial blocked the full 10s timeout → test failed at the 2s window.
- **Passes-after:** the ctx-honoring dial returns at once with an error wrapping `context.Canceled`.

Existing syslog transport tests remain green (no-regression).

## Pre-flight (in worktree, immediately before PR)

- `gofmt -l` — clean
- `go build ./...` — pass
- `go vet ./...` — pass
- `go test -race -short ./...` — **all packages ok** (`internal/transport` ok)

author: avrabe
body:
Release-planning pass for the next loop after v3.1.0 "actionable". A two-release **big-domain-bet** program on rivet's `release:` axis, sequenced segmentation → polyhedra.

## Why this order
Segmentation (v3.2) attacks scry's **biggest current precision cliff** — linear memory is havoc'd to one ⊤ blob today (visible in the FEAT-040 gap report as "non-i32 memory address" / havocked loads → ⊤). Since Wasm implements structs/arrays/strings through linear memory, per-segment content sensitivity compounds interval precision, OOB-trap classification (FEAT-046), and the region domain (REQ-001) all at once. Polyhedra (v3.3) is the numeric-precision ceiling above the octagon — valuable but marginal over the existing octagon/pentagon, so it follows.

## What's in the plan (all `proposed` = planned, not yet cuttable)
| ID | Release | What |
|---|---|---|
| **REQ-019** (new) | — | Content-sensitive linear memory: per-segment value tracking, weak-by-default stores as the soundness keystone |
| **FEAT-058** | v3.2.0 | Linear-memory segmentation (Cousot-Cousot-Logozzo functor, AC-015). Slices: pure `scry-sai-segment` + Rocq `Segment.v` → interpreter memory-model wiring → OOB-trap/gap payoff. DD-018 |
| **FEAT-057** | v3.3.0 | Convex polyhedra (Cousot-Halbwachs, AC-012), ELINA-decomposed (TE-012). Slices: pure `scry-sai-poly` + Rocq `Poly.v` (LATTICE only) → wire above octagon + relational surfacing → precision/cost differential. DD-019 |
| **DD-018 / DD-019** | — | Domain designs |

## Soundness & honesty discipline (carried from the WasmCert-Coq pass)
- **Segmentation:** a store through a non-singleton offset is a **weak** update (join into every possibly-touched segment), never strong; the segment count is capped for termination; growable/imported memory stays ⊤ (no regression).
- **Polyhedra:** `Poly.v` mechanizes the **lattice algebra only**; the convex-hull transfers are **γ-sweep-validated, not mechanized**, and the dossier records them as such — no "mechanized" overclaim for the hull (mirrors the float-domain precedent).

Artifact-only. `rivet validate` PASS (107 warnings, all pre-existing house-style "prose mentions X" nudges; 0 errors, 0 broken cross-refs). `rivet list --release v3.2.0` / `v3.3.0` resolve.

author: sylvaincombes
body:
## Summary
A DNS sidecar that disappears permanently strands every existing container on its network: upstream's rotating address allocator never re-issues the freed IP, and containers keep the old sidecar address baked into `resolv.conf` at create time (verified live — MAC pinning does not help, the allocator is hostname-keyed and rotating; there is no static-IP attachment option in apple/container 1.1.0). This PR closes every path that loses a sidecar instead of chasing the unwinnable recreate-at-same-IP:

1. **Hide + protect sidecars via the Docker API** — filtered from `/containers/json`, by-id resolution and prune, so `docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq)`-style cleanup scripts cannot remove them; direct `rm`/`stop`/`inspect` answer 404. This extends the exclusion `ClientNetworkService` already applied to network inspect, now consolidated on `ClientContainerService.isDNSSidecar`.
2. **Adopt healthy sidecars at daemon startup** instead of deleting them — a plain socktainer restart no longer breaks DNS for already-running containers (the adopted sidecar keeps its IP; its upstream is the stable `gateway:2054` the new daemon re-binds). Only sidecars that are stopped or whose network no longer exists are removed.
3. **Right-size sidecar VMs** — 1 CPU / 256 MiB instead of the 4 CPU / 1 GiB defaults; the forwarder is a ~388 KB static binary. 256 MiB is the practical floor: Virtualization.framework rejects anything below 200 MiB (verified live with 128 MiB).

## Related Issue
Follow-up to the DNS reliability work in #264 / #262 — live integration testing showed the sidecar-loss scenarios still broke name resolution on current main.

## Changes
- `ClientContainerService`: `withoutDNSSidecars(_:)` filter applied to list/getContainer/prune; `isDNSSidecar(_:)` as the single label check
- `NetworkDNSManager`: `adoptOrRemoveSidecarsFromPreviousRun()` (replaces delete-all `cleanupStaleDNSContainers`), `shouldAdoptSidecar(status:networkExists:)`, sidecar VM sizing constants
- `ClientNetworkService`, `ContainerStartRoute`, `configure.swift`: reuse `isDNSSidecar`
- `Tests/socktainerTests/Clients/DNSSidecarVisibilityTests.swift`: visibility filter, label detection, adoption contract

## Testing
- [x] `make fmt` passes (no formatting drift)
- [x] `make test` passes
- [x] Unit tests added or updated (required for features and bug fixes)
- [x] Manual testing performed:
  - `docker rm -f <sidecar>` refused (404), sidecar invisible in `docker ps`, DNS keeps resolving after client stop/start
  - `docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq)` wipes user containers, sidecar survives, fresh containers resolve immediately
  - daemon restart: sidecar adopted at the same IP, resolution works immediately afterwards
  - 256 MiB sidecar boots (1 CPU / 256 MB in `container ls`) and holds 20/20 lookups under burst; 128 MiB rejected by Virtualization.framework with 'minimum memory amount allowed is 200 MiB'
  - full live integration suite: 87 passed, 0 failed

- [x] Follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] All commits are signed off ([DCO](https://probot.github.io/apps/dco/))

## What

Phase A of the interface-kind plan (per the capability-matrix design dialogue), four commits:

**1 — The model + table correctness.** `interface_kind.go` is the domain model: kinds classified by name family (Ethernet / PortChannel / IRB(VlanX) / Loopback), capabilities lifted verbatim from DESIGN_PRINCIPLES §6's enumeration (routing, VLAN membership, ACL binding, QoS binding, BGP peering, port properties), the kind×capability matrix pinned by test, and the one authoring split modeled explicitly (IRB *has* routing; `configure-irb` authors it — refusals redirect, never deny). `InterfaceExists` and `ListInterfaces` derive from the same classifier, closing the §24 gap where SVIs were operable but unlisted. Delivery-side, verified against the pinned 202511 yang tree: **LAG L3 moves to `PORTCHANNEL_INTERFACE`** (`INTERFACE` keys are leafrefs to PORT only — our `INTERFACE|PortChannelN` write passes intfmgrd by accident and fails yang-strict reload), added in all three required places (schema+struct+hydrator); `INTERFACE` narrowed to Ethernet keys and yang fields; **`PORT_QOS_MAP` narrowed** (`ifname` is `global`|PORT — LAGs were never legal, so the PortChannel/QoS matrix cell is ✗, a SONiC limitation, and the planned qos-on-lag scenario is cancelled); the twin PORT-vs-PORTCHANNEL property switches converged into one owner.

**2 — The gates.** `OpSpec.Needs` on the registry (single owner of op knowledge); one choke point in `n.precondition` keyed by forward wire verb — reverse ops are structurally exempt (§15). Content-derived ops (`configure-interface`, `apply-service`) compute needs from request content through the same checker. Two mutation-proven fences: registry conformance (an unclassified interface op fails the build's tests) and an end-to-end op×kind matrix test asserting refusal text cell by cell.

**3 — update-irb + SVI single-author guards.** The missing in-place lifecycle verb (§48): gateway IP as a keyed sub-entry move (the ghost-gateway-IP pathology, pinned in reverse), anycast MAC as a SAG field edit (refused while shared), VRF moves refused naming the honest teardown path. §27 guards both directions: configure-irb refuses service-owned SVIs; irb-type apply-service refuses operator-authored ones. Full wire chain (`POST /update-irb`, client, `vlan update-irb` CLI).

**4 — Wire-level pins.** 1node-vs-config grows to 27: every refused cell asserted with its message, plus the update-irb lifecycle. The gate scenario immediately caught a real layering bug — bind-qos resolved its policy spec before the gate (in two twin call sites); resolution moved inside the internal op (§33/§25).

`go test ./...` green after each commit; 1node-vs-config **27/27**; both fences mutation-proven (flipped cell + dropped Needs each failed, restored); the 13-suite audit confirmed no existing scenario drives a newly-refused path.

Device-level §38 scenarios (bgp-peer-on-irb on 2node-vs E16 with an update-irb continuity leg; acl-on-lag + `PORTCHANNEL_INTERFACE` assertions in both 56-portchannel twins; service-on-portchannel), cold runs on both platforms, `/status` LAG/SVI legs (blocked on #431), api.md capability-matrix docs + newtcon briefing, and the Checkpoint-1 full 13-suite sweep.

author: josephdviviano
body:
## Summary

**Stacks on #525** (fixed-length KV-cache). With `use_kv_cache=True`, sampling runs under `no_grad`, so gradients must come from a loss-time recompute. torchgfn's existing recompute for recurrent estimators (`is_vectorized=False`) re-runs the estimator **per step**, re-paying the sequential rollout cost inside the loss.

This PR adds an **opt-in teacher-forced (parallel) recompute**: one causal forward over the whole committed trajectory `[BOS, w0, …, w_{L-1}]`, gathering per-step action log-probs. It **reuses the estimator's own full-prefix forward**, so the loss-time input is built identically to sampling; the result matches the per-step path to tolerance (`atol=1e-5`) with a **single grad-bearing forward** and a **shallow** autograd graph.

## Changes

- **`RecurrentDiscretePolicyEstimator(teacher_forced_loss=…)`** — recompute PF log-probs with one parallel forward per trajectory instead of the per-step loop. **Auto-enabled by `use_kv_cache`**, so a cached policy stays trainable out of the box (you only pass `recalculate_all_logprobs=True` at loss time).
- **`get_trajectory_pfs`** takes a teacher-forced branch for recurrent estimators; the per-step / vectorized paths are unchanged (their shared mask + scatter bookkeeping is now factored into small helpers). Fixed-length trajectories only (guarded; see the Gap-2 `TODO`).
- **Fail-fast guard**: `get_trajectory_pfs` now raises an actionable error when asked to reuse detached (`no_grad`-sampled) log-probs under an active autograd graph, instead of the previous opaque `backward()` failure.

## Result

Together with `use_kv_cache=True` (`recalculate_all_logprobs=True`), this turns the sampling win into an **end-to-end training speedup**.

Measured on this branch — single CPU run (Apple Silicon), batch 32, dim 64 / 4 heads / 2 layers, `word_size=1`:

| seq_len | sample base | sample cached | sampling ×| train base | train cached | training × | \|Δ log_pf\| |
|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|--:|:--:|:--:|
| 8  | 15.36 ms | 10.62 ms | 1.4× | 38.92 ms | 17.53 ms | 2.2× | 2.4e-07 |
| 16 | 38.27 ms | 19.99 ms | 1.9× | 93.00 ms | 33.02 ms | 2.8× | 3.6e-07 |
| 32 | 120.12 ms | 44.14 ms | 2.7× | 268.07 ms | 59.86 ms | 4.5× | 3.6e-07 |
| 64 | 424.81 ms | 102.28 ms | **4.2×** | 899.33 ms | 131.55 ms | **6.8×** | 3.6e-07 |

The `|Δ log_pf|` residual is the equivalence gate: both configurations are the same model, so the wall-clock gap is the optimization. Absolute figures are CPU- and machine-dependent and vary run to run; the robust claim is the **trend** — the training-step gap widens with sequence length, because the cached rollout is O(L²) instead of O(L³) *and* the loss recompute collapses to one parallel forward.

## Tests

`testing/test_kv_cache.py`: teacher-forced `log_pf` == per-step recompute; the teacher-forced path carries gradients; `use_kv_cache` auto-enables `teacher_forced_loss`; and the detached-log-probs guard fires with an actionable message.

## Unaffected

Non-recurrent estimators and the default (`teacher_forced_loss=False`) path are unchanged. Stateless policies and the `Sampler` API are unaffected. Full `testing/` suite green on this branch.

> Review note: this PR is stacked on #525, so its diff is shown against `feat/kv-cache`. Please merge #525 first (GitHub will then retarget this PR to `master`).

author: ivanvyazinin
body:
## Problem
The `ci.yml` **Run tests** step (`bun test`) hangs indefinitely on GitHub's runner — setup/install finish in ~9s, then `bun test` never exits, burning the 6h default job timeout. Every CI run since the workflow was added has been stuck this way.

## Diagnosis
The suite completes in ~3.3s under every reproducible condition (bun 1.2.19, no `.env`, network blackholed, `io_uring` blocked, restricted sandbox) — the app/test code is fully mocked and is not the cause. Docker-on-Mac shares the host kernel, not GitHub's, so the kernel-sensitive component can't be reproduced locally. Prime suspect: `tests/cloudflare.infra.test.ts` boots native **workerd** via miniflare 11× — an exit-hang where a workerd child isn't reaped on GitHub's kernel keeps bun from exiting.

## Changes
- **`ci.yml`**: `timeout-minutes: 10` (no more 6h burns) + split into two `timeout`-wrapped steps — core suite vs the miniflare/workerd test in isolation — so a wedge is contained and **named in the log** instead of hanging the whole job.
- **`tests/helpers/paths-mock.ts`**: fix a separate, pre-existing bug (2 failures in `make test`). `mockPaths()` mocked `@config/paths` with a tmp PATHS missing the `bench` key; `mock.module` is process-global and persists across files, so `PATHS.bench` became `undefined` everywhere → `bench-summaries.test.ts` crashed on `PATHS.bench.dataDir`. Merge the real config into the mock so only tmp-relevant keys are overridden.

## Result
Full suite **125/0** locally (was 123/2), with and without `.env`, under bash.

author: tanhuoo
body:
## Summary

- replace window and view resizing with a fixed transparent canvas and an immutable CGImage-backed CALayer
- animate one uniform Core Animation transform so scale and translation stay synchronized throughout every frame
- constrain the widget to its canonical 100x100 and 320x320 square sizes without disabling custom window dragging
- serialize lifecycle resets and wait for the destination WebKit surface before the native snapshot handoff
- add transition regression coverage and a reproducible build/run verification entrypoint

## Root cause

The live WKWebView, temporary NSWindow, and NSImageView layout could update in separate compositor transactions. During collapse, a smaller presentation boundary could therefore clip content that was still rendered at the previous size, producing a visible hard edge and broken rounded corners.

## Impact

Expand and collapse transitions now scale the complete captured surface proportionally. Arbitrary non-square resize states are blocked, while normal dragging and the existing lock/fixed-position semantics remain unchanged.

## Validation

author: pradeep0153
body:
Closes #1756.

### Description
This PR resolves a highly destructive frontend rendering bug on mobile viewports where massive, unbroken strings of text (like raw JSON payloads or un-minified code) pasted inside Markdown code blocks would violently force the parent container to expand horizontally, breaking the entire page layout.

### Changes Made
- **CSS Audit:** Investigated the global stylesheet governing the Markdown parser's HTML output, specifically targeting the `<pre>` and `<code>` HTML tags generated when a user utilizes triple backticks in the Q&A forums.
- **Strict Boundary Enforcement:** Injected strict CSS overflow containment rules into the core Markdown styling configuration.
- **Implementation:** Applied `max-width: 100%;` to ensure the block respects its parent container. Applied `overflow-x: auto;` to specifically trigger a localized horizontal scrollbar *only* if the text exceeds the boundary. 
- **Word Wrapping Fallback:** For inline code snippets (single backticks), applied `white-space: pre-wrap; word-wrap: break-word;` to guarantee the string naturally wraps to the next line rather than bleeding off the screen.

### Impact
- **Mobile Readability & UX:** Our platform sees over 60% of its traffic from mobile devices. When a student on their phone opened a forum thread where a mentor had pasted a massive, single-line error stack trace, the `<pre>` tag lacked CSS containment. It forced the entire website layout to stretch 300% wider than the physical screen. This forced the student to frantically pinch-and-zoom and horizontally scroll the entire website left and right just to read basic text sentences outside the code block. It made the platform virtually unusable. By enforcing strict, localized CSS overflow boundaries, we guarantee the structural integrity of the main page layout. Long code snippets now neatly generate their own isolated horizontal scrollbar entirely inside the dark code block, preserving a flawless, professional reading experience on all devices.
