author: jonahgabriel
body:
## Summary

Fixes **Bug 2 of OMN-14245** (the SAFE-BOUNDED half): `ContractMergeEngine` silently dropped `handler_routing` and the YAML event declarations on every merge.

`ContractMergeEngine._apply_patch_to_base` constructed its output `ModelHandlerContract` from only 9 named fields (name/version/description/input_model/output_model/behavior→descriptor/capability_inputs/capability_outputs/tags). `ModelHandlerContract` had **no** `handler_routing`, `yaml_consumed_events`, or `yaml_published_events` fields at all — so it was structurally unable to carry those facts even though the base `ModelContractBase` from `ContractProfileFactory.get_profile()` declares them. Any base profile that declares routing/events had them silently dropped on `merge()` and across overlay chaining.

## Changes

- **`model_handler_contract.py`**: add `handler_routing: ModelHandlerRoutingSubcontract | None`, `yaml_consumed_events: list[ModelConsumedEventEntry]`, `yaml_published_events: list[ModelPublishedEventEntry]` (additive; model is `frozen=True, extra="ignore"` → backward compatible). Forward refs resolved in `_rebuild_model_handler_contract()`.
- **`contract_merge_engine.py`**: thread `base.handler_routing` / `base.yaml_consumed_events` / `base.yaml_published_events` through `_apply_patch_to_base()` and both call sites (`_merge_internal`, `_apply_overlay_entry`). Pure preservation — `ModelContractPatch` has no override for these fields, so this is not a new merge policy.
- **`model_handler_contract_extended.py`**: the infra subclass re-widens `handler_routing` to dict-form; annotate the now-incompatible override with `# type: ignore[assignment]`, matching the existing `input_model`/`output_model` override idiom.
- **`node_contract_verify_replay_compute/handler.py`**: set the three fields on the synthetic `MagicMock` base so it validates against the widened model.

## Test evidence (RED→GREEN)

New `TestHandlerRoutingAndEventPreservation` (4 tests) proves the fields survive `merge()` and `merge_with_overlays()`:
- **RED** (engine change reverted, model+tests present): all 4 fail — `handler_routing == None`, `yaml_consumed_events == []`, `yaml_published_events == []` (fields dropped).
- **GREEN** (fix present): all 4 pass.

Local verification: 3364 tests in the affected dirs (merge / models.contracts / validation-pipeline-events / node_contract_verify_replay_compute) pass; contract-hash registry + diff-computer (154) and contract-yaml-schema (42) pass; mypy clean on changed modules + the widened subclass; ruff format + check clean; pre-commit passed at commit time. Full 43k suite runs in CI (shared-model change → governed selector escalates to full).

## Out of scope (design-gated)

**Bug 1 of OMN-14245** — the public contract-model schema drift (flat `descriptor` / `terminal_event` / `event_bus` / `handler` / `metadata`, plus the `input_model`/`output_model` retype and the `dependencies` name collision) — is explicitly **RISKY-RIPPLE, not fixed here** per the ticket. It needs a design decision first (breaking change across ~17 non-model files; `dependencies` PyPI-vs-protocol-DI name collision; `descriptor` vs. existing `behavior`/`behavior_spec` overlap). No live call site parses real `contract.yaml` through these models today, so this drift causes no runtime breakage.

Closes OMN-14245 (Bug 2). Bug 1 recommended as a follow-up design ticket.

author: leandroalonso
body:
Generated chapters carry start times on the AI **reference timeline**. Dynamic ads shift the listener's **playback timeline** away from it, so seeking to a chapter's raw `startTime` lands in the wrong place. This PR makes every way of jumping to a generated chapter first resolve the true playback position — by fingerprinting a bounded region of the audio and matching it against the reference — then seek there, with a graceful fallback to the raw position when it can't.

It builds on the existing transcript fingerprint infrastructure (`FingerprintTimingManager`, added earlier for transcript highlighting) but adds a **separate, isolated on-demand resolve path** for chapters.

### Scope — both places a user jumps to a generated chapter
- **Chapters list** — tapping a chapter row resolves + seeks (with a per-row spinner).
- **Full player** — the next/previous chapter controls resolve + seek (with a per-button spinner).

Non-generated chapters (embedded / podcast-index) already carry real playback times and are untouched — they seek instantly as before. Everything is gated behind `FeatureFlag.generatedChapters` + `FeatureFlag.syncedTranscripts`.

### What's included
- **On-demand resolve in `FingerprintTimingManager`** — a one-shot, side-effect-free resolve (`resolvePlaybackTime`) that fingerprints a bounded window into its own scratch mapping and never touches the continuous transcript mapping. Includes a warm-prior optimization (reuses an active transcript mapping to narrow the search), a bounded cold/warm search window, a hard timeout, "last tap wins" supersession, and streaming/region handling.
- **`GeneratedChapterSeeker`** (new) — shared resolve → seek → analytics → fallback helper used by both the list and the player, so they behave identically. Caches the resolved position on `ChapterInfo.resolvedPlaybackStartTime`, guards against the listener switching episodes mid-resolve, and falls back silently to the raw reference seek on failure.
- **`ChapterInfo`** — `resolvedPlaybackStartTime` cache + `effectiveStartTime`, so a resolved chapter's progress fills from 0% rather than the ad-shifted offset (progress calcs clamped to avoid negative/backwards values).
- **`PlaybackManager`** — `nextPlayableChapter()` / `previousPlayableChapter()` accessors and `chapterSkipped` analytics parity for the generated path.
- **UI** — resolving spinners (per-row in the list, per-button in the player), cancel of in-flight resolves on teardown.
- **Analytics** — `syncedTranscriptsChapterSeekUsed` / `syncedTranscriptsChapterSeekFailed` for resolve outcomes.
- **Tests** — `searchWindow` bounds and mapping-isolation coverage.

## To test

2. Play an episode with generated chapters and dynamic ads (so the reference and playback timelines diverge), you can use The Daily.
3. **Chapters list:** open the chapters list and tap a chapter row — a spinner shows briefly on the row, then playback lands at the real start of that chapter's content (not the ad-shifted reference offset).
4. **Full player:** tap the **next chapter** and **previous chapter** controls — a spinner shows briefly on the button, then playback lands at the correct resolved position. Both should match where the list tap lands for the same chapter.
5. On the last chapter, tap next — it still skips to the end of the last chapter.
6. Tap a second chapter while one is still resolving — the latest tap wins (no late seek from the earlier one). Dismiss the player mid-resolve — playback does not jump afterwards.
7. Confirm a non-generated (embedded / podcast-index) chapter episode still seeks instantly with no spinner.
8. Streaming: for a region not yet buffered, the seek falls back silently to the raw position.

## Checklist

- [x] I have considered if this change warrants user-facing release notes and have added them to `CHANGELOG.md` if necessary.
- [x] I have considered adding unit tests for my changes.
- [x] I have updated (or requested that someone edit) [the Event Horizon schema](https://github.com/Automattic/EventHorizonSchemas/blob/trunk/schema/pocket-casts.yml) to reflect any new or changed analytics.

## fix(ci): bump Go toolchain to 1.26.5 for GO-2026-5856

`govulncheck` flags **GO-2026-5856** in `crypto/tls@go1.26.4` (fixed in `go1.26.5`), failing the `build-and-test` job on **every branch — including `main`** since the advisory was published (`main`'s CI has been red since 2026-07-08; the prior 07-07 runs were green). govulncheck floats its vuln DB (`@latest` + live DB), so this started failing with no code change.

Pins the Go version to `1.26.5` in the three workflows that set up Go (`ci.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `release.yml`) and bumps the `go.mod` directive to match. No code changes.

Merging this unblocks `main` and all in-flight PRs on re-run (the CVE is in the stdlib TLS the whole app links, so nothing app-specific is involved).

author: sjtrotter
body:
## Summary

Re-derives the 24 discrepancies filed in #241 directly against the current compiler
(`RuleCompiler` facade + `PredicateCompiler`/`ParseExpressionCompiler`/`EffectEntryCompiler`/
`TransformRegistry`/`ValidateRegistry`, post-#714 split), per the bounded spec's one rule: **the
compiler is the SSOT — docs and schema align to it, never the reverse.** Several additional
discrepancies surfaced during re-derivation (the DSL kept moving since the 06-10 audit — #293
landed 2026-07-05, after the issue was filed) and are fixed alongside the original 24.

**No runtime behavior changed.** Only `docs/adr/ADR-0001-matcher-rule-format.md`,
`docs/rules.schema.json`, and `docs/effect-verbs.md` are touched — zero `.kt` files, zero test
files, zero rule JSON5. `docs/rules.fragment.schema.json` needs no direct edit since it `$ref`s
the main schema's `$defs` (the `intent`/`hasAnyText`/boolean fixes below propagate to it
automatically).

## ADR-0001 discrepancies (issue's 21 fixes)

| # | Issue claim | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `target:` field doesn't exist (`deriveTargetFromId` instead) | **Fixed** — removed `target:` from every JSON5 example (~20 occurrences); added "Derived name: …" comments; multi-branch examples now use the real per-branch `intent:` override (`RuleCompiler.compileBranch` line ~513) |
| 2 | `on: "$name"` modifier not implemented | **Fixed** — rewrote "Reject entries" + replaced "The `on` modifier in require" with "Anchoring a check to a specific node", showing the real `exists`+`all` re-anchor pattern (verified against the shipping `doordash.screen.dropoff_navigation` rule) |
| 3 | `bound: "$name"` predicate not implemented | **Fixed** — removed the table row + the `require: { bound: "$taskTitle" }` example line; added explanatory note (`PredicateCompiler.compileTreePred`/`compileNodePred` take no `Bindings` parameter — reject/require cannot see bindings at all) |
| 4 | `{ id: "s" }` shorthand doesn't exist (use `hasIdSuffix`) | **Fixed** — mechanically replaced all ~50 occurrences (verified none were rule-`id` fields, which always contain a dot) |
| 5 | Navigate `findChild`/`findDescendant` are strings, not objects | **Fixed** — table + both examples now show `"findChild(s)"` (`CompilerHelpers.compileNavigation`) |
| 6 | `each` takes the predicate directly, not wrapped in `findAll` | **Fixed** — all 3 `each` examples (orders/tasks/metrics) unwrapped (`ParseExpressionCompiler.compileEach` reads `obj["each"]` directly) |
| 7 | `each.scope` is a string `"ancestor(N)"`, not `{ ancestor: N }` | **Fixed** — same edit as #6 |
| 8 | `join` is an array + sibling `separator`, not `{ parts: [...] }` | **Fixed** — "Join" section + PickupNavigationMatcher example + migration table row (`ParseExpressionCompiler.compileJoin` reads `obj["join"]!!.jsonArray` directly) |
| 9 | `replace` needs `{ pattern, replacement }` object, not `"x", with: "y"` | **Fixed** — every occurrence (Navigate example, Coalesce example, transform catalog, chaining example) |
| 10 | `split` needs `{ separator, index }` object, not `"sep", index: 0` | **Fixed** — parameterized transform table |
| 11 | `parseOffers`/`addressBetweenAnchors`/`extractMatchingPrefix` don't exist | **Fixed** — removed from both transform tables; the `each` example that used `extractMatchingPrefix` now derives the same enum via `conditionalEnum` (a real, working pattern already used elsewhere in the same example) |
| 12 | `lowercase` should be `lower`; `upper` missing | **Fixed** — transform catalog now lists `lower`/`upper` (matches `TransformRegistry.knownPlainTransforms`) |
| 13 | Validate args are flat keys, not nested `args: {...}` | **Fixed** — "Validate (Phase 5)" section + both Representative Examples (DashSummary uses `fieldsLe`'s real `field`/`le` keys, DeliverySummary uses `sumApproxEquals`'s real `fields`/`target` keys — verified against `ValidateRegistry.kt`) |
| 14 | `onFail: "simple"` doesn't exist (only `skip`/`dropParsed`) | **Fixed** — replaced with `dropParsed` + corrected description |
| 15 | `engine_version` not read by the loader | **Fixed** — status table + "Rule File Structure" callout + "TransformRegistry Design principles" item 2, all marked not-implemented (`RulesetLoader` only reads `format_version`/`platform_id`) |
| 16 | Nested `platform: {...}` envelope doesn't exist (flat `platform_id`) | **Fixed** — same callouts as #15; also caught that the status table previously claimed `pipelines` was "Implemented" — it isn't (grep confirms zero uses in the loader or any `matchers/rules/**` file) |
| 17 | Notification parse uses `fromGroup`, not `from`/`find`/`group` | **Fixed** — rewrote the `additional_tip` example: each field now runs its own `from`/`find`/`group` regex (there's no shared-capture-group shorthand — verified against `ParseExpressionCompiler.compileNotifParseExpression`) |
| 18 | `parseDeadline` returns `Long?`, not `ParsedTime` | **Fixed** — transform catalog row |
| 19 | Notification predicate table missing `isOngoing`/`channelId*`/`categoryEquals`/`hasAction` | **Fixed** — added all 5 rows (verified against `PredicateCompiler.compileNotifPred`) |
| 20 | Bare `{ isClickable }` invalid — JSON requires `{ isClickable: true }` | **Fixed** — every node-predicate boolean example/table row now shows an explicit value |
| 21 | ADR says click rules have no bind/reject — reject IS supported, bind isn't | **Fixed** — rewrote the Click Rules intro: `reject` uses the same node-predicate vocabulary as `require`; `bind` is schema-legal but inert for CLICK context (`RuleCompiler.compileBranch`: `effectiveBindObj` is `null` unless `context == SCREEN`) |

## Schema discrepancies (issue's 3 fixes)

| # | Issue claim | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | `isClearable`/`isOngoing` should get `const: true` (impl ignores the value) | **Already-resolved, differently** — #293 (merged 2026-07-05, *after* the issue was filed and the 06-10 audit) changed `PredicateCompiler.boolFlag` to honor `false` for every boolean predicate, notification ones included. The premise is now false: `isClearable: false`/`isOngoing: false` are meaningful, honored assertions. Schema is correctly left as plain `type: boolean` (no `const`) — adding `const: true` would now *wrongly* forbid a legitimate `false`. |
| 23 | `clickBranchObject` has `bind` — remove (impl ignores it) | **Fixed** — removed; description now explains why (`bind` compiles for SCREEN rules only) |
| 24 | Top-level `clickRule` has `bind` — remove (same reason) | **Fixed** — same edit |

**Mirror-image finding from the same #293 change:** the schema's node-predicate booleans
(`isClickable`/`isEnabled`/`isChecked`/`hasChildren`/`isLeaf`/`hasNoId`) all carried `const: true`
— which used to be correct (the old `boolFlag` silently coerced everything to true-only) but is
now **stale in the opposite direction**: it forbids the legitimate `false` values #293 made
meaningful. Removed all 6 `const: true` constraints; added descriptions documenting that both
`true` and `false` are honored.

**Also found (schema too narrow, not in the original 24):**
- `hasAnyText` (a real, compiled, currently-used-3×-in-`matchers/rules/**` node predicate —
  `PredicateCompiler.kt:149`) was entirely absent from `nodePredicate`'s `oneOf` list. A rule using
  it would show a false "unknown predicate" error in any schema-validating editor. Added.
- `branchObject` (screen-rule branches) was missing `intent` as an allowed property, even though
  `RuleCompiler.knownBranchKeys(SCREEN)` accepts it and it's the *only* way to give sibling
  branches different output names (their shared rule id derives one name for all of them
  otherwise). Added — this is also what item #1's `target:`-removal fix for multi-branch rules
  now demonstrates.

## effect-verbs.md (issue's 1 fix)

| # | Issue claim | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove `"target": "OFFER_POPUP"` from the example | **Fixed** — replaced with `"intent": "offer_popup"` + a note that `target` doesn't exist on a branch |

author: blarghmatey
body:
## What & why

Implements **Phase 1a** of the dbt-warehouse CI/QA hardening effort (project `wp-dbt-warehouse-ci-qa-hardening-data-trust-021724`, spec `docs/specs/DBT_WAREHOUSE_CI_QA_SPEC.md` §5): a `dimensional_layering` check in `ol-dbt validate` that automates the #2072 Definition of Done.

The rule — *marts/reporting models must reference only dimensional (`dim_*`/`tfact_*`/`afact_*`/`bridge_*`) or other mart/reporting models, never `staging/`/`intermediate/` directly* — has until now lived only as prose in `models/dimensional/README.md` and is violated by ~38 models today. This makes it a machine-checked gate that blocks **new** regressions while the migration is in flight.

## How it works

- **Dual-mode detection** (`lib/dimensional_layering.py`):
  - Authoritative **manifest** mode — walks `depends_on` parent edges + `original_file_path` when a `manifest.json` is present (Phase 1 CI runs `dbt parse` first).
  - Static **`ref()` fallback** — maps each model's `ref()` names to its directory layer when no manifest exists, so the lint also runs locally (and seeded this PR's baseline without a working dbt env).
- **Baseline** (`src/ol_dbt/dimensional_layering_baseline.txt`, 198 `child -> parent` edges across 38 models): only violations **not** in the baseline error and fail CI. Known debt collapses to a single INFO summary; resolved entries are surfaced to prompt shrinking the list. Regenerate with `ol-dbt validate --update-baseline`.
- Wired into the existing `--only`/`--skip`/`--format` machinery, so Phase 1 CI gates on `ol-dbt validate --only dimensional_layering --format json` (exits 1 on any new violation).

## Acceptance criteria (spec §5.4)

- [x] Manifest-based check (with static fallback); correct on the current ~39 known violators (38 models / 198 edges).
- [x] Baseline lets the check pass CI today while blocking *new* `int__`/`stg__` refs.
- [x] `--format json` includes `dimensional_layering` issues; ready to wire into the P1 workflow.

## Tests

`src/ol_dbt_cli/tests/test_dimensional_layering.py` — 25 tests covering layer classification, manifest + SQL-fallback violation detection, baseline round-trip/comments, and the validate integration (new→ERROR, baselined→tolerated, stale→INFO, manifest precedence). Full CLI suite: 279 passed. pre-commit (ruff + mypy) clean.

Refs #2407, #2072.

body:
The `risky-effect-parameter-default-value` rule (fires when a policy effect is parameterized and its `defaultValue` is an enforcement effect) missed `denyAction`, and its finding message fabricated an `allowedValues` recommendation that could contradict the policy's actual set.

## Rule (`RiskyEffectParameterDefaultValue.cs`)
- **Add `denyAction`** to the enforcement effect set, with `auditAction` as its safe counterpart -- same shape as the existing `deployIfNotExists -> auditIfNotExists` special case. Taxonomy corroborated by the sibling `EffectAllowedValuesShouldNotMixIncompatibleEffects`, which already categorizes both.
- **Rename `RiskyDefaultEffectParameters` -> `EnforcementEffects`.** The set holds effect values, not parameters; the name now matches `HardCodedEnforcementPolicyEffect` and the architecture doc.
- **Trim the message.** Drop the fabricated `{auditCounterpart, defaultValue, "disabled"}` allowedValues suggestion; emit only the safe-default recommendation (3 placeholders, not 4). Reword to remove the clumsy colon-quote phrasing.

```
The policy effect is parameterized, but the referenced parameter 'effect' defaults to
an enforcement effect 'denyAction'. This increases the risk of accidentally assigning
the policy with an enforcement effect. Consider setting the parameter default value to 'auditAction'.
```

## Doc (`risky-effect-parameter-default-value.md`)
- 4-column metadata table (adds Severity, Rule Set).
- Fix typo `auditIfNotexists` -> `auditIfNotExists`.
- Add Examples section and a Microsoft Learn effect-basics link; align the suggestion with the trimmed message.

## Tests
- Firing cases: `deny`, `deployIfNotExists`, `denyAction`, case-insensitive `Deny`, static parameter-name expression.
- Passing cases: safe default (`audit`), parameterized with no `defaultValue`, hard-coded effect.

author: thibautmelen
body:
> **Disclosure, first:** this PoC uses [Nika](https://github.com/supernovae-st/nika), an open-source workflow engine (AGPL engine, Apache-2.0 spec) whose founder I am — the same disclosure is the first line of the contribution's README and was stated in my get-involved form. Please evaluate the *pattern* (runs as reviewable, permission-bound, replayable files) on its merits, and treat the tool as swappable.

## New Contribution Check List

- [x] I created a subdirectory named with the format `contrib/<my_github_user_name>-<feature_name>`: `contrib/thibautmelen-reproducible-runs/`.
- [x] I included a short `README.md` that describes the contribution, its motivation and status, and how to try/evaluate it (with a **Status: Speculative** badge, per #142).
- [x] I added a `LICENSE` with the repository-default block.
- [x] Code in a subdirectory (`workflows/`) and the unit tests in `tests/`.

## Description of Contribution

Tapestry's contribution process asks for work that is *reviewed, audited, versioned, and governed*, and the anti-capture principle wants sovereignty *enforced through the architecture*. This PoC applies that standard to **pipeline runs themselves**, using the repository's own consortium-training demo as the subject:

* **The plan is a file** — one YAML workflow, diffable and statically auditable before anything executes (`nika check`, or `make reproducible-runs-check`). A nice honesty note: during development the static audit **refused this very workflow** until the exec command used the array form it can verify against the program allowlist.
* **Permissions are default-deny, declared in-file** — the workflow may run exactly one program (`uv`), write exactly one directory (its own `out/`), and touch no network. The runtime enforces this; convention doesn't have to.
* **Every run leaves evidence** — a hash-chained, replayable trace plus a small JSON receipt (exit code + the demo's own N+1 summary tail). A real captured receipt is committed under `examples/`.

For the Evaluation & Certification lens: this is the "audit evidence for *how* a result was produced" layer — complementary to what the evals measure (`nguyennm1024-sociocultural-alignment`, `jneums-cultural-cpt-validation`) and to the evidence taxonomy in `oli-sovereign-eval-evidence`.

Deliberately scoped to **one workflow**: extending to the contrib experiment runners and future eval harnesses is left until the pattern itself has been discussed.

## How to Run It

Prereqs: normal repo setup + the `nika` binary (single static binary: `brew install supernovae-st/tap/nika`). From the repo root:

```shell
nika check contrib/thibautmelen-reproducible-runs/workflows/consortium-demo-receipt.nika.yaml   # static audit
nika run   contrib/thibautmelen-reproducible-runs/workflows/consortium-demo-receipt.nika.yaml   # run + receipt
```

Expected: demo runtime (~5-10 s, CPU-only, no keys — the audit prices it at $0.00), receipt at `out/consortium-demo-receipt.json`, trace verifiable with `nika trace verify`.

## Testing Performed

* The full per-contribution quality pass is green: `make SRC_DIR=contrib/thibautmelen-reproducible-runs --include-dir=contrib/thibautmelen-reproducible-runs format ruff pylint type-check tests` (2/2 tests, 100% coverage on the test module).
* The unit test runs the static audit itself and **skips cleanly when `nika` is absent** (e.g. CI runners), so nothing here blocks anyone's toolchain.
* End-to-end exercised for real: check green → run 3/3 tasks → receipt written → `nika trace verify` reports the chain intact with the head the run printed.

## Note on the contribution index

`contrib/README.md` isn't touched here to avoid colliding with #153 (which adds the index); if #153 lands, I'll add this contribution's row in a follow-up one-liner (or fold it into #153 if you prefer).

body: ## Summary PR #5880 swapped the ladder filter's `std::tanh` saturator for the Padé `signal::FastMath::tanh` **as the default**, a non-bit-exact change to the ladder's saturation character that shipped without a fidelity review. This PR quantifies the change and **gates it behind a compile flag, defaulting to exact `std::tanh`**. ## Measured (on origin/main, which has #5880) FastMath::tanh vs std::tanh, pointwise: | domain | max abs err | dBFS | |---|---|---| | \|x\| < 2 | 1.4e-7 | -133 | | \|x\| < 4 | 1.5e-5 | -96 | | \|x\| > 4 (hard clamp) | 6.7e-4 | **-63** | The Padé form hard-clamps to ±1 beyond \|x\|=4 where real tanh is still climbing. Ladder-filtered output, fast vs std::tanh (48 kHz), genuine phase-stable error: | scenario | max tanh arg | err RMS | err peak | |---|---|---|---| | normal levels (≤ +6 dBFS in), any resonance | < 2.3 | -147 dBFS | -138 dBFS | | self-oscillation (res 1.0) | 3.0 | -172 dBFS | -143 dBFS | | **hot input 4x / +12 dBFS, res 0.7** | **6.1** | **-79 dBFS** | **-68.8 dBFS** | The ladder only drives the >±4 hard-clamp region under ~3-4x overdrive at high resonance — a signature Moog "drive" setting. There the worst genuine error is **-68.8 dBFS peak**, inside the plausibly-audible -60..-80 dBFS band. Not "provably inaudible." The large (-6 dBFS) deltas on fast cutoff sweeps are **chaotic phase drift, not the tanh's character**: a 1e-6 input perturbation (100× smaller than the tanh error) reproduces them identically. ## Verdict: GATE (not revert) The ~1.2-1.4x RT win is real and worth keeping as opt-in; for any input ≤ +6 dBFS the error is ~-130 dBFS (inaudible). But default fidelity wins for a signature nonlinearity, so: - `PULP_SIGNAL_FAST_LADDER_TANH` (default `0` = exact `std::tanh`; `1` = Padé fast path). - `signal::ladder_tanh()` is the single source of truth — both `LadderFilterT` (interpreter) and the live-kernel `f2_ladder_tanhf` export route through it, so the per-node **bit-exact null test stays green under either setting** (0 → both libm, 1 → both Padé). - Tests pin the FastMath::tanh error bound directly and assert the default float ladder is **bit-exact `std::tanh` under hard drive**; the opt-in build tracks the Padé reference and is provably non-exact. Full `pulp-test-signal-filters` suite green (3272 assertions), plus fast-math and dsp-enhancements suites; `lk_entry.cpp` syntax-checked. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Gated the ladder filter’s Padé tanh behind `PULP_SIGNAL_FAST_LADDER_TANH`, defaulting to exact `std::tanh` to restore bit‑exact behavior and avoid overdrive character shifts. Both interpreter and live kernel now call `signal::ladder_tanh()` so outputs match under either setting. - **Bug Fixes** - Added `PULP_SIGNAL_FAST_LADDER_TANH` (default 0) and `signal::ladder_tanh()` to choose `std::tanh` vs `FastMath::tanh`. - Routed `LadderFilterT` and `f2_ladder_tanhf` through `signal::ladder_tanh()`; waveshaper stays on libm via `f2_tanhf`. - Expanded tests to pin `FastMath::tanh` error bounds and prove the default build is bit‑exact; in fast builds, verify Padé tracking and non‑exactness. author: ahmed-arb
body:
Custom MFE translation files (`translations-custom/*/src/i18n/messages/*.json`) carried empty strings for untranslated custom keys. Since the JSON keys are opaque IDs (e.g. `authoring.details.topic.label`), translators had no way to see what each key means. This fills every empty value with the English source string from the sibling `transifex_input.json`, so a translator opening a custom locale file sees the source text to translate.

It also wires the fill into `update_custom_layer`, so future unified syncs keep custom placeholders populated.

Safe by construction: the custom keys are custom-only (verified 0 overlap with upstream across all MFEs), so filling them never overrides an upstream translation. `merge_final` adds them as custom-only entries that render in English until a translator replaces them. Real (non-empty) translations are never touched. PO files are intentionally left alone — the `msgid` already shows the English source.

Scope: 2,251 placeholders across 221 files in the four MFEs that have custom strings (account, course-authoring, learning, messenger), all languages.

## Summary

Two runtime tuning changes:

1. **Causal-hint resolution stall timeout: 60s → 15m.** The stall-detection
   timeout was implemented via a two-tick mark-and-sweep on the shared
   `ACTOR_TICKER_INTERVAL` (60s), which also governs idle tracing cadence for
   all three actor loops. This decouples the two: a new
   `CAUSAL_HINT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT` (15m) is enforced via a stalled-tick
   counter, while the tracing tick stays at 60s. A `WARN` is emitted once a
   stall persists past the first tick.

2. **Producer prune byte horizon: 8GB → 2GB** (`FRONTIER_PRUNE_BYTE_HORIZON`).
   Stale committed-frontier producers are pruned sooner during recovery.

author: senomorf
body:
## What

- `StripRepair.repair` now diffs the live file's CRC-valid frames against the cache by frame fingerprint (id + trailing crc, `FrameLog.frameKey`) and appends ONLY the missing frames, byte-exact and in cache order, as carry frames. Nothing is re-encoded; the mirror caption comes from the cache's `Memory` reading view.
- Carry-only embeds are now legal: the four `require(newRecords.isNotEmpty())` guards (JpegEmbedder, PngEmbedder, Mp4Codec.embed, Mp4Files.appendRecords) accept a write whose payload is only carried frames, so a cache holding nothing but future-format records can still repair.
- The crash-recovery sidecar fingerprints every intended frame including carried opaque ones, and `RecordScanner.presentIds` reads ids from the frozen envelope offsets (8..24) of every CRC-valid frame instead of only typed records.

## Why

Three verified defects around repair:

1. `strippedItems()` fires on partial strips (`cache.recordCount > item.recordCount`) but `repair()` resubmitted the whole cache while every embedder keeps the frames the file still has. Repairing live `{A}` with cache `{A,B}` wrote `{A,A,B}`, and repeat repairs compounded the duplicates.
2. An opaque-only cache (unknown kind or future wire version) was rejected with "cache is empty or corrupt", so exactly the frames the format promises to preserve were the ones repair refused to restore.
3. `recoverPending` verified a completed write by typed-record ids only. A carry write that landed successfully looked incomplete (its opaque ids were invisible to `presentIds`), so recovery rolled back a good file to its pre-write backup.

## Tests

Failing-first (all three failed against the old logic in a captured baseline run): `repairAppendsOnlyTheMissingFrames` (wrote 3 frames before, exactly 2 now), `opaqueOnlyCacheRepairsByteExact` (repairs a future-wire-version frame byte-exact; also the PR1 end-to-end survivability check), `recoveryKeepsATargetWhoseCarriedOpaqueFrameLanded` (recovery no longer reverts a completed carry write).

Existing repair, safety, and unknown-kind tests pass unchanged; `./gradlew build` green (unit + integration + ktlint + detekt + AGP lint + kover floors) plus the iOS tripwire for the embedder guard changes.

author: eryxiz
body:
### Goal of this PR

Let a resource replace `ptxclipregions.dat`, the particle-texture UV clip-region
table, through a new `replace_ptxclipregions_file` manifest statement.

Custom particle assets can already be streamed, but if a particle uses a custom
texture atlas whose frame layout differs from the base game there is currently no
way to tell the engine how that atlas is split into frames, so such particles fall
back to the full-texture default `(0,1,0,1)` and render incorrectly. This gives
creators a way to supply the matching clip-region data.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20f85809-9c54-4d45-b5f2-3fbde75c4cb4

### How is this PR achieving the goal

Adds a `replace_ptxclipregions_file 'file.dat'` manifest statement, parsed in
`citizen-resources-gta`.

The game parses `ptxclipregions.dat` once at ptfx init and keeps the pointers
`rage::ptxClipRegions::GetData` returns alive for the process lifetime, so
rebuilding its table in place would dangle them. Instead, this hooks `GetData`
(the single accessor every particle draw goes through) and serves the
resource-provided overrides from its own store, leaving the game's table
untouched; lookups that miss fall through to the original.

The store is populated when the resource mounts and cleared on disconnect. Reads
use a `shared_mutex` with an `atomic` fast-path, and the backing pool is
append-only so the pointers handed back stay valid.

Resource usage:

```lua
-- fxmanifest.lua
files {
    'ptxclipregions.dat',
}

replace_ptxclipregions_file 'ptxclipregions.dat'
```

The file must be declared in `files{}` so the client downloads it and the VFS can
read it.
### This PR applies to the following area(s)

FiveM


### Successfully tested on

**Game builds:** 2372, 2545, 2612, 2699, 2802, 2944, 3095, 3258, 3323, 3407, 3570

**Platforms:** Windows


### Checklist

- [x] Code compiles and has been tested successfully.
- [x] Code explains itself well and/or is documented.
- [x] My commit message explains what the changes do and what they are for.
- [ ] No extra compilation warnings are added by these changes.

author: antareske
body:
# PR: feat(starry,ax-net): return L2 frame length from Device send/recv for net_stats byte counters

## 概述

将 `ax-net` 内部字节计数器从 IP payload 长度对齐到 L2 帧长度，与 Linux `/proc/net/dev` 语义一致。

## 动机

`net_stats` 暴露的字节计数器应对齐 Linux `/proc/net/dev`，即统计 L2 帧字节数（Ethernet frame，不含 FCS）。此前 `count_rx()`/`count_tx()` 传入的是 IP payload 长度（`packet.len()`），缺少 L2 头部的 14 字节（Ethernet header），对短帧还缺少 ETH_ZLEN 补齐部分。需要让 Device 层显式返回 L2 帧长度，使 router 层统计值语义正确。

## 改动

### Device trait 语义变更

`recv()` 和 `send()` 返回值从 `bool`（有无包）改为 `usize`（L2 帧字节数）：

- **`recv() -> usize`**：返回入站 IP 包的 L2 帧字节数；ARP 等非 IP 帧记录到内部延迟队列后返回 0
- **`send() -> usize`**：返回实际发出的 L2 帧字节数；排队等待（如 ARP 未就绪）或发送失败返回 0
- 新增 **`drain_deferred_tx() -> Vec<usize>`**：收集 `recv()` 期间异步发出的帧长度（ARP 请求与应答），每次调用清空内部累加器
- 新增 **`drain_deferred_rx() -> Vec<usize>`**：收集 `recv()` 期间收到的非 IP 帧长度（ARP 请求/应答及其他已通过 L2 有效性检查的帧），每次调用清空内部累加器

### 各 Device 实现

| 实现 | recv 返回值 | send 返回值 | drain_deferred |
|------|------------|------------|----------------|
| **EthernetDevice** | IP 帧：raw Ethernet frame 长度；非 IP：0（长度记入 deferred_rx_frame_lens） | 成功：补齐 ETH_ZLEN 的线缆帧长；失败：0 | TX：ARP 请求/应答帧长；RX：ARP 帧及未知 EtherType 的有效 L2 帧长 |
| **Loopback** | 原始数据长度 | 原始数据长度 | 默认空 |
| **Driver (VirtIO)** | 适配新签名 | 适配新签名 | 默认空 |

**EthernetDevice 关键细节**：
- `handle_frame()` 返回值从 `bool` 改为 `usize`（L2 帧长），非 IP 的有效 L2 帧（ARP 及未知 EtherType）记录到 `deferred_rx_frame_lens`
- `send_to()` 返回 `usize`，发送成功后记录到 `deferred_tx_frame_lens`（ARP 请求/应答通过 side channel 发送，不由 TX worker 计数）
- `set_ipv4_addr()` 在重配置前 drain 已积累的延迟帧长并原地计数，避免因 IP 地址变化丢失已成功交给设备的 TX 统计事件

### Router 层

- TX worker：`count_tx(frame_len)`，frame_len 来自 `device.send()` 返回值，仅非零时计数
- RX worker：轮询循环中 `recv()` 返回的 (packet, frame_len) 压入持久 `local_batch` FIFO，再通过 `drain_local_batch_step()` 推入共享 RX 队列；每次迭代后调用 `drain_deferred_tx()` / `drain_deferred_rx()` 统计 side channel 帧
- 新增 `drain_local_batch_step()` 辅助函数：生产 worker 与测试共用，保证 frame_len:packet 1:1 配对在背压场景下不脱钩

### 测试

**router 层 `l2_counter_tests`（12 个用例）**：

- `count_rx_accumulates_bytes_and_packets` / `count_tx_accumulates_bytes_and_packets` — 累加正确性
- `stats_starts_at_zero` / `stats_reflects_current_counters_after_counting` — 计数器生命周期
- `send_returns_frame_len_tx_counts_l2_not_ip_payload` — TX 统计 L2 帧长而非 IP payload
- `send_returns_zero_no_tx_counted` / `recv_returns_zero_no_rx_counted` — 零值不计数
- `recv_returns_frame_len_rx_counts_it` — RX 统计 L2 帧长
- `drain_deferred_tx_default_returns_empty_vec` / `drain_deferred_rx_default_returns_empty_vec` — 默认无延迟帧
- `rx_backpressure_preserves_frame_len_pairing` — 背压下 frame_len 与 packet 配对不脱钩
- `rx_worker_three_path_combined_drain` — RX worker 三条路径组合 drain

**ethernet 层 `arp_counter_tests`（9 个用例）**：

- `arp_request_tx_is_counted_in_drain_deferred_tx` / `arp_reply_tx_is_counted_in_drain_deferred_tx` — ARP TX 帧经 drain_deferred_tx 统计
- `arp_request_rx_is_counted_in_drain_deferred_rx` / `arp_reply_rx_is_counted_in_drain_deferred_rx` — ARP RX 帧经 drain_deferred_rx 统计
- `consecutive_arp_frames_accumulate_in_drain_deferred_rx` — 连续 ARP 帧累加
- `send_to_wire_len_respects_eth_zlen_padding` — ETH_ZLEN 补齐
- `combined_arp_ip_recv_drain_cycle` — ARP+IP 混合接收 drain 周期
- `set_ipv4_addr_preserves_undrained_frame_lens` — 重配置保留未 drain 的帧
- `unknown_ethertype_frame_is_counted_in_drain_deferred_rx` — 非 ARP 未知 EtherType 帧计数

## 提交

```
f5db842e8 fix(ax-net): preserve deferred counters on reconfig, count non-ARP frames, and extract drain helper
17aa03629 fix(ax-net): refine L2 frame counter drain API and add integration tests
1729ba360 style(ax-net): apply cargo fmt to router.rs l2_counter_tests
d5d50d8f0 feat(starry,ax-net): return L2 frame length from Device send/recv for net_stats byte counters
```

## 文件变更

```
 net/ax-net/src/device/driver.rs   |  13 +-
 net/ax-net/src/device/ethernet.rs | 677 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 net/ax-net/src/device/loopback.rs |  13 +-
 net/ax-net/src/device/mod.rs      |  49 ++-
 net/ax-net/src/router.rs          | 563 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 5 files changed, 1227 insertions(+), 88 deletions(-)
```

author: glowwserrano7
body:
## Summary

Adds `run_on_bind`, a standalone plugin that executes host or guest commands when a guest
service binds a port exposed to the host by the VPN plugin.

This started as an extension to `fetch_web`. It is split into its own plugin so that:

- `fetch_web` remains responsible only for detecting web services and retrieving content.
- Bind-triggered execution works for any service, not just HTTP/HTTPS.
- Command execution can be tested independently of web fetching.

## Changes

### New: `run_on_bind` 

- Subscribes to the VPN `on_bind` event and filters by `proto`, `ports`, and an optional
  `endpoints` allowlist. No longer limited to ports 80/443.
- De-duplicates per endpoint, and drains a queue from a single worker thread so two
  simultaneous binds can never produce concurrent `guest_cmd.py` invocations.
- **Host mode**: runs on the host (inside the container), with the working directory set to
  penguin's `proj_dir` argument.
- **Guest mode** (default): runs inside the emulated guest via `guest_cmd.py`. Requires
  `core.guest_cmd: true`.
- `delay` (default 20s) before running, and a per-command `timeout` (default 120s) so an
  unresponsive guest cannot hang the run.
- An attempt succeeds if **any** configured command succeeds. Configurations routinely
  include commands that only apply to some targets, so requiring all of them to pass would
  keep retrying endpoints on account of commands that were never going to work.
- A failed attempt is not terminal: the next endpoint to bind gets its own try, uncapped.
  This keeps a run from wedging when the first endpoint to appear (often a loopback bind)
  isn't the one that works. The first successful attempt is the last.
- `shutdown_after_cmd` ends the emulation after the first successful attempt.
- Writes `run_on_bind_output.txt` — one block per command per attempt, recording endpoint,
  attempt, mode, command, `Status: SUCCESS|FAILED`, return code, stdout and stderr. Every
  command is recorded regardless of outcome, including timeouts and missing executables.

### New: `run_on_bind_testing` 

- `host_marker`: a file a host-mode command is expected to create. Relative paths resolve
  against `proj_dir` — the same working directory host commands run in — so a command
  writing a relative path and this check agree on where the file lands. `results/…` resolves
  against the output directory; absolute paths are used as-is.
- `output_contains`: strings expected in `run_on_bind_output.txt`.
- `wait_timeout` (default 30): polls for each expected file rather than sleeping a fixed
  interval, so a passing run finishes as soon as the files appear.
- Writes results to `run_on_bind_test.txt`.

### `fetch_web_testing` scoped back to fetch_web only

Removed `cmd_on_bind_marker`, `cmd_on_bind_guest_output_contains`, and `cmd_wait_timeout`;
those checks now live in `run_on_bind_testing`. Web-service verification (the
`web_<ip>_<port>` output files) is unchanged.


## Example

```yaml
core:
  guest_cmd: true
  timeout: 600

plugins:
  run_on_bind:
    ports: [80]
    commands:
      - mode: host
        run:
          - touch hello.txt
      - mode: guest
        run:
          - echo "im here" > /tmp/temp.txt && cat /tmp/temp.txt
    shutdown_after_cmd: true

  run_on_bind_testing:
    host_marker: hello.txt
    output_contains:
      - here
    wait_timeout: 30
```

This verifies that host-mode commands create the expected marker file and that guest-mode
commands execute and produce the expected output.

`commands` also accepts a bare string or a list of strings, both of which default to guest
mode:

```yaml
  run_on_bind:
    commands: python3 example.py
```

## Running alongside `fetch_web`

The two plugins share no state — separate subscriptions, queues, worker threads and output
files — but either can end the emulation. When both are loaded, enable at most one shutdown
flag (`shutdown_after_cmd`, `shutdown_after_www`, `shutdown_on_failure`); otherwise whichever
finishes first calls `end_analysis()` and truncates the other's in-flight work. To let both
complete, leave all three unset and bound the run with `core.timeout`, which is otherwise
unbounded.

body:
## Summary
- Removes the unused, ~18-year-old vendor script `com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` (AJILE 1.2.1, a 2003–2007 JS module loader) and its `js.txt` clientlib entry from the on-prem connector's `brightcoveadmin` author tools clientlib.
- Requested by **Mercer** (BGS-1706 / SFDC 01587171) to clear a recurring DOM-based XSS finding flagged by their security scanner, which is blocking a compliance audit (hard deadline 2026-07-16).
- Ships in the next on-prem `6.0.x`-prem build — the track that actually applies to Mercer (AEM 6.5, on-prem). A version upgrade does **not** clear the finding because ajile is present in every on-prem tag including the latest `6.0.12-prem`.

## Context
Mercer's SAST tooling flags `com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` as DOM-based XSS. The file is a generic third-party module loader that traces `window.location.href` (`:555`, `:689`) into a dynamically-injected `<script>` `src` (`:1007`, `:1031`, `:1033`) and a `setTimeout` string eval (`:1011`, `:1047`) — a textbook tainted-source→sink pattern that any DOM-XSS rule matches. It is **dead code**: the only reference in the whole tree is the `js.txt` manifest line; there are **zero `aja.*` calls** anywhere in `current/`. It loads only in the classic author console (`channels="[!touch]"`, under `/apps/.../tools/`), never on visitor pages or players — so the theoretical XSS is author-instance-only and, in any case, the loader is never invoked. Because the file is not exploitable-yet-not-suppressible, the only durable remediation is to stop shipping it. Deleting it + its manifest line is fully non-breaking.

## References
- 💬 **Slack thread:** Escalation posted in `#external-brightcove-ts-escalations` (C03SY03N11U, ts `1783704412.344369`) — "Mercer's security scanning has flagged a DOM-based XSS vulnerability in `com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js`". (No permalink was captured on the request row; BGS-1706 below is the canonical record.)
- 🎫 **Jira:** [BGS-1706 — Mercer | AEM Connector — DOM XSS Vulnerability](https://brightcove.atlassian.net/browse/BGS-1706) — High, BGS Managed Services; today's comment from David Yael Hernandez already scoped ajile as removable.
- 🎫 **SFDC:** `01587171` — "Request for Updated Vendor JavaScript / Guidance on DOM XSS Vulnerability" (Pending-Internal, 2026-06-18) — the originating Mercer TS case.
- 🔗 **Companion PR (cloud track):** `brightcove/Adobe-AEM-Brightcove-Connector` branch `fix/2cb3424d-remove-ajile-cloud` (off `cloud-master`) — the same removal for the 7.2.x-cloud build.
- 📂 **Code refs:** `.../brightcoveadmin/clientlibs/js.txt:4` (the manifest entry removed); `.../js/vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` (the file deleted); `.content.xml` `channels="[!touch]"` (author-only).

## Diff at a glance
| File | Change | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `.../brightcoveadmin/clientlibs/js.txt` | drop `vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` line | +0/-1 |
| `.../brightcoveadmin/clientlibs/js/vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` | delete unused vendor file | +0/-1540 |

Total: 2 files, +0/-1541.

## How it works
Single-clientlib, no-code change — no Mermaid diagram warranted. AEM builds the `brc.brightcove-api` clientlib category from `js.txt`; removing the file + its manifest line means the connector no longer serves the script to the author console. Because nothing calls the `aja` global, no admin functionality changes.

## Test plan
- [ ] `mvn clean install` builds `ui.apps` cleanly (no missing-resource error from `js.txt`).
- [ ] Deploy to an AEM 6.5 author instance; open the Brightcove admin tools console (Library Management Console) — verify all admin actions (account list, asset search, insert video/playlist) work; confirm no `aja is not defined` / 404 for the removed script in the browser console/network tab.
- [ ] Re-run the customer's SAST scan (or an equivalent DOM-XSS scan) against the built package — confirm the `com.iskitz.ajile` finding is gone.
- [ ] CI checks green.

## Rollback
Plain `git revert` is safe — no state migration, no data touched. The file is self-contained vendor code with no consumers, so reverting simply re-adds the (unused) script and its manifest line.

## Related conversation
Generated as a follow-up to a customer triage request handled by the etri-assistant. Full investigation at:
`http://assistant.localhost:4244/requests/2cb3424d-c542-42a0-8727-6575a8c111ab` (private to ETRI).

🤖 Investigated and drafted by [@etri-claw](https://github.com/apps/etri-claw) (etri-assistant), powered by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

author: justmaier
body:
## What

Watchdog for the one failure mode the existing `is_finished()` panic check cannot see: a background rebuild worker that HANGS (thread alive, never sends). Today that leaves `bucket_rebuild_in_flight` stuck true forever, silently disabling all future rebuilds — tb add-path misses then accumulate unhealed in every period feed.

Mechanism: spawn time is stamped; if an in-flight worker produces nothing for **max(1200s, 4× rebuild interval)** (healthy scan ≈ 10s at 107M), log loudly, abandon it (leak the thread — it holds only snapshot Arcs; a late result is still drained and re-validated harmlessly by the existing apply loop), and re-arm with the standard 60s retry backdate. Trip condition is a pure function with unit tests (None never trips, mid-scan never trips, strict-> at horizon, interval scaling, saturation).

## Post-mortem: the 2026-07-10 "rebuild scheduler stall" (task #17)

**Verdict: the stall almost certainly never existed.** Evidence timeline:

1. Suspected v1.1.37 stall: repeated `kubectl logs --since=X | grep 'FULL rebuild'` on bitdex-0 returned zero across 75+ min; interval atomic confirmed 300 via PATCH log line. Filed as worker-hang-leaves-in_flight-stuck.
2. Post-v1.1.38 roll it appeared to reproduce: bitdex-1 (passive) logged 3 rebuilds/12min, bitdex-0 (active) logged zero. Load-correlation hypotheses (busy-cycle skip / hung worker) were investigated in code — **no gating path exists**: the rebuild block runs every flush iteration, and no loop-body-depth flow control precedes it.
3. Live thread inventory on bitdex-0 showed no `bitdex-tbucket-rebuild` thread AND no spawn/panic/completion logs — contradictory under every hang theory.
4. **Root cause of the observations:** bitdex-0's retained kubectl log spans ~78 SECONDS — per-query INFO logging on the serving pod churns rotation so fast that `--since` greps see only the last minute. Every zero-count was rotation blindness. The passive pod logs slowly, so its rebuilds were visible — manufacturing the load-correlation.
5. Metric-grade check (counters don't rotate): `bitdex_time_bucket_full_rebuild_total` on bitdex-0 went 3 → 5 over 400s — **healthy 300s cadence**. Historical counter readings (67 rebuilds over 3.6h last night ≈ 3.2min at the then-180s interval) were also healthy. No metric has ever shown a stall.
6. #306 (fuse-once) is NOT what the scan needed: `scan_fresh_in_window` reconstructs via `fused_contains` point queries and never materialized layers per scan.

**Lessons wired into this PR:** the watchdog message + docs point at the counter as the reliable signal; the trip horizon is generous because a false trip is nearly free. Ops lesson (runbook): on the serving pod, never diagnose scheduler liveness from logs — use `bitdex_time_bucket_full_rebuild_total` deltas.

## Tests
- `test_rebuild_watchdog_trip_conditions`, `test_rebuild_watchdog_horizon_floor_and_scale` (pure fn, 2/2 green)
- Full lib suite running at PR time; watchdog integration compiles into the flush loop with state cleared on all three reset paths (completion, panic-detect, watchdog).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: antoinetoussaint
body:
Closes #309.

## Summary
- **Dismissability ≠ persistence.** Severity conflated the two: a
  transient error you wanted gone *now* made you wait out its 5s/15s
  fade, and a sticky Permanent/Auth error (like the merge false-error in
  #305) had no clear key to swat it. Now `Esc` clears the current footer
  notice regardless of severity; severity still only decides whether a
  notice *auto*-fades.
- **A durable half for the transient footer.** Notices flash *and*
  accumulate in a bounded ring, surfaced by a new `Shift-M` messages
  window — so "an error flashed and I missed it" / "what was that error
  again?" is answerable. Severity-colored, scrollable, `c` to clear.
- **Errors stay messages, never modal.** Provider errors are mostly
  transient background hiccups (sync retry, rate-limit); routing them
  through modals would seize the whole UI during polling, against
  lazybox's reactive-inbox ethos. They belong in the notice/log stream.

## Design notes
- `DismissNotice` is a first-class catalog action (default `Esc`,
  remappable via `ui.action_keys.dismiss_notice`) so it shows in `?`
  help. It's routed through an explicit branch in `handle_pane_key`
  rather than generic catalog dispatch, sequenced *after* the
  leader/`]]` cancels and gated on a notice actually being up. That lets
  `Esc` keep yielding to its two established owners: a live terminal
  (Esc reaches the PTY) and a sidebar `v` multi-select (Esc drops the
  selection first, then a second Esc clears the notice).
- Every non-hint notice is recorded in `StatusCtx::messages` from the
  single `flash()` choke point. One-shot Hints (`scroll: alt-screen`)
  are excluded as ephemeral UI nudges.
- The messages window mirrors the existing `Shift-D` sync-status window
  (read-only overlay, dismiss-on-outside-click); `c` sends
  `Msg::MessagesCleared`, which wipes the log and re-renders the window
  on its empty placeholder.

Per #309's own note, once #305 lands the merge case produces no error at
all — but the dismissability + log gap is general, so this stands alone.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build -p lazybox-tui` / `cargo clippy` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p lazybox-tui-core` (194) and `-p lazybox-tui --lib` (847) green
- [x] New `dismiss_and_messages_tests`: Esc dismisses a sticky notice; Esc is inert with a quiet footer; **Esc yields to a sidebar multi-select** (clears selection first, notice survives, second Esc clears it); `flash` logs all non-hint notices; `Shift-M` opens the window; `c` clears the log and keeps the window open
- [x] New `Messages` component tests: empty placeholder, severity+age rendering, scroll/clear/dismiss key routing
- [x] Existing catalog collision-detector and `?`-help tests still pass with the two new Global bindings

## Summary
- Removes the same unused vendor script `com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` and its `js.txt` entry from the **Cloud (AEMaaCS) 7.x** connector, where the clientlib was restructured under `clientlibs/clientlib-tools/`.
- Companion to the on-prem removal (`fix/2cb3424d-remove-ajile-onprem` off `master`); this branch targets the next `7.2.x-cloud` build for parity so no AEMaaCS customer's scanner re-flags it.
- Directly satisfies the "next Cloud (7.2.x) build" half of Mercer's ask (BGS-1706), even though Mercer themselves run on-prem.

## Context
Identical finding and identical fix as the on-prem PR, on the other mainline. In the cloud tree ajile lives at `clientlibs/clientlib-tools/js/vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` (the 7.x AEMaaCS clientlib reorganization moved it out of `components/tools/brightcoveadmin/`). It is byte-identical to the on-prem copy and equally unused: the only reference is `clientlib-tools/js.txt:8`, with **zero `aja.*` consumers** on `cloud-master`, and the clientlib is `channels="[!touch]"` (author-only). Deleting the file + its manifest line is non-breaking.

## References
- 💬 **Slack thread:** Escalation in `#external-brightcove-ts-escalations` (C03SY03N11U, ts `1783704412.344369`).
- 🎫 **Jira:** [BGS-1706 — Mercer | AEM Connector — DOM XSS Vulnerability](https://brightcove.atlassian.net/browse/BGS-1706).
- 🎫 **SFDC:** `01587171` — "Request for Updated Vendor JavaScript / Guidance on DOM XSS Vulnerability" (Pending-Internal, 2026-06-18).
- 🔗 **Companion PR (on-prem track):** branch `fix/2cb3424d-remove-ajile-onprem` (off `master`) — the removal that actually unblocks Mercer's 6.5 on-prem deployment.
- 📂 **Code refs:** `.../clientlib-tools/js.txt:8` (manifest entry removed); `.../clientlib-tools/js/vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` (file deleted).

## Diff at a glance
| File | Change | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `.../clientlib-tools/js.txt` | drop `vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` line | +0/-1 |
| `.../clientlib-tools/js/vendor/com.iskitz.ajile.1.2.1.flat.js` | delete unused vendor file | +0/-1540 |

author: huangruiteng
body:
Closes #1823

## Motivation

The issue-fix domain already persisted feasibility and PR lifecycle evidence, and the Lark sink already rendered outcome projections, but the default goal sync only wrote todo cards. Operators had to manually compose and sync the issue read model, so issue-oriented views could remain empty after a PR was published.

## Implementation

- add an optional public-safe `--issue-ref` link to PR lifecycle observations; no title or branch-name inference
- derive a goal-level outcome collection from existing feasibility and explicitly linked lifecycle ledgers without adding an outcome ledger
- make default `lark-kanban sync-loopx-todos` upsert stable issue outcome rows beside todo rows
- keep unlinked feasibility rows visible as work in progress and report unlinked lifecycle rows without guessing
- document the contract in the English and Chinese capability guides and the Lark adapter

## Validation

- `python3 examples/issue-fix-pr-lifecycle-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/issue-fix-outcome-projection-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/lark-kanban-control-plane-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/issue-fix-capability-guide-smoke.py`
- `python3 examples/issue-fix-workflow-contract-smoke.py`
- `python3 -m loopx.cli --format json check`
- `loopx canary premerge --from-git-diff`: 17/17 selected checks passed, no failures, warnings, or manual holds; public/private boundary clean

## Risk and non-goals

The join is intentionally exact on repository plus explicit issue reference. Existing lifecycle rows without that link remain unassociated until replayed; they are not guessed. Automatic projection reuses existing domain state and does not persist delivery evidence or create a parallel state machine. No credentials, local runtime state, raw logs, private material, or local paths are included.

body:
## What changed

### Buffet counter → a cart (`5488e3f`)
- Prices were a bare number that didn't read as a price — each chip now shows a gold **"N mi"** pill.
- Tapping no longer buys instantly. You **select treats into a cart** (gold highlight), see a running total and what you'll have left, then hit **Purchase · N mi ✦** to buy the whole order at once. Funds + the ticket-home reserve are checked against the total, and the button disables with the reason shown when it won't go through. Owned items are dimmed and not selectable.
- Shop feedback used to fire as a toast **behind the blurred game view** (unreadable); it now lives in a status line inside the panel.

### A starter book + a distinct Novel (`7127db6`)
- The barebones backpack was a touch too bare — you now set off owning a **book** alongside your headphones (existing saves get it once via a `starterKit` migration, so it won't re-grant if you drop it).
- Since you can't buy what you own, the buffet's book slot becomes a distinct new read — a **Novel** with its own render.

### Hand-drawn book art (`4a26c7f`)
Six hand-drawn book sprites replace the procedural/emoji ones:
- your starter book is the **open book**, laid out on the table;
- the buffet's Novel is the **navy closed hardback**;
- passengers reading a book each show one of **four closed colours** (navy/brown/maroon/green), deterministic per seat, so the carriage isn't everyone holding the same book;
- the **orange+teal stack** sits on the buffet counter as reads-for-sale.

Removed the now-unused old `bookImg`; kept small procedural fallbacks so nothing blanks before the sprites load.

Headless: cart selection with running total, reserve block (disabled button + in-panel reason), combined purchase and single deduction, owned-item message, headphone-colour buying; fresh save owns headphones + book, shop offers Novel not Book, dropped book persists across reload without re-granting; open book + navy novel render on the player table, an NPC reads a green book, the stack shows on the buffet counter. ## Summary

`test_consecutive_order` flaked on main ([failing run](https://github.com/livekit/agents/actions/runs/29038961457/job/86191045556)): when asked "Can I get two mayonnaise sauces?", the LLM occasionally responds with a confirmation question ("Just to confirm, you want two separate mayonnaise sauces added to your order?") instead of calling `order_regular_item` twice, so the state assertion sees 0 items.

author: pkgdemon
body:
## Why

`nextbsd/main/tests/boot-test.sh` drifted behind the copy in nextbsd-userland. It is the script the **nextbsd-kernel smoke-test fetches** (`build.yml`: `curl .../nextbsd/main/tests/boot-test.sh`) and the ISO build uses — so both inherited the observability problems that made the amd64 boot markers invisible and flaky throughout the #369 investigation.

This blocks upcoming kernel work: validating a kernel change via the smoke-test needs the markers to actually be visible.

## What

Ports the three fixes proven in #369, adapted to this script's structure:

1. **`set boot_mutemsgs=NO`** at the loader `OK` prompt. nextbsd-overlays bakes `boot_mutemsgs="YES"` for a macOS-clean login console; that mutes kernel `printf` for the whole boot. The on-image markers ride the same console, so muted CI times out on markers that *were* emitted. (`RB_MUTEMSGS` gates kernel `printf` only — markers reach the console via the tty, so this never hid userland output; un-muting is purely what makes them visible.) `=NO` not `unset`, because `boot_env_to_howto()` tests `strcasecmp(val,"no") != 0`.
2. **Gate `mach.debug_enable` + `launchd_trace` behind `BOOT_TRACE=1`** (default off). Un-muted, that trace is thousands of blocking kernel `printf`s over the emulated UART — it buries the markers and perturbs the notifyd/syslogd Mach handshake. `BOOT_TRACE=1` restores it for root-cause runs.
3. **`catch { close }` / `catch { wait }`** — a clean halt hits `eof` and auto-closes the spawn, so an explicit `close` throws `spawn id not open` and fails an otherwise-green boot.

No on-image assertions change — only how CI drives the loader and tears down. Brings this copy to parity with nextbsd-userland's `boot-test.sh`.

## Note on divergence

`boot-test.sh` now lives in two repos (here + nextbsd-userland) and has diverged; nextbsd-userland's copy additionally has loader send/echo-race hardening this one lacks. Worth a follow-up to converge them (or share one source), but out of scope here.

Refs: nextbsd-redux/nextbsd#369, nextbsd-redux/nextbsd#363

## H447 — Saraswati trainer suite, Phase 1 (enable-and-connect)

Executes [H447](https://github.com/gasyoun/Uprava/blob/main/handoffs/H447-Sonnet_Systema-Sanscriticum_saraswati_trainer_suite_10.07.26.md) per design doc [SARASWATI_TRAINERS_2026.md](https://github.com/gasyoun/Uprava/blob/main/docs/SARASWATI_TRAINERS_2026.md) §2/§5. Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`) executed in an isolated worktree; verified + shipped by the orchestrating session.

### What landed (Phase 1 only — Phases 2–3 out of scope)
1. **`SRS_ENABLED` flipped on** — [`config/srs.php`](https://github.com/gasyoun/Systema-Sanscriticum/blob/h447-saraswati-trainer/config/srs.php) default `true`; the built+tested FSRS engine is now live.
2. **Cyrillic-only deck** — [`SrsSanskritDeckSeeder`](https://github.com/gasyoun/Systema-Sanscriticum/blob/h447-saraswati-trainer/database/seeders/SrsSanskritDeckSeeder.php): a `sanskrit-cyrillic-only` system deck whose cards carry only `cyrillic`+`translation` (no `devanagari` key), for the true-zero 28-Aug cohort. No IAST→Devanagari conversion involved — sidesteps the broken `iast_to_devanagari`.
3. **Prana XP per review** — `ReviewService::grade()` calls the idempotent `PranaService` with `reason='srs_review'`, `source_id`=the review log; **awarded on wrong answers as well as right** (deliberate, anxiety-sensitive audience). Idempotency unique key prevents double-awards on replay.
4. **Per-trainer stats view** — `SrsController::stats()` + `/dvaram/srs/stats`: per-deck progress bar, correct/incorrect ratio + accuracy %, error list, over `srs_review_logs`.
5. **Leaderboard A/B** — `marathon_enrollments.ab_arm` (new migration), assigned once at enrolment (deterministic 50/50, stable across sessions). Arm A = name-masked (current behavior); Arm B = un-masked.

### 🔒 Privacy safety
**Arm B (un-masked real names) defaults OFF** — `marathon.leaderboard_unmask_enabled` defaults `false`. Arm A (masked) ships to everyone; the un-masking path exists and is tested but stays inert **pending an enrolment-consent decision** (`/publish-safety-check` gate). Do not flip the env flag on without that decision.

### ⚠️ @DECIDE for the author — design deviation
Design doc §5 says "hash of `user_id`", but `marathon_enrollments` has **no `user_id`** (only `lead_id` — no account exists yet at enrolment). The arm is hashed from `lead_id` instead (documented in `MarathonEnrollment::computeArm()`; `PranaLeaderboard::armFor()` bridges `User→Lead→enrollment.ab_arm` for rendering). **A human should confirm this substitution** or decide to add a `user_id` column. Arm B being off-by-default means nothing renders from this until that + the consent decision land.

Also fixed a latent bug found en route: `PranaLeaderboard::rows()` dropped `lead_id` from its select, which would have null'd every arm lookup.

### Verification
- **43 tests / 110 assertions pass** (independently re-run: 28 safety-critical incl. the Arm-B masking matrix + XP idempotency + flag-gating, all green).
- **Pint clean** on the touched file set (18 files; unrelated repo-wide style drift deliberately not touched).
- Commit `4129847`, explicit-pathspec (no vendor/env leakage).

author: smana
body:
## Why

Instant recall built its BM25 query from `title + message` only (`buildRecallQuery` in `internal/investigate/recall.go`). For a real **label-derived** Kubernetes alert (`KubePodNotReady`, `pod=harbor-registry-…`) the discriminating object (namespace/name) lives only in the labels and fed nothing but the structural pre-filter — so the query is ~1–2 generic tokens against a differently-worded runbook ("Harbor Registry Down due to IAM Access Key Quota Limit"). That is the classic **vocabulary-mismatch** problem; measured live it scored **0.096**, an order of magnitude below the production `solo_floor` of 4.0, so recall never fired despite a perfect KB entry.

Crucially, **every existing recall test drops the gates to 0.001–0.01** with a `fakeScored` stub, so the real-threshold failure was **tested nowhere**.

## What

**Part 1 — real-threshold retrieval eval harness** (`internal/investigate/recalleval_test.go`, in-tree, CI-run, no env gate):
- a **real** `catalog.Catalog` (real bleve BM25, no fake scorer) over a **15-entry fixture KB** modeled on `github.com/Smana/runlore-kb`, each runbook **worded differently** from the alert that should match it;
- **15 labeled incident cases** built as raw alerts actually arrive (label-derived: generic alertname, pod/namespace label, terse-or-empty annotation; plus GitOps and negatives), each paired with a **list** of acceptable targets (multi-ground-truth, per the IBM RCA finding);
- reports **Recall@1/3/5 + MRR** over pure `SearchScored` ranking (before the gates) and the **short-circuit fire-rate + precision** through `lookup` at **production thresholds** (SoloFloor 4.0), every metric printed via `t.Log`;
- a **pinned baseline regression** that documents the gap honestly (gates are NOT tuned down).

**Part 2 — deterministic query enrichment** (no LLM): `buildRecallQuery` now folds the workload ref (namespace + pod-hash-normalized name) and the alertname (only when it isn't already the title) into the query — LM/entity-expansion in front of BM25. The name is normalized with the **same** function as the structural gate; the ref is additive so the GitOps source (title already carries `Kind/Name`) is not harmed — a dedicated test asserts GitOps runbooks stay top-3.

## Measured before → after (real bleve BM25, production thresholds)

| metric | raw `title+message` | + structured-entity enrichment |
|---|---|---|
| Recall@1 / @3 / @5 | 0.69 / 0.69 / 0.69 | **1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00** |
| MRR | 0.692 | **1.000** |
| fire-rate @ prod gates (SoloFloor 4.0) | 0/11 (0.00) | 0/11 (0.00) |

The 4 "hard" cases (workload identity only in the label, empty annotation) go from **zero BM25 hits → rank #1**.

## Honest verdict

Query enrichment **fully fixes retrieval** but **does NOT close the end-to-end loop**: the enriched top scores (~0.5–1.2) remain an order of magnitude below `SoloFloor` 4.0, so nothing short-circuits at production thresholds. **A reranker (calibrated scores) or a threshold-philosophy change is still required.** The thresholds are deliberately not lowered to manufacture a fire — the harness pins fire-rate at 0 so the gap stays visible, and a future reranker is what should move it. Landing the harness + honest numbers is the win: the gap is now **measured**, at real thresholds, in CI.

## Gate
`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go test ./...`, `-race` on `internal/investigate` + `internal/catalog`, `golangci-lint run ./...` → **0 issues**.

## Diagnóstico e correção

A 1ª execução (16 histórias, orçamento FIXO de palavras por célula) estrangulava o realizador: em R1-n1, ~110 palavras de material contra alvo de 1×25 ⇒ compressão 4–5× ⇒ telegrama sem artigos/verbos ("Vento pula."). A recalibração (C-1..C-5) trocou o teto fixo por orçamento **proporcional ao material** — `alvoPalavras = clamp(round(material×0.45), piso[nível], teto[nível][rodada])`, tabela-semente calibrável — adicionou a regra de **tempo PRESENTE** ao prompt, alinhou a Camada 1 (crescimento medido sobre o ALVO registrado, +25%; aviso de tempo verbal), preservou os lotes antigos em `_pre-recalibracao/` e cobriu tudo com testes sem rede (BLOCO 6). Micro-lote de sanidade (4×R1-n1) aprovado antes do lote completo.

## Grade — PASS Camada 1 (rodada × nível, somando gêneros e temperaturas)

| rodada | n1 | n2 | n3 | n4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 1/18 | 7/18 | 1/18 | 1/18 |
| R2 | 0/18 | 3/18 | 3/18 | 1/18 |
| R3 | 0/18 | 2/18 | 1/18 | 0/18 |
| R4 | 1/18 | 1/18 | 0/21 | 0/18 |

**Total: 22/291 (7,6%).** Por gênero: Joana/f **13/147 (8,8%)** · Pietro/m **9/144 (6,3%)**. Por temperatura: t0.2 9/97 · t0.4 5/97 · t0.7 8/97. Artefatos completos em `saida/avaliacao/` (grade.json · para-leitura.md · reprovados.md · consolidado.md).

## Padrões dos reprovados (agrupados)

1. **Crescimento sobre o alvo — 220 ocorrências (motivo dominante).** O realizador ignora a instrução branda "Alvo: cerca de N palavras" e escreve perto do tamanho do material (estouros típicos de 40–114%, crescendo com a rodada — daí a queda R1→R4 na grade). A QUALIDADE desses textos é alta (a testemunha abaixo reprova só por orçamento); a tensão é entre o fator-semente 0,45 e a verbosidade natural do modelo — exatamente o que a tabela "calibrável" existe para ajustar.
2. **Ritmo n1 — 68 ocorrências.** Consequência do mesmo estouro: mais palavras ⇒ mais pontos finais ⇒ frases/beat acima de 2. Os textos n1 agora têm frases completas (o objetivo da C-1), mas o gate de ritmo herdado pune o volume.
3. **Cauda pequena:** 13 âncoras ausentes, 9 beats sem marca de corpo, 1 gênero, 1 nome — o núcleo de fidelidade está sólido.

## Custo e tempo

291 chamadas Gemini (0 falhas de provedor; 3 lotes da t0.7 regenerados após queda de rede LOCAL), 230.673 tokens de entrada + 79.801 de saída ≈ **US$ 0,27**, **2h36** de geração + juiz OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) nos 22 aprovados. Detalhe por temperatura em `consolidado.md`.

## Melhor n1 APROVADO — r1-n1-f-p05 (t0.2; fluidez 4 · adequação 4,5 · naturalidade 4)

> O quintal sussurra segredos, Joana quer ver tudo. A grama fria toca seu pé. Uma luz pisca no fundo, os olhos de Joana seguem. Uma folha desce rodando, o dedo de Joana segue. O vento pula o muro, a pele de Joana sente o fresco. O quintal conta tudo, Joana sente os segredos.

## Pior n1 APROVADO — r4-n1-m-p04 (t0.7; fluidez 4 · adequação 4 · naturalidade 3,5)

> O quintal sussurra segredos. Pietro vê uma luz no fundo, um vagalume pisca. Os olhos seguem a pisca. O pé sente a grama fria do orvalho, gotas de luz. Uma folha cai rodando, o dedo segue no ar.
>
> Um gato quieto na cerca, olhos acesos. Ele olha a luz e pisca. Pietro fica em silêncio. A lua grande sobe, prata. O queixo sobe pra ver a lua e a faísca. Pietro segura um pote de vidro, frio e liso, nas duas mãos.

## Testemunha R4×n3 (t0.2) — reprovada SÓ por crescimento (+41% sobre alvo de 157)

> O quintal sussurra segredos, contando um por um a quem vem ver. A grama fria nos pés descalços de Joana faz ela querer descobrir. No canto escuro, uma luzinha acende e apaga: um vaga-lume pisca devagar. Os olhos de Joana seguem a pisca, e ela quer chegar perto na ponta dos pés. Um pote de vidro na grama, frio e liso, entorta o mundo lá dentro. Joana o segura com as duas mãos, fecha um olho e espia. A lua sobe por trás das árvores, enorme e redonda, acendendo com luz de prata. Joana ergue o queixo para ver, a prata acende em seu rosto.
>
> Em cima da cerca, um gato aparece sem barulho, quieto feito sombra, olhos verdes acesos. Joana fica em silêncio, prende a respiração, troca um olhar demorado. O vento chega rolando por cima do muro, fresco, corre pelo quintal, mexendo em tudo. A pele dos braços de Joana arrepia, o cabelo dela mexe. O vento sacode os galhos, uma coisinha se solta, descendo rodando. Uma folha se solta do galho mais alto e desce no ar escuro, sem pressa. O dedo de Joana acompanha cada volta, sua mão fica aberta, espalmada, esperando. A folha desce rodando na frente do gato, que acompanha de olhos arregalados, e o quintal colhe a vontade de Joana em sua mão aberta.

## Antes/depois da recalibração — mesmo estado (r1-n1-f-p01, t0.2, material 103 palavras)

**ANTES (orçamento fixo 1×25):**

> Quintal sussurra, Joana quer ver. Grama fria. Folha rodando, dedo segue. Luz pisca, olhos seguem. Vento fresco, pele sente. Contou.

**DEPOIS (alvo proporcional 46):**

> O quintal sussurra segredos. Joana quer ver. A grama fria no pé. Uma folha desce rodando. O dedo de Joana segue no ar. Uma luz pisca no fundo. Os olhos de Joana seguem a pisca. O vento pula o muro. A pele de Joana sente o fresco. O quintal contou tudo.

---

🛑 **Parada Dura 2 — NÃO MESCLAR.** O merge é o veredito humano: a leitura em voz alta do autor decide, incluindo o CRITÉRIO do fase12-12-05 (n1: realizador ou A+ cru). A grade sugere que a próxima calibração está no fator 0,45 vs. a instrução branda de alvo (e no gate de ritmo n1) — decisão do autor, não deste PR.

author: bobbiebarker
body:
## Summary

Added a new Credo check, `ForgeCredoChecks.NoApplicationGetEnvInLib`, that flags `Application.get_env/2,3` calls inside `lib/` source files (the default scope), steering authors toward `Application.compile_env/2,3` for compile-time values or `Application.fetch_env!/2` for runtime-set values that must fail loudly. The check matches only the `:get_env` reader atom, so `compile_env` is structurally excluded by construction rather than suppressed by an allowlist. Scope is gated by an `included_paths` param (default `[~r"^lib/"]`) checked before the AST prewalk, and a single `allowed_paths` param (default `[]`) permits the rare `lib/` module that legitimately reads runtime config. `fetch_env`/`fetch_env!` are deliberately out of scope.

## Why

`Application.get_env/2,3` silently returns `nil` or a stale value when the application environment is not yet loaded — a bug class that is invisible in `mix` and surfaces only in a packaged release during boot ordering. Nothing in the library previously prevented this pattern inside `lib/`, where `compile_env` is almost always the correct reader.

## Changes Made

- `lib/forge_credo_checks/no_application_get_env_in_lib.ex` (new): the check module. `use Credo.Check` with `param_defaults: [included_paths: [~r"^lib/"], allowed_paths: []]`; `@env_readers [:get_env]` hardcoded module attribute; `run/2` early-returns `[]` when the source file path is out of scope via `in_scope?/2`, then `Credo.Code.prewalk/3` with a `traverse/3` clause matching `{{:., _, [{:__aliases__, _, [:Application]}, fun]}, meta, args}` when `fun in @env_readers`; issues emitted through `format_issue/2`.
- `lib/forge_credo_checks.ex`: added `NoApplicationGetEnvInLib` to the `@moduledoc` registry list.
- `test/forge_credo_checks/no_application_get_env_in_lib_test.exs` (new): 13 fixture tests covering both directions and near-misses.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: added an entry under `## Unreleased` / `### Added` naming the check and its param surface.

## Acceptance Criteria Addressed

- [x] `ForgeCredoChecks.NoApplicationGetEnvInLib` exists at `lib/forge_credo_checks/no_application_get_env_in_lib.ex` and is listed in the `ForgeCredoChecks` `@moduledoc` registry in `lib/forge_credo_checks.ex`.
- [x] The check declares exactly one path-allowlist param `allowed_paths` (default `[]`) plus a scope param `included_paths` (default `[~r"^lib/"]`); no `compile_env_allowed_paths` param exists.
- [x] `run_check` fixture: `Application.get_env(:app, :key)` in a `lib/*.ex` source file yields exactly one issue.
- [x] Fixture: `Application.compile_env(:app, :key)` in a `lib/*.ex` file yields NO issue, asserted with NO allowlist param set.
- [x] Fixture: a `lib/*.ex` file whose path matches the `allowed_paths` param yields NO issue for `get_env`.
- [x] Fixture: passing an `allowed_paths` override flips a previously-flagged `get_env` file to no-issue.
- [x] Fixture: `Application.get_env` in a non-`lib/` file (e.g. `test/foo_test.exs`) yields NO issue.
- [x] Fixture: `Application.fetch_env(:app, :key)` / `Application.fetch_env!(:app, :key)` in a `lib/*.ex` file yields NO issue (explicitly out of scope).
- [x] `mix credo --strict`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix test`, `mix format --check-formatted` pass; `CHANGELOG.md` gains a `## Unreleased` entry naming the check.

## Decisions Made

- Single `allowed_paths` list only (no `compile_env_allowed_paths`), per the Additive Grooming Notes: because `@env_readers` is hardcoded to `[:get_env]`, `compile_env` is excluded by construction — it never matches the traverse clause — so a second allowlist would be dead config. This is directly asserted with no param set.
- `included_paths` is checked before the prewalk (early `[]` return), mirroring the established `unsupervised_spawn.ex` / `port_producer_boundary.ex` early-return pattern in the codebase.
- Non-binary filenames (e.g. in-memory `"nofile"`) are treated as out of scope: there is no path to gate on, so the check does not fire.
- `fetch_env`/`fetch_env!` recorded as explicitly out of scope for this ticket; a follow-up can add those atoms plus matching fixtures if the consumer wants them.

## Testing

All CI gates pass locally:
- `mix format --check-formatted` — exit 0
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — exit 0
- `mix credo --strict` — 69 checks on 59 files, no issues
- `MIX_ENV=dev mix dialyzer` — Total errors: 0, passed successfully
- `mix test` — 241 passed, 0 failures (including the 13 new tests)

- Symphony CI summary: `mix format --check-formatted && mix credo --strict && mix compile --warnings-as-errors && MIX_ENV=dev mix dialyzer && mix test` ran cleanly on the first attempt.
Fixes FGE-1394

author: jagguji
body:
Follow-up from the #132 review (finding 2).

TypeScript has a second any-flavored intrinsic — `unresolvedType` (`intrinsicName === 'unresolved'`) — used by some unresolvable-reference paths. The #107 detection now matches both `error` and `unresolved`, so a sibling path reaching classify gets the same 🛑-flagged placeholder instead of the silent `'a` salvage.

No author-written `any` carries either intrinsic, so there is no false-positive risk: all 90 goldens and all 9 benchmark baselines are byte-identical. The `error-any-unresolved` fixture remains the executable contract; `docs/TYPE_MAPPING.md`'s ERROR-`any` row now names both intrinsics.

For the other #132 review findings: the report.mjs escaping (finding 1) was already fixed in #132 itself (`mdCell`, CodeQL green pre-merge); the report-bucket blindness reminder (finding 3) is now tracked as #133.

body:
Cierra #118.

## Resumen

bambuddy-cfs tiene K-profiles sincronizados en vivo con la impresora (MQTT, ~20 slots por printer/extruder/nozzle) — no aplica acá, no hay impresora en LAN (ver #121). Se implementa 100% manual.

- `FilamentProfile` gana 3 columnas nullable: `k_value`, `nozzle_diameter` (el K depende del diámetro con el que se calibró) y `calibrated_at`. Sin tabla separada ni FK a printer — CFS no tiene la multiplicidad printer/nozzle/AMS que sí tiene bambuddy, así que columnas directas alcanzan.
- Nuevos campos en el form de "Perfil de impresión (slicer)" del drawer de filamento en Inventario.
- Test nuevo: `k_value` fuera de rango (negativo o >99) → 422.

## Verificación local

- Backend: `py_compile` completo + `test_migrations_smoke.py` (10/10, cadena íntegra).
- Frontend: Vitest (149 tests) + build de InventoryPage — todo verde.
- Depende del job **Tests Backend** de CI (Postgres real) para validar el endpoint end-to-end, no se pudo correr localmente (sin fastapi/sqlalchemy instalados en este entorno).
