author: suttonmay
body:
## Summary

- add explicit effective-graph publication via `save_graph/2`, returning `Docket.GraphRef{graph_id, graph_hash}`
- snapshot each distinct node `config_schema/0` once, canonicalize its complete schema contract, and materialize omitted defaults before graph hashing/storage
- make `start_run/3` and durable graph-semantic signals validate and compile the saved effective document locally without injecting defaults introduced after publication
- permit unbounded cyclic graphs; `max_supersteps` remains an optional graph policy or host/runtime safety limit
- add `Docket.Lifecycle` for run/event start, fenced moment commits, serialized signals, and disposition-to-schedule mapping
- add durable fetch/inspect/cancel/retry/await APIs with strict tenant scope
- separate asynchronous post-commit checkpoint observers from the legacy veto-capable checkpoint committer

## Ownership

- Locked-spec changes moved to DCKT-34 / draft PR #25 as a no-code amendment.
- DCKT-20 owns claimed-vehicle compile-once-per-claim reuse, cache generation, and deployment compatibility.
- DCKT-35 owns unresolved pre-execution compilation-failure claim disposition.
- DCKT-14 now correctly treats graph publication as preceding the atomic run/wake/event start transaction.

## Validation

- `mix format --check-formatted`
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
- regular suite at deterministic low concurrency: 473 tests, 0 failures, 17 excluded
- dependency-free core: 444 tests, 0 failures
- live PostgreSQL migration/claim suites: 17 tests, 0 failures

author: brianlane
body:
## Summary

Adds the embeddable website chat widget (Standard+): businesses paste one script tag into their own website and visitors chat with their coworker — info + lead gen ONLY.

- **Restricted tool surface, enforced at 3 independent layers**: new `WebchatCoworker`/`WebchatCoworkerLocal` agents (deploy-client.sh seed) declare only `webchat_business_knowledge_lookup`, `webchat_capture_lead`, `webchat_calendar_find_slots`, `webchat_calendar_book_appointment`; the tool-call dispatcher allowlists exactly those `webchat_*` names (no SMS/email/call/image fulfilment reachable); the chat-worker's webchat path never runs email/memory sentinel fulfilment and strips any hallucinated `<<EMAIL_SEND>>` blocks.
- **Delivery pipeline**: mirrors the proven PR #79 job queue — `POST /api/widget/message` enqueues `webchat_jobs`, the per-tenant VPS chat-worker claims + calls the local Rowboat (always-stateless forced startAgent, shared owner/SMS spend-cap routing to the free local twin), and the widget polls **only while a turn is in flight and the tab is visible**, with backoff.
- **Migration** `20260819000000_webchat_widget.sql`: `chat_widget_settings`, `webchat_sessions`, `webchat_messages`, `webchat_jobs` (all RLS-on/no-policies) + claim/reclaim RPCs, and widens the contact channel set with `webchat` so captured leads roll up to the Contacts page.
- **Auth model**: public site key (`ncw_pub_…`, plaintext by design) + per-session bearer (`ncws_…`, sha256-stored, 7-day idle TTL). Origin allowlist enforced by a per-tenant `frame-ancestors` CSP on `/widget/frame` (the global no-framing header now excludes exactly that path) plus a soft Referer check; per-IP/per-session rate limits and a per-business rolling-24h message ceiling protect the tenant's AI budget.
- **Dashboard**: Settings card (enable, embed snippet, key rotation, allowed origins, pre-chat form toggle, theming), new "Web chat" section with session list + transcripts, and a `webchat` agent key under Settings → Coworker tools.
- **Marketing**: pricing comparison row + features entry (Standard+).

Tier gate is server-side everywhere (`src/lib/webchat/tier-gate.ts`); Starter tenants see upgrade CTAs and the public API refuses even an enabled row.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 7,032 tests green, 100% line/branch/function coverage held (7 new webchat suites: keys, tier gate, origins/theme schema, prompt building, db accessors, request auth/service, lead capture)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` green
- [x] `bash -n deploy-client.sh`; jq workflow seed compiled and verified to emit the 6 agents with the restricted webchat tool list
- [ ] Post-merge: apply migration, fleet-redeploy chat-worker (`tsx debug/update-all-vps.ts`), enable on a Standard tenant and smoke the embed end-to-end

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large new anonymous public API with embed CSP and a deliberately narrow tool allowlist; misconfiguration could expose chat or allow abuse of tenant AI budget, and worker/migration deploy is required for end-to-end behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **Standard+ website chat widget** so businesses embed one script (`public/widget.js`) that opens an iframe to `/widget/frame` and keeps chat UI and credentials on the New Coworker origin.
> 
> **Public surface:** New `/api/widget/session`, `/message`, and `/poll` routes authenticate with a tenant site key plus per-session bearer, apply rate limits and a rolling daily message cap, and enqueue `webchat_jobs` for VPS workers (poll-based delivery for anonymous visitors). **`next.config.ts`** excludes `/widget/frame` from global `frame-ancestors 'none'` so the frame route can set per-tenant embed CSP; **`src/proxy.ts`** exempts `/api/widget/*` from CSRF.
> 
> **Restricted AI surface:** A new **`webchat`** agent in the tool registry and Rowboat dispatcher allowlists only knowledge lookup, lead capture, and calendar tools—no SMS/email/call paths. **`webchat_capture_lead`** writes activity logs and merges leads into sessions/contacts.
> 
> **Owners:** Dashboard widget settings API and UI (snippet, origins, pre-chat form, theme, key rotation), **Web chat** session list and read-only transcripts, and marketing/pricing updates. **Migration** adds widget settings, sessions, messages, jobs (RLS, no policies), claim RPCs, and **`webchat`** as a contact channel.

author: brullik
body:
### Motivation

- The v4 semantic audit was failing with "adjacent grid ratio is not constant" due to lossy 10-decimal JSON rounding of float64 grid levels which breaks low-priced symbols.  
- The outcome build is also too slow because it re-filters full symbol frames repeatedly, rescans SL for each grid count, accumulates all rows in memory, and uses a fixed small worker count.  
- The goal is to preserve existing economic semantics while providing lossless grid-level serialization, a numerically robust audit, a non-destructive repair path for past runs, and a scaffolding for a much faster core.  
- Keep all economic IDs/labels/interval fields unchanged while only changing grid serialization and audit metadata.

### Description

- Replace lossy rounding in `levels_json` with float64 round-trip-safe JSON and add the canonical `GRID_LEVELS_SERIALIZATION_VERSION = "float64_roundtrip_v1"`, and emit `grid_levels_serialization_version` on outcome rows.  
- Harden `scripts/audit_outcome_semantics.py` to validate serialization version, endpoints, strict monotonicity, and adjacent ratios in log-space with scale-aware tolerances and record the first failing row diagnostic.  
- Add `scripts/repair_outcome_grid_serialization.py` which reads a source run and writes a new target run by regenerating only canonical grid geometry fields (`geometric_grid_levels_json` and `grid_levels_serialization_version`), rebuilding summaries, running the audit, comparing non-grid invariants, and writing a machine-readable repair report.  
- Add fast-core scaffolding and orchestration changes: `src/bybit_grid/research/outcome_core/symbol_arrays.py`, `outcome_fast.py`, `outcome_reference.py`, `scripts/benchmark_outcome_cores.py`, `scripts/profile_outcome_core.py`, and updates to `scripts/build_candidate_outcomes.py` to support `--core reference|numpy_fast_v2`, `--executor`, `--workers auto`, streaming symbol-at-a-time writes, improved progress/telemetry and an enriched `outcome_perf.json`; also update review-pack maker/checker to require the repair report.

### Testing

- Environment and lint checks: `python scripts/check_numeric_environment.py` and `python -m pip check` succeeded and `ruff check .` passed.  
- Automated tests: `python -m pytest -q` completed with `132 passed` (including the new `tests/test_sprint_04_5_outcome_core.py` tests for low-price serialization round-trip, symbol arrays, and reference-vs-fast parity).  
- Targeted unit tests: `tests/test_sprint_04_5_outcome_core.py` passed (low-price regression asserts exact float JSON round-trip and log-ratio error < 1e-12).  
- Note: repaired-run generation, full semantic audit of the repaired run, and reference vs fast benchmarks were not executed locally because the repository in this environment does not contain the processed `data/processed/outcome_runs` and raw market partitions; the scripts are in place and should be run on the owner machine with data present.

author: stephtea
body:
Polishes the ordinance flow chat after the smooth-streaming reconciliation, and adds one shared-runtime capability the chat needed.

What changed and why:

- Restore the "Thinking..." indicator. The smooth-streaming rewrite had narrowed it so it only showed before the first token; it no longer covered the wait while the agent composes a clarify question. It now shows in the initial compose gap and while a tool's arguments generate, and never over text that is actively typing.

- Restore the subtle-gray source pill. The ordinance clarify widget's source chip had reverted to the styleguide default bordered surface; override it back to the understated bg-muted / muted-text pill that matches the Lovable prototype and the briefings source pills. The favicon letter-badge is unchanged.

- Stop the double lead-in before a clarify question. The clarify prompt let the model write a lead-in, search, then write a second lead-in, so the first turn read "Let's start with X. [search] Let's start with Y." It now writes one lead-in, then any research, then straight to the question.

- Stream a "generating" signal. The runtime only emitted tool_call once its arguments were complete, so the gap where the clarify question generates had no signal (the question and options ARE the tool's arguments). Surface the AI SDK's tool-input-start through a new transient tool_input_start stream chunk (llm.service to chatStream to SSE to chatClient). It is not persisted as a segment, and other chat surfaces ignore the new type. The ordinance chat uses it to show "Writing your question..." while the question generates.

- Stop tool pills shimmering after the tool finishes. The live turn shimmered every pill for the whole turn; now running is tracked per tool segment (set on tool_call, cleared on tool_result), so a "Searching the web" pill stops as soon as its results return. Reloaded history pills are always static.

Whole feature stays dark behind the serve-ordinances flag.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive streaming event and UI polish; shared chat path is backward-compatible (new SSE type ignored elsewhere). No auth or persistence contract changes beyond skipping `tool_input_start` in segments.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **transient `tool_input_start`** signal from the AI SDK through `llm.service` → `chatStream` → SSE/`chatClient`, so the UI can show per-tool “generating” labels (e.g. “Writing your question…”) before `tool_call` completes. That chunk is **not persisted**; tests assert ordering and segment assembly unchanged.
> 
> **Ordinance flow chat** uses the new event for smarter wait shimmer (initial gap + tool-arg generation, keyed on revealed text so it doesn’t flash over typing). **Tool pills** shimmer only while `running` (set on `tool_call`, cleared on `tool_result`); reloaded history stays static. **Clarify** prompt allows one lead-in then research, then straight to the question—no double lead-in. **Source chips** in the clarify widget revert to subtle muted pills.
> 
> Shared types: `LiveSegment` gains optional `running`; `InlineSegments` drops turn-wide `running`.
>

author: joseprupi
body:
**Operational hardening of the multi-process scaling model** — the final step of the concurrency sequence.

- **Worker count from cores:** the container entrypoint defaults `QUANTRA_WORKERS` to `min(nproc, 8)` (floored at 1) computed at start; an explicit env override still wins. Was hard-coded 4.
- **Envoy health checks TCP → gRPC:** the engine serves standard `grpc.health.v1.Health` now, so all three config sources (generator, the manager's inline copy, the static template) use `grpc_health_check`. TCP only detected dead processes; gRPC health answers on gRPC's own threads, so it distinguishes a dead worker from a compute-busy one.
- **"Scaling Model" doc** (docs/process-manager.md): single-threaded worker processes sized ≈ cores; least-request routing around busy workers; independent per-process caches (N× memory, cold per worker); cross-worker cache sharing noted as future work, not promised.
- Stale ROUND_ROBIN / TCP-health mentions updated. +1 config-gen test asserting the gRPC health check.

Full suite green (537 cases).

author: abrahem79
body:
This PR implements several performance optimizations and documentation updates:

### Smart Contract Optimizations (Bolt ⚡)
- **OneInch.sol**: Replaced `SafeMath.sub` with raw subtraction in `transferFrom` and `burnFrom`. This saves approximately 114 gas per call by avoiding internal library call overhead while maintaining safety with explicit `require` checks.
- **EIP712.sol**: Inlined the `chainid()` assembly call and updated `_buildDomainSeparator` to accept `chainId` as a parameter. This reduces gas by eliminating redundant assembly calls and internal function overhead.

### Wallet Service Performance & Fixes
- **WalletManager.ts**: Switched to `crypto.randomBytes(32)` for SECP256K1 key generation, providing a ~93% performance improvement by skipping expensive mnemonic generation in `ethers.Wallet.createRandom()`.
- **Ethers v6 Compatibility**: Fixed a bug where private keys without the `0x` prefix would fail in ethers v6 by ensuring all hex key instantiations are properly prefixed.

### Documentation (Jules REST API)
- **README.md**: Updated the Quickstart guide to reflect the latest Jules REST API specifications.
- **Formatting**: Converted custom `<ApiNote>` tags to standard Markdown blockquotes for better rendering.
- **Asset Integrity**: Replaced relative documentation links and image paths with absolute URLs (`https://jules.google/docs/`) while preserving existing production-hashed filenames.

All changes have been verified with gas benchmarks and functional test suites.

author: joottunatish
body:
## What and why

The transaction list signalled income vs expense by **colour alone** (`.income`/`.expense` green/red on the amount), which breaches `.claude/rules/design.md` ("Never signal meaning by colour alone (income/expense, over-budget, dedup) - pair with sign/icon/label"). A colour-blind, low-vision, or screen-reader user had no reliable direction cue: the money pipe renders a minus for expenses but no plus for income, so income rows previously carried no non-colour signal at all.

Closes #53

## Changes (presentation-only)

- `src/app/features/transactions/transactions.html` - each amount row now shows a sign-driven directional icon (`lucideArrowUp` income / `lucideArrowDown` expense, `aria-hidden`, `[size]="16"`) and a `.visually-hidden` "Income"/"Expense" label, both placed before the signed amount so a screen reader announces "Income, Rs 500". Sign-guarded on `amountMinor > 0` / `< 0`, so nothing renders for a zero amount.

author: anjay-goel
body:
On the homepage, clicking a tag on the featured post opened the **post**, not the tag archive — because the whole card was one `<a href={post}>` and the tags were `<span>`s nested inside it. (A real nested `<a>` can't fix this: it's invalid HTML and the browser un-nests it.)

## Fix — "stretched link" pattern (no JS)
- Card is now a `<div>` instead of an `<a>`.
- The **title** is the post link; its `::after` stretches over the whole card body (`position: relative` on `.post-body`), so clicking anywhere on the card still opens the post.
- The **tags** are real `/tags/{tag}/` links, lifted above the overlay with `z-index`, so a tag click hits the tag link.

### Why not z-index alone / why not JS
z-index can't help while the tags are nested inside a single card `<a>` — clicking any descendant of a link follows that link regardless of stacking. Once the card is no longer an `<a>` (tags are their own links + a stretched post link), z-index is exactly what gives the tags precedence. Everything stays as real, accessible links (keyboard-focusable, ⌘/right-click to open in a new tab) with no client JavaScript.

## Verified
- Click a tag → its archive; click the title/excerpt/card body → the post (both confirmed in-browser).
- Featured card renders visually identical; `pnpm build` → 0 errors.

author: orcawin
body:
## Description

This is a follow-up to the Windows native Parcel watcher crash isolated in #7757 while auditing the 11 crash submissions collected from July 6–10.

The packaged app already forks `@parcel/watcher` from `app.asar.unpacked`, but unpackaged electron-vite builds did not always exercise that protection. In dev/E2E, Electron reports `app.getAppPath()` as `<repo>/out/main`. The watcher client appended another `out/main`, looked for:

```text
<repo>/out/main/out/main/parcel-watcher-process-entry.js
```

Because that file does not exist, it silently fell back to loading the native watcher in the host process—the exact unsafe architecture that the crash isolation was meant to remove.

This PR resolves an adjacent built entry first for unpackaged Electron layouts, while preserving the existing project-root and packaged `app.asar.unpacked` layouts. The path logic is split into a focused module so the existing watcher client remains below the repository's max-lines limit.

### All 11 crash reports audited

| Reports | Field signature | Reproduction result / action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `33403b63`, `9fb92a8b`, `ac931617`, `dfd9076a`, `a8aa5a64` | Renderer OOM / memory-pressure family. `dfd9076a` was the unambiguous heap case: 3,586 MB JS heap and 4,338 MB renderer working set. | The current large-source-control workload stayed at 24.80 MB JS heap across three refresh cycles with 46 mounted rows, and the retained-agent leak suite passed. Those protections are already on `main` via #7528, #7619, and #8022. The exact remaining low-heap OOM exits did not reproduce, so this PR does not claim to fix them. |
| `92d6438a`, `53cfba60`, `54445e13` | Paired GPU/renderer `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` (`0x80000003`) after `gpu_fallback_applied`. | A software-rendering crash attempt produced a renderer-only `0xC0000005`, not the field's paired breakpoint failure. This is hardware/driver-specific on the available Windows machine; no speculative GPU flag change is included. |
| report 06 (`not captured`, issue #7742) | Main-process/native watcher crash under heavy multi-worktree churn, followed by terminal pipe loss. | Reproduced directly in 921 ms with `@parcel/watcher` in-process. #7757 fixed packaged builds; this PR closes the discovered dev/E2E entry-path hole so those builds also keep the native watcher out of the host. |
| `e101441e`, `af19c3b1` | Generic renderer `crashed` / exit `-1`, low stable heap. | The bundles contain no process-gone span, renderer exception, or causal breadcrumb, and the workload did not reproduce the exit. There is no evidence-backed code change to make for these two reports. |

## CLEAR UNDENIABLE fix evidence

### Red: native crash reproduced first

```text
node tools/repro-watcher-crash-7547/run.cjs delete-root 3 15000

iteration 1: exit=3221225477 (0xC0000005) after 921ms
*** NATIVE CRASH REPRODUCED ***
```

### Red: this path bug fails the regression test

With the adjacent-entry branch removed and the test retained:

```text
Expected: <repo>\out\main\parcel-watcher-process-entry.js
Received: <repo>\out\main\out\main\parcel-watcher-process-entry.js

Test Files  1 failed
Tests       1 failed | 13 passed
```

### Green: same native failure is contained after the fix

Against a fresh `electron-vite build --mode e2e` artifact:

```text
[parcel-watcher-process] watcher process exited (code=3221226505, signal=null)
[parcel-watcher-process] watcher process crashed; resubscribing 5 root(s)
[fixed-harness] subs=453 unsubs=453 events=364 watchErrors=0
[fixed-harness] containedCrashes=1 healthy=true fallback=false
[fixed-harness] PASS: host survived; watcher functional
```

The child hit Windows `0xC0000409`, but the host survived, delivered file events, recovered a healthy watcher, and never used the in-process fallback.

## ELI5

Orca put the crash-prone file watcher in a separate safety box. Development builds accidentally looked for that box inside another copy of the same folder, could not find it, and quietly brought the watcher back into Orca itself. This change looks beside the running development app first, finds the real safety box, and keeps a watcher crash from taking Orca down with it.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/ipc/parcel-watcher-entry-path.test.ts src/main/ipc/parcel-watcher-process.test.ts` — 2 files, 16 tests passed
- `pnpm typecheck:node` — passed after rebasing onto current `origin/main`
- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` — passed; no new suppression or limit bump
- changed-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` — passed
- `pnpm exec electron-vite build --mode e2e` — passed; emitted `out/main/parcel-watcher-process-entry.js`
- live Windows pre-fix and isolated watcher stress commands shown above

## Trade-offs

- Unpackaged Electron dev/E2E sessions now pay the intended cost of one watcher child process plus IPC instead of using the lower-overhead unsafe in-process fallback.
- Packaged behavior is unchanged. Project-root Node harnesses retain the nested `out/main` lookup, and packaged apps retain the `app.asar.unpacked/out/main` lookup.
- If an unpackaged adjacent entry does not exist, behavior still falls back to the previous nested lookup and warning path.
- There is no UI behavior change and no SSH/remote-provider routing change; this only selects the local watcher executable path. All paths use Node's cross-platform path utilities.

## Security audit

No new network, shell, or user-controlled execution surface is introduced. The code selects between existing build artifacts using `path.join` and `existsSync`; the fork target and `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` behavior are unchanged.

author: brain-crumbs
body:
## Summary

Closes #33. Implements the Phase F "live childhood run protocol" from `docs/neural-stream-agent.md`:

- **Checkpoint-or-`--fresh` gate**: `--backend remote` runs now refuse to start for `online`/`actor-critic` policies unless the model path already has a checkpoint or `--fresh` is passed explicitly — a live run can no longer silently start from scratch.
- **Always record, frames included**: live runs reject `--no-record` outright and auto-enable `--record-frames`, so every live session is fully reviewable.
- **Crash-resume hardening**: `BridgeError` is now a `RecoverableEpisodeError` (`cognitive_runtime/core/program.py`). When the Mineflayer bridge connection dies mid-episode, the runtime ends that episode (`termination_reason: "bridge_error"`), checkpoints the online learner, and continues to the next episode instead of crashing the process. `RemoteBridge.start()` now detects and respawns a dead subprocess so the next `reset()` reconnects.
- **Model-side streams**: the policy's critic value estimate is now published every tick as `model.value_estimate`, alongside the existing `model.novelty` stream, so a recording shows what the agent predicted next to what happened. Both show up in `view`/`review` decision lines.
- **Post-run review**: a new `python -m cognitive_runtime review --session <dir> --record-dir sessions` command summarizes a run and compares it against baseline sessions recorded on the same curriculum step, plus recent-episode detail — the loop-closing step before advancing to the next curriculum stage.
- **Docs**: new `docs/childhood-runs.md` documents the full workflow (pretrain in sim → eval gates → live fine-tune → review → next curriculum step); `docs/online-learning.md` and `docs/neural-stream-agent.md` link to it and record what landed.

Existing checkpoint/save-every/checkpoint-on-exit machinery (`_checkpoint_online` in `CognitiveRuntime.run`, `save_every_ticks`/`save_every_updates` on the online learners) already covered periodic saves and checkpoint-on-exit/exception/`KeyboardInterrupt`; this PR adds the missing crash-resume, enforcement, model-stream, and review pieces around it.

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_live_run_protocol.py`: checkpoint-or-`--fresh` gate (both directions), `--no-record` rejection, auto frame recording, `model.value_estimate` stream recorded, bridge-crash mid-episode ends the episode (not the process) across two episodes, a real OS `SIGINT` during a live run leaves a valid checkpoint that a rerun resumes (tick counters + weights), and the `review` command reports a run against a baseline session.
- [x] Updated `tests/test_online_q_live_rollout.py` call sites to pass `--fresh` where the new gate now requires it.
- [x] Full suite: `pytest -q` → 304 passed, 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change (`test_online_q_acceptance.py::test_simulated_online_q_beats_random_reproducibly`, fails identically on `main` before this branch's changes).

### Motivation

- Provide a controlled-pilot sandbox API so carriers, emergency partners, municipalities, and internal teams can test SKYGRID intake without any autonomous control or production actions.
- Surface a clear, auditable proof-of-intake and lightweight provider registry for pilot integration and partner review.
- Keep the interface operator-assist and fail-closed while providing developer artifacts (OpenAPI, Postman) to speed onboarding.

### Description

- Added Next.js provider-facing routes for the SKYGRID Emergency Data On-Ramp: `GET /api/provider/health`, `GET /api/provider/status`, `POST /api/provider/events`, `GET /api/provider/proof/:requestId`, and `POST /api/provider/replay/test`, returning structured JSON and safety posture flags.
- Implemented provider gateway core logic in `identity-gate-bot/lib/provider/gateway.ts` including event validation (`validateProviderEvent`), deterministic local-safe proof hashing (`buildProofHash` / `proofForRequest`), and acceptance response (`acceptProviderEvent`) with explicit safety fields (operator_assist true, autonomous_control false, etc.).
- Added sandbox provider registry fixture `identity-gate-bot/fixtures/provider-registry.json` containing `att-sandbox`, `verizon-sandbox`, `municipal-emergency-sandbox`, and `internal-skygrid` with required metadata.
- Added artifacts for integration and procurement: OpenAPI draft `docs/provider/openapi-provider-gateway-v1.yaml`, JSON schema `docs/provider/provider-event.schema.json`, Postman collection `postman/skygrid-provider-gateway-v1.collection.json`, procurement readiness doc `docs/procurement/provider-gateway-readiness.md`, and carrier one-pager `docs/sales/carrier-provider-one-pager.md`.

body:
Le user signalait qu'il voyait toujours des badges **Client** dans la modale annonce, alors que sémantiquement le bucket "docs de l'annonce" ne contient QUE ce que Strada ou le seller a fourni (carte grise italienne, contrôle technique, factures d'origine). Les justificatifs client appartiennent au bucket "conversation" ou "réservation", pas "annonce".

## Cause

Le fetch remontait les docs par `listingId` sans filtre category. Les 4 docs existants en prod : 3 `admin_provided` + 1 `user_uploaded` orphelin sur `listingId=e5eccf88` (Alfa Romeo) → le `user_uploaded` apparaissait alors qu'il ne devrait pas.

## Fix

Nouvelle prop optionnelle `categoryFilter` sur `ListingDocuments`. Le fetch reste identique (par listingId), un filter côté client masque les docs hors bucket.

**Callers mis à jour** :
- `listings.index.tsx` (modale annonce) : `categoryFilter="admin_provided"`
- `conversation-detail.tsx` sidebar section "Docs de l'annonce" : `categoryFilter="admin_provided"` + copy claire "Documents officiels de l'annonce (fournis par Strada)"

**Non touché** :
- Sidebar conv section "Justificatifs échangés" (mode `conversationId`) → 2 catégories légitimes dans une conv
- Fiche annonce dédiée `/listings/$id` onglet Documents → vue plein écran 2-colonnes conservée pour la gestion admin

## À part — erreur 500 devis

Rapporté en parallèle : `POST /quotes/request` renvoie 500 avec :
```
PrismaClientInitializationError: FATAL: (EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 30
```

Pas un bug de code, **pool Supabase saturé**. Fix immédiat : restart Coolify. Fix propre : passer `DATABASE_URL` en transaction mode (port 6543 + `?pgbouncer=true&connection_limit=1`).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` OK
- [ ] Modale Alfa Romeo (clic row) → 3 docs admin (pas de badge Client), le user_uploaded ne s'affiche plus
- [ ] Sidebar conv Alfa Romeo section "Docs de l'annonce" → mêmes 3 docs, tous badges `Strada`
- [ ] Sidebar conv Alfa Romeo section "Justificatifs échangés" → vide (aucun doc conversationId)
- [ ] Fiche annonce `/listings/{id}` onglet Documents → 2 colonnes toujours affichées, user_uploaded visible côté "Envoyés par le client"

body:
## What this is (D1, your approval)

The bullets council re-deliberates against an **objective bar** — a true loop, not a bolt-on judge. **SHADOW MODE: it logs what it *would* ship and ships nothing** until you set `BULLETS_METRIC_LOOP=shadow` (default off = zero cost, zero change).

Approach 1 (your pick): **the gate is deterministic math; the deliberation is the council.**

- **Where:** `metricGatedBulletsLoop` at the full-path **final assembly point** (after the truth gate; only `assertCoreHealthy` + the trademark scrub follow) — *not* inside the council, per the earlier BLOCKER. `enableLoop` decided **once** so the per-design fan-out can't multiply calls.
- **Metric:** `0.5·design-identity + 0.3·coherence + 0.2·structure`. Keyword coverage **excluded** (Content-step-2); `<100`-char dock **excluded** (anti-Goodhart) — by construction.
- **On fail → re-deliberate:** a deterministic critique ("design token X missing", "bullet 3 incoherent", "weak structure") feeds the council's judge-style re-synthesis prompt for **≤2** rounds. The LLM rewrites to feedback; the math judges.
- **Guards** (every one from the prior adversarial review): explicit `enableLoop`; **double-gated OFF** by default; fail-open seed with `length<5` guard (quota outage → 0 calls); `cand.length<5` break before any compare; strict `<` keep-best; measures the **ship artifact** (applies the deterministic ship gates before scoring; baseline is already post-everything).
- **Prereq refactor:** `bulletHasCoherenceDefect` lifted **verbatim** out of `coherenceGateBullets` into a shared module predicate.

## v1 scope (noted, not hidden)
- **Full path only** — a full regen exercises it. Partial bullets-only path wiring is a follow-up.
- **Multi-design:** `effectiveDesignName` is `''` there → design-identity is vacuous (di=1), metric scores co/st only.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` → 0
- Loop safety invariants unit-tested **6/6**: disabled→unchanged, quota-outage→0 calls, shadow-ships-nothing, length guard, already-perfect→0 calls, cost ceiling ≤2
- Adversarial review (safety + correctness lenses + refutation) in progress — verdict + any fixes before merge

## How you'd turn it on later
Set `BULLETS_METRIC_LOOP=shadow` in Coolify → the next full regen logs `[bullets-metric-loop][shadow] … WOULD improve …` + the candidate, shipping nothing. Read the logs, then we decide whether to promote it to enforce.

author: vitorebatista
body:
Ports `nikitabobko/AeroSpace#2165` (refs longstanding upstream #1097).

Introduces `NativeFocusRaceProtection` (in `focusCache.swift`) — a small set of time-windowed guards that prevent macOS's **asynchronous** focus fallout from stealing focus to a window on a *different* workspace right after AeroSpace deliberately changed focus:

- **Workspace switch** (`workspace`, `workspace-back-and-forth`) marks a 3s protection window on its target workspace; a delayed Launch Services / launcher app-activation to another workspace is suppressed. A left-click **cancels** the protection (explicit user intent wins).
- **Window close** marks a 250ms protection on the closed window's workspace (macOS picks a replacement focus asynchronously).
- **App activation** records a 150ms grace window; a cross-workspace native focus is *deferred* (`.deferredNativeFocus` refresh) and reconciled, or superseded by a newer workspace command / same-workspace focus.

**Fork adaptations:**
- Kept the fork's **sticky-window early return** in `updateFocusCache` (fork PR #21, `layout sticky`) ahead of the new race-protection logic.
- Used the fork's `Task { @MainActor in }` idiom (the fork has no `Task.startUnstructured`) at all 3 sites.
- Used `macAppUnsafe` (the fork's accessor) instead of upstream's `macApp` in the `updateLastNativeFocusedWindow` helper.
- Clean-applied: `WorkspaceCommand`, `WorkspaceBackAndForthCommand`, `MacWindow` (close hook), `commonUtil` (`.deferredNativeFocus` case).

**Tests:** ports `FocusCacheTest` (9 cases) covering the pure `NativeFocusRaceProtection` struct — close/app-activation/workspace-switch suppression, expiry, targeting, and cancellation. All execute and pass. The integration wiring (GlobalObserver hooks, deferred refresh) is runtime focus-timing behavior, not unit-testable here.

`./build-debug.sh -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` ✅ and `./swift-test.sh` ✅.

All credit to @nikitabobko and contributors; MIT license + attribution preserved.

author: ormeilu
body:
## What

Adds a per-provider `also_track_via_llm_call` flag (default **off**) and `llm_probe_model`. When enabled, each active-health sweep sends a minimal `max_tokens = 1` completion to the provider instead of the free `/v1/models` liveness probe — a healthy result then proves end-to-end inference works, not merely that the API answers.

- Outcome recorded as `source = llm_call` in `provider_health_events` (ROL-197) and fed through the **same** failure/recovery thresholds and 429 backoff as free probes (ROL-196).
- The sweep resolves a per-provider `ProbePlan` (`Free` GET vs `LlmCall` POST) while it holds the config, so spawned tasks own everything they need — no borrow of the snapshot.
- OpenAI-style → `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer`; Anthropic → `POST /v1/messages` with `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`.
- Flag set without `llm_probe_model` or a resolvable api key → logs a warning and **degrades to the free probe** rather than reporting the provider down.

## Acceptance

- **Off by default**: no LLM calls unless the flag is set (`plan_defaults_to_free_probe`).
- When on, outcome feeds the same thresholds as probes (shares `Health::observe`).
- Token-cost tradeoff documented next to the flag: `docs/deployment/configuration.md`, `user-docs/reliability/health-checks.mdx`, `user-docs/configuration/config-file.mdx`.

## Test

- `cargo test --workspace` — 165 passing (free-default, llm-call openai/anthropic construction, misconfig fallback). `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Closes ROL-199. Refs ROL-123

author: trivenidigital
body:
**Batch PR-2** of the 2026-07-10 improvement backlog. Closes **auth #5, auth #9**.

## Email normalization (auth #5)
Login/register already lowercase+trim email, but two paths didn't:
- **ForgotPasswordDto** — a mixed-case address built a different `password_reset:` rate-limit key and missed the (lowercased) stored account → the reset email **silently never sent**, and rotating case bypassed the 3/hr cap.
- **InviteUserDto** — a mixed-case invite created an account that later (lowercased) logins could **never match**, and the duplicate check missed case-variants.

Fix: `@Transform` lowercase+trim on both DTOs, plus defense-in-depth normalization in `AuthService.forgotPassword` and `UsersService.invite` for non-HTTP callers.

## Password policy (auth #9)
`reset-password` required only uppercase + a digit (**no lowercase**) — a user could reset to a password `register` rejects; reset and change had **no maximum**, and bcrypt **silently truncates at 72 bytes**.

Fix: a shared `StrongPassword()` decorator — upper + lower + (digit or special), ≥8 chars, **≤72 bytes via a real byte-length validator** (not a char cap, which under-counts multibyte) — applied to register/change/reset so the three paths can't diverge again.

## Tests
- `StrongPassword` accepts a valid password; rejects no-lowercase, too-short, >72 ASCII bytes, and a **multibyte** password that is <72 chars but >72 bytes.
- DTO `@Transform` lowercases+trims both emails.

## Verification
- middleware auth + users specs: **258/258** pass · `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · `eslint` 0 errors.

## Note
The register max moved from `MaxLength(100)` chars to a 72-byte cap — chars beyond byte 72 were silently ignored by bcrypt anyway, so this removes a false sense that they mattered. The invite **email** (currently returns a plaintext temp password) is a separate concern tracked in **PR-22**.

author: mkaizen
body:
## Summary
A second engineering deep-dive (~1,300 words), grounded in the **actual** rating engine (`services/api/src/rating/elo.ts`) rather than generalities.

It covers:
- Why classic two-player Elo doesn't fit an N-player contest (and why naive pairwise summing is unstable).
- The Codeforces-style **expected-rank / "seed"** approach built on the one piece of classic Elo we keep — the `winProb` logistic.
- **Geometric-mean targeting** (`sqrt(seed × actualRank)`) with binary-search inversion of the seed function to find the new rating.
- **Halving the delta** as a damping / K-factor for stability, and the **zero-sum correction** that conserves total rating across the field.
- The fairness properties encoded in the test suite (upsets pay more, favorites who flop lose, ties share rank, fully deterministic).
- How the single `recomputeRatings` engine powers **both** contests and real-time Battle Royale / Duel matches.

Uses real code snippets (`winProb`, `seed`, the recompute) and stays in the existing author voice.

## Mechanics
- New `public/content/blog/designing-a-fair-elo-system.md` + an entry in the blog list. The prerender step picks it up automatically (no wiring), so it ships as a fully prerendered, crawlable page.

body:
The workspace file-search modal (`FileSearch` in `file-tree.tsx`, opened with Ctrl+Shift+F) shows an "Esc to close" hint in its footer, but pressing Escape did nothing — the component had no Escape handler at all, so it could only be closed via the ✕ button or by selecting a result.

## Fix
Added an Escape key listener that's active only while the modal is open and calls `onClose()`. Registered in the **capture phase with `stopPropagation`** so it preempts the window-level Escape-to-abort handler — otherwise pressing Escape while a turn is streaming would both close the modal *and* abort the response. Verified via `dev:hot`: Escape dismisses the modal and leaves a streaming response running.

author: mattias800
body:
## Problem
`pm4_registers.hpp` carried a vendored copy of Kyty's GNM-era `IT_NOP` sub-opcode enum that **diverged** from the values prosper actually encodes/decodes: `R_DISPATCH_DIRECT` was `0x08` vs the real `0x1a`, the packets prosper emits (DMA_DATA `0x19`, INDEX_BASE `0x1b`, INDEX_COUNT `0x1c`, DRAW_INDEX_OFFSET `0x1d`, JUMP `0x1e`, SET_PRED `0x1f`) were missing, and Kyty-only sub-ops it never emits were present.

The block was **dead** — no consumer reads these `R_*` from `pm4_registers.hpp` (tests and the command processor use `pm4_decode.hpp`'s authoritative enum, mirrored by the encoder `hle_agc.cpp`). Left in place it's a latent foot-gun: `if (sub_op == Pm4::R_DISPATCH_DIRECT)` would silently never match a real dispatch packet.

## Fix
Remove the block; leave a pointer comment to `pm4_decode.hpp` as the single source of truth. This header now owns only hardware register offsets.

## Verification
Build + full ctest 82/82 green — nothing referenced the removed block (grep-confirmed and compile-confirmed).

Fixes #385

author: hovborg
body:
## Summary

- restore the UniFi Protect Bridge config flow on Home Assistant 2026.7+
- keep strict webhook and Protect origin validation outside the serializable schema
- reject malformed ports, missing hosts, paths, queries, fragments, embedded credentials, and control characters
- redact config-entry titles and detailed runtime errors from downloadable diagnostics
- test the real schema/API boundary against exact Home Assistant 2026.3.0 and the latest stable release
- align package and integration metadata at v0.2.22

## Root cause

Home Assistant serializes config-flow schemas before sending them to the frontend. The webhook base URL field embedded a custom Python validator directly in its Voluptuous schema. Home Assistant 2026.7 cannot serialize arbitrary validator functions, so opening the integration flow raised `ValueError` and returned HTTP 500.

Validation now runs after form submission, where invalid input returns the existing field error without attempting a Protect connection.

## User impact

The integration form loads again on Home Assistant 2026.7, while existing URL normalization, blank-override clearing, password retention, reconfigure, and reauthentication behavior remain covered by tests.

## Validation

- `pytest -q`: 104 passed
- Ruff: passed
- Python compileall: passed
- Bandit medium/high: no findings
- pip-audit: no known vulnerabilities
- exact Home Assistant 2026.3.0 schema/API smoke: passed
- Home Assistant 2026.7.1 schema/API smoke: passed
- source distribution and wheel build/inspection: passed
- independent Sol/high review: no Critical findings; all Important and Minor findings addressed
- GitHub CI: passed
- Hassfest: passed

## Known HACS bootstrap check

This branch now includes the standard MIT license. HACS Validation still reports 8/9 checks passed because its license validator reads GitHub's repository-level license metadata from the default branch, where no license exists yet. The check cannot become green on this PR branch until `main` first contains a recognized license; all checkout/ref-based HACS checks pass.

Fixes #1.

This incorporates the compatibility direction identified by @garyt72 in #2. Thanks to Gary for reporting the issue, contributing the initial patch, and confirming that moving validation out of the schema restores the flow.

author: mssonicbld
body:
#### Why I did it

The NVIDIA AST2700 BMC `installer.conf` did not set `bootconf`. When `bootconf` is empty, `platform_arm64.conf`'s `prepare_boot_menu` skips the `fw_setenv bootconf` call entirely, leaving the pre-existing factory EVB value in U-Boot. The board then boots the generic AST2700 EVB DTB, which enables the FMC SPI-NOR flash and triggers a NULL-pointer kernel panic in `spi-aspeed-smc`, leaving the BMC in an endless reboot loop.

##### Work item tracking

#### How I did it

Set `bootconf` in `device/aspeed/arm64-aspeed_nvidia_ast2700_bmc-r0/installer.conf` to `sonic-ast2700-nvidia-spc6-bmc` so the installer writes the hardware-correct FIT boot configuration to the U-Boot env instead of leaving the pre-existing EVB factory value.

#### How to verify it

After `sudo sonic-installer install <bmc.bin>`, run `sudo fw_printenv bootconf` and confirm it retains the value `sonic-ast2700-nvidia-spc6-bmc` (previously it was reset to `ast2700-evb`). After reboot, `cat /proc/device-tree/model` should show the correct BMC platform string with no `spi-aspeed-smc` kernel panic or reboot loop.

author: craigpnnl
body:
# Description

The `develop` branch CI is fully red. Every build job fails at the dependency-install step with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'wheel.wheelfile'` while building the `modbus-tk` and `treelib` sdists. This blocks the whole branch, not just one PR.

Root cause: pip's `use_pep517` legacy fallback picks the non-isolated build path when `setuptools` and `wheel` are already importable in the environment and the requirement ships no `pyproject.toml`. `bootstrap.py` installs the pinned `wheel==0.30` right before it resolves the extras, so the legacy path builds those sdists against the ambient `wheel==0.30`, whose `bdist_wheel` unconditionally imports `wheel.wheelfile.WheelFile`, an API that `wheel==0.30` does not have.

Fix: add `--use-pep517` to the extras/editable install so pip provisions a fresh, isolated build environment per requirement, supplying its own modern build-time `setuptools`/`wheel` pair. The runtime `wheel==0.30` pin is left in place, because `packaging.py` imports the removed `wheel.install.WheelFile` and still needs 0.30 at runtime. Build-time isolation and the runtime pin are now independent.

Fixes # (develop CI build failure; no separate issue filed)

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

# How Has This Been Tested?

Proven green on Python 3.10 (the CI interpreter) running the full `bootstrap.py --all --force`:

- [x] `modbus-tk` and `treelib` sdists build clean under the isolated PEP 517 path

body:
Upstream `ponder` published **0.16.9** as `latest` on 2026-07-10, so a fresh `npm install ponder` now resolves to a version the fork didn't yet cover. This registers the compat row and adds `wiring/0.16.9.patch` (a **verbatim copy** of `wiring/0.16.8.patch`).

## What changed upstream (0.16.8 → 0.16.9)
A **single source file**: `src/indexing-store/cache.ts` — [ponder-sh/ponder#2323](https://github.com/ponder-sh/ponder/pull/2323): fix `p.bytes()` bytea encoding on the Postgres `COPY` flush path (emit `\x<hex>` for `Buffer` values), fixing `DelayedInsertError: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00`. Confirmed by diffing the 0.16.8 vs 0.16.9 npm tarballs (only `cache.ts` + its compiled `dist` + `CHANGELOG` differ).

## Why the seam is untouched
`indexing-store/cache.ts` is **not on the graft surface** (`sync-historical`, `runtime/historical`, `sync-store`, `rpc`, `sync`, `sync-realtime`). **Every upstream file the wiring patch modifies is byte-identical between 0.16.8 and 0.16.9**, so the 0.16.8 patch applies to 0.16.9 with zero rejects. The fork passively inherits the upstream bytea-COPY correctness fix.

## Verification — `scripts/sync-upstream.sh 0.16.9 --test`
- patch applies cleanly (zero rejects), builds `@subsquid/ponder@0.16.9-sqd.1`
- full Portal suite **328/328 green** on ponder@0.16.9 (18 test files)
- `biome check` clean; secret-scan clean

## Scope
- `published: false` — **not** cutting/publishing a release here; publishing to npm is a deliberate, human-reserved step. `0.16.8-sqd.1` stays `--tag latest` until then.
- Mirrors the #129 precedent (which registered 0.16.8 as `published:false` before the separate publish step).

Compat rests on seam-identity + the full suite, as for 0.16.8/0.16.7/0.15.17.

author: kdonovan
body:
## What

`Axn::Reflection::Schema` (PRO-2842) only represents **single-level** subfields. A deep subfield — a dotted `on:` path (`on: "address.billing"`), a subfield-of-a-subfield, or a dotted field name (`expects "bar.baz", on: :foo`) — validates at runtime but is **silently omitted** from the reflected input schema. That's the safe direction correctness-wise (schema stricter than runtime), but the *silence* is the problem: an adapter author building tooling on the schema gets an incomplete contract with no signal, and a client can't send a field it can't see.

This makes the omission honest without changing the emitted schema:

- Adds `Axn::Reflection::Schema.dropped_deep_subfields` — a side-effect-free query that identifies exactly the omitted deep configs (reusing `shallow_subfields` as the source of truth for "shallow", and skipping the deliberately-excluded `ambient_context` subtree, whose absence is intentional rather than a nesting-depth gap).
- `SchemaReflection#input_schema` logs a **one-time-per-class** warning via `Axn.config.logger` naming the omitted field(s) and pointing at PRO-2872 (the full-nesting follow-up).

Full deep-nesting support is tracked separately in PRO-2872.

## Verification

Observed on a class with one shallow + two deep subfields:

```
W, [...] WARN -- : [Axn] BillingTool input_schema omits deep subfield(s) not representable at a single
nesting level: id (on: meta), ref (on: payload.meta). They validate at runtime but are absent from the
reflected input schema; flatten them to single-level subfields, or handle them in the adapter (PRO-2872).
```

Second `input_schema` call is silent (dedup); schema properties unchanged. New specs cover the query (three deep cases, shallow no-ops, ambient exclusion) and the warn/dedup behavior.

The goal of this is to **enable migration of chain protocol structures without deeply refactoring the STF code**, and to decouple the STF code from the concrete tx types in the same way it's decoupled from the concrete state types.  It also makes it easier to make use of the SSZ `*Ref` types without having to modify the STF code.  Client code not related to protocol execution can still use the concrete types, as we can iterate on this much more freely.

body:
## Description

Unblocks dashboard listing, list, and image mutations while a warm-cache background refresh is fetching its primary snapshot.

The refresh now fetches outside the shared mutation queue and acquires the queue only to apply the completed snapshot. If any queued dashboard work completes during the fetch, the stale snapshot is discarded instead of overwriting newer local mutation state.

This addresses the production behavior where Rolling Oaks could see Save and Refresh appear frozen behind an 11–19 second full-catalog refresh.

## Files changed

- `apps/main/src/app/dashboard/_lib/dashboard-db/dashboard-db-persistence.ts`
  - Tracks completed queued work with a small revision counter.
  - Moves only the primary background snapshot fetch outside the shared queue.
  - Skips applying a snapshot when intervening mutation work makes it stale.
  - Leaves cold primary and replica bootstrap behavior unchanged.

- `apps/main/tests/dashboard-db-collections.test.tsx`
  - Updates the existing integration test to verify an optimistic listing update completes while a stale full refresh remains suspended.
  - Verifies the stale refresh does not overwrite the saved listing value.

author: george-dilthey
body:
## What changed

Added a new FAQ entry to `docs/find-companies.md` explaining why companies sourced with a revenue filter can have different enriched revenue values afterward. Also added a brief clarifying note to the **Company types** filter bullet indicating that these values reflect how companies self-classify on their profiles.

## Why

A customer (Kristen Siewert, Trulioo) asked three questions about Find Companies in Intercom conversation #215475014047828:
1. Why did filtering for Revenue > $500M result in ~63% of ~6,300 imported companies showing enriched revenue values below $500M?
2. How reliable are the Company Types filter values?
3. What is the full list of Industries available in Find Companies?

The human support agent (Bo Morin) answered all three questions directly in the Slack thread. The existing `find-companies.md` doc:
- Already documented the company types list — but not that they are self-classified
- Already had an FAQ for industries (open-ended taxonomy from profile data)
- Had **no explanation** of why the revenue filter can diverge from post-enrichment revenue values — this was the primary source of confusion

The verifier sub-agent confirmed all three underlying product claims PASS (available to all customers, no gate). The revenue mismatch occurs because Find Companies queries Clay's internal MixRank-backed OpenSearch index (estimated from third-party sources, field `yearly_revenue_range` in `company-query-builder.ts:786`), while post-enrichment providers (Clearbit via `metrics.annualRevenue`, Owler via `revenue`, Clay's `lyne-find-revenue-data` via `annual_revenue`) each use their own independent methodology — an intentional architectural separation especially impactful for private companies whose revenue is never publicly disclosed. Company types confirmed as exactly 8 values matching a LinkedIn self-classification enum (`cpj-schemas.ts:116-125` and `input-parameter-schema.ts:57-99`).

## Source link(s)

- Intercom conversation: https://app.intercom.com/a/inbox/w28k1kwz/inbox/conversation/215475014047828
- Slack thread (Bo's answer): https://clay-hq.slack.com/archives/C0AKQ5XUZPY/p1783551020952169?thread_ts=1783544382.515119&cid=C0AKQ5XUZPY
- Verifier file:line evidence — revenue filter: `public-actions/apps/cpj/actions/search-companies-with-mixrank-shared/input-parameter-schema.ts:197-255` + `company-query-builder.ts:786`; revenue enrichment providers: `clay-base/libs/shared/src/attributes/attribute-paths.ts:955-962`; company types enum: `clay-base/libs/shared/src/sources/cpj-schemas.ts:116-125`; industries predefined list: `clay-base/libs/shared/src/sources/cpj-autocomplete-options.ts:4258-4895`

## Uncertainties

None. All three underlying claims were verified as PASS with no feature gate.

## Related observations

The customer also asked for the full list of Industries available. The existing doc says "approximately 457 common values" in the "What are the available AI Subindustry filter values?" FAQ, but the verifier found ~637 industry strings in the `industries` autocomplete options array (`cpj-autocomplete-options.ts:4258-4895`). This discrepancy is in an untouched section and may reflect an outdated count or a difference in how the two lists are scoped — worth a separate look. No change made in this PR since it is outside the scope of this ticket.

Closes DOC-1091

author: gunkl
body:
## Summary
Continues the nat-vent architecture-reset direction (v0.5.1) / #452's test consolidation. The two existing old-vs-new differential comparators (`nat_vent_gate_compare.py`, `fan_thermostat_decision_compare.py`) were structurally parallel — each hand-rolled its own `Call`/`ComparisonRun` dataclass pair, input-reconstruction wiring, and instrumentation contextmanager. The four upcoming architecture-consolidation Phase A extractions (sleep-aware floor resolver, fan-suppression predicate, occupancy-defer predicate, comfort-band branch) all return a value — matching `nat_vent_gate_compare`'s shape — so extracting that shape into a reusable base now means each gets a comparator by supplying only `(production_method, reconstruct_inputs, pure_fn)` instead of a fifth copy-pasted comparator file.

- Add `tools/sim_harness/decision_compare_base.py`: `DecisionCall`/`DecisionComparisonRun`, `instrumented_value_decision()` (shadow mode), `compare_scenario()`, `substitute_new_decision()` (substitution mode).
- Refactor `nat_vent_gate_compare.py` onto the base, keeping its exact public API (`GateCall`/`GateComparisonRun`/`compare_scenario`/`substitute_new_gate`) unchanged for existing callers.
- `fan_thermostat_decision_compare.py` deliberately **not** refactored — its production method returns nothing (outcome inferred from side-effect calls) and requires pre-call input capture, a genuinely different instrumentation shape. Added a docstring cross-reference explaining why.

**Caught during verification, not by the test suite alone:** a first cut of the refactor introduced a real import-order bug — resolving the production `AutomationEngine` class before anything imported `run_production.py` (which installs the test HA stub modules as a side effect) broke the CLI comparator tool with `ModuleNotFoundError`, even though pytest stayed green throughout. Running `tools/nat_vent_gate_diff.py` directly (not just the test suite) surfaced it; fixed before this PR.

author: basilsuhail
body:
## What

All four reported issues, one root cause fixed properly:

1. **Table jitter** — the hover boxes were absolutely-positioned *inside* `overflow-x-auto` containers, so opening one inflated the scrollable width and the table slid. Tooltips now render through a **document.body portal at `position: fixed`** (new shared `Tip` primitive) — they exist outside every scroll/stacking context, so nothing ever resizes on hover. Sort arrows also reserve their width (`opacity-0` when inactive) instead of appearing/disappearing.
2. **Popups clipping / going behind things / ignoring screen edges** — same root cause, same fix; the portal tooltip **clamps to the viewport** horizontally and **flips above the anchor** when the bottom of the screen is crowded. It can never be clipped by `overflow-hidden` or sit under a sibling card (single top z-index).
3. **Narrow side-pane wonkiness** — bar-chart labels shrink (`w-24` → `sm:w-36`) and truncate, stat tiles get `min-w-0` so the KPI row wraps cleanly in the deck card.
4. **Short forms** — country codes expand to full English names via the built-in `Intl.DisplayNames` (zero new dependencies): *United States* in the coverage table with the ISO code kept as a small grey chip, full names on the loudness top-10 bars. Malformed codes fall back verbatim, tested.

## Verified

- 95 frontend tests pass (new: `countryName` expansion + malformed fallback; found en route that `ZZ` legitimately means 'Unknown Region' in CLDR — test uses genuinely invalid input), `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint 0 errors, zero `group-hover` tooltip remnants.
- Live dev server compiles and serves (HTTP 200) — hot-reloaded on localhost:3000, hover things and scroll the tables to confirm the jitter is gone.

author: jonathanmoregard
body:
## What

One-line dependency addition: `pkgs.tesseract` joins `pkgs.uv` in the `runtimeInputs` of the `research-agent-mcp` wrapper (`home/research-agent-mcp.nix`).

## Why

[research-agent PR #14](https://github.com/jonathanmoregard/research-agent/pull/14) adds browser-session screenshot artifacts. The host-side gate (`mcp_server/artifact_gate.py`) OCRs each screenshot with tesseract and feeds the text through the injection scanner before anything lands in `reports/`. The mcp_server process is spawned via this wrapper, so `runtimeInputs` is the tightest declarative scope — no global `environment.systemPackages` pollution.

Default nixpkgs tesseract ships all language packs (~469 MiB download / ~1 GiB unpacked). Deliberate: the OCR gate is a security scan, and a script it can't read would OCR to garbage and weaken the gate. Shout if you'd rather pin `enableLanguages` to a subset.

## Evidence

- `vm-base` lane green locally (`GATE_ALL_GREEN`, detached unit; re-verified wrapper build on the rebased tree).
- Built the actual wrapper derivation out of the dellan config: its PATH export resolves `tesseract-5.5.2`.
- Ran the exact invocation the artifact gate uses — `tesseract /tmp/ocr-smoke.png stdout` on a rendered test PNG → `HELLOARTIFACTGATE`.

## Ordering

Merge this before or together with research-agent PR #14's deploy; without it the artifact gate fails closed (screenshots get isolated with `ocr_error:FileNotFoundError`, reports still deliver).

body:
The headline **"Meta will never do this"**: watch a metric — including the live **lead-quality score** — and act. e.g. *quality below 60 → pause the campaign*; *quality above 95 → increase budget by 200%*.

## What's here
- **Data** — `freehold_campaign_rules` + `lib/freehold/campaign-rules.ts` (CRUD + a pure, side-effect-free evaluator). Metric ∈ `quality | cpl | leads | spend | ctr`, operator below/above, action `pause | resume | budget±% | notify`.
- **API** — `GET/POST /api/freehold/campaign-rules`, `PATCH/DELETE /[id]`, `POST /evaluate` (recomputes **quality server-side so it can't be spoofed**; returns which rules fire — no side effects).
- **UI** on the Campaign Command page — a plain-language rule builder (*"If \<metric\> \<is below/above\> \<n\> then \<action\>"*), enable/disable + delete, a **"Check rules now"** that lists firing rules, and an explicit **Apply** per rule.

## Safety by design
Rules **never spend or pause money on their own.** Evaluation and application are separate, explicit steps, and Apply reuses the already-tested status/budget control endpoints (optimistic, reverts on failure). Continuous background evaluation (cron) is a deliberate later add — I didn't want silent money-moving actions until you've seen rules behave.

Completes **Campaign Command P2** (quality score + Refiner + rules). Trilingual EN/AR/RU, RTL-safe, mobile.

## Verification
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `pnpm i18n` → full EN/AR/RU parity
- `pnpm build` → compiled successfully (all 3 rule routes registered)

author: 5omeotherguy
body:
First live campaign (pilot-a, PR #559) validated the `live_harness` module and surfaced two findings. Both are fixed with in-gate deterministic tests; the live path stays double-gated (`#[ignore]` + `IRIS_BENCH_LIVE=1`). Details: `docs/benchmarks/pilot-a-findings.md`.

## Finding 1 -- S1 could not exercise compaction (fixed)
S1 seeded the whole runaway context pre-turn and drove ONE provider round-trip, so `compaction_governor::govern` -- which runs only at pair-closed boundaries between round-trips within a continuing turn -- never fired. S1 reached `tier=hard` (34k) yet `compaction_generation_applied` stayed null in every row.

- S1 now loads the seed BELOW the start tier and drives several sequential tool-call round-trips inside ONE turn (mirrors `auto_compaction_live_loop`'s real-tool loop). Seed + scripted reads cross start then hard before the final round-trip, so a continuing hard-tier boundary lets #552 current-turn coverage fire.
- S1 carries its own success criteria via `Scenario::verify_run`: a run must observe >= 3 boundaries AND >= 1 compaction, else it is a Fail with reason `S1 produced no compaction`. The runner marks such a run `HardFailure` (fails the verdict) and the `.md` report records it under `## Scenario failures` -- an under-driving scenario is now loud, not a silent green.

## Finding 2 -- estimate_error was a per-turn broadcast, not a per-request delta (fixed; case b)
S4-small opening requests showed a consistent ~-3,650-token `estimate_error`. Reproduced from the jsonl: `context_estimate_tokens` was `context_diagnostics().measured` (provider-anchored `measure_context`, NOT the estimator) sampled once per turn and broadcast to every request in the turn -- it equals each turn's LAST request `input + output`. The opening request of a two-round-trip turn was diffed against the turn-end total (the ~3.6k read mass added later), a like-for-unlike delta.

Case **(b)**, a harness sampling artifact -- NOT a runtime undercount. The runtime triggers on `measure_context` (provider-anchored once a usage lands), so trigger timing is unaffected. Fix: `RecordingProvider` captures the pure estimator (`message_token_estimate` summed) over each request's exact payload; the row reports that per-request value against the same request's provider input, so `estimate_error` is a genuine like-for-like delta. No runtime estimator change, so no issue filed.

## Tests (in-gate, no provider)
- `scenario::tests::s1_seed_loads_below_start_and_scripted_reads_cross_hard_within_planned_round_trips`
- `scenario::tests::s1_verify_run_fails_without_compaction_and_passes_with_one`
- `runner::tests::s1_drives_multiple_boundaries_and_compacts_mid_turn` (real Harness/governor + scripted provider)
- `runner::tests::estimate_error_is_per_request_not_a_turn_end_broadcast`
- `campaign::tests::report_surfaces_scenario_failures_verbatim`

Gate: `bash scripts/gate.sh` PASS (fmt + clippy + test + scripts). No live provider calls.

author: paulfidika
body:
## The two live failures (J24 qwen lane, 2026-07-10)

1. **ENOSPC mid-clone**: 40GB Qwen/Qwen-Image on a 20GB conversion pod — no free-space check despite HF file sizes being known pre-download; failed workdirs also accumulated forever.
2. **Whole-job fatal at 19/20 shards**: tensorhub's /complete lost the staged bytes (th#699) and 503'd every retry; the worker had no file-level recovery.

## Changes

**Disk (fail fast + never leak scratch)**
- `run_clone` preflights free space against the plan's known sizes: `required = source_bytes x COZY_CONVERT_DISK_HEADROOM (2.5) + 2 GiB`; typed `CloneDiskSpaceError` — "need ~X GiB free … have Y GiB" — before any byte downloads.
- Workdir removed after EVERY job, success and failure (`COZY_CONVERT_RETAIN_WORKDIR=1` opts a failed job's scratch back in for debugging). Cross-run resume is the publish bank (th#592) + CAS dedup, not retained bytes.
- Every run sweeps stale `clone-*` scratch from crashed predecessors: flock-free AND idle past `COZY_CONVERT_SCRATCH_TTL_S` (1h).

**Publish (resume, don't restart)**
- `409 staging_object_missing` from /complete → re-open that ONE file (`POST .../commits/<rev>/uploads`, new th#699 endpoint) and re-upload just it, bounded at 2 re-uploads; a dedup hit on re-open short-circuits with zero bytes moved.
- Part PUTs and hub POSTs use (connect=15s, read) timeout tuples (gw#456 parity on the upload side).
- Errors name the file, attempt count, and last status. Existing retry ladder unchanged: 5 attempts, 1s→30s exponential backoff + jitter on 5xx/429/network for every part PUT and hub POST; /complete additionally re-POSTs through severed connections and 409-in-progress races up to 30min.

## Tests (real codepaths, no mocks)

Fake-hub (real threaded HTTP server): staging-gone re-upload touches only the lost file; bounded-then-typed exhaustion; re-open dedup short-circuit; finalize 503x3-then-success; single failing part retries only that part (3-part upload, per-URL counts). Clone hygiene on a real filesystem with real flocks: preflight boundary (incl. tunable headroom), stale-sweep keeps live/fresh/own dirs, failure cleanup + opt-in retention. Full suite: **693 passed, 10 skipped**.

Tracker: gw#462. Counterparts: tensorhub th#699 (PR #213), e2e#150 (PR #61). Release 0.13.8 to PyPI after merge (conversion image consumes the wheel).

## Summary

- **Bug found**: the first real `.fit` file ingested (a kayak session, 2026-07-09) parsed as `swim_pool` with no warning. Non-swim `.fit` imports (kayak/run/ride) were silently mislabeled as swims, which would pollute swim-volume math.
- **Fix**: add a `cross_train` sport (`engine/swim_coach/models.py` `Sport` literal). New pure helper `_fit_sport(session_sport, session_sub_sport, warnings)` in `engine/swim_coach/parse_files.py` replaces the inline mapping in `parse_fit`:
  - open-water sub_sport → `swim_ow`
  - missing sport → `swim_pool` + warning
  - sport containing "swim" → `swim_pool`
  - anything else → `cross_train` + warning naming the original FIT sport
- `cli.py`'s `ingest --sport` choices now include `cross_train`.
- **Load-math semantics**: `cross_train` counts toward sRPE (it's still training stress) but is excluded from swim-volume totals — covered by `tests/unit/test_load.py`.
- **New real fixture**: `tests/unit/fixtures/fit/real_swim.fit` — a real pool swim from a Garmin Instinct (2026-03-14, 1623m, 54.0min). Verified via `fitdecode` (every frame, including all 3241 `record` messages) that it carries no `position_lat`/`position_long` or other GPS/location data before committing it to this public repo. This activates the previously-skipped `test_parse_fit_real_fixture_extracts_session_and_laps`, which now passes.
- Raw device `.fit` exports (including the kayak file, which *does* have GPS data) moved out of `library/` (curated research library, not a device-export dropbox) to `athletes/andrew/logs/files/`, which is now gitignored. Removed a stray Windows `Zone.Identifier` junk file from `library/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit -q` — 267 passed, 0 skipped (up from 266 passed / 1 skipped)
- [x] Dry-run ingested `AndrewSwimPool_ACTIVITY.fit` (no `--save`): parses as `swim_pool`, 1623m, 54.0min, 2026-03-14, no warnings
- [x] Dry-run ingested `AndrewKayak_ACTIVITY.fit`: parses as `cross_train`, 11494m, 303.3min, 2026-07-09, with warning naming the original FIT sport
- [x] `git status` confirms no raw `.fit` file is tracked or untracked outside the vetted fixture

## PR checklist
- [x] Vitest unit tests: not applicable — engine-only Python change, no `web/` changes
- [x] Playwright e2e: not applicable — no UI surface touched
- [x] No dead code or commented-out code
- [x] DOD items: engine-owned plan math stays deterministic; new `cross_train` sport documented at the `models.py` Literal with rationale; every parsing branch covered by a unit test

body:
## What

Two SEO visibility features for verified client reviews (builds on #173–#175).

### Feature A — "What {city} clients say" on area pages

**Before:** area pages showed only 2 generic Google reviews rotated by city slug — no project-linked, city-specific social proof.

**After:** cities whose portfolio projects have verified reviews get a new section right above the generic reviews block — up to 3 verbatim quotes, each linking to the reviewed project's case study, plus an "All reviews" link to `/reviews`:

| Area page | Review cards |
|---|---|
| `/areas/richmond/` | 3 (Lisa J., Henry W., Jianyi Y.) |
| `/areas/burnaby/` | 2 (Fiana L., Angela L.) |
| `/areas/delta/` | 1 (Zoe C., zh original) |
| other 11 cities | section renders nothing |

- New `getReviewsByCityFromDb` (per-city `cachedQueryWithArgs`, tag `reviews:by-area`), joined on `projects.location_city` with the same case-insensitive equality as `getProjectsByAreaFromDb`; one-row-per-project duplicates collapsed.
- Quotes are **verbatim** — original language with `lang` attr, never machine-translated.
- Labels via the self-contained 14-locale map technique (VerifiedGoogleReviews pattern).
- **Deliberately NO Review schema on area pages** — the reviews' structured data lives on the project pages; duplicating the same reviews on a second entity risks spam signals.

### Feature B — /reviews hub upgrade

**Before:** `/reviews` showed only the 5 cached Google reviews; `project_reviews.project_id` was NOT NULL so a review without a mappable case study couldn't exist.

**After:**
- **Migration 0007** (generated via `drizzle-kit`, applied to the local prod DB by psql per repo convention — `drizzle/` stays gitignored, artifacts synced to the prod checkout): `project_id` DROP NOT NULL + FK `ON DELETE SET NULL` (deleting a project now unlinks its reviews instead of deleting the client's testimony). 8 existing rows intact.
- **Merged hub:** `lib/reviews-hub.ts` (pure, unit-tested) merges `project_reviews` (8 rows) + live `google_reviews_cache` payload (5) + 3 legacy testimonials rows, **deduped** (same author + similar text = one, project copy preferred since it links to a case study). Result: **14 unique reviews** (6 unique project-linked — Henry Wang/Jianyi Yi multi-project rows collapse — + 5 Google + 3 testimonials; zero cross-source overlaps today, the guard is for future ones).
- **Render:** hero keeps live `rating`/`userRatingCount` from the cache (never hardcoded) + prominent "Read all 77 reviews on Google" CTA via `GOOGLE_REVIEWS_URL`; existing Google grid (deduped); new **grouped-by-city sections** (server-built, no client filtering — the simpler robust option): Richmond (4) → Burnaby (3) → Delta (1) → Vancouver (1). City headings link to area pages; project-linked cards link to case studies; testimonials render with a "Client Testimonial" eyebrow (not claimed as Google reviews).
- **Meta:** `metadata.reviews.title` refreshed in all 14 locales to the "Reno Stars Reviews — Vancouver Renovation Company Reviews" pattern (≤70 chars; zh/zh-Hant use the 聚星装修 brand). Descriptions untouched (their "75+" stays truthful at 77).
- **No aggregateRating/Review schema added** to the page (self-serving-review rules) — site-wide LocalBusinessSchema in the layout already carries it.
- Existing revalidation behavior kept (force-dynamic SSR + 5-min CF edge); new data reads carry tags `reviews:hub` / `reviews:by-area` with 24h TTL floor.

### Internal links
- `VerifiedGoogleReviews` (project pages): quiet "All reviews" → `/reviews` under the cards; card markup extracted into shared `components/reviews/ReviewQuoteCard.tsx` (one implementation across project pages, area pages, hub).
- Area review section links to `/reviews`; hub city headings link back to `/areas/{slug}` (bidirectional equity).

### Admin
- Review form gains an optional **"Linked Project"** select (defaults to the current project; "No linked project" option). Create reads `projectId` from the form; update can re-link/unlink; lookups use a LEFT join so unlinked reviews resolve.
- Revalidation on every review mutation now refreshes the project page, the project's **city area page** (service_areas name lookup) and the `/reviews` hub.
- New **`/admin/reviews`** page (+ sidebar entry, en/zh strings) manages unlinked reviews — they're invisible in the per-project section.

## Testing
- `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` (0 errors) / `pnpm test:run` (647 passed, incl. new reviews-hub dedupe suite + reworked action tests with unlinked cases) / `pnpm build` — all green.
- Verified against the live DB on a local `next start`: Richmond/Burnaby/Delta sections render with correct cards, `port-moody` renders nothing, `/en/reviews/` shows the hero CTA with the live count (77), 4 city groups, deduped grid; `/zh/areas/delta/` shows the localized heading (三角洲客户怎么说).
- Migration applied + verified on prod DB (FK now `ON DELETE SET NULL`, column nullable, 8 rows).

⚠️ Merging does NOT deploy (self-hosted) — after merge: build + `launchctl kickstart -k system/com.renostars.reno-stars-web`.

body:
## What changed

- reject duplicate asset columns before per-column dtype inspection
- reject positive and negative infinity while preserving genuine numeric `NaN`
- enforce complete date-symbol coverage after long-price CSV pivot when `allow_missing=False`
- preserve intentionally sparse panels only through explicit `allow_missing=True`
- document the corrected input contracts and add deterministic regressions

## Root cause

`validate_panel_data` selected each label before checking whether column labels were unique. With duplicate labels, pandas returned a DataFrame rather than a Series, producing an unclear `AttributeError` during dtype inspection. The validator also converted numeric panels to float without rejecting infinity.

`load_long_price_csv` validated missing source cells before pivoting. An absent date-symbol pair therefore created a new `NaN` during pivot and bypassed the default strict missing-data contract.

## Evidence

Failing-baseline reproductions on merged PR #139 showed:

- duplicate asset labels raised `AttributeError("'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'dtype'")`
- `+inf` was accepted
- a sparse three-row/two-symbol long CSV was accepted with one missing post-pivot cell

The new regressions require a clear duplicate-column error, reject both signs of infinity, preserve real `NaN`, reject the sparse pivot by default with field/date/asset context, and preserve it only when `allow_missing=True`.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_operators.py tests/test_csv_loader.py` — 61 passed
- `python -m pytest -q` — 523 passed
- `python -m compileall -q src tests research lean`
- scoped `ruff check` — passed
- `git diff --check`
- scoped hidden Unicode/control-character scan

## Scope and boundaries

- no feature formula, signal date, execution timing, portfolio accounting, report value, data fetch, vendor API, credential, brokerage, order, live/paper trading, or performance-claim change
- the separate momentum window validator remains explicitly deferred to its own small contract PR

## Contexte

Revue de bugs sur l'ensemble du code (5 sous-agents par domaine, chaque trouvaille vérifiée de façon contradictoire). 22 trouvailles confirmées → 20 bugs distincts corrigés. `pnpm typecheck` et `pnpm build` passent.

## Sécurité / contrôle d'accès

- **`subscriptions` — deux IDOR** : `PUT …/subscription` n'exigeait aucune adhésion (n'importe qui pouvait s'abonner à n'importe quel enfant et recevoir ses notifications/e-mails) ; `GET …/subscribers` exposait nom + e-mail de tout le cercle sans contrôle. Désormais : adhésion requise pour s'abonner, liste réservée à l'admin (comme `/members`).
- **Fuite post-révocation** : les notifications ne partent qu'aux abonnés **encore membres** (jointure `memberships`), et l'abonnement est supprimé au retrait d'un membre.
- **Réutilisation de token d'invitation** : l'acceptation est maintenant à **usage unique** (garde atomique `WHERE status = 'pending'`) et **liée à l'e-mail invité** — un lien transféré n'onboarde plus un tiers.
- **Secret par défaut** : `validateConfig()` **refuse de démarrer en production** si `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`/`DATABASE_URL` restent aux valeurs par défaut ; `NODE_ENV=production` ajouté au compose de prod.
- **Drapeaux d'inscription** : `SIGNUP_ENABLED`/`SMTP_SECURE` parsés de façon robuste (`0/no/off` ferme bien l'inscription).
- **Injection HTML e-mail** : échappement du nom d'enfant et du destinataire dans les e-mails de notification (plus de balises/phishing injectables).

## Robustesse / correction

- **`PATCH /entries/:id`** : validation de la date (→ 400) et traduction des collisions d'unicité (→ 409) au lieu d'un 500 ; **publication détectée atomiquement** (`UPDATE … WHERE status <> 'published' RETURNING`) → plus de notifications/e-mails en double sur double-clic.
- **`processEntry`** : garde compare-and-set (ne pas écraser une relecture humaine par la sortie VLM), bloc `catch` isolé, et `.catch` sur l'appel fire-and-forget (plus de promesse rejetée non gérée).
- **Ingestion** : nettoyage des fichiers orphelins sur 409 / erreur avant rattachement en base.
- **VLM** : les champs « tableau » sont forcés en vrais tableaux (`Array.isArray`).
- **Notifications** : notif in-app persistée **avant** l'e-mail, `Promise.allSettled` (un échec par destinataire n'annule plus les autres).
- **Config** : parsing entier sûr (`INVITATION_TTL_DAYS`, `PORT`, `SMTP_PORT`) — plus de `NaN`/date invalide.

## Front

- **Share** : garde anti-course au changement d'enfant (drapeau `ignore`) ; gestion d'erreur sur la révocation d'invitation.
- **Timeline** : déduplication à la pagination par offset (plus de cartes / clés React dupliquées).
- **NotificationsBell** : rollback de l'état optimiste si le marquage « lu » échoue.

## Tests

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm build` ✅ (server `tsc` + web `vite build`)

Aucune migration de schéma nécessaire : la course sur les notifications en double est résolue par une transition transactionnelle plutôt que par une contrainte d'unicité.
